general_translation: Can, Should, It'd be good if
formation: Verb［ば］+ いい
casual_structure: Verb［ば］+ いい
polite_structure: Verb［ば］+ いい + です
explanation: A hypothetical phrase that highlights or asks questions about what would be good.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動をすればいいだろう。
example_sentences.english: It would probably be good if you exercised.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに疲れているなら、仕事を休めばいい。
example_sentences.english: If you are that tired, you should just take a day off.

example_sentences.japanese: どれを食べればいいか迷ってるところ。
example_sentences.english: I'm a little lost as to which one would be good to eat.

example_sentences.japanese: 行ければいいけど、行けるか分からない。
example_sentences.english: It would be good if I could go, but I don't know if I can.

example_sentences.japanese: テストでいい点を取りたかったら、勉強すればいいんじゃない？
example_sentences.english: If you want a good grade on your test, shouldn't you just study?

example_sentences.japanese: それいつまでにやればいい？
example_sentences.english: When would it be good to do it by?

example_sentences.japanese: 眠たいならちょっと仮眠をとればいいのに。
example_sentences.english: If you are sleepy it would be good to take a short nap.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事に早くいけばいいと思いますよ。
example_sentences.english: I think that it would be better to go to work early.

example_sentences.japanese: 道の案内を、誰にきけばいいのか分からない。
example_sentences.english: I don't know who would be good to ask directions from.

example_sentences.japanese: ドライブに行きたいなら、運転免許をとればいいです。
example_sentences.english: If you want to go driving, it would be good to get a driver's license.

example_sentences.japanese: すぐにあやまればいいのに、結局謝らなかった。
example_sentences.english: It would have been good to apologize right away, but he/she didn't apologize after all.

example_sentences.japanese: 欲しいならいえばいいのに、誰も何も言ってくれない。
example_sentences.english: If they want it, then it would be good to say something, but no one is saying anything.

example_sentences.japanese: テニス上手くなりたいなら、もっと練習すればいいのに。
example_sentences.english: If you want to get better at tennis it would be good to practice more.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕がでていけばいいんでしょう。悪いのは僕の方なんだから。
example_sentences.english: It would be better if I leave, right? Since I am the one who has done wrong.

example_sentences.japanese: 少し運動すればいい。きっとスッキリするはず。
example_sentences.english: It would be good if you exercised a little bit. You will definitely feel better.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに無理しないで休憩すればいいのに。
example_sentences.english: It would be good to take a break and not over-work yourself that much.

example_sentences.japanese: 早く寝れればいいのに、全然寝れない。
example_sentences.english: It would be good if I could fall asleep quickly, but I can't sleep at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 好きなら彼にそう言えばいいのに。
example_sentences.english: Even though you should just say it if you like him… (Why don't you)

example_sentences.japanese: 休めばいいのに、皆真面目だから休まない。
example_sentences.english: They should take a break, but because they are all very diligent, they won't.

general_translation: It would be nice if, It would be good if, Should, I hope
formation: Verb［たら］+ いいVerb［ば］+ いいVerb + と + いい［い］Adjective［た］+ ら+ いい［い］Adjective［い］+ ければ+ いい［い］Adjective + と + いい［な］Adjective + だった + ら+ いい［な］Adjective + であれば+ いい［な］Adjective + だ + といい
casual_structure: Verb［たら］+ いいVerb［ば］+ いいVerb + と + いい［い］Adjective［た］+ ら+ いい［い］Adjective［い］+ ければ+ いい［い］Adjective + と + いい［な］Adjective + だった + ら+ いい［な］Adjective + であれば+ いい［な］Adjective + だ + といい
polite_structure: Verb［たら］+ いい + ですVerb［ば］+ いい + ですVerb + と + いい + です［い］Adjective［た］+ ら+ いい + です［い］Adjective［い］+ ければ+ いい + です［い］Adjective + と + いい + です［な］Adjective + だった + ら+ いい + です［な］Adjective + であれば+ いい + です［な］Adjective + だ + といい + です
explanation: A hypothetical phrase that expresses the time or consequence of (A) as being hoped for.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日、好きな番組がみれたらいい。
example_sentences.english: It would be nice if I could watch my favorite TV show everyday.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日までに届けばいいんだけど、多分届かないと思う。
example_sentences.english: It would be good if it gets delivered by tomorrow, but I don't think it will.

example_sentences.japanese: 私もあんなに速く走れたらいいな。
example_sentences.english: It would be nice if I could also run that fast.

example_sentences.japanese: 来年は海外旅行に行けるといいね。
example_sentences.english: It would be nice if we could travel abroad next year, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 自由にしたらいいでしょう。
example_sentences.english: It would be nice to just do whatever you want, wouldn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: 明日と明後日もはれるといいですね。
example_sentences.english: It would be nice if the weather was clear tomorrow and the day after, wouldn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: 文句を言わないで！どうしたらいいのか教えてよ。
example_sentences.english: Stop complaining! Tell me what would be good to do!

example_sentences.japanese: 僕もイルカみたいに上手におよげたらいいのに。
example_sentences.english: I wish I could swim well like a dolphin. (it would be good if...)

example_sentences.japanese: いつか一緒に日本に行けるといいな。
example_sentences.english: I hope that I can go to Japan with you someday. (it would be good if...)

example_sentences.japanese: いつかまたどこかであえたらいいね。
example_sentences.english: I hope that we can meet each other again somewhere, someday.

example_sentences.japanese: 昔大好きだったお店、まだやっているといいな。
example_sentences.english: I hope the restaurant (shop) that I loved is still open. (it would be good if...)

example_sentences.japanese: 辛すぎて、何をいったらいいか分からない。
example_sentences.english: It's so darn spicy that I don't know what I should say. (would be good to say...)

example_sentences.japanese: 失敗してもいいからやってみるといい。
example_sentences.english: It doesn't matter if you mess up. It would be better if you just tried it.

example_sentences.japanese: どの道をいったらいいのかもっと詳しく教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please tell me in more detail which way would be good to go.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人に聞いてみるといい。何でも答えてくれるから。
example_sentences.english: It would be good to ask that person. He will answer any question.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を上手にしゃべれるようになりたかったら、日本人としゃべったらいい。
example_sentences.english: You should speak to Japanese people if you want to improve your Japanese conversational ability. (it would be good if...)

general_translation: During, While, Throughout, In the process of
formation: Noun + 中（ちゅう） （に）
casual_structure: Noun + 中（ちゅう） （に）
explanation: An expression that highlights an action in process, or the entire scope of something. To be within or throughout (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 一日じゅう、勉強をした。
example_sentences.english: I studied (all) throughout the day.

example_sentences.japanese: 食事ちゅうに電話がかかってくると、イラっとする。
example_sentences.english: It ticks me off when I get a phone call while I'm eating.

example_sentences.japanese: ゴミが家じゅうに広がっていて、歩くスペースがない。
example_sentences.english: There is so much garbage throughout my house, that there is no room to walk.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年じゅうにイタリアに行きたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to go to Italy this year. (Within this year as the limit)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日じゅうにレポートを提出してください。
example_sentences.english: Please submit your papers by today. (Within today as the limit)

example_sentences.japanese: 今は仕事ちゅうなんだ。
example_sentences.english: I am in the middle of working right now.

example_sentences.japanese: 締め切りは今月ちゅうなんです。
example_sentences.english: The deadline is sometime (during) this month.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は休憩ちゅうに本を読む。
example_sentences.english: He reads books during his break. (At some point during the act of taking a break)

example_sentences.japanese: 私は勉強ちゅうに話されるのが嫌いだ。
example_sentences.english: I don't like being talked to while studying. (At some point during the act of study)

example_sentences.japanese: 授業ちゅうに、トイレに行きたくなった。
example_sentences.english: During class, I began to feel I needed to go to the restroom.

example_sentences.japanese: 食事ちゅうにスマホをいじるのはやめなさい。
example_sentences.english: Quit playing on your smartphone while you are eating!

example_sentences.japanese: まだ考えちゅうだから、決めていないよ。
example_sentences.english: I am still in the process of thinking, so I haven't decided yet.

example_sentences.japanese: テストちゅうに私の携帯が鳴ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: My phone accidentally rang during the test.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕はダイエットちゅうなのに、ケーキがあったら食べてしまう。
example_sentences.english: Even while I am on a diet, if there is cake, I end up eating it.

example_sentences.japanese: 今晩じゅうにこの仕事を終わらせないといけないから、今夜は徹夜だ。
example_sentences.english: Because I have to finish this work tonight, I must stay up (all) throughout the night. (During tonight)

example_sentences.japanese: ポケモンは、日本じゅうだけでなく、世界じゅうで流行ったゲームだ。
example_sentences.english: Pokémon is popular not only all over Japan, but throughout the world.

example_sentences.japanese: 何度かけても電話ちゅうだ。誰と長電話しているんだろう…
example_sentences.english: No matter how many times I ring, they're in the middle of a call. Who is she talking to for so long?

example_sentences.japanese: 試合ちゅうに足を怪我してしまって、松葉杖がなければ歩けない。
example_sentences.english: I got hurt during the game so I cannot walk without crutches.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年じゅうにこのプロジェクトを完成させなかったら、他社に遅れをとってしまう。
example_sentences.english: We must complete this project by the end of this year, otherwise we could fall behind other companies. (During, throughout this year)

example_sentences.japanese: あの同僚は仕事ちゅうなのにいつも彼女とメールをする不真面目な奴だ。
example_sentences.english: That co-worker is so incompetent, always texting his girlfriend during work.

general_translation: While, During, Between, Period
formation: Verb + 間（あいだ）に［い］Adjective + 間（あいだ）に［な］Adjective + な + 間（あいだ）にNoun + の + 間（あいだ）に
casual_structure: Verb + 間（あいだ）に［い］Adjective + 間（あいだ）に［な］Adjective + な + 間（あいだ）にNoun + の + 間（あいだ）に
explanation: A grammar point which highlights a physical or time-based space or interval within which something else happens or exists.

example_sentences.japanese: あくびをしている間に笑わせないでって前も言ったじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: I told you before not to make me laugh while I'm yawning!

example_sentences.japanese: 若い間に色々な経験をした方がいいです。
example_sentences.english: It would be better if you experience many different things while you are young.

example_sentences.japanese: 暇な間に、部屋の片付けをしておこう。
example_sentences.english: While I'm free, I should clean my room. (Because I can't when I am busy)

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫とシンクの間に箸を落としてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I accidentally dropped a chopstick between the sink and the refrigerator.

example_sentences.japanese: １月から４月までの間に日本に行きたいと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think I want to go to Japan sometime between January and April.

example_sentences.japanese: １３時から１５時までの間に連絡をください。
example_sentences.english: Please give us a call from the period of between 1 pm and 3 pm.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は冬休みの間に地元へ帰った。
example_sentences.english: She went back to her home town during winter break.

example_sentences.japanese: コンタクトと目の間にゴミが入って、目がとても痛い。
example_sentences.english: My eye is extremely sore because I got something between my contact and my eye.

example_sentences.japanese: いつも眠っているあいだに歯軋りをしてしまう。
example_sentences.english: I always grind my teeth while I'm asleep.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が暇なあいだに、電話をかけてください。
example_sentences.english: Please call me while I am free.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事に行くまでのあいだに掃除したかったけど無理だった。
example_sentences.english: During the time that I had before going to work I wanted to clean, but it was not possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が家にいるあいだに、電話をかけてください。
example_sentences.english: Please call me while I am at home.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕が東京に行っていた５年のあいだに、彼は変わってしまった。
example_sentences.english: He had changed during the 5 years I was in Tokyo.

example_sentences.japanese: この山とあの山のあいだの谷に、僕の実家がある。
example_sentences.english: My parents' house is in the valley between this mountain and that mountain.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜寝ているあいだに、泥棒に入られた。
example_sentences.english: A robber broke in while we were sleeping at night.

example_sentences.japanese: 背が高い二人のあいだに挟まれて、ちょっと嫌だった。
example_sentences.english: I felt uncomfortable being sandwiched between those two tall people.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっと見ないあいだに随分大人になったね。
example_sentences.english: You have certainly matured in the short time while I had not seen you.

example_sentences.japanese: 長い航海のあいだに、僕は本物の船乗りになったんだ。
example_sentences.english: During a long voyage, I became a real sailor.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「わぁ、その鼻どうしたの？」 Ｂ：「やっぱり変？空手の稽古中に、壁と相手の拳のあいだに挟まれて折れちゃったんだよね。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Woah, what happened to your nose?' B: 'It looks funky right? I broke it during karate practice when it got sandwiched between the wall and my opponent's fist.'

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の午後の２時から３時までのあいだには、荷物が届くだろう。
example_sentences.english: The package will probably arrive between 2pm and 3pm today.

general_translation: While, During
formation: Verb［ている］+ うちに［い］Adjective + うちに［な］Adjective + な + うちにNoun + の + うちに
casual_structure: Verb［ている］+ うちに［い］Adjective + うちに［な］Adjective + な + うちにNoun + の + うちに
explanation: A grammar point which highlights (A) as being the optimal time to do (B), or that (B) happened at some imprecise time within (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 近いうちに連絡します。
example_sentences.english: I'll be in touch within the near future.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼と毎日会ううちに、だんだんと彼のことが好きになってきた。
example_sentences.english: As I meet with him every day, I have gradually come to like him. (As I spend more time with him every day, I have grown to like him)

example_sentences.japanese: 熱いうちに食べて！
example_sentences.english: Eat it while it's hot!

example_sentences.japanese: お爺ちゃんがまだ元気なうちに家族皆で旅行に行こう！
example_sentences.english: Let's all go on a family trip while grandpa is still healthy!

example_sentences.japanese: 今のうちに明日の準備をしておこう。
example_sentences.english: Let's get ready for tomorrow while we have time. (Before it is too late)

example_sentences.japanese: 運転している間に眠くなったので、コンビニで休憩をした。
example_sentences.english: I got sleepy while driving, so I took a break at a convenience store. (While in the process of driving)

example_sentences.japanese: 運転しているうちに眠くなったので、コンビニで休憩をした。
example_sentences.english: I got sleepy while driving, so I took a break at a convenience store. (At one point while driving)

example_sentences.japanese: 鉄は熱いうちに打て。
example_sentences.english: Strike while the iron is hot.

example_sentences.japanese: 授業を受けているうちに、宿題を完成させた。
example_sentences.english: I was able to finish my homework while taking a class.

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんは食べているうちに寝てしまった。
example_sentences.english: The baby fell asleep while eating.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本にいるうちに東京に行ってみたい。
example_sentences.english: While I am in Japan, I want to see Tokyo.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝顔はみるみるうちに成長し、大きくなった。
example_sentences.english: The Morning Glory grew taller and got bigger within / during a short time.

example_sentences.japanese: 一晩のうちに性格を変えることはできない。
example_sentences.english: It is impossible to change your personality over the course of / during one night.

example_sentences.japanese: 明るいうちに家に帰ろう。あの道は暗いから。
example_sentences.english: Let's go home while it's still light out. Since that street is dark.

example_sentences.japanese: 若いうちにお酒を飲んだりタバコを吸ったりしてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: You must not drink and smoke while you are young.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕が仕事をしているうちに、君が夕食を作ってくれるから助かる。
example_sentences.english: It is quite helpful that you make dinner while I do my work.

example_sentences.japanese: やっているうちにどんどん上達するから、あきらめてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: You must not give up because you will continue to get better while doing it.

example_sentences.japanese: 一生のうちに一度は聖書を読んでみたいと思っている。
example_sentences.english: I would like to try to read the Bible at least once in / during my lifetime.

general_translation: Before it becomes, Before ~ occurs, Without
formation: Verb［ない］+ うちに + Phrase
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ うちに + Phrase
explanation: A construction that highlights a period of time in which (A) didn't happen, or wasn't noticed, often leading to a negative result.

example_sentences.japanese: くらくならないうちに帰って来なさいよ。
example_sentences.english: Come back home before it gets dark.

example_sentences.japanese: こうき君、全然会わないうちに、凄く大きくなったね！
example_sentences.english: Kouki-kun, you have grown so much during the time we haven't met. (Since the last time I saw you)

example_sentences.japanese: また電話をかけ忘れるところだった。忘れないうちに電話しておかなきゃ。
example_sentences.english: I was just about to forget to make a phone call again. I should call before I forget.

example_sentences.japanese: 私がしらないうちに、友達が離婚していた。
example_sentences.english: Before I knew it, my friend was divorced.

example_sentences.japanese: さめないうちにお召し上がりください。
example_sentences.english: Please eat it before it gets cold.

example_sentences.japanese: ねむくならないうちに宿題を終わらせよう。
example_sentences.english: Let's finish the homework before I get sleepy.

example_sentences.japanese: いくらもおよがないうちに、向こう岸についてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Without swimming that much, I reached the other shore.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ親しくならないうちに、同僚が辞めてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Before we became close, my co-worker quit.

example_sentences.japanese: 先方の気がかわらないうちに、契約を済ませてください。
example_sentences.english: Close the deal with them before they change their mind.

example_sentences.japanese: 第１巻を読みおわらないうちに、第２巻が出てしまった。
example_sentences.english: The second volume came out before I had finished reading the first volume.

example_sentences.japanese: わすれないうちに言っておきますが、私は来週から出張です。
example_sentences.english: I should tell you, before I forget, I am going on a business trip next week.

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんが何人もあつまらないうちに、スピーチが始まった。
example_sentences.english: The speech began before many people had gathered.

example_sentences.japanese: きづかないうちに、列車が出発してしまっていた。
example_sentences.english: Before I could notice, the train had started to depart (without me). (without noticing・before noticing occurs)

example_sentences.japanese: あきられないうちに、新商品を出した方がいいな。
example_sentences.english: I think we should introduce a new product before the people lose interest.

example_sentences.japanese: 出かける前にバイオリンの練習をしないといけない。
example_sentences.english: I need to practice playing my violin before I go out.

example_sentences.japanese: 知らないうちに家の前にあるラーメン屋が潰れていた。
example_sentences.english: Without realizing it, the ramen shop in front of my house went out of business.

general_translation: Must, Should , Ought to
formation: Verb + べき + だVerb + べき + Noun［い］Adjective + くある + べき + だ［な］Adjective + である + べき + だNoun + である + べき + だExceptions:する  ￫ す（る）べき
casual_structure: Verb + べき + だVerb + べき + Noun［い］Adjective + くある + べき + だ［な］Adjective + である + べき + だNoun + である + べき + だExceptions:する  ￫ す（る）べき
polite_structure: Verb + べき + ですVerb + べき + Noun［い］Adjective + くある + べき + です［な］Adjective + である + べき + ですNoun + である + べき + ですExceptions:する  ￫ す（る）べき
explanation: A very strong, sometimes critical way to express how something ought to be.

example_sentences.japanese: 税金をはらうべきです。
example_sentences.english: You should pay taxes.

example_sentences.japanese: そういう事は本人に言うべきだ。
example_sentences.english: You ought to say things like that to the person themselves.

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんの意見はちゃんと聞くべきだ。
example_sentences.english: You ought to properly listen to customers' opinions.

example_sentences.japanese: ハマサキさんは尊敬するべき人だ。
example_sentences.english: Hamasaki-san is someone you ought to look up to.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたに教えるべき事はこれで全部です。
example_sentences.english: With this, I have now taught you all of the things that I ought to.

example_sentences.japanese: かんがえるべきことが多すぎて、頭が痛い。
example_sentences.english: There are too many things I should think about, so my head hurts.

example_sentences.japanese: いうべきことを言うのは親の義務だ。
example_sentences.english: Saying things that you should say is a duty of a parent.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰も見ていなくても、法律はまもるべきだ。
example_sentences.english: Even when no one is looking, you should obey the law.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の会議は重大な話があるので、出席をするべきだ。
example_sentences.english: Because we will talk about something important at tomorrow's meeting, everyone should attend.

example_sentences.japanese: 君が責任をとるべきだ。リーダーなんだから。
example_sentences.english: You should take responsibility since you are the leader.

example_sentences.japanese: この茶碗をかうべきだ。こんな掘り出し物はあまりないよ。
example_sentences.english: You should buy this bowl. It is not often that you come across such a bargain.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を声に出してよむべきだ。その方が上達するから。
example_sentences.english: You should read Japanese aloud, because you will get better that way.

example_sentences.japanese: 失敗したら早めに報告すべきだ。隠すと余計に大変なことになる。
example_sentences.english: If you make a mistake, you should report it as soon as possible. If you try to hide it, it will only get worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 痩せたい人は運動をすべきだと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think people who want to slim down should exercise.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を学ぶ人がしっておくべき情報がこの本にはたくさん書かれている。
example_sentences.english: This book has a lot of information that people who learn Japanese should know.

example_sentences.japanese: さっきあの人に言われたことを妻にいうべきかどうか悩む。
example_sentences.english: I'm wondering if I should tell my wife what that person said to me.

example_sentences.japanese: やばいやばい、車が止まりそう！高速に乗る前にガソリンを入れておくべきだった。
example_sentences.english: This is not good… ahhh not good, the car is about to stop! I should have filled the car up with gasoline before I got on the highway.

example_sentences.japanese: 大変申し訳ございません。こちらがもっと早く気づくべきでした。
example_sentences.english: We are very sorry. We should have noticed this earlier.

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚する前に相手と将来の話しをするべきだ。
example_sentences.english: Before marrying, you should talk about the future with your partner.

example_sentences.japanese: 家族は何があっても大切にすべきだ。
example_sentences.english: You should prioritize family no matter what happens.

general_translation: Should not, Must not , Ought not to
formation: Verb + べき + ではないVerb + べき + じゃない［い］Adjective + くある + べき + ではない［い］Adjective + くある + べき + じゃない［な］Adjective + である + べき + ではない［な］Adjective + である + べき + じゃないNoun + である + べき + ではないNoun + である + べき + じゃない
casual_structure: Verb + べき + ではないVerb + べき + じゃない［い］Adjective + くある + べき + ではない［い］Adjective + くある + べき + じゃない［な］Adjective + である + べき + ではない［な］Adjective + である + べき + じゃないNoun + である + べき + ではないNoun + である + べき + じゃない
polite_structure: Verb + べき + ではありませんVerb + べき + じゃありません［い］Adjective + くある + べき + ではありません［い］Adjective + くある + べき + じゃありません［な］Adjective + である + べき + ではありません［な］Adjective + である + べき + じゃありませんNoun + である + べき + ではありませんNoun + である + べき + じゃありません
explanation: A very strong, sometimes critical way to express how something ought not to be.

example_sentences.japanese: あなた一人だけできめるべきではない。
example_sentences.english: You should not decide alone.

example_sentences.japanese: 濡れている手でコンセントに触れるべきではない。
example_sentences.english: You must not touch the outlet with wet hands.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなにいう事を聞かなくても、子供に手をあげるべきじゃない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much a child doesn't listen to what you say, you ought not to raise your hand at them.

example_sentences.japanese: 腐っている食べ物をたべるべきではない。
example_sentences.english: You shouldn't eat food that is rotten.

example_sentences.japanese: 禁煙場所では、タバコをすうべきではない。
example_sentences.english: You should not smoke in places that are non-smoking.

example_sentences.japanese: 大したことないよ。心配をするべきではない。
example_sentences.english: It's not important. You shouldn't worry about it.

example_sentences.japanese: 人が嫌がることをするべきではない。
example_sentences.english: You should not do things people dislike.

example_sentences.japanese: 人の悪口をいうべきではない。
example_sentences.english: You should not speak ill of others.

example_sentences.japanese: 図書館で大きな声をだすべきではない。
example_sentences.english: You should not speak loudly in a library.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな天気の悪い日にでかけるべきではない。
example_sentences.english: You should not go out in a bad weather day like this.

example_sentences.japanese: ストレスをためるべきではない。病気になってしまうから。
example_sentences.english: You should not build up stress because you will become ill.

example_sentences.japanese: 「嫌がっている人がいる」という事実を無視するべきではない。
example_sentences.english: You should not ignore the fact that some people don't like it.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなくだらないことに時間を無駄にすべきではない。
example_sentences.english: You should not waste your time for such a worthless thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 人の家庭のことに口出しすべきではない。
example_sentences.english: You should not butt into another family's business.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人であの山に行くべきではない。
example_sentences.english: You must not go to that mountain alone.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人であの山に行くべきじゃない。
example_sentences.english: You must not go to that mountain alone.

example_sentences.japanese: テストの前に徹夜をするべきではない。
example_sentences.english: You ought not to stay up all night before a test.

example_sentences.japanese: くだらないことで警察に電話すべきではない。
example_sentences.english: You must not call the cops for something trivial.

general_translation: As for, Speaking of, Casual は (Sentence topic marker)
formation: Sentence topic + って
casual_structure: Sentence topic + って
explanation: A casual way of marking the general topic of a sentence.

example_sentences.japanese: このパスタって美味しいよね。
example_sentences.english: As for the pasta, it is delicious, don't you think?

example_sentences.japanese: 私って皆に嫌われている？
example_sentences.english: Am I disliked by everyone?

example_sentences.japanese: トマトって野菜なの？フルーツなの？
example_sentences.english: Are tomatoes vegetables? Are they fruits?

example_sentences.japanese: あの人って誰？
example_sentences.english: As for that person, who is it?

example_sentences.japanese: 先生って優しいね。
example_sentences.english: As for the teacher, she is nice, don't you think?

example_sentences.japanese: ギターって弾けますか？
example_sentences.english: As for guitar, can you play it?

example_sentences.japanese: 冬って寒いけど、雪は綺麗だ。
example_sentences.english: As for winter, it is cold, but snow is pretty.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日って何曜日なの？
example_sentences.english: As for tomorrow, which day of the week is it?

example_sentences.japanese: 北海道っていいところですか？
example_sentences.english: As for Hokkaido, is it a nice place?

example_sentences.japanese: スマホって高くないですか？
example_sentences.english: As for smartphones, they are expensive, aren't they?

example_sentences.japanese: 豆腐の木綿と絹ごしってどう違うの？
example_sentences.english: As for 'momen' and 'kinugoshi' tofu, how do they differ?

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事って大変なことが多いですね。
example_sentences.english: As for work, it is full of difficult things, don't you think?

example_sentences.japanese: 諺って覚えた方がいいんですか。
example_sentences.english: As for kotowazas (proverbs), would it be better to memorize them?

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の勉強って難しいな。
example_sentences.english: As for studying Japanese, it is hard.

general_translation: Very, Quite, Considerably
formation: なかなか + Adjectiveなかなか + の + Noun
casual_structure: なかなか + Adjectiveなかなか + の + Noun
explanation: A word that expresses a very high level of (A), by stating that it is at the most center of what would be expected of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: このお菓子はなかなかおいしい。
example_sentences.english: This snack is quite good.

example_sentences.japanese: あのシェフが作るパスタはなかなかの物だ。
example_sentences.english: The pasta that the chef makes is very good.

example_sentences.japanese: ミムラさんもなかなか可愛いよ。
example_sentences.english: Mimura-san is very cute.

example_sentences.japanese: ここのラーメンはなかなか美味しいね。
example_sentences.english: The ramen here  is pretty tasty.

example_sentences.japanese: 元カノはなかなかの美人でしたが、性格が悪かったので別れました。
example_sentences.english: My ex-girlfriend was considerably beautiful, but her personality was bad, so I broke up with her.

example_sentences.japanese: なかなかの事をしてくれたな。こんな事をお客さんにどう説明したらいいんだ。
example_sentences.english: You have done something that is difficult to dismiss, haven't you? How am I supposed to explain this to our client? (What you did cannot be taken lightly. How am I supposed to explain what has happened to our client?)

example_sentences.japanese: ここからの景色はなかなかいいですね。
example_sentences.english: The view from here is quite decent.

example_sentences.japanese: ここの会員になるのはなかなか難しい。
example_sentences.english: Becoming a member here is considerably difficult.

example_sentences.japanese: 富士登山はなかなか大変です。
example_sentences.english: Reaching the top of Mt. Fuji is quite grueling.

example_sentences.japanese: この子が描く絵はなかなかのものです。
example_sentences.english: The paintings that this child paints are quite (extraordinary).

example_sentences.japanese: それはなかなか厳しい注文ですね。
example_sentences.english: That is quite a harsh request.

example_sentences.japanese: この作品はなかなかの出来栄えですよ。
example_sentences.english: This piece (of art) is quite good.

example_sentences.japanese: なかなかかっこいい車だと自分では思っている。
example_sentences.english: I believe that the car is quite cool.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はなかなか頼りになる奴だよ。
example_sentences.english: He is quite a reliable fellow.

example_sentences.japanese: 今月の目標を達成するのはなかなか大変です。
example_sentences.english: It's going to be quite difficult to reach this month's target.

example_sentences.japanese: これはなかなか難しい問題ですね。
example_sentences.english: This is quite a tough question.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はなかなか素直でいい子じゃないか。
example_sentences.english: She's quite honest and good, isn't she?

example_sentences.japanese: 先月始めたばかりなの？なかなか上手じゃないか。
example_sentences.english: You just started last month? You are quite a lot better than I expected!

general_translation: So much...that
formation: Verb + あまり + (Negative Result) Phrase［い］Adjective［さ］+ の + あまり + (Negative Result) Phrase［い］Adjective［み］+ の + あまり + (Negative Result) Phrase［な］Adjective + な + あまり + (Negative Result) PhraseNoun + の + あまり + (Negative Result) Phrase
casual_structure: Verb + あまり + (Negative Result) Phrase［い］Adjective［さ］+ の + あまり + (Negative Result) Phrase［い］Adjective［み］+ の + あまり + (Negative Result) Phrase［な］Adjective + な + あまり + (Negative Result) PhraseNoun + の + あまり + (Negative Result) Phrase
explanation: A structure that often highlights an excessive amount of (A) that causes a negative result.

example_sentences.japanese: トムは驚きのあまり、何も言えなかった。
example_sentences.english: Tom was so surprised that he was speechless.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は仕事を終わらせることに集中するあまり、終電を逃しました。
example_sentences.english: He was so concentrated on finishing his work that he missed the last train.

example_sentences.japanese: トムは暑さのあまり、気を失った。
example_sentences.english: It was so hot that Tom fainted.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は彼と別れて、悲しみのあまりボーっとしている。
example_sentences.english: She broke up with her boyfriend and is so sad that she is spacing out a lot.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は音楽が好きなあまり、仕事を辞めてバンドを作った。
example_sentences.english: He likes music so much that he quit his job and started a band.

example_sentences.japanese: ヤスエは初めてのライブで、緊張のあまり上手く歌えなかった。
example_sentences.english: Yasue had her first concert, and she was so nervous that she couldn't sing well.

example_sentences.japanese: 美味しさのあまり、食べ飽きることはない。
example_sentences.english: It is so delicious that I can never get tired of eating it.

example_sentences.japanese: 悲しさのあまり、言葉を失った。
example_sentences.english: I was so distraught that I was at a loss for words.

example_sentences.japanese: 苦しさのあまり、大きな声を出してしまった。
example_sentences.english: The pain was so unbearable that I shouted out loud.

example_sentences.japanese: 喜びのあまり、涙がとまらない。
example_sentences.english: I am so overjoyed that I cannot stop crying.

example_sentences.japanese: 感動のあまり、鳥肌が立った。
example_sentences.english: I was so touched that I got goosebumps.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行が楽しみなあまり、今日は寝れなさそう。
example_sentences.english: I am so excited for my trip that it seems like I won't be able to sleep tonight.

example_sentences.japanese: 怒りのあまり、暴言を吐いてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I was so angry that I said something rash.(so much)

example_sentences.japanese: ある日、王様は食べすぎたあまり、立ち上がることができなかった。
example_sentences.english: One day, the king ate so much that he wasn't able to stand up.

example_sentences.japanese: 金融危機の間、インフレが深刻化するあまり、政府は価格を設定し始めた。
example_sentences.english: During the financial crisis, the inflation was becoming so intense that the government started to regulate the prices. (so much)

example_sentences.japanese: お化け屋敷に入ったけど、怖さのあまり、座り込んでしまった。
example_sentences.english: I went into the haunted house but I was so afraid that I huddled in fear.

example_sentences.japanese: 若い頃、試験のため一生懸命、勉強したあまり、とても疲れて、集中できなかった日があった。
example_sentences.english: When I was young, I studied so hard for an exam that there was a day when I was completely exhausted and I couldn't concentrate.(so much)

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩は飲み会でお酒を沢山飲んだあまり、一人で帰ることができなかった。
example_sentences.english: Senpai drank so much at the party that he couldn't get home by himself.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近彼女と別れた友達を心配するあまり、友達の話しを聞きに行った。
example_sentences.english: I was so worried about my friend, who has broken up with his girlfriend recently, that I went to his place to listen to him vent.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長は社員全員に恐れられているあまり、誰も社長の提案を否定しない。
example_sentences.english: The CEO of our company is so feared by all of the workers that no one will criticize his decisions.

general_translation: Not really, Hardly, Not easily or readily, By no means, Far from
formation: なかなか + Phrase + Verb［ない］
casual_structure: なかなか + Phrase + Verb［ない］
explanation: A phrase that expresses a very low level of (A), by stating that it is nowhere near the center of what would be expected of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: このシステムはなかなか改善されない。
example_sentences.english: This system is far from being improved.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生、風邪がなかなか治らないんですけど、どうした方がいいですか？
example_sentences.english: Doctor, my cold is hardly getting any better, what should I do?

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事が忙しくてなかなか休みが取れないんだよね。
example_sentences.english: Work is getting so busy that I can hardly take a day off.

example_sentences.japanese: 調査がなかなか進まない。
example_sentences.english: The survey hardly makes any forward progress.

example_sentences.japanese: 貯金がなかなかできない。
example_sentences.english: I can hardly save any money.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、あたしはなかなかやる気が出ない。
example_sentences.english: Recently I am not easily motivated. (hardly)

example_sentences.japanese: 痛みがなかなか良くならない。
example_sentences.english: The pain is not really getting better. (hardly)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はなかなか本当のことを言ってくれません。
example_sentences.english: He is far from telling the truth.

example_sentences.japanese: この飲み物はなかなか飲めない珍しい飲み物です。
example_sentences.english: This is a rare and not so easily drinkable drink.

example_sentences.japanese: 結果がなかなか出ないから不安です。
example_sentences.english: I am anxious because it is taking quite some time for the results to be released. (by no means)

example_sentences.japanese: 山の頂上がなかなか見えてこない。
example_sentences.english: The mountain top is not easily seen. (hardly)

example_sentences.japanese: 事件の犯人がなかなか捕まらない。
example_sentences.english: The criminal responsible for the incident is far from being caught. (By no means)

example_sentences.japanese: 何度この文法の解説を読んでも、なかなか理解できないんだ。
example_sentences.english: No matter how many times I read the explanation for this grammar, I am far from understanding it. (by no means)

example_sentences.japanese: あいつはなかなかトイレから出てこない! 何をしてるんだ？
example_sentences.english: He is taking forever to come out of the toilet. What is he doing in there? (by no means)

example_sentences.japanese: あいつなかなか来ないね。連絡もないし、俺たちだけで行こう。
example_sentences.english: He is not coming at all. Since he hasn't contacted us, let's just go without him.

general_translation: According to
formation: Noun + によると(1)Verb + ところ + によると(1)(1) によれば
casual_structure: Noun + によると(1)Verb + ところ + によると(1)(1) によれば
explanation: A semi-formal expression that highlights information that is according to (A), or stems from (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 天気予報によると、明日は晴れです。
example_sentences.english: According to the weather forecast, tomorrow will be sunny.

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝の天気予報によると、今夜から雪が降るらしいですよ。
example_sentences.english: According to the forecast, it is apparently going to start snowing from tonight.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生に聞いたところによると、来週からオンライン授業になるらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: Going off of what I heard from the teacher, we are going to be taking online classes from next week.

example_sentences.japanese: 愛知県警によりますと、犯人は四十代の男性だと言う事です。
example_sentences.english: According to the Aichi Prefectural Police, the criminal is a 40 year old male.

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝のニュースによれば、来月末から海外旅行が出来るようになる。
example_sentences.english: According to this morning's news, we are going to be able to travel abroad starting from the end of next month.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が聞くところによると、部長が転職するそうだ。
example_sentences.english: Going off of what I heard, the manager is going to be switching jobs.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察によると、犯人が逃げたそうです。
example_sentences.english: According to the police, the criminal escaped.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩の話によると、あの会社はブラック企業らしい。
example_sentences.english: According to what my senior said, that company is one of those 'black companies'.

example_sentences.japanese: 目撃者によれば、犯人は２０代男性だ。
example_sentences.english: According to the witness, the criminal is a man in his 20s.

example_sentences.japanese: 聞くところによれば、彼はあの子が好きみたいだ。
example_sentences.english: According to what I hear, it seems as though he likes that girl.

example_sentences.japanese: 統計によれば、明日は雨が降る確率が高い。
example_sentences.english: According to statistics, there is a high probability it will rain tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 地震速報によると、この地域は震度３だ。
example_sentences.english: According to the Earthquake Early Warning System, this area is having an earthquake with an intensity of three.

example_sentences.japanese: 医者によれば、二、三日ゆっくりすればよくなるらしい。
example_sentences.english: According to the doctor, I will get better if I take it easy for 2 or 3 days.

example_sentences.japanese: 専門家によれば、あの歌い方だと喉に悪いらしい。
example_sentences.english: According to an expert, that style of singing is bad for your throat.

example_sentences.japanese: この地図によるともうすぐ着くはずなのに、家が全然見えてこない。
example_sentences.english: According to the map here, I should be arriving soon, but I don't see the house at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の母によると、毎日野菜を食べる必要があるらしいです。
example_sentences.english: According to my mother, it is necessary to eat vegetables every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝の新聞によると、あの犯人はまだ逃走しているようだ。
example_sentences.english: According to the newspaper issued this morning, that criminal is still on the run.

example_sentences.japanese: 警視庁によると、イマダ容疑者は寝ている母親を包丁で刺していたという事です。
example_sentences.english: According to the Tokyo Metropolitan Police department, Imada, the suspect, stabbed his mother who was sleeping, with a knife.

general_translation: By means of, According to, Depending on, Because of, Due to
formation: Noun + によってNoun + により
casual_structure: Noun + によってNoun + により
explanation: A semi-formal expression that highlights information that is according to (A), or stems from (A).

example_sentences.japanese: その車の値段によって、決めます。
example_sentences.english: I will choose depending on the price of that car.

example_sentences.japanese: ベンおじさんは強盗により、命を奪われた。
example_sentences.english: Uncle Ben's life was taken by a robber.

example_sentences.japanese: 地域によって、ゴミ出しルールが違う。
example_sentences.english: Depending on the area, the rules for throwing out garbage are different.

example_sentences.japanese: 行けるか行けないかは休みが取れるか取れないかによる。
example_sentences.english: Whether I can go or not depends on if I can take a day off.

example_sentences.japanese: 国によって、いろいろな伝統があります。
example_sentences.english: There are a variety of traditions depending on the country.

example_sentences.japanese: 調査によって新たな事実が明らかになった。
example_sentences.english: Through investigation, a new truth was discovered. (by means of)

example_sentences.japanese: 納豆が好きかどうかは人による。
example_sentences.english: It depends on the person whether they like natto or not.

example_sentences.japanese: 話し合いによって決まったのだから、文句言わないで。
example_sentences.english: Our decision was made through discussion, so don't complain.

example_sentences.japanese: 何色を選ぶかは好みによる。
example_sentences.english: It depends on a person's preference what color they choose.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカでは州によって法律が違う。
example_sentences.english: In America, laws differ depending on the state.

example_sentences.japanese: 季節によって体調も変化するから大変だ。
example_sentences.english: It's rough because my physical condition changes depending on the season.

example_sentences.japanese: あきば・いつきさんは火事によってすべての資産を失った。
example_sentences.english: Ms. Itsuki Akiba lost all her assets due to the fire.

example_sentences.japanese: なんでも力によって解決するのは横暴すぎると思います。
example_sentences.english: I think it's too violent to solve everything through force.

example_sentences.japanese: 動かない生活により、人々は以前より心疾患にかかりやすくなってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Due to sedentary lifestyles, people became more prone than before to suffer from heart diseases.

example_sentences.japanese: カーテンによって仕切られたところが僕の部屋だ。
example_sentences.english: The section which is divided by the curtain is my room. (By means of)

example_sentences.japanese: このミスはヒューマンエラーによるものです。
example_sentences.english: This mistake is caused by human error.

example_sentences.japanese: この地震による津波の心配はありません。
example_sentences.english: There is no need to worry about a tsunami brought about from this earthquake.

general_translation: Not~at all
formation: まったく + Phrase［ない］
casual_structure: まったく + Phrase［ない］
explanation: A slightly formal phrase which means in whole, but is primarily used with negative phrases to mean not at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はまったく勉強しない。
example_sentences.english: He does not study at all.

example_sentences.japanese: この子はまったく吠えないですよ。
example_sentences.english: This dog does not bark at all. (子（こ） may sometimes be used about pets, if it is obvious what is being discussed)

example_sentences.japanese: あんたに褒められてもまったく嬉しくない。
example_sentences.english: Even if I did get complimented by you, it wouldn't make me happy at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 店員さんが「この扇風機は静かですよ」って言ったから買ったのに、まったく静かじゃない。
example_sentences.english: The shopkeeper said 'This fan is very quiet', so I bought it. However, it was not quiet at all.

example_sentences.japanese: まったく筋肉がないので私だけでは持てません。
example_sentences.english: I don't have any muscles at all, so I can't carry this by myself.

example_sentences.japanese: まったく変化がない。
example_sentences.english: There is no change at all.

example_sentences.japanese: まったく負けたことがない。
example_sentences.english: I have never lost. Ever.

example_sentences.japanese: まったく学ぶつもりがない。
example_sentences.english: I have no intention of learning at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 実はまったく泳げないんです。
example_sentences.english: To be honest, I can't swim at all.

example_sentences.japanese: まったく冒険する気がない。
example_sentences.english: I do not at all have the desire to go on an adventure.

example_sentences.japanese: まったく見込みがないという意味ではない。
example_sentences.english: It doesn't mean there is no hope at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 鑑定の結果、この絵にはまったく価値がないと判明した。
example_sentences.english: The result of the appraisal revealed that the painting was worth nothing at all.

example_sentences.japanese: テストにまったく知らない問題が出て困った。
example_sentences.english: I ran into trouble when I came across a question on the test that I didn't know at all.

example_sentences.japanese: まったく問題ありません。好きなようにやってください。
example_sentences.english: No problem at all. Please do as you like.

example_sentences.japanese: まったく心にもないお世辞を言うのはやめてください。
example_sentences.english: Please stop flattering me with empty praise. (Praise that isn't at all in from the heart)

example_sentences.japanese: まったくやる気がない人と一緒に働くとか嫌だ。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to work with someone that isn't motivated at all.

example_sentences.japanese: まったく分からないので、手伝ってください。
example_sentences.english: I don't understand at all, so please help me.

example_sentences.japanese: 全然わからない。手伝って。
example_sentences.english: I have no clue. Can you help me?

general_translation: Should, Ought
formation: Verb［る］ + こと + だVerb［ない］ + こと + だ
casual_structure: Verb［る］ + こと + だVerb［ない］ + こと + だ
polite_structure: Verb［る］ + こと + ですVerb［ない］ + こと + です
explanation: A particle construction that is often used for presenting orders or expectations from an authority.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回は、相手を信じてみることだ。
example_sentences.english: I think you ought to trust him/her this time.

example_sentences.japanese: 面倒くさくても朝ご飯を食べることだ。
example_sentences.english: Even though it might be a pain, you should eat breakfast.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の朝８時から試験が始まる。何があっても、時間通りに来ることだ。みんな、分かったか。
example_sentences.english: The exams will begin tomorrow at 8 am. No matter what happens, you should come on time. Understood?

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに疲れていても諦めないことだ。
example_sentences.english: You should not give up, no matter how tired you are.

example_sentences.japanese: 怪我をしたら、我慢をしないことだ。すぐ責任者に報告するように。
example_sentences.english: If you get hurt, you shouldn't just suffer in silence. Immediately call your supervisor.

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒は、先生に従うことだ。
example_sentences.english: Students should obey their teachers.

example_sentences.japanese: 医者からもらった薬は必ず飲むことだ。
example_sentences.english: You should take the medicine your doctor prescribed.

example_sentences.japanese: まずはやってみることだ。改善点が見えてくるから。
example_sentences.english: You ought to try it first because you'll find out what needs to be improved.

example_sentences.japanese: 覚えたらすぐにしゃべってみることだ。上達するから。
example_sentences.english: As soon as you memorize something, you ought to say it out loud. If you do that, you will get better.

example_sentences.japanese: なんでも自分一人で決めないで、社員に相談してみることだ。
example_sentences.english: Don't decide everything by yourself, you ought to try to discuss it with the employees.(someone giving advice on how to run a business)

example_sentences.japanese: 成功したいなら、何があってもあきらめないことだ。
example_sentences.english: If you want to succeed, you should never give up, no matter what.

example_sentences.japanese: 子どもたちに安心感を与えたいのなら、いつもそばにいてあげることだ。
example_sentences.english: If you want your children to feel secure, you should always be there for them.

example_sentences.japanese: コツをつかみたいなら、とにかく何回もやってみることだ。
example_sentences.english: If you want to get the hang of it (get better), for the time being, you should do it over and over again.

example_sentences.japanese: 分からないことがあれば、先生に聞いてみることだ。
example_sentences.english: If there is something you don't understand, you should ask the teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 君はすぐに物事を忘れてしまうね。もっとメモを取ることだよ。
example_sentences.english: You always instantly forget things. You should take more notes.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は大切な試合があるから、練習をすることだ。
example_sentences.english: Because there is an important game tomorrow, you should practice.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩、後輩はもっと大切にすることだ。
example_sentences.english: Senpai you should treat your kouhai with great care.

general_translation: I heard that, It is said that
formation: Verb + そう + だ［い］Adjective + そう + だNoun + だ + そう + だ［な］Adjective + だ + そう + だ
casual_structure: Verb + そう + だ［い］Adjective + そう + だNoun + だ + そう + だ［な］Adjective + だ + そう + だ
polite_structure: Verb + そう + です［い］Adjective + そう + ですNoun + だ + そう + です［な］Adjective + だ + そう + です
explanation: An expression that highlights how (A) seems to be, based on what someone has heard.

example_sentences.japanese: おいしいそうだから、たくさん買った。
example_sentences.english: I heard they taste good, so I bought a bunch.

example_sentences.japanese: 次の患者さんは酷い事故にあったそうです。
example_sentences.english: I heard that the next patient was in a bad accident.

example_sentences.japanese: あそこから見る夕日は綺麗だそうです。
example_sentences.english: I heard that the sunset that you can see from there is beautiful.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩は明日も仕事だそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that senpai will be working tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: この種類の鳥はよく鳴くそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that this bird chirps a lot.

example_sentences.japanese: トムの彼女は女優だそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Tom's girlfriend is an actress.

example_sentences.japanese: あの方は親切だそうです。
example_sentences.english: I heard that that person is kind.

example_sentences.japanese: 来週から気温がさがるそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that from next week the temperature is going to drop.

example_sentences.japanese: 今晩雨がふるそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard it will rain tonight.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は怒ったら怖いが、普段はやさしいそうだ。
example_sentences.english: That person is scary when he/she gets angry, but I heard that he/she is usually kind.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らは来月、ずっと行きたがっていたアメリカに旅行にいくそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that they will go to America next month, the place they had been wanting to go to for a long time.

example_sentences.japanese: さむくなるそうだから、僕の上着を貸してあげよう。
example_sentences.english: I heard it's going to get cold, so I will lend you my jacket.

example_sentences.japanese: これは明日のテストにでるそうだ。覚えておこう。
example_sentences.english: I heard that this will be on the test tomorrow. I should memorize it.

example_sentences.japanese: あと一つの課題をクリアすれば、この仕事はうまくいくそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that if I complete one more task, I will do well at this job.

example_sentences.japanese: 点数が伸びれば、あのチームは合格ラインに到達するそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that that team is going to reach a passing grade if they get more points.

example_sentences.japanese: ぶんぽうちゃんは１１時ぐらいにここにくるそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Bunpou-chan will come around 11 o'clock.

general_translation: Having done..., If...is done..., (And/just) then, Thereupon, If so
formation: Phrase。すると + (Result) Phrase
casual_structure: Phrase。すると + (Result) Phrase
explanation: A sentence starter which highlights that upon the previous (A) being done, the uncontrollable result of (B) then also happened. Going off (A) being done, (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 口笛を吹いた。すると、小鳥がやって来た。
example_sentences.english: I whistled. Having done that, a small bird came.

example_sentences.japanese: 久しぶりに押入れの掃除をした。すると、無くしたと思っていた服が出てきた。
example_sentences.english: I cleaned my closet for the first time in a long time. Upon that, I found clothes that I thought I had lost.

example_sentences.japanese: お祖母ちゃんが川で洗濯をしていた。すると、川の向こうから桃が流れてきた。
example_sentences.english: An old lady was washing her clothes in the river. Just then, a peach flowed down the river from a distance.

example_sentences.japanese: 目を閉じた。すると、一瞬で眠ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: I closed my eyes. And then I fell asleep immediately.

example_sentences.japanese: 川に魚を釣りに行った。すると、そこで旧友に会った。なんという偶然？
example_sentences.english: I went fishing on the river. And then I met an old friend there. What a coincidence!

example_sentences.japanese: 従兄弟が絵を描いていた。すると、弟も真似をして描き始めた。
example_sentences.english: My cousin was drawing a picture. And then my younger brother, imitating him, started to draw too.

example_sentences.japanese: A：「僕は◯◯年生まれです。」B：「すると、車を運転できる歳ですね。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I was born in XX year.'B: 'Then, you are old enough to drive, right?'

example_sentences.japanese: ハロウィンで魔女の格好をした。すると、とてもかわいいと言ってもらえてうれしかった。
example_sentences.english: I dressed up as a witch for halloween. And then, people told me I was very cute which made me happy.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日夢を見はじめた。すると、弟に起こされた。
example_sentences.english: I was starting to dream yesterday. And then I was woken up by my brother.

example_sentences.japanese: 老夫婦は桃を見つけた。すると、桃が割れて、その中に赤ん坊がいた。
example_sentences.english: An elderly couple found a peach. And then it split, and there was a child inside.

example_sentences.japanese: ある日、灯りをつけた。すると、電球が破裂した。あんなにびっくりしたことはなかった。
example_sentences.english: One day, I turned on the light. And then the light bulb exploded. I have never been that surprised in my life.

example_sentences.japanese: 手伝ってくれるかどうか聞いた。すると彼はめんどうくさいなぁという顔をした。
example_sentences.english: I asked if he could help me. And then he made a 'this is going to be bothersome' face.

example_sentences.japanese: 午後３時ぐらいに出かけた。すると助けを求める悲鳴が聞こえた。
example_sentences.english: I went out around 3 p.m. And then I heard a cry for help.

example_sentences.japanese: ピアノの演奏が終わった。すると、観客が一斉に拍手をした。
example_sentences.english: They finished playing the piano. And then the audience started clapping all at once.

example_sentences.japanese: 猿にバナナをあげた。すると、猿がどんどん集まってきた。
example_sentences.english: I gave a banana to a monkey. Having done that, more and more monkeys started to gather around me.

example_sentences.japanese: １９歳なの？すると、大学１年生でしょう？
example_sentences.english: You are 19? So you mean to say that you are a freshman, right?

general_translation: Having done that..., If that is done..., (And/just) then, Thereupon, If so
formation: Phrase (A)。 そうすると + (Result) Phrase
casual_structure: Phrase (A)。 そうすると + (Result) Phrase
explanation: A hypothetical expression pointing out that if something is done like that thing which was previously mentioned, (B) will be the result.

example_sentences.japanese: もう少し音量を上げて。そうするとみんな聞こえるから。
example_sentences.english: Raise the volume up just a little more. If that is done, then everyone can hear.

example_sentences.japanese: もう少し遅く走ってみれば。そうすると、もっと長い距離走れるよ。
example_sentences.english: Try to run a little slower. Once you do that, you will be able to run a longer distance.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べる前に軽く炙ってください。そうすると、もっと美味しく食べれます。
example_sentences.english: Please roast before eating. Having done that, it will taste even more delicious.

example_sentences.japanese: この道を右に曲がってください。そうすると案内板がありますから。
example_sentences.english: Please turn right at this street. Having done that, you will see a street map.

example_sentences.japanese: この時刻には家を出てください。そうすると間に合いますから。
example_sentences.english: Please leave the house at this time. If that is done you will be on time.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょっと右に寄ってくれる？そうするとみんな見れるから。
example_sentences.english: Could you move a little to the right? Having done that, everyone will be able to see.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい機械を導入するんですね。そうすると、僕の仕事はなくなるということですか？
example_sentences.english: The new machines are being introduced, huh? If that happens, does it mean that I will lose my job?

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日少しずつ日本語の勉強をしてみて。そうするといつしか上達しているよ。
example_sentences.english: Study Japanese everyday, bit by bit. Having done that, you will improve before you know it.

example_sentences.japanese: 素直で正直に生きるようにして。そうすると周りに人が集まってくるよ。
example_sentences.english: Please, try to live honestly. If you do so, people will gather around you.

example_sentences.japanese: 君は問題を避けているだけだよ。そうするとしばらく楽なのかもしれないけど、きっと後悔するよ。
example_sentences.english: You are only avoiding problems. If you do so, you might temporarily be at ease, but you will certainly regret it.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事に集中してください。そうすると時間が過ぎるのが早く感じますから。
example_sentences.english: Please focus on your job. If you do so, time will feel like it is flying by.

example_sentences.japanese: そのボタンを押してください。そうするとエンジンがかかります。
example_sentences.english: Please push that button. Having done that, the engine will start.

example_sentences.japanese: もうすぐ佐藤さんが仕事を辞めてしまう。そうすると私の仕事が増えるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Sato-san will quit soon. (He) having done that, my workload will increase.

example_sentences.japanese: スペインが負けそうだ。そうするとドイツの優勝かな。
example_sentences.english: It looks like Spain will lose. If so, Germany will probably take the title.

example_sentences.japanese: この餌を使ってみ。そうすると、もっと大きい魚が釣れるよ。
example_sentences.english: Try using this bait. If you do so, you'll be able to catch a bigger fish. (Whether a fish bites or not cannot be controlled)

example_sentences.japanese: １９９３年生まれなんですか？そうすると、２９歳と言う事ですね。
example_sentences.english: You were born in 1993? So that means that you are 29, right?

general_translation: It is...that..., It is...who..., ...is the one that..., ...is the one who...
formation: Phrase + のは + Noun + の方（ほう）だな-Adjective+ な + のは + Noun + の方（ほう）だNoun + な + のは + Noun + の方（ほう）だ
casual_structure: Phrase + のは + Noun + の方（ほう）だな-Adjective+ な + のは + Noun + の方（ほう）だNoun + な + のは + Noun + の方（ほう）だ
polite_structure: Phrase + のは + Noun + の方（ほう）ですな-Adjective+ な + のは + Noun + の方（ほう）ですNoun + な + のは + Noun + の方（ほう）です
explanation: A phrase indicating the general situation of (A), and then something which is more that way. The one who is (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 危険なのはオレの方だよ。
example_sentences.english: I am the one who is dangerous.

example_sentences.japanese: 言い出したのは俺の方だから、俺がなんとかしておくよ。
example_sentences.english: I am the one that said it, so I will do something about it.

example_sentences.japanese: そのコップを壊したのはタケルの方だ！俺は関係ないよ！
example_sentences.english: The one that broke the cup is Takeru! I have nothing to do with it!

example_sentences.japanese: 主な賞を受賞するのはあちゃんの方だといいな。
example_sentences.english: I hope that the one who will win the main prize will be A-chan.(A-chan is the one who...)

example_sentences.japanese: ドアを開けっぱなしにしたのはキちゃんのほうだと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think that Ki-chan was the one who left the doors open (not me).

example_sentences.japanese: あのときサカモトくんを誘いたかったのは、あたしの方だ。
example_sentences.english: I am the one who wanted to invite Sakamoto-kun at that time.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしが怖いのは、犬ではなく飼い主のほうだ。
example_sentences.english: The owner is the one who I am afraid of, not the dog.

example_sentences.japanese: お前に言いつけたのはオレの方だから、彼女はほっておいて。
example_sentences.english: It was I  who told on you, not her, so leave her alone.

example_sentences.japanese: フランシス：「お金を持っているのはアイツのほうだ。でも権威を持っているのはオレさまのほうだ。」
example_sentences.english: Francis: 'It is he who has money. However, I am the one who has power.'

example_sentences.japanese: 北海道と沖縄とでは暖かい気候なのは後者の方だ。
example_sentences.english: Out of Hokkaido and Okinawa, it is the latter that has a warm climate.

example_sentences.japanese: きみをいろいろ助けてあげたのに、裏切ったのはきみのほうだ。信じられない。
example_sentences.english: Even though I did so much for you, you are the one who betrayed me. I can't believe it.

example_sentences.japanese: ギャング１：「赤いズボンを履いているのが奴なのか？」ギャング２：「いいえ、私達が追っているのはタバコを吸ってる奴の方だろう。」
example_sentences.english: Gangster1: 'Is it the guy wearing red pants?'Gangster2: 'No, we are probably searching for the guy who is smoking.'

example_sentences.japanese: でもお母さん、晩ご飯のまえにお菓子を食べたのは兄貴のほうだよ。
example_sentences.english: But mom, big bro is the one who ate sweets before dinner (not me)!

example_sentences.japanese: 「あたしがわるいの。ごめんなさい！」「君が悪いんじゃないよ。謝るべきなのはぼくのほうだ。」
example_sentences.english: 'It is my fault! I am so sorry!''You are not at fault. I am the one who should apologize.'

example_sentences.japanese: 謝らなければいけないのは私の方ですよ。あなたは何も悪くないです。
example_sentences.english: The one that needs to apologize is me. You are not in the wrong at all.

general_translation: Model, Type, Pattern, Kind, Shape, Size(d)
formation: Noun + がた(1)Noun + の + かたNoun + がた(1) +（の）+ Noun［い］Adjective + かた(1) けい
casual_structure: Noun + がた(1)Noun + の + かたNoun + がた(1) +（の）+ Noun［い］Adjective + かた(1) けい
explanation: A suffix which defines the shape, pattern, or model of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 整数はデータがたの一つである。
example_sentences.english: An integer is one of the data types.

example_sentences.japanese: この紙を星がたに切ってください。
example_sentences.english: Please cut this paper into the shape of a star.

example_sentences.japanese: このかたのスマホはよく壊れます。
example_sentences.english: This type of smartphone breaks often.

example_sentences.japanese: 九十年代には犬がたのロボットのおもちゃが人気だった。
example_sentences.english: During the 90s, dog-type robots were popular.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいかたの自転車はいつ発売されますか？
example_sentences.english: When is the new model of this bike coming out?

example_sentences.japanese: 次はどんな髪がたにしよう。
example_sentences.english: What kind of hairstyle should I get next?

example_sentences.japanese: 私はハートがたのアクセサリーが好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like heart-shaped accessories.

example_sentences.japanese: きみの血液がたは何？
example_sentences.english: What is your blood type?

example_sentences.japanese: 「よう」という表現はさまざまな文けいに使われている。
example_sentences.english: The expression 'よう' is used in various sentence patterns.

example_sentences.japanese: 君が言ったように、はるこは２０００年がたのモペットを持っている。
example_sentences.english: It is like you said, Haruko has a year 2000 model moped.

example_sentences.japanese: 母はハートがたの枕を編み上げた。
example_sentences.english: Mom has finished knitting a heart-shaped pillow.

example_sentences.japanese: この星がたのネックレスは金でできています。
example_sentences.english: This star-shaped necklace is made from gold.

example_sentences.japanese: 土壌のかたによってさまざまな野菜が栽培できる。
example_sentences.english: Various vegetables can be cultivated depending on the type of soil.

example_sentences.japanese: 黒帯を持つにはすべての基本のかたを知っていなければなりません。
example_sentences.english: In order to achieve a black belt, you have to know all the basic forms.

example_sentences.japanese: これは君を殺すために送り込まれた人間がたのロボットに違いない。
example_sentences.english: There is no doubt that this is a humanoid robot that has been sent in to kill you.

example_sentences.japanese: スマホ時代にはポケットがたの電子辞書の人気が減っていく一方だ。
example_sentences.english: In the age of smartphones, pocket-sized electronic dictionaries are losing popularity.

example_sentences.japanese: スタイリスト：「今日はどうされますか？」クライアント：「最近トレンドの髪がたにできますか？」
example_sentences.english: Stylist: 'What would you like us to do for you today?'Client: 'Could you style my hair into some trendy-type hairstyle?'

example_sentences.japanese: 統合がたのグラフィックのラップトップは電池寿命が長いながらも、単体のグラフィックに比べてパフォーマンスはより低い。
example_sentences.english: Although laptop models with integrated graphics cards have a long battery life, when compared with the ones with a dedicated graphics card, the performance is lacking.

example_sentences.japanese: 文型は基本なのでしっかりと勉強しておきましょう。
example_sentences.english: Grammar structures are the basics, so make sure to properly study them in advance.

general_translation: (Please) try to, (Please) look
formation: Verb［て］+ ごらんVerb［て］+ ごらんなさい
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ ごらんVerb［て］+ ごらんなさい
explanation: An honorific expression used to ask someone to attempt to do (A), or to peruse at their leisure.

example_sentences.japanese: その景色をみてごらん。
example_sentences.english: (Try to) take a look at that scenery.

example_sentences.japanese: この本を読んでごらん。この本を読んだら日本について色々と学べるよ。
example_sentences.english: Try reading this book. If you read it, you will learn various things about Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 外を見てごらん。虹が出ているよ。
example_sentences.english: Look outside. There is a rainbow.

example_sentences.japanese: ニュースをみてごらん。あなたが映っているよ。
example_sentences.english: (Try to) take a look at the news. You are on TV.

example_sentences.japanese: あの蝶々をつかまえてごらんなさい。
example_sentences.english: Try to catch that butterfly.

example_sentences.japanese: 手をかしてごらん。手袋をはめてあげるから。
example_sentences.english: (Try to) give me your hands. I will put your gloves on.

example_sentences.japanese: もう一度やってごらん。きっとうまくできるよ。
example_sentences.english: Try it once more. I know you can do it.

example_sentences.japanese: 怒らないから…正直にいってごらんなさい。
example_sentences.english: I won't get angry... Try telling the truth.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ学んでいない文法を勉強してごらん。
example_sentences.english: Try studying grammar you haven't learned yet.

example_sentences.japanese: 耳をすましてごらん。小鳥の歌声が聞こえるよ。
example_sentences.english: Try listening carefully. You'll hear the birds singing.

example_sentences.japanese: もっと練習してごらん。絶対できるようになるから。
example_sentences.english: Try practicing more. You will definitely be able to do it.

example_sentences.japanese: さわってごらん。こんな手触り初めてだよ。
example_sentences.english: Try touching it. This is the first time I have ever felt something like this.

example_sentences.japanese: まずは辞書でしらべてごらん。それでも分からなかったら質問してね。
example_sentences.english: First, try looking it up in the dictionary. If you still don't understand, ask me.

example_sentences.japanese: もう一つの方法をためしてごらん。うまくいくかもしれないよ。
example_sentences.english: Try to do it another way. It just might work.

example_sentences.japanese: これ食べてごらん。あなただったら絶対に好きだと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: Try eating this. If it's you, I think you'll definitely like it.

example_sentences.japanese: 見てごらんなさい。こんな酷いことをネットに書かれたんだよ、酷くない？
example_sentences.english: Look at this. Someone wrote something this cruel on the internet. Don't you think this is awful?

general_translation: To have the honor of doing, To take the liberty of doing, To do (polite, formal)
formation: Verb［causative・て］+ もらうVerb［causative・て］+ いただく
casual_structure: Verb［causative・て］+ もらうVerb［causative・て］+ いただく
polite_structure: Verb［causative・て］+ もらいますVerb［causative・て］+ いただきます
explanation: An expression used to politely inform someone that you will perform a specific action after obtaining their permission.

example_sentences.japanese: 従兄弟の車を運転させてもらったら、すごくスピードが出て、楽しかったよ！
example_sentences.english: When I was given the honor of driving my cousin's car, I went really fast and had a lot of fun!

example_sentences.japanese: 初めてのことで不安も大きかったですが、皆様の協力で貴重な経験をさせてもらいました。
example_sentences.english: Since it was my first time, I was very anxious, but thanks to everyone's cooperation, I had the honor of gaining a valuable experience.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は体調が悪いので、先にかえらせてもらいます。
example_sentences.english: I'm not feeling well today, so I will take the liberty of leaving early.

example_sentences.japanese: その資料を少しみさせてもらってもいいですか？
example_sentences.english: May I take the liberty of looking at those documents for a moment?

example_sentences.japanese: この問題は、私から説明させてもらいます。
example_sentences.english: I will take the liberty of explaining this issue.

example_sentences.japanese: 時間がないので、先に結論をいわせてもらいますね。
example_sentences.english: Since we don't have time, I'll take the liberty of stating the conclusion first.

example_sentences.japanese: ここで、書類のコピーをさせてもらってもよろしいでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: May I take the liberty of making a copy of the documents here?

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩たちだけの飲み会に僕も参加させてもらうことになったんだ。
example_sentences.english: I've been given the honor of participating in the drinking party that was just for my seniors.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回は特別に大学の研究室をつかわせてもらいました。
example_sentences.english: This time, we had the honor of using the university laboratory as a special exception.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日から海外出張だから、早めに退社させてもらったよ。
example_sentences.english: Because I have an overseas business trip starting tomorrow, I took the liberty of leaving the office early.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻：「昨日はどこにいたの？」夫：「終電に乗れなかったから友人の家にとめさせてもらったんだ！」
example_sentences.english: Wife: 'Where were you yesterday?' Husband: 'I missed the last train, so I took the liberty of staying over at a friend's house!'

example_sentences.japanese: 担当の挨拶：「皆さん、初めまして。今回のプロジェクトを担当させてもらいます、田中と申します。」
example_sentences.english: Greeting from the person in charge: "Nice to meet you all. I'm Tanaka, and I will have the honor of being in charge of this project."

example_sentences.japanese: こちらの件、まだ十分に理解できていない部分があるので、もう少し時間をかけてかんがえさせてもらいたいと思います。
example_sentences.english: Regarding this matter, there are still parts I don't fully understand, so I want to take the liberty of thinking about it for a little more time.

example_sentences.japanese: 申し訳ないのですが、本日は都合により営業時間を午後３時までにさせてもらえませんか。
example_sentences.english: I apologize, but due to certain circumstances, could we take the liberty of ending our business hours at 3 PM today?

example_sentences.japanese: 皆さんのご意見を参考にして、この案ですすめさせてもらおうと考えています。
example_sentences.english: Using everyone's opinions as a reference, I am thinking I will take the liberty of proceeding with this plan.

example_sentences.japanese: 親の仕事を手伝わせてもらう。
example_sentences.english: I will take the liberty of helping with my parents' work.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の公演で歌わせていただきます。
example_sentences.english: I will have the honor of singing at tomorrow's performance.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が先生に質問させてもらいました。
example_sentences.english: I took the liberty of asking the teacher a question.

example_sentences.japanese: 詳しい内容を確かめさせてもらいたいです。
example_sentences.english: I would like to take the liberty of confirming the details.

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちも会議に参加させてもらいませんか？
example_sentences.english: Could we also be allowed to participate in the meeting?

example_sentences.japanese: 温かいお茶をお持ちいたします。
example_sentences.english: I will bring you some hot tea. (Regular humble speech)

example_sentences.japanese: それでは、会議を始めさせていただきます。
example_sentences.english: Well then, I will take the liberty of starting the meeting. (Implying that permission has been received)

example_sentences.japanese: お伺いさせていただきます。
example_sentences.english: I will humbly take the liberty of visiting you. (Slightly stilted)

general_translation: Combined particles
formation: Noun + Particle(1) + の + Noun(1) から、と、へ、で、まで
casual_structure: Noun + Particle(1) + の + Noun(1) から、と、へ、で、まで
explanation: A particle construction which shows the ownership or relationship of (B) with where (A) is from, going, done with, done until, etc.

example_sentences.japanese: あちゃんとの握手会に行こう！
example_sentences.english: Let's go to the handshake event with A-chan!  (A-chan's event)

example_sentences.japanese: 出発までの時間、何をします？
example_sentences.english: What do you want to do until departure?

example_sentences.japanese: これはアメリカからのお土産です。
example_sentences.english: This is a souvenir from America.

example_sentences.japanese: 別れた後、彼との関係はどうなるんだろう。
example_sentences.english: After breaking up with him, I wonder what our relationship would be like.

example_sentences.japanese: 海外への手紙はこちらのポストにお入れください。
example_sentences.english: Please put letters to be sent internationally into this mailbox.

example_sentences.japanese: 環境に悪いので車での通勤は控えてください。
example_sentences.english: Because it is bad for the environment, please refrain from commuting by car.

example_sentences.japanese: これまでの話はなかなかおもしろい。
example_sentences.english: The story so far is interesting.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は癌との戦いに勝ったそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that he won the battle with cancer.

example_sentences.japanese: なぎさんは、はやてさんへの手紙をずっと書いている。
example_sentences.english: Nagi constantly writes letters to Hayate.

example_sentences.japanese: サマーキャンプでの生活はとても楽しいですよ！
example_sentences.english: Life at summer camp is very fun.

example_sentences.japanese: １４時からのパネルディスカッションに出るつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: I plan on attending the panel discussion that starts from 2 p.m.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨晩からの雨はやっと止んだよ。とうとう友達に会いに行けるよ。
example_sentences.english: The rain that started from yesterday evening finally stopped! I can finally go meet up with my friends!

example_sentences.japanese: おじいちゃんはポーランドでの思い出をだんだんと忘れてきた。
example_sentences.english: Grandpa has been slowly forgetting his memories of Poland.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は彼女への愛情でいっぱいのメッセージをいつも書いている。
example_sentences.english: He always writes messages that are filled with love towards her.

example_sentences.japanese: 今までの対立の原因は広く知られていない。
example_sentences.english: The reason for the conflict up until now is not widely known.

example_sentences.japanese: クライアントからの手紙には私への不満がいっぱい書かれていた。
example_sentences.english: The letter from the client was full of complaints about me.

example_sentences.japanese: 郵便屋さんから母からの小包を受け取った。
example_sentences.english: I took the package from my mother from the postman.

general_translation: Formal or literary だ, Authoritative, Copula
formation: Noun + である［な］Adjective + である
casual_structure: Noun + である［な］Adjective + である
polite_structure: Noun + であります［な］Adjective + であります
explanation: A formal way to determine what (A) is, that may also sometimes sound authoritative.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はとてもハンサムである。
example_sentences.english: He is very handsome.

example_sentences.japanese: ここから悲しいことが起きるのである。
example_sentences.english: This is where something sad starts to happen. (Here comes the sad bit)

example_sentences.japanese: 私達が会えたのは運命であります。
example_sentences.english: It is destiny that we met.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本一デカイ博物館はこの博物館である。
example_sentences.english: The largest museum in Japan is this one.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はパイロットであった。
example_sentences.english: He was a pilot.

example_sentences.japanese: とても面白いドラマである。
example_sentences.english: It is a very interesting drama.

example_sentences.japanese: 題名：「吾輩は猫である。」
example_sentences.english: Title: 'I am a cat.'

example_sentences.japanese: 夢は海外で成功することである。
example_sentences.english: My dream is to be successful overseas.

example_sentences.japanese: この資料は極秘である。
example_sentences.english: These documents are top secret.

example_sentences.japanese: 優勝するのはほとんど確実である。
example_sentences.english: Winning the championship is  almost certain.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はうちの会社の株主である。
example_sentences.english: He is a stockholder of our company.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はテニス部のキャプテンである。
example_sentences.english: She is captain of the tennis team.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のリアクションはとてもオーバーである。
example_sentences.english: His reaction is way over the top.

example_sentences.japanese: 我が社の去年の業績は黒字であった。
example_sentences.english: My company was in the black last year.

example_sentences.japanese: 本来、ミノキシジルは 高血圧のための薬であるはずだったが、今では 脱毛を予防する薬になっている。
example_sentences.english: Originally, minoxidil was expected to be a medication for high blood pressure, but nowadays it has become a medication that prevents hair loss.

example_sentences.japanese: 大変であることを人にやらせるのは良くない。
example_sentences.english: It is not good to make others do things that are difficult.

example_sentences.japanese: 重要である箇所をまとめた資料がこちらです。
example_sentences.english: Here is a document summarizing the sections that are essential.

example_sentences.japanese: 名前はタナカであります！
example_sentences.english: My name is Tanaka! (Responding to a person in a higher rank in a military)

example_sentences.japanese: 最後のプリンを食べたのは私であります。
example_sentences.english: I am the one who ate the last pudding. (Jokingly polite)

general_translation: Even so, However, Even though, But
formation: (Expectation) Phrase + ところが + (Unexpected Result) Phrase
casual_structure: (Expectation) Phrase + ところが + (Unexpected Result) Phrase
explanation: An expression used after presenting an ideal situation or place, in order to express that the actual result was unexpected.

example_sentences.japanese: パンを買いに行きました。ところが、もう売り切れでした。
example_sentences.english: I went to buy bread. However, it was already sold out.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は早く起きないといけなかったから９時に寝た。ところが、目覚ましがならなかったから寝坊した。
example_sentences.english: I had to wake up early today so I went to sleep at 9pm. However, my alarm didn't go off, so I overslept.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい洗濯機を買った。ところが、洗濯機が大きすぎて家に入らなかった。
example_sentences.english: I bought a new washing machine. However, it was so big that it didn't fit in my house.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本のチームが勝つと思っていた。ところが負けてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I thought that the Japanese team would win. However, they lost.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は非常に優しそうでした。ところが、裏がありました。
example_sentences.english: That person seemed extremely nice. However, they had ulterior motives.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達によると、テストは難しかったそうだ。ところが、彼は百点を取った。
example_sentences.english: According to my friend, the test was difficult. Even so, he got a perfect score.

example_sentences.japanese: テストに出そうなところを予想して勉強した。ところが、全然違う問題しか出なかった。
example_sentences.english: I studied what I thought would be on the test. However, the questions were totally different from what I had studied.

example_sentences.japanese: 勝てる試合だった。ところが、怪我をして負けてしまった。
example_sentences.english: It was a match I could win. However, I got injured and lost.

example_sentences.japanese: あの資格なら簡単に取れると思っていた。ところが、３年もかかってしまった。
example_sentences.english: I thought I could easily get that qualification. However, it took three whole years.

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚するはずだった。ところが、彼女が急に「結婚できない」と言い出した。
example_sentences.english: We were sure to be married. However, she suddenly said, 'I can't get married.'

example_sentences.japanese: あの店に最近行っていなかったから行ってみた。ところが、そこはもう空地になっていた。
example_sentences.english: I hadn't been to that shop in a while, so I stopped by. However, the shop had been abandoned.

example_sentences.japanese: 美味しそうなお菓子を買った。ところが、全然美味しくなかった。
example_sentences.english: I bought a snack that looked good. However, it didn't taste good at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日会う約束をしていた。ところが、彼が曜日を間違えて来なかった。
example_sentences.english: We had agreed to meet today. However, he didn't come because he thought we were going to meet on a different day.

example_sentences.japanese: 締め切りは明日だと思っていました。ところが、実は今日だったと気づき、今急いでやっています。
example_sentences.english: I thought the deadline was tomorrow. However, I realized it was actually today, and am busily working on it.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達に勉強の手伝いを頼んだら嫌がると思っていた。ところが、喜んで手伝ってくれた。
example_sentences.english: I thought my friend was not going to like it if I asked him to help me with studying, however, he did so without hesitation.

general_translation: By the way, Incidentally
formation: ところで + (New Topic) Phrase
casual_structure: ところで + (New Topic) Phrase
explanation: A grammar point that uses the situation or place of (A) as a good point to incidentally start talking about a new topic.

example_sentences.japanese: ところで、どこに行くつもりですか。
example_sentences.english: By the way, where do you plan on going?

example_sentences.japanese: ところで、昨日の話はどうなった？
example_sentences.english: By the way, what happened to the plan you told me about yesterday?

example_sentences.japanese: ところで、お宅の旦那さんは元気にしていますか。
example_sentences.english: By the way, is your husband doing well?

example_sentences.japanese: ところで、明日のパーティーに何を持って来ますか？
example_sentences.english: By the way, what are you going to bring to the party tomorrow?

example_sentences.japanese: ところで、パソコンの使い方をご存知ですか。
example_sentences.english: By the way, do you know how to use a computer?

example_sentences.japanese: ところで内本さんはどこ出身？
example_sentences.english: By the way, where is Uchimoto-san from?

example_sentences.japanese: ところでもう雨はやみましたか？
example_sentences.english: By the way, has it stopped raining yet?

example_sentences.japanese: ところで大谷さんも一緒に旅行に行くんですか？
example_sentences.english: By the way, is Otani-san going with you on the trip?

example_sentences.japanese: ところで昨日渡した報告書は読んでもらえましたか？
example_sentences.english: By the way, have you read the report I submitted yesterday?

example_sentences.japanese: ところでそばとうどん、どっちが食べたい？
example_sentences.english: By the way, which would you like to have, soba or udon?

example_sentences.japanese: ところであの話はどうなったの？ちゃんと考えてくれた？
example_sentences.english: By the way, what happened to what we talked about? Have you thought about it?

example_sentences.japanese: ところで来週の予定はどうしますか？
example_sentences.english: By the way, what will you do about next week's plans?

example_sentences.japanese: ところで部長はいつ帰ってくるの？
example_sentences.english: By the way, when was it that our department head was coming back?

example_sentences.japanese: ところで北海道で一人暮らしをしている娘さんは元気？
example_sentences.english: By the way, is your daughter, who lives alone in Hokkaido, well?

general_translation: The more, About, To the extent that, So much… that
formation: Verb + ほど［い］Adjective + ほど［な］Adjective + な + ほどNoun + ほど
casual_structure: Verb + ほど［い］Adjective + ほど［な］Adjective + な + ほどNoun + ほど
explanation: A phrase that somewhat confidently highlights the rough degree, amount, or span of something.

example_sentences.japanese: 遅れてごめんなさい。あと１０分ほどで着きます。
example_sentences.english: I'm sorry that I'm late. I will be there in about 10 minutes. (degree・bounds・limit)

example_sentences.japanese: あと１０分ほどで着きます。
example_sentences.english: I will be there in about 10 minutes.

example_sentences.japanese: 死ぬほど練習したけれど、試合に出られなかった。
example_sentences.english: I practiced myself to death, but I was not able to participate in the match.

example_sentences.japanese: その気持ちは痛いほど分かるけど、だからってそういう事言ってもいいと言う訳では無いよ。
example_sentences.english: I understand how you feel to the point that it hurts, but that doesn't mean that you can say stuff like that.

example_sentences.japanese: それは嫌なほど聞かされたから、分かってる。
