example_sentences.english: I have been told that so much that I don't want to hear it anymore, I get it.

example_sentences.japanese: ピンが落ちた音が聞こえるほど、静かだった。
example_sentences.english: It was quiet to the extent that you could hear a pin drop. (degree・bounds・limit)

example_sentences.japanese: もう二度と食べたくないと思うほど、ピザを食べた。
example_sentences.english: I ate pizza to the extent that I don't think that I ever want to eat it again. (degree・bounds・limit)

example_sentences.japanese: 他の人がわがままだと言うほど甘やかしている。
example_sentences.english: I am spoiling them to the extent that people would say they're selfish. (degree・bounds・limit)

example_sentences.japanese: 今回は一週間ほど旅行するつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: This time, I plan to go on a trip for about one week. (degree・bounds・limit)

example_sentences.japanese: あの二人は他人なのに、驚くほどよく似ている。
example_sentences.english: Those two are complete strangers, but they look surprisingly similar. (so much so)(They look similar to the extent that I am surprised) (degree・bounds・limit)

example_sentences.japanese: 今年の夏も暑いけど、去年ほどではない。
example_sentences.english: This summer is also hot, but not to the extent of last summer. (degree・bounds・limit)

example_sentences.japanese: あの人ほどよく働く人に今まで会ったことがない。
example_sentences.english: Until now, I have never met anyone that has worked to the extent that he has. (degree・bounds・limit)

example_sentences.japanese: この絵は一時間見ても飽きないほど素晴らしい。
example_sentences.english: This painting is amazing to the extent that I could stare at it for an hour and not get tired of it. (degree・bounds・limit)

example_sentences.japanese: 調子がいい時ほど、慎重に行動すべきだ。
example_sentences.english: When things are at the extent of progressing well, you should move cautiously. (the more) (degree・bounds・limit)

example_sentences.japanese: 死ぬほど勉強しなければ、あの試験には受からない。
example_sentences.english: You will not pass that test unless you study to the extent that you will die. (so much so) (degree・bounds・limit)

example_sentences.japanese: こんなプレゼントを本当にもらえていいの！？ 涙が出るほど嬉しいよ。
example_sentences.english: Can I really have this present? I am happy to the extent that I could cry! (degree・bounds・limit)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はもう二度と走りたくないと思うほど走った。
example_sentences.english: Today, I ran so much that I feel like I never want to run again.

general_translation: The more…the more
formation: （Verb［ば］）+ Verb ［る］(*) + ほど（［い］Adjective［ば］）+ ［い］Adjective(*) + ほど（［な］Adjective + なら（ば））+ ［な］Adjective(*) + な + ほど（［な］Adjective + であれば）+ ［な］Adjective(*) + である + ほど（Noun + なら（ば））+ Noun(*) + ほど（Noun + であれば）+ Noun(*) + である + ほど(*) The same Adjective, Verb or Noun has to be repeated
casual_structure: （Verb［ば］）+ Verb ［る］(*) + ほど（［い］Adjective［ば］）+ ［い］Adjective(*) + ほど（［な］Adjective + なら（ば））+ ［な］Adjective(*) + な + ほど（［な］Adjective + であれば）+ ［な］Adjective(*) + である + ほど（Noun + なら（ば））+ Noun(*) + ほど（Noun + であれば）+ Noun(*) + である + ほど(*) The same Adjective, Verb or Noun has to be repeated
explanation: A phrase that highlights a hypothetical (A), and how something will increase or decrease as much as (A) does.

example_sentences.japanese: この豆を食べれば食べるほど痩せるらしい。
example_sentences.english: I hear that the more of these beans you eat, the thinner you will become.

example_sentences.japanese: いい肉は噛めば噛むほど味が出る。
example_sentences.english: The more you chew good meat, the more flavorful it gets.

example_sentences.japanese: 公園は広ければ広いほどいい。
example_sentences.english: The bigger the park is, the better it is.

example_sentences.japanese: ビルは丈夫ならば丈夫なほど安心できる。
example_sentences.english: The stronger a building is, the safer you feel.

example_sentences.japanese: プロならばプロほど速く泳げる。
example_sentences.english: The more of a pro you are, the faster you can swim.

example_sentences.japanese: アプリが便利であれば便利であるほどユーザーが増える。
example_sentences.english: The more useful an app is, the more users will increase.

example_sentences.japanese: 職人であれば職人であるほど凄いものが作れる。
example_sentences.english: The more of a craftsman a person is, the more likely that they will be able to make something amazing.

example_sentences.japanese: 早ければ早いほどいい。
example_sentences.english: The sooner the better.

example_sentences.japanese: きれいならば綺麗なほど見続けたくなる。
example_sentences.english: The more beautiful it is, the more I want to continue looking at it.

example_sentences.japanese: かてば勝つほど、またやりたくなる。
example_sentences.english: The more you win, the more you want to play again.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強すればするほど、日本語が上手くなる。
example_sentences.english: The more you study, the better you will be at Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: きけば聞くほど怪しい話だ。
example_sentences.english: The more I hear that story, the more suspicious it becomes.

example_sentences.japanese: 会えば会うほど、あの人のことが好きになっていく。
example_sentences.english: The more we meet, the more I grow fond of that person.

example_sentences.japanese: かけば書くほど書きやすくなるペンだな。
example_sentences.english: The more I write with this pen, the easier it becomes to write with.

example_sentences.japanese: 鍛えれば鍛えるほど、筋肉がつくからやめられない。
example_sentences.english: The more I workout, the more muscle I gain, so I can't stop.

example_sentences.japanese: スーパーは近ければ近いほど買い物に行きやすい。
example_sentences.english: The closer the supermarket, the easier it is to go shopping.

example_sentences.japanese: すすめば進むほど、引き返すのが難しくなる。
example_sentences.english: The further you go, the harder it will become to turn back.

example_sentences.japanese: 言えば言うほど、あの人との関係は悪くなる。
example_sentences.english: The more I say, the worse my relationship with that person becomes.

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字の勉強をすればするほど色んな本が読めるようになる。
example_sentences.english: The more you study kanji, the more various books you will be able to read.

example_sentences.japanese: 掃除をすればするほど、部屋が綺麗になっていく。
example_sentences.english: The more you clean, the cleaner your room will get.

example_sentences.japanese: 身体を鍛えるほど、身体が強くなる。
example_sentences.english: The more you workout, the stronger your body gets.

general_translation: Is not as…as, Isn't... like..., Not to the extent of...
formation: Verb + ほど + Verb［ない］(1)Noun + ほど + Verb［ない］(1)(1) ［い］Adjective［ない］、［な］Adjective + ではない、［な］Adjective + じゃない
casual_structure: Verb + ほど + Verb［ない］(1)Noun + ほど + Verb［ない］(1)(1) ［い］Adjective［ない］、［な］Adjective + ではない、［な］Adjective + じゃない
explanation: A grammar point that highlights the extent of (A) as insufficient to cause (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 君の母ほど優しい人はいない。
example_sentences.english: There isn't anyone as nice as your mom.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は思ったほど暑くなかった。
example_sentences.english: Today wasn't as hot as I expected.

example_sentences.japanese: 悩むほどの事じゃない。
example_sentences.english: It is nothing to worry about so much. (This is not as serious as you think it is)

example_sentences.japanese: 自転車は車ほど速くないけど、健康にいいから自転車で会社に行っています。
example_sentences.english: Bicycles aren't as fast as cars, but it is good for my health, so I ride my bike to work.

example_sentences.japanese: この世にこのカレーほど辛い食べ物はない。
example_sentences.english: There is no food as spicy as this curry in the world.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんほどケーキ作りが上手な人はどこにもいない。
example_sentences.english: There is no one in this world that is as good as my mom at baking cakes.

example_sentences.japanese: 待って！あなたほど速くはしれないんだ！
example_sentences.english: Wait! I can't run as fast as you!

example_sentences.japanese: タイタニックほど感動する映画はないわ。
example_sentences.english: There is no movie as touching as 'Titanic'.

example_sentences.japanese: 思っていたほど大変な仕事ではなかった。
example_sentences.english: The job was not as rough as I thought it would be.

example_sentences.japanese: 宇宙では誰もがフリゾほど強くなかった。
example_sentences.english: There was no-one as strong as Frizo in the universe.

example_sentences.japanese: 他の人を手伝うことほどいいことはないと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think that there is nothing as good as helping others.

example_sentences.japanese: 人に褒めてもらえるかどうかはそれほど重要ではない。
example_sentences.english: It is not that important whether or not you can be praised by others.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京ほど人口が多い都会はないと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think that there isn't another city with a large population like Tokyo's.

example_sentences.japanese: 魔王さんは言われているほど悪くないです。職場でクライアントに優しいし従業員たちの役に立つからです。
example_sentences.english: The Demon King is not as bad as they say. Because, at work, he is nice to clients and helpful to employees.

example_sentences.japanese: トム・ソーヤくんほど元気な男の子を（私は）しらない。
example_sentences.english: I do not know a boy as lively as Tom Sawyer.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車は飛行機ほど速くないけど、電車ほど安い乗り物はない。
example_sentences.english: Trains are not as fast as planes, but there isn't anything like a train when it comes to cheap transportation.

example_sentences.japanese: 地図形式が持つ歪みから、ロシアは世界地図上に描かれているほど大きくない。
example_sentences.english: Geographical features are distorted on maps so, Russia is not as large as it is depicted to be.

general_translation: If so, Well (then), In that case
formation: （それ ）+ では(1) + Phrase(1) じゃあ、じゃ
casual_structure: （それ ）+ では(1) + Phrase(1) じゃあ、じゃ
explanation: A common phrase used to say and with that, usually in order to start a new topic, or excuse oneself.

example_sentences.japanese: じゃあ、ここで失礼します。
example_sentences.english: Well then, I will take my leave.

example_sentences.japanese: それでは、あなたは行きたくないという事ですか？
example_sentences.english: In that case, you mean that you don't want to go?

example_sentences.japanese: では、こちらの商品はどうでしょう？
example_sentences.english: Well then, how about this product over here?

example_sentences.japanese: 用意できた？じゃあ、５分で出よう。
example_sentences.english: Are you ready? In that case let's leave in 5 minutes.

example_sentences.japanese: それでは、あなたがやったってことでいいですね？
example_sentences.english: In that case, would it be correct to say that you did it?

example_sentences.japanese: では、こうしたらどうでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Well, how about trying it this way?

example_sentences.japanese: では、次の問題です。
example_sentences.english: Well then, on to the next question!

example_sentences.japanese: じゃあ…本を取ってくるから。ちょっと待ってて。
example_sentences.english: Well... I'll go grab my book. Hang on a sec.

example_sentences.japanese: では、また来週の火曜日に会いましょう。
example_sentences.english: Well, let's meet again next Tuesday.

example_sentences.japanese: それでは次会う時までに考えておいてください。
example_sentences.english: In that case, please think about it before we meet again.

example_sentences.japanese: では、必要な書類に記入して、明後日までに提出してください。
example_sentences.english: In that case, please fill out the necessary documents and submit them by the day after tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: それでは、今日の授業はここまでです。また明日。
example_sentences.english: Well then, that is all for today's class. See you tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: それでは発表します。優勝は田中さんです！
example_sentences.english: Well then, I will announce the winner now. It is Tanaka-san!

example_sentences.japanese: じゃあしょうがない。明日でいいから、忘れないで持ってきてね。
example_sentences.english: Well, it can't be helped. Tomorrow is fine, so don't forget to bring it okay?

example_sentences.japanese: それでは、合格した人はこちらに並んでください。
example_sentences.english: Well then, those who passed, line up here please.

example_sentences.japanese: では、明日の予定をお伝えしますので、メモしてください。
example_sentences.english: Well then, I'm going to tell you the plans for tomorrow, so please write it down.

example_sentences.japanese: では、私はこれで失礼します。
example_sentences.english: Well, this will be when I'm going to excuse myself.

general_translation: In order to
formation: Verb + のに
casual_structure: Verb + のに
explanation: A structure which indicates the desired result of (A), and then what is required to lead toward that end.

example_sentences.japanese: 本を読むのに眼鏡を買った。
example_sentences.english: I bought glasses in order to read books.

example_sentences.japanese: トラックは車と違って、ブレーキをかけてから止まるのに時間がかかる。
example_sentences.english: Unlike cars, trucks take longer to stop after stepping on the brakes.

example_sentences.japanese: 風が強すぎて、ピクニックシートを広げるのに苦労した。
example_sentences.english: The wind was so strong that I struggled to spread out the picnic blanket.

example_sentences.japanese: 背中をかくのに孫の手を使う。
example_sentences.english: I use my backscratcher in order to scratch my back.

example_sentences.japanese: 宿題をするのに、３時間かかる。
example_sentences.english: It takes 3 hours in order to do homework.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べるのに時間がかかりすぎて、昼休みが終わってしまった。
example_sentences.english: It took too long in order for me to eat lunch, so my lunch break unfortunately came to an end.

example_sentences.japanese: お茶を飲むのに必要なコップがありません。
example_sentences.english: I do not have the necessary cup in order to drink tea.

example_sentences.japanese: 寝るのに時間がない。夜更かししすぎた。
example_sentences.english: I don't have any time (in order) to sleep. I stayed up too late.

example_sentences.japanese: 連絡するのに連絡先が分からない。
example_sentences.english: I don't know his contact information in order to get in touch with him.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動をするのに丁度いい靴がない。
example_sentences.english: I don't have the right shoes (in order) to exercise.

example_sentences.japanese: 靴を履くのに靴べらを使いますか？
example_sentences.english: Would you like to use a shoe horn in order to put on your shoes?

example_sentences.japanese: 料理を作るのに時間がかかりすぎて、食べる時間が少ししかない。
example_sentences.english: I took too much time (in order) to cook, so I only have a short time to eat.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車で音楽を聴くのにイヤフォンを忘れてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I forgot to bring the earphones I use in order to listen to music on the train.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行に行くのに何を持って行けばいいですか？
example_sentences.english: What should I bring in order to go abroad?

example_sentences.japanese: さっき食べたばかりなのに、またお腹が空いた。
example_sentences.english: I just ate earlier, but I am hungry again.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べるのに時間をかけすぎて寝る時間が遅くなった。
example_sentences.english: I took so long to eat, so I slept at a later time.

general_translation: For, For the sake of, In order to
formation: Verb［る］+ ため(に)Noun + の + ため(に)
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ ため(に)Noun + の + ため(に)
explanation: A grammar point that indicates something done for the sake of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 家を買うためにローンを組んだ。
example_sentences.english: I took a loan in order to buy a house.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい家を建てるために、土地を買った。
example_sentences.english: In order to build a new house, I bought land.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強をするために、親に机を買ってもらった。
example_sentences.english: In order to study, I got my parents to buy me a desk.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のためにやって。
example_sentences.english: Please do this for me.

example_sentences.japanese: 君のために買ってあげたのに、誰かにあげちゃったの？
example_sentences.english: I bought this for you, but you gave it to someone?

example_sentences.japanese: 僕はただいい点を取るために勉強していません。
example_sentences.english: I am not studying just for the sake of getting a good score.

example_sentences.japanese: 何のために生きているのか、それが知りたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to know what I am living for.

example_sentences.japanese: お金のためだけに仕事をするのは、つらいです。
example_sentences.english: It's very hard to only work for money.

example_sentences.japanese: 老後のためにちゃんと貯金しておかなければならない。
example_sentences.english: You have to save enough money for your retirement.

example_sentences.japanese: 確認のためにもう一度聞いた方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: You should ask her/him once again in order to make sure.

example_sentences.japanese: 君のためだよ。すぐに答えは教えないよ。もうちょっと考えてみて。
example_sentences.english: It's for your sake! I won't just give you the answer. Think about it a little bit more.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語のレベルを上げるために、文法を勉強すべきです。
example_sentences.english: You should study grammar in order to increase your Japanese level.

example_sentences.japanese: 健康のために、嫌いでも少しは野菜を食べたほうがいい。
example_sentences.english: Even if you don't like them, you'd better eat some vegetables for your health.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語能力試験に受かるために頑張って勉強している。
example_sentences.english: I am studying hard in order to pass the JLPT.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日遊びに行くために、今日仕事を終わらせないといけない。
example_sentences.english: I have to finish my work today so that I can go out tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: 君のためなら何でもするよ。なぜなら、愛しているから。
example_sentences.english: I would do anything if it's for you. Because I love you.

example_sentences.japanese: ２年前、車を買うために、親からお金を借りました。
example_sentences.english: In order to buy a car two years ago, I borrowed money from my parents. (Use showing a purpose)

example_sentences.japanese: 骨折したため、明日からしばらく仕事を休みます。
example_sentences.english: Since I broke a bone, I am going to take some time off of work starting tomorrow. (Use showing a cause)

general_translation: Due to, Because of, As a result of
formation: Verb + ため(に)［い］Adjective + ため(に)［な］Adjective + な + ため(に)Noun + の + ため(に)
casual_structure: Verb + ため(に)［い］Adjective + ため(に)［な］Adjective + な + ため(に)Noun + の + ため(に)
explanation: A somewhat formal way to indicate an event, and then the positive or negative results that occured for that sake.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜更かししたため朝寝坊してしまった。
example_sentences.english: I woke up late this morning, due to the fact that I stayed up late last night.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の飲み会でお酒を沢山飲んだために、今日は二日酔いで身体がだるい。
example_sentences.english: Because I drank a lot of alcohol at the party last night, I am tired today with a hangover.

example_sentences.japanese: 暑いために、職場で何人かが倒れた。
example_sentences.english: Due to it being hot, a few people have passed out at work.

example_sentences.japanese: このアプリは便利なために、ユーザーがどんどん増えてきた。
example_sentences.english: Due to this app being useful, the number of users is steadily growing.

example_sentences.japanese: 大雨のため、サッカーの試合を中止します。
example_sentences.english: Due to heavy rain, we will be canceling the soccer tournament.

example_sentences.japanese: 空手の試合で勝つために、毎日夜遅くまで練習しています。
example_sentences.english: In order to win the karate tournament, I practice every day until late at night.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は夜遅くまで練習していたため、今日は何もしたくないです。
example_sentences.english: Due to me practicing until late at night last night, I don't want to do anything today.

example_sentences.japanese: 台風のため、試合が中止になった。
example_sentences.english: The game was canceled due to the typhoon.

example_sentences.japanese: お金を使いすぎたために、貯金がもうほとんどない。
example_sentences.english: As a result of us having used too much money, we have almost no savings.

example_sentences.japanese: 寒いために、車が故障してしまった。
example_sentences.english: My car broke down due to the cold.

example_sentences.japanese: 寒さのために、車が故障してしまった。
example_sentences.english: The car broke down due to the cold.

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪のため、今日は休ませていただきます。
example_sentences.english: Due to a cold, I would like to take a day off.

example_sentences.japanese: コーヒーを飲みすぎたために眠れない。
example_sentences.english: I have a hard time getting to sleep due to drinking too much coffee.

example_sentences.japanese: 大雪のため、高速道路が通行止めだ。
example_sentences.english: The highway is closed due to heavy snow.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事が忙しすぎるために、最近実家に帰れていない。
example_sentences.english: Due to me being too busy at work, I haven't been back to my parents' house in a while.

example_sentences.japanese: 高齢のために、歩くのも大変になってきた。
example_sentences.english: It's getting hard even to walk, due to my old age.

example_sentences.japanese: 試験に合格できたために、一番行きたかった学校に入学できた。
example_sentences.english: As a result of passing the exam, I was able to go to my first pick school.

example_sentences.japanese: 報告しなかったために、余分な仕事が増えてしまった。
example_sentences.english: As a result of not submitting the report, I got extra work.

general_translation: Called, Named, Known as, As much as
formation: Noun (A) + という + Noun (B)
casual_structure: Noun (A) + という + Noun (B)
explanation: A grammar point that establishes what something is called, or commonly known as.

example_sentences.japanese: ポケモンというゲームを知っている？
example_sentences.english: Do you know the game called 'Pokemon?'

example_sentences.japanese: ローラというモデルさんを知っていますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you know the model called Rola?

example_sentences.japanese: 本山という駅で降りてください。
example_sentences.english: Please get off at a station named Motoyama.

example_sentences.japanese: タナカタロウという少年を見つけたら、ここにお電話をください。
example_sentences.english: If you find a child named Tanaka Tarou, please call us.

example_sentences.japanese: 今は梅雨という時期です。
example_sentences.english: We are now in the time of year called 'Tsuyu' (rainy season).

example_sentences.japanese: スマホというものは便利なものだね。
example_sentences.english: The things known as smartphones are very convenient.

example_sentences.japanese: 秋という季節が大好きだ。
example_sentences.english: I love the season (known as) 'Autumn.'

example_sentences.japanese: 佐藤浩一という人を知っていますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you know a man named 'Sato Koichi'?

example_sentences.japanese: 「何も見なかった」という話は嘘です。
example_sentences.english: The story that you 'didn't see anything' is a lie. (a story called/known as)

example_sentences.japanese: 先生という職業は、けっこう大変な仕事だ。
example_sentences.english: The job (known as a) teacher is quite hard.

example_sentences.japanese: 涙というものはどうしてこんなに綺麗なんだろう。
example_sentences.english: Why are things known as tears so beautiful?

example_sentences.japanese: 一人暮しという生活は結構寂しいです。
example_sentences.english: The lifestyle known as 'hitori gurashi' is quite sad.

example_sentences.japanese: 夢というものは簡単には叶わないですよ。
example_sentences.english: Dreams don't come true easily. (Things known as dreams don't come true easily)

example_sentences.japanese: 「機会があれば会いましょう」という言い方は大抵社交辞令だ。
example_sentences.english: The words (known as) 'Let's meet each other again, if we have a chance' is mostly just a courteous saying.

example_sentences.japanese: リンという焼き肉屋に行ったことはありますか。
example_sentences.english: Have you ever gone to a yakiniku restaurant named 'Rin?'

example_sentences.japanese: ここにボブという名前の男の人が来ませんでしたか。
example_sentences.english: Did a man called Bob come here? (Natural)

example_sentences.japanese: ここに小さいという男の人が来ませんでしたか。
example_sentences.english: Did a man known as small come here? (Unnatural)

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は強いというんだけど、ステロイドを使っているんじゃない？
example_sentences.english: That person is known as strong, but don't you think he uses steroids? (He looks strong, but isn't)

general_translation: I heard that, Rumor has it that, It is said that, It means that
formation: Phrase + ということ + だ
casual_structure: Phrase + ということ + だ
polite_structure: Phrase + ということ + です
explanation: A construction that expresses an entire phrase as either hearsay, a rumor, or one's explanation of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 人によって考え方が違うということだ。
example_sentences.english: It is said that different people have different ways of thinking.

example_sentences.japanese: 地域によってルールが違うということだ。
example_sentences.english: It means that the rules differ depending on the area.

example_sentences.japanese: 地域によってルールが違うとのことだ。
example_sentences.english: It is said that the rules differ depending on the area.

example_sentences.japanese: この井戸水は汚染されているということだ。
example_sentences.english: It is said that this well water is contaminated.

example_sentences.japanese: この魚は全く臭くない。まだ新鮮ということだ。
example_sentences.english: This fish doesn't smell at all. It means that it's fresh.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生によると、この病気は薬では治せないということだ。
example_sentences.english: According to the doctor, (it is said that) this sickness cannot be cured with medicine.

example_sentences.japanese: 大阪府警によれば、犯人はまだ逃げているということだ。
example_sentences.english: It is said that the criminal is still on the run, according to the Osaka prefectural police.

example_sentences.japanese: イルカは動物の中で頭が一番いいということだ。
example_sentences.english: It is said that dolphins are the smartest of all animals.

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんと山田さんは、秘密で付き合っているということだ。
example_sentences.english: It is said that Tanaka-san and Yamada-san are dating in secret. (rumor has it)

example_sentences.japanese: それはただ文化が違うということだ。
example_sentences.english: That   just means that  their cultures are different. (it is said)

example_sentences.japanese: 忍耐先生によりますと、ガンの治療方法がとうとう見つかったということです。
example_sentences.english: According to professor Nintai, (it is said that) the cure for cancer has been finally discovered.

example_sentences.japanese: それは君がミスをしたということだから、謝った方がいい。
example_sentences.english: That means you made a mistake, so you should apologize. (it is said)

example_sentences.japanese: 悪気はないということだから、許してあげようよ。
example_sentences.english: It means that there is no ill intent, so let's forgive them. (it is said)

example_sentences.japanese: 忍耐先生によれば、タイムマシンが開発されたということだ。
example_sentences.english: According to professor Nintai, (rumor has it that) a time machine has been developed. (it is said)

example_sentences.japanese: 今回は失敗だったけど、新しいことにチャレンジしたということだ。
example_sentences.english: I failed this time, however, it means I challenged myself with new things. (it is said)

example_sentences.japanese: 証人によると、記者は怒った忍耐先生に攻撃されたということだ。
example_sentences.english: According to the witness, (it is said that) the reporter was attacked by an angry Mr. Nintai.

example_sentences.japanese: 苦しいこともある。でもそれが生きるということだ。
example_sentences.english: Sometimes you will go through something difficult, but that's just part of life. (it is said)

example_sentences.japanese: 意見を言ってはいけないということではなくて、もっと冷静に話してほしい。
example_sentences.english: I don't mean you can't give your opinion, but I want you to speak more calmly. (it is said)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は家族に内緒で旅行に行ったそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that he went on a trip without telling his family.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は家族に内緒で旅行に行ったということだ。
example_sentences.english: It is said that he went on a trip without telling his family.

general_translation: ~ Known as ~ is, ~ Called ~ is, ~ Means ~, Because
formation: Phrase + というのは(1) + (Definition) Phrase(2)(1) とは、って(2) (Reason) Phrase
casual_structure: Phrase + というのは(1) + (Definition) Phrase(2)(1) とは、って(2) (Reason) Phrase
explanation: A structure that presents the thing referred to as (A), before defining it further.

example_sentences.japanese: 雪というのは、自然現象です。
example_sentences.english: (The thing called) Snow is a natural phenomenon.

example_sentences.japanese: 筋肉というのは、鍛えないとすぐになくなる。
example_sentences.english: (The thing known as) Muscles need to be trained, or you lose them quickly.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察というのは市民を犯罪から守らなければいけません。
example_sentences.english: (Things known as) Police need to protect the citizens from crime.

example_sentences.japanese: 人生というのは儚いものだな。
example_sentences.english: (The thing known as) Life is such a fleeting thing, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: 働くというのは大変なことだ。
example_sentences.english: (The thing known as) work is a hard thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供というのはかわいいものだな。
example_sentences.english: (The thing known as) Children are cute.

example_sentences.japanese: 習慣というのは恐ろしいものだ。
example_sentences.english: (The thing known as) Habit is such a scary thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 自販機というのは、自動販売機のことだ。
example_sentences.english: Jihanki (vending machine) means jidouhanbaiki (vending machine).(the thing called... is)

example_sentences.japanese: 外国語というのは、母国語以外の言語。
example_sentences.english: Foreign language means a language other than your native language.(the thing called... is)

example_sentences.japanese: お金というのは、良くも悪くも力がある。
example_sentences.english: (The thing known as) Money is powerful, both in good and bad ways.

example_sentences.japanese: 時間というのはあっと言う間に過ぎてゆくものだ。
example_sentences.english: (The thing known as) Time passes by before you even know it.

example_sentences.japanese: 頼みというのは結局、お金を貸してほしいということなの？
example_sentences.english: So what you really mean by your request is that you want to borrow money?(the thing called... is)

example_sentences.japanese: 親というのはいつでも子供のことを思うものだ。
example_sentences.english: (Those who are known as) Parents generally think about their children all the time.

example_sentences.japanese: 失敗というのは、成功の始まりだ。
example_sentences.english: (The thing known as) Failure is where success begins.

example_sentences.japanese: 今週末は遊べなくなっちゃった。というのも、義理の両親が来ることになったからだ。
example_sentences.english: It looks like I won’t be able to hangout this weekend. The reason for this is because it has been decided for my in-laws to come.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年も大会で優勝することができた。というのも、コーチが頑張ってくれたからだ。
example_sentences.english: We were able to win the competition again this year. The reason for this is because the coach worked so hard (for us).

example_sentences.japanese: 差別になることを言ってはいけません。というのは、私達はみんな同じ人間だからです。
example_sentences.english: You shouldn't say anything that could be taken as discriminatory. What I mean to say is, we're all human.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが言った事を否定するつもりで言っていません。というのは、私はそれが間違っていると思ったから言ったのです。
example_sentences.english: I don't mean to disprove what you just said. What I mean is that, I said what I said because I personally thought that it was wrong.

example_sentences.japanese: おかずとはなんですか。
example_sentences.english: What are side dishes?

example_sentences.japanese: あの人が７０歳とは信じられない。
example_sentences.english: I can't believe that person is 70. (70 years old, as I know it)

example_sentences.japanese: 夢って簡単に諦められないよね。
example_sentences.english: Dreams are so hard to give up. (Dreams as we know them)

example_sentences.japanese: 法律ってほんとうに必要なのか。
example_sentences.english: Are laws actually necessary? (Laws as we know them)

general_translation: ~ly・~like・~al, Typical
formation: Noun + 的（てき） + にNoun + 的（てき） + な + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + 的（てき） + にNoun + 的（てき） + な + Noun
explanation: A structure used for creating adjectives implying that (A) is expressing typical features of (A), or can be said from within the field of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 印象てきな絵。
example_sentences.english: An impressive picture.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな感情的にならなくてもいいのに。
example_sentences.english: You don't have to get that emotional. (Speaking in terms of emotions, there's no need to get like that)

example_sentences.japanese: フィルターは定期的に掃除してください。
example_sentences.english: Please clean the filter regularly. (Speaking in terms of regularity, please clean the filter as such)

example_sentences.japanese: それは個人的な考えですよね？
example_sentences.english: That is a personal way of thinking, isn't it? (Speaking in terms of individuality, it's that kind of thought, right?)

example_sentences.japanese: さっきなんかの宗教的な人たちが家に来た。
example_sentences.english: Earlier, some religious people came to the house. (Speaking in terms of religion, some people like that came earlier)

example_sentences.japanese: 一般てきな考え方。
example_sentences.english: A popular way of thinking.

example_sentences.japanese: 一時てきな大雨。
example_sentences.english: Temporary heavy rain.

example_sentences.japanese: 悪魔てきな手口。
example_sentences.english: A devilish trick.

example_sentences.japanese: 時期てきに雨が降りやすい。
example_sentences.english: Typical of the season, it is more likely to rain.

example_sentences.japanese: 感動てきな映画だった。
example_sentences.english: It was an emotional movie.

example_sentences.japanese: あの台風は破壊てきだった。
example_sentences.english: That typhoon was destructive.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいつも楽観てきだ。
example_sentences.english: He is always optimistic.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいつも自発てきに掃除をしてくれます。
example_sentences.english: He always spontaneously cleans for me.

example_sentences.japanese: それは個人てきな問題なので、言いたくありません。
example_sentences.english: Because that is a personal problem, I don't want to say it.

example_sentences.japanese: 比較てき簡単な問題が多くて助かりました。
example_sentences.english: There were many relatively easy questions which saved me (from getting a bad score).

example_sentences.japanese: なんだって肯定てきな意見と否定てきな意見がある。
example_sentences.english: There are both positive and negative opinions at any issue.

example_sentences.japanese: リサ的にはどう思う？
example_sentences.english: In a Lisa-way, what do you think? (What is your opinion)

example_sentences.japanese: それは本当にタナカ的な考え方だな。
example_sentences.english: That is such a Tanaka-way of thinking.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は英語圏の国に引っ越しました。
example_sentences.english: He moved to an English speaking country. (A country within the English speaking world)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は国民的アイドルです。
example_sentences.english: She is a national star. (Speaking in terms of the nation, she is a star)

general_translation: Because, Cause
formation: Verb + （んだ） + もの(1)い-Adj + （んだ） + もの(1)な-Adj + （なん） + だ + もの(1)Noun + （なん） + だ + もの(1)(1) もん
casual_structure: Verb + （んだ） + もの(1)い-Adj + （んだ） + もの(1)な-Adj + （なん） + だ + もの(1)Noun + （なん） + だ + もの(1)(1) もん
polite_structure: Verb + （んです） + もの(1)い-Adj + （んです） + もの(1)な-Adj + （なん） + です + もの(1)Noun + （なん） + です + もの(1)(1) もん
explanation: A feminine or childish way to express the cause or reason for something.

example_sentences.japanese: まずいんだもん。
example_sentences.english: (Because) it tastes bad!

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが言う事は何も信じられないわ。だって、あなたはいつも嘘をつくもの。
example_sentences.english: I can't believe anything you say. Cause you always lie.

example_sentences.japanese: だって、彼女が悪いんだもの。
example_sentences.english: Cause she is the one in the wrong.

example_sentences.japanese: これはあなたにあげられない。大切だもの。
example_sentences.english: I can't give this to you, cause it is important.

example_sentences.japanese: すぐ泣くに決まってるじゃん、まだこどもだもの。
example_sentences.english: Of course he will cry, cause he is still a child.

example_sentences.japanese: エアコンをつけて寝ているよ。だって、暑くて寝れないんだもの。
example_sentences.english: I sleep with the A/C on. Cause it's so hot that I can't sleep, you see.

example_sentences.japanese: この子は失敗するに決まってるでしょう、まだ新人なんだもの。
example_sentences.english: Of course this kid will make mistakes. Cause he's still new here.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は嘘をついているもの。
example_sentences.english: (Because) she is lying.

example_sentences.japanese: 怒らないでね。子供なんだもん。
example_sentences.english: Don't be angry. (Because) he is just a kid.

example_sentences.japanese: 寒いんだもん。風邪をひいてしまうよ。
example_sentences.english: (Because) it's freezing. I'm gonna catch a cold, man!

example_sentences.japanese: 「食べすぎ！」って言われても…、美味しいんだもん！
example_sentences.english: Even if someone says 'you are eating too much!'... (Because) it's delicious! (so I can't help it)

example_sentences.japanese: 僕はそう感じたんだもん。仕方ないじゃない？
example_sentences.english: (Because) that's how I felt. It can't be helped, right?

example_sentences.japanese: A：「タマはもう一度カーペットにおしっこした！」B：「だって子猫だもの。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Tama urinated on the carpet again!' B: '(Because) it's a kitten!'

example_sentences.japanese: A：「どうしてそんなに遅くなったの？」 B：「渋滞が起きたんだもの。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Why are you so late?'B: '(Because) there was a traffic jam!'

example_sentences.japanese: A：「どうしてあの時計を買わなかったの？」 B：「高すぎたんだもん。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Why didn't you buy that clock?' B: '(Because) it was too expensive.'

example_sentences.japanese: A：「どうして彼と別れたの？」 B：「だって、ずっと嘘をついていたもの。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Why did you break up with him?' B: 'Why? (Because) he was lying all the time.'

example_sentences.japanese: A：「どうしてコールしなかったの？」　 B：「忙しかったもん。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Why didn't you call?' B: '(Because) I was busy.'

example_sentences.japanese: A：「なんで何も食べないの？ 」B：「食べたくないもん。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Why aren't you eating anything?' B: '(Because) I don't want to eat.'

example_sentences.japanese: もうお腹いっぱいだもん。
example_sentences.english: Cause I'm already full.

example_sentences.japanese: いいよ、お前とはもう遊ばないもん！
example_sentences.english: It's all good! (Because) I'm not going to play with you anymore! (Showing mild anger/jokingly)

example_sentences.japanese: こんなものすぐに壊れるに決まっているじゃないですか、紙から出来てるんですもの。
example_sentences.english: Of course something like this will break instantly. (Because) it is made of paper.

example_sentences.japanese: しょうがないですよ、あの人は何も考えていないんですもの。
example_sentences.english: We can't help it. (Because) that person doesn't think about anything.

general_translation: Supposed to, Should, That's the way it is
formation: Verb + もの(1) + だ(2)［い］Adjective + もの(1) + だ(2)［な］Adjective + な + もの(1) + だ(2)(1) もん(2) ではない、じゃない
casual_structure: Verb + もの(1) + だ(2)［い］Adjective + もの(1) + だ(2)［な］Adjective + な + もの(1) + だ(2)(1) もん(2) ではない、じゃない
explanation: A structure that strongly suggests that (A) is what is expected, or how it is supposed to be. It's an (A) thing.

example_sentences.japanese: ケーキは甘いものだ。
example_sentences.english: Cake is supposed to be sweet.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事は一生懸命するものだ。
example_sentences.english: Work is something you should put all your effort into.

example_sentences.japanese: ユウキが自分からプランを立てるのは珍しいものだ。
example_sentences.english: It is rare for Yuki to plan something out on his own.

example_sentences.japanese: こどもは元気なものだ。
example_sentences.english: Kids should be energetic. (Man, kids are energetic)

example_sentences.japanese: 人生はそんなに簡単なものではない。
example_sentences.english: Life is not something that is easy.

example_sentences.japanese: 家族は捨てるものじゃない。
example_sentences.english: Family is not something you should throw away.

example_sentences.japanese: 親は親切なものだ。
example_sentences.english: Parents are supposed to be kind.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べ物はムダにするものじゃないよ！
example_sentences.english: You shouldn't waste food! (not supposed to)

example_sentences.japanese: 悪いことは続くものだ。
example_sentences.english: Bad things usually continue. (That's just the way it is)

example_sentences.japanese: 子供は父母の言うことを聞くものだ。
example_sentences.english: Children are supposed to listen to their parents!

example_sentences.japanese: お金はあれば使ってしまうものだ。
example_sentences.english: Money is something you inevitably use if you have it. (That's just the way it is)

example_sentences.japanese: 通りを渡るとき車に気をつけるものだ！
example_sentences.english: When you cross the street you should look out for cars!

example_sentences.japanese: うまい話は大抵怪しいものだ。
example_sentences.english: Stories that are too good to be true, are supposed to be suspicious.

example_sentences.japanese: 目上の人と話すときは敬語を使うものだ！
example_sentences.english: You should use keigo (polite speech) when conversing with superiors!

example_sentences.japanese: 生きるのは大変だ。人生とはそういうものだ。
example_sentences.english: Life is tough. That is just what life is.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事は自分から進んでするものだ。
example_sentences.english: Work is something you should do proactively. (supposed to)

example_sentences.japanese: 親友は困っている時に助けてくれるものだ。
example_sentences.english: Good friends are supposed to help you when you are in trouble.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日やっている作業だから、手慣れたものだ。
example_sentences.english: I am used to this work because I do it every day. (That's just the way it is)

example_sentences.japanese: 東大に入れたのか？大したもんだ。
example_sentences.english: You were able to get into Tokyo University? That is impressive.

example_sentences.japanese: ゴミを道に捨てるもんじゃない！
example_sentences.english: You should not throw garbage on the street!

general_translation: In the middle of
formation: Verb［ている］+ 最中（さいちゅう）に + PhraseNoun + の + 最中（さいちゅう）に + PhraseVerb［ている］(1) + 最中（さいちゅう） + だ(1) Noun+の
casual_structure: Verb［ている］+ 最中（さいちゅう）に + PhraseNoun + の + 最中（さいちゅう）に + PhraseVerb［ている］(1) + 最中（さいちゅう） + だ(1) Noun+の
polite_structure: Verb［ている］+ 最中（さいちゅう）に + PhraseNoun + の + 最中（さいちゅう）に + PhraseVerb［ている］(1) + 最中（さいちゅう） + です(1) Noun+の
explanation: A phrase that expresses (A) as being right in the middle of occuring, or at the highest intensity.

example_sentences.japanese: それについては考えているさいちゅうです。
example_sentences.english: I am in the middle of thinking about that.

example_sentences.japanese: お祖母ちゃんの歯がお餅を食べているさいちゅうにポロっと取れた。
example_sentences.english: Grandma's tooth fell out right in the middle of eating mochi.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事のさいちゅうに怪我をしたら、黙っていないですぐに責任者に電話をしてください。
example_sentences.english: If you get hurt in the middle of work, please don't keep it to yourself and notify your supervisor.

example_sentences.japanese: 今、犯人を追いかけているさいちゅうだ。
example_sentences.english: Right now, I'm in the midst of chasing a criminal.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝の散歩のさいちゅうに、犬に噛まれた。
example_sentences.english: I was bitten by a dog while right in the middle of my morning walk.

example_sentences.japanese: 寝ているさいちゅうに声をかけるのはやめてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to stop trying to talk to me while I am sleeping.

example_sentences.japanese: テストのさいちゅうに眠ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: I fell asleep in the middle of taking the test.

example_sentences.japanese: 話しているさいちゅうに邪魔をするのはやめてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to stop disturbing me while I am talking.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事のさいちゅうに旅行の話ばかりするのはやめてください。
example_sentences.english: Please stop talking about traveling while you are at work.

example_sentences.japanese: 試合のさいちゅうに怪我をして、担架で運んでもらった。
example_sentences.english: I got hurt in the middle of the game and was taken away on a stretcher.

example_sentences.japanese: 今確認を取っているさいちゅうです。少しお待ちください。
example_sentences.english: I am in the middle of getting confirmation. Please wait a moment.

example_sentences.japanese: コンサートのさいちゅうに気分が悪くなってしまった。
example_sentences.english: I got sick in the middle of the concert.

example_sentences.japanese: 家族と食事のさいちゅうに、携帯を触らないで。
example_sentences.english: Don't use your cellphone while in the middle of dinner with your family.

example_sentences.japanese: 映画を見ているさいちゅうに彼は電話をした。
example_sentences.english: He made a phone call in the middle of watching the movie.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行のさいちゅうに 、今すぐ家に帰らなければならないと母親からメッセージをもらった。
example_sentences.english: In the middle of a trip I received a message from my mother saying that I have to come back home immediately.

example_sentences.japanese: 冗談でも悲しいさいちゅうに悪口を言われると、もっと悲しくなる。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is a joke, when someone says something mean when I am really sad, I get even more sad.

example_sentences.japanese: 一生懸命なさいちゅうに話し掛けられると、一気に集中力がなくなる。
example_sentences.english: When someone talks to me when I am highly concentrated, I suddenly lose my concentration.

general_translation: After, Upon
formation: Verb［た］+ 上（うえ）でNoun + の + 上（うえ）で
casual_structure: Verb［た］+ 上（うえ）でNoun + の + 上（うえ）で
explanation: A slightly formal expression that highlights something that logically occurs after or upon (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 家の中を見たうえで、買おうと思っている。
example_sentences.english: I am thinking that I will buy the house after I have seen the inside. (upon)

example_sentences.japanese: この企画は社長と相談したうえで、キャンセルすることに決めました。
example_sentences.english: Upon consulting the CEO of the company, we have decided to cancel this project.

example_sentences.japanese: 色んな車を運転したうえで、どの車を買うか決めたいと思います。
example_sentences.english: Upon driving various cars, I would like to choose which car to purchase.

example_sentences.japanese: 以下の内容を確認のうえで、サインをしてください。
example_sentences.english: Upon confirming the details below, please sign your name.

example_sentences.japanese: 以下のリンクからログインのうえで、内容変更をしてください。
example_sentences.english: Upon logging in from the link below, please change your information.

example_sentences.japanese: こちらの商品は医者に相談したうえで、使用してください。
example_sentences.english: Please use this product upon consulting with a doctor.

example_sentences.japanese: 説明書を読んだうえで、ご使用ください。
example_sentences.english: Please use it after reading the instructions. (upon)

example_sentences.japanese: 変更したうえで、間違いがあるかどうか確認するべきだ。
example_sentences.english: After making changes, you should check whether or not there are any mistakes. (upon)

example_sentences.japanese: 妻と相談したうえで、手術を受けることを決めたいと思う。
example_sentences.english: I would like to make the decision about undergoing surgery, after I discuss it with my wife. (upon)

example_sentences.japanese: 慎重な調査のうえで、被告は有罪と決定しました。
example_sentences.english: Upon careful investigation, the defendant has been found guilty. (after)

example_sentences.japanese: 十分付き合ったうえで、彼女と結婚したいかどうか決めます。
example_sentences.english: After going steady for a sufficient amount of time, I will decide whether or not I want to marry her. (upon)

example_sentences.japanese: アンケート用紙に記入したうえで、来店していただけると助かります。
example_sentences.english: It would help us a lot if you would fill out the questionnaire before (upon) coming into our shop/restaurant. (after)

example_sentences.japanese: ３年間、日本語を勉強したうえで、日本に仕事を見つけに行くことを決めた。
example_sentences.english: After learning Japanese for three years, I decided to go to Japan to look for a job. (upon)

example_sentences.japanese: ちゃんと調査したうえで、報告書を提出してください。
example_sentences.english: I want you to submit your report after you have done the proper amount of research. (upon)

example_sentences.japanese: メンバー全員に確認したうえで、結果を教えてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to let me know the results after confirming with all members. (upon)

example_sentences.japanese: 住民と協議のうえで、橋を開通するかどうか結論を出したいと思います。
example_sentences.english: We would like to come to a conclusion on whether or not to open the bridge to traffic upon consulting with the inhabitants. (after)

example_sentences.japanese: わが社は研究結果を詳細に分析したうえで、その化学物質を製造することに決めた。
example_sentences.english: After detailed analysis of study results, our company decided to produce that chemical substance. (upon)

example_sentences.japanese: 医者に教えられた上で、使用してください。
example_sentences.english: Please use this upon being told to by a doctor. (Unnatural)

general_translation: Thanks to, Because of
formation: Verb + おかげで［い］Adjective + おかげで［な］Adjective + な + おかげでNoun + の + おかげで
casual_structure: Verb + おかげで［い］Adjective + おかげで［な］Adjective + な + おかげでNoun + の + おかげで
explanation: A phrase gives thanks to (A) for causing some particular result, sometimes sarcastically.

example_sentences.japanese: 薬のおかげでだいぶよくなりました。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to the medicine, I got much better.

example_sentences.japanese: タケルくんに手伝ってもらったおかげで仕事が早く終わったよ。今日は本当にありがとうね。
example_sentences.english: We were able to finish work early, thanks to you helping us Takeru. Thank you so much for today.

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋が汚いおかげでどこに何があるか全く分からない。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to my room being so dirty, I don't know where anything is. (Sarcasm)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達が有名なおかげで、どんな高級レストランでも予約なしで入れる。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to my friend being famous, we can go to any fancy restaurant without a reservation.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたのおかげで不自由のない生活ができている。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to you, we can live a life free of inconvenience.

example_sentences.japanese: 風が強いおかげで、ヨットのスピードが上がった。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to the strong wind, the yacht gained speed.

example_sentences.japanese: おかげで助かったよ。来てくれてありがとう。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to you, I was saved. Thank you for coming.

example_sentences.japanese: スマホのおかげで、目的地にスムーズに着きました。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to my smartphone, I had no trouble arriving at my destination.

example_sentences.japanese: 君のおかげで取引は失敗だったよ。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to you the deal was a failure!

example_sentences.japanese: 彼がいてくれたおかげで、諦めないで頑張れた。
example_sentences.english: Because he was there for me, I was able to push through.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強をしたおかげで、試験に合格した。
example_sentences.english: I passed the test thanks to studying.

example_sentences.japanese: 文プロのおかげで文法を理解できるようになってきた。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to Bunpro, I am starting to understand grammar.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の運転の仕方が上手なおかげで、ちょうど間に合った。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to his skillful driving, we arrived on time.

example_sentences.japanese: オニヅカ先生に日本語を教えてもらったおかげで、ぺらぺらと話せるようになった。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to Onizuka-sensei teaching me Japanese, I have come to speak it fluently.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰のおかげでこんなにいい家に住めると思っているんだ！
example_sentences.english: To whom do you think you should be thankful for being able to live in such a nice house?

example_sentences.japanese: 君のおかげでいい思い出になったよ。また一緒に旅行に行こうね。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to you, I had a great experience. Let's go on another trip together (someday).

example_sentences.japanese: お前が変な事言ったおかげで、俺が言いたい事を忘れちゃったじゃん！
example_sentences.english: Thanks to you saying something weird, I forgot what I wanted to say! (Sarcasm)

example_sentences.japanese: あいつのおかげでまた残業だよ。
example_sentences.english: We have to work overtime again thanks to him. (Sarcasm)

example_sentences.japanese: おかげで、テストに合格することができました。
example_sentences.english: Thankfully, I was able to pass my test.

example_sentences.japanese: おかげで、いい休暇を過ごせました。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to you, I was able to enjoy a nice holiday.

general_translation: Based on, In accordance with
formation: Noun + に基（もと）づいてNoun +  に基（もと）づいた + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + に基（もと）づいてNoun +  に基（もと）づいた + Noun
explanation: An expression showing that something is based on (A), by expressing the foundation to which it adheres.

example_sentences.japanese: 信用にもとづいて、お金を貸す。
example_sentences.english: I lend money based on trust.

example_sentences.japanese: クライアントの指示にもとづいて、編集をしておきました。
example_sentences.english: I have edited this based on the client's instructions. (Edited in advance, assuming that would be the client's wishes)

example_sentences.japanese: 以前成功した計画にもとづいて、新しい計画を立てようと思っています。
example_sentences.english: I am thinking of making a new plan based on the previous successful plan.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は実話にもとづいた映画が好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like movies based on true stories.

example_sentences.japanese: 来週までに、アンケートにもとづいたグラフを作成してください。
example_sentences.english: By next week, please make a graph based on these surveys.

example_sentences.japanese: 法律にもとづいて、判断させていただきます。
example_sentences.english: I will make my judgment based on the law.

example_sentences.japanese: ちゃんと計画にもとづいて、動いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please proceed in accordance with the plan.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの意見にもとづいて、変更を加えました。
example_sentences.english: I implemented a modification based on your opinion.

example_sentences.japanese: 間違った前提にもとづいているから、当然結果も間違っている。
example_sentences.english: The results are incorrect because (the experiment) is being based on incorrect assumptions.

example_sentences.japanese: 長年の観察にもとづいて、この結論に至った。
example_sentences.english: I came to this conclusion based on many years of observation.

example_sentences.japanese: 実話にもとづいたドラマには説得力がある。
example_sentences.english: Dramas based on true stories are very convincing.

example_sentences.japanese: 教授の理論にもとづいて、研究を続けてみます。
example_sentences.english: I will try to continue the research according to the professor's theory.

example_sentences.japanese: 分析結果にもとづいて、評価しました。
example_sentences.english: I made an appraisal based on the results of the analysis.

example_sentences.japanese: 今までの経験にもとづいて、今後の計画をたてようと思う。
example_sentences.english: I will make future plans based on my experiences.

example_sentences.japanese: 個人的な意見にもとづいて、書かれた文章。
example_sentences.english: An essay based on my personal opinion.

example_sentences.japanese: 歴史的事実にもとづいて、作られた映画。
example_sentences.english: A movie based on actual historical events.

example_sentences.japanese: あの国の法律は宗教にもとづいて作られている。
example_sentences.english: That country's law is founded on religion.

example_sentences.japanese: 先月貰った資料にもとづいて、このレポートを書きました。
example_sentences.english: I wrote this paper based on the documents you gave me last month.

example_sentences.japanese: この小説は歴史的実話にもとづいて書かれている。
example_sentences.english: This novel is written based on true historical events.

general_translation: Aspect, Respect, Point, Way, In terms of, In that, From the point of view
formation: Verb + 点（てん）(で)［い］Adjective + 点（てん）(で)［な］Adjective + な + 点（てん）(で)Noun + の + 点（てん）(で)Phrase + という + 点（てん）(で)
casual_structure: Verb + 点（てん）(で)［い］Adjective + 点（てん）(で)［な］Adjective + な + 点（てん）(で)Noun + の + 点（てん）(で)Phrase + という + 点（てん）(で)
explanation: An expression which highlights that with the specific aspect or point of (A), (B) is true.

example_sentences.japanese: このてんでそのスマホの方がいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: In this respect, that smartphone is better.

example_sentences.japanese: 漢字の一番難しい点は、読み方が沢山あることです。
example_sentences.english: The most difficult aspect of kanji is that there are many ways to read them.

example_sentences.japanese: 分からない点がありましたら、こちらまでお電話をください。
example_sentences.english: Please call here if there are any points that are hard to understand.

example_sentences.japanese: アプリは使いやすさと便利さが一番重要な点で、見た目などはあまり綺麗じゃなくてもいい。
example_sentences.english: Ease of use and convenience are the most important aspects of an app, so it is okay if it doesn't look too pretty.

example_sentences.japanese: イギリスの食文化はいくつかの点でスペインの食文化と違う。
example_sentences.english: Food culture of England and Spain is different in several aspects.

example_sentences.japanese: 十万人のユーザーが居るという点では凄いと思う。
example_sentences.english: In terms of having 100,000 users, I think it is amazing.

example_sentences.japanese: 分からない点について質問はありますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you have any questions in regards to something you don't understand?

example_sentences.japanese: 以上の点から言うと、来月までにオープンすることは不可能という事ですね。
example_sentences.english: Based on the points mentioned above, this means that it is impossible to start business by next month, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語にひらがなとカタカナと漢字があるという点から考えると、中国語は大分違う。
example_sentences.english: Japanese is very different from Chinese in that Japanese has hiragana, katakana, and kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 英語はあらゆるてんで日本語と違っている。
example_sentences.english: English differs from Japanese in all respects. (all points)

example_sentences.japanese: 何らかのアクションが必要であるというてんを総株主は認めた。
example_sentences.english: All shareholders agreed on the point that some action is needed.

example_sentences.japanese: いくつかのてんで韓国語やトルコ語は日本語に似ている。
example_sentences.english: In some respects, Korean and Turkish are similar to Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はちょっと忘れっぽいというてんで彼の父と同じだね。
example_sentences.english: In terms of being a bit forgetful he is just like his father, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語は、文章の最後のポジションに動詞があるというてんで、ユニークである。
example_sentences.english: Japanese is unique in that the verb is in the last position of a sentence.

example_sentences.japanese: 多数の研究に基づいて、燃焼機関は電動機よりあらゆるてんで効率が低いという理論が確立された。
example_sentences.english: Based on numerous studies, the theory that combustion engines are in every aspect less efficient than electric motors, has been established.

example_sentences.japanese: これらのＣＰＵはパフォーマンスのてんでは同じくらいだが、値段のてんでは著しく異なっている。
example_sentences.english: Those processors are about the same in terms of performance, but in terms of price, they differ considerably.

example_sentences.japanese: 爆裂魔法を撃てるというてんでは、めぐみんは誰にも負けない。
example_sentences.english: In terms of being able to shoot explosive magic, Megumin won't lose to anyone.

example_sentences.japanese: しかし、かなり値段が安いながらも、このノートパソコンは重要な全てのてんで素晴らしい。
example_sentences.english: However, this laptop, despite being quite cheap, is superb in all respects of importance.

example_sentences.japanese: この他のてんでは彼の若い頃については謎に包まれている。
example_sentences.english: Apart from this aspect, his youth is shrouded in mystery.

example_sentences.japanese: オレはドアを開けっぱなしにするべきではなかったというてんだけについてはあなたに賛成です。
example_sentences.english: I only agree with you in that I shouldn't have left doors open.

general_translation: Because, The reason is, That is because
formation: Phrase (A)。なぜなら(ば) + Reason for (A) Phrase + から + だ
casual_structure: Phrase (A)。なぜなら(ば) + Reason for (A) Phrase + から + だ
polite_structure: Phrase (A)。なぜなら(ば) + Reason for (A) Phrase + から + です
explanation: An expression that enquires why a question would be asked, then gives the answer to it.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は泳ぎに行けなかった。なぜなら、寒かったから。
example_sentences.english: He couldn't go swimming because it was cold.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は仕事に来ません。なぜなら、明日は友達の結婚式に行くからです。
example_sentences.english: I will not come to work tomorrow. Why? That's because I will be going to my friends' wedding.

example_sentences.japanese: 卵を使わないで作ってください。なぜなら、私は卵アレルギーだからです。
example_sentences.english: Please make it without using eggs. Why? Because I'm allergic to them.

example_sentences.japanese: すみませんが、正直に言えないんです。なぜなら、秘密だから。
example_sentences.english: I'm sorry but I can't tell you truthfully. The reason is that it is a secret.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らは来るかどうかわからない。なぜなら、まだ連絡がきていないからです。
example_sentences.english: I don't know if they are coming or not because they haven't contacted me yet.

example_sentences.japanese: もうすぐ会えます。なぜなら、今度僕は日本に行くから。
example_sentences.english: We can see each other soon. Why? Because I'll go to Japan next time.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は仕事を休みました。なぜなら、インフルエンザにかかってしまったからです。
example_sentences.english: I took the day off today. Why? Because I caught the flu.

example_sentences.japanese: ケーキを焼いてみました。なぜなら今日は、結婚記念日だからです。
example_sentences.english: I had a go at baking a cake. Why? Because today is our wedding anniversary.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は雨が嫌い。なぜなら、持ち物が濡れてしまうから。
example_sentences.english: I hate rain. Why? Because everything I am carrying gets wet.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は彼女が大好きです。なぜなら、優しい人だからです。
example_sentences.english: I love her. Why? Because she is nice.

example_sentences.japanese: 少し遅れます。なぜなら、雪で渋滞しているからです。
example_sentences.english: I will be a little late. Why? Because there is traffic due to snow.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語は難しい。なぜなら、ひらがなとカタカナと漢字もあるからです。
example_sentences.english: Japanese is difficult. Why? Because it has hiragana, katakana and kanji too.

example_sentences.japanese: もう少し安くしてください。なぜなら、ネットではもっと安く売っているんですから。
example_sentences.english: Please lower the price. Why? Because I can find it cheaper on the internet.

example_sentences.japanese: 一生懸命日本語の勉強をしています。なぜなら、日本語能力試験に合格したいからです。
example_sentences.english: I am studying Japanese hard. Why? Because I want to pass the JLPT.

general_translation: For sure, For certain, Even more so, Underlined or bolded text
formation: Noun + こそ
casual_structure: Noun + こそ
explanation: An expression that shows (A) as being moreso something, in a similar way to capitalization of a word in English.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたこそリーダーにふさわしい！
example_sentences.english: You are fitting to be the leader!

example_sentences.japanese: この曲こそ俺がずーっと探していた曲だ！やっと曲名が分かった。
example_sentences.english: This song is exactly the song I have been searching for! I finally figured out the title.

example_sentences.japanese: 今度こそ勝つぞ！
example_sentences.english: I will win for sure next time!

example_sentences.japanese: 今度こそ達成してみせる！
example_sentences.english: I will achieve (it) this time!

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かが「愛こそすべてだ」って言っていました。
example_sentences.english: Someone once said that 'love is everything'.

example_sentences.japanese: 困った時こその友達じゃないか。
example_sentences.english: Without a doubt, friends help when you are in trouble, don't they?

example_sentences.japanese: そんな時こそ僕の出番だ！
example_sentences.english: That is the time I will make my debut!

example_sentences.japanese: それでこそ僕の選んだ妻だ。
example_sentences.english: That's exactly the wife I have chosen.

example_sentences.japanese: それこそ僕に与えられた使命だと思っています。
example_sentences.english: I believe that, indeed, is the mission that was given to me.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日こそ十分に睡眠を取りたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to finally get enough sleep today.

example_sentences.japanese: こちらこそいつもお世話になっております。
example_sentences.english: It is I that should say: thank you for always taking care of me.

example_sentences.japanese: いえいえ、謝らないでください！私こそ悪いことをしてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: No, no! Please do not apologize. It was (for sure) me that was in the wrong.

example_sentences.japanese: 辛い時こそ、大切なことを学べるチャンスだ。
example_sentences.english: Difficult times are chances to learn something important.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人でも手助けをすることができたら、それこそ最高の気持ちになる。
example_sentences.english: Even if we can only help one person, that (for sure) is the best feeling.

example_sentences.japanese: いえいえ、私こそありがとうございます。
example_sentences.english: No no no no, I am the one that should be thankful.

general_translation: Emphasized because, Precisely because
formation: Verb + からこそ + PhraseNoun + だ + からこそ + Phrase
casual_structure: Verb + からこそ + PhraseNoun + だ + からこそ + Phrase
explanation: A phrase emphasizing that precisely from (A), (B). In a similar way to capitalizing a word in English.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたがいるからこそ、安心できるんです。
example_sentences.english: Precisely because you're here is why I can relax.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺は努力したからこそ、試験に合格できたんだよ。頭がいいからだけじゃないよ。
example_sentences.english: I was able to pass the test, precisely because I gave it my all. It's not only because I am smart.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩に色々と教えて貰ったからこそ、私はここまでこれたのです。
example_sentences.english: I was able to get to where I am now because of all the things you, senpai, have taught me.

example_sentences.japanese: 君だからこそできたんだよ。俺にはまだそんな凄い事は出来ない。
example_sentences.english: You were able to do it precisely because it was you. I can't do anything that amazing yet.

example_sentences.japanese: ここは綺麗な川だからこそ、こんな美味しい魚が釣れるんですよ。
example_sentences.english: You can catch great fish here precisely because the river is so clean.

example_sentences.japanese: タナカ君が休みなのに仕事に来てくれたからこそ、準備が早く終わったり、締め切りまでに仕事を終わらせることができたんです。
example_sentences.english: We were able to finish with the prep work and finish work by the deadline, precisely because you, Tanaka-kun, came into work even though it was your day off.

example_sentences.japanese: 仲間がいるからこそ、頑張れる。
example_sentences.english: I can do my best precisely because I have friends.

example_sentences.japanese: 難しい状況だからこそ生まれるアイデアもある。
example_sentences.english: There are also ideas that are born precisely because of difficult situations.

example_sentences.japanese: 君が励ましてくれたからこそ、ここまでやってこれたんだ。
example_sentences.english: I could make it this far precisely because you have given me so much support.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日努力をしたからこそ、一番になれた。
example_sentences.english: Precisely because I worked hard every day, I was able to become number one.

example_sentences.japanese: 君の手伝いがあったからこそ、大きな石を動かすことができた。
example_sentences.english: Precisely because you helped, we were able to move the large rock.

example_sentences.japanese: 操作が簡単だからこそ、お年寄りにも人気がある。
example_sentences.english: That is even popular among the elderly precisely because it is easy to control.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんが一生懸命働いているからこそ、何不自由なく暮らせている。
example_sentences.english: We can live in comfort precisely because dad works hard.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日までの苦労があったからこその達成感だ。
example_sentences.english: It feels great precisely because I had been putting so much effort into it until yesterday. (emphasis)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女がいたからこそ、兎を捕まえることができた。
example_sentences.english: I was able to catch the rabbit precisely because she was there.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日運動をしているからこそ、健康でいられるのだ。
example_sentences.english: I can stay healthy precisely because I exercise every day.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが案内してくれたからこそ、楽しい旅行ができた。
example_sentences.english: Precisely because you were our guide, we were able to enjoy our trip.

general_translation: Just, Only, Nothing but
formation: Verb［て］+ ばかりNoun + ばかり
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ ばかりNoun + ばかり
explanation: A slightly formal way of subjectively expressing the only thing that is happening. Nothing but (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 先生はいつも怒ってばかりいる。
example_sentences.english: Our teacher does nothing but get angry.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近はお菓子ばかり食べているから、お腹がでてきた。
example_sentences.english: Recently, I've been eating nothing but sweets, so my stomach is bulging out.

example_sentences.japanese: 先月生まれた息子がずっと泣いてばかりいて、全然寝れない。
example_sentences.english: My son who was born last month does nothing but cry, so I can't sleep.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は毎日残業してばかりで、全然家の事を手伝ってくれない。
example_sentences.english: All he does is work overtime everyday, and he won't help me with house chores.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は口を開けると文句ばかりで、一緒にいるだけで疲れる。
example_sentences.english: When he opens his mouth, all he can do is complain, so just being with him is exhausting.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいつも嘘ばかり言っている。
example_sentences.english: He does nothing but tell lies.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の弟はゲームをしてばかりですよ。
example_sentences.english: My little brother does nothing but play video games.

example_sentences.japanese: 知らない顔ばかりだから緊張する。
example_sentences.english: Because there are only/nothing but unfamiliar faces I feel nervous.

example_sentences.japanese: 甘い物をたべてばかりいると、虫歯が増える。
example_sentences.english: If you only/do nothing but eat sweets, you will have more cavities.

example_sentences.japanese: いつももらってばかりですみません。
example_sentences.english: It seems that I do nothing but receive (gifts) from you. Sorry about that.

example_sentences.japanese: 人生つらいことばかりではない。いい日もあるよ。
example_sentences.english: Life is not always (nothing but) hard. There are good days too.

example_sentences.japanese: まけてばかりだから、もうあのゲームはしたくない。
example_sentences.english: I do nothing but lose, so I don't want to play that game anymore.

example_sentences.japanese: あそんでばかりで勉強しないなら、大人になってから苦労するよ。
example_sentences.english: If you do nothing but play and don't study, you will have a rough time when you get older.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は夢をおいかけてばかり、現実を無視している。
example_sentences.english: He does nothing but chase his dreams. He completely disregards reality.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の役目は皿を洗うことなのに、おとしてばかりです。
example_sentences.english: Even though he should be washing the dishes, he does nothing but drop them.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの子は毎日スマホで映画を見たりゲームをしたりしてばかり、全然勉強しないわ。
example_sentences.english: My child does nothing but watch movies on his smartphone and play games. He does not study at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 口先ばかりで、結局何もやってくれない。
example_sentences.english: She is all talk and doesn't do anything for me in the end. (only / nothing but)

general_translation: (Only) continue to, Keep on -ing, More and more
formation: Verb［る］+ ばかりだVerb［る］+ ばかりで + Phrase
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ ばかりだVerb［る］+ ばかりで + Phrase
polite_structure: Verb［る］+ ばかりですVerb［る］+ ばかりで + Phrase
explanation: A slightly formal phrase that presents some kind of trend that is only intensifying further.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は傲慢になるばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: He continues to get more arrogant. (only)

example_sentences.japanese: ガソリンの値段は上がっていくばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: The price of gas keeps rising.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近は全然体を鍛えていないから、筋肉がなくなっていくばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: Recently I haven't been working out, so I keep on losing muscle.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の人口は減るばかりです。
example_sentences.english: Japan's population continues to drop.

example_sentences.japanese: この辺は犯罪が多いので、治安が悪くなるばかりです。
example_sentences.english: Because there are so many crimes around here, the public safety of the area continues to get worse.

example_sentences.japanese: この町の治安が悪くなるばかりで、しばらく良くなりそうもない。
example_sentences.english: The public order of this town keeps on getting worse, and it doesn't look like it will get better anytime soon.

example_sentences.japanese: 観光客が減るばかりで、周りの店が潰れていっている。
example_sentences.english: The amount of tourists keeps on dropping, and the stores around us are closing.

example_sentences.japanese: おじいさんの健康が衰えるばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: The state of grandpa's health keeps on declining. (only)

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、ビットコインの価値が下がるばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: Recently, the price of bitcoin keeps on dropping. (only)

example_sentences.japanese: 癌のため、体が弱っていくばかりです。
example_sentences.english: Because of the cancer, my body continues to get weaker. (only)

example_sentences.japanese: 夏休みになってから、日本語を忘れていくばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: I have been continuously forgetting Japanese since summer vacation started. (only)

example_sentences.japanese: 値段が上がるばかりで、安くなる気配がない。
example_sentences.english: The price only continues to go up and there is no indication of it ever going down. (only)

example_sentences.japanese: ほうっておけば悪くなるばかりだ。なんとかしないと。
example_sentences.english: If I continue on like this it will get even worse. I must do something... (only)

example_sentences.japanese: 一生懸命治療しているのに、この患者の体調は悪くなるばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: Despite receiving dedicated therapy, this patient's condition continues to get worse. (only)

example_sentences.japanese: 金融危機なのに、ビットコインの価値は上がるばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: Despite the financial crisis, Bitcoin's value continues to rise. (only)

example_sentences.japanese: 近くにゴミ捨て場があるので、この辺りの土地の価値は減るばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: Because the garbage dump is nearby, the value of land around here continues to decrease. (only)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本のような先進国では、出生率は低下するばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: In developed countries similar to Japan the birth rate keeps on decreasing. (only)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は妻を亡くしてから、うつ病が重くなるばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: Since his wife's death, his depression continues to worsen. (only)

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日夜遅くまで働いているから、疲れがたまっていくばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: Because I work until late at night everyday, I keep getting more exhausted.

example_sentences.japanese: 病院を変えてから、体調が良くなっていくばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: Ever since I changed hospitals, my health keeps on getting better.

general_translation: Simply because, Only because, Just because, Simply on account of
formation: Verb［た］+ ばかりに［い］Adjective + ばかりに［な］Adjective + な(1) + ばかりにNoun + な(1) + ばかりに(1) である
casual_structure: Verb［た］+ ばかりに［い］Adjective + ばかりに［な］Adjective + な(1) + ばかりにNoun + な(1) + ばかりに(1) である
explanation: A slightly formal phrase used to show that just (A) caused (B), often despite being a minor thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 財布を忘れたばかりに、お弁当を買えなかった。
example_sentences.english: Simply because I have forgotten my wallet, I couldn't buy a bento.

example_sentences.japanese: ボールをキャッチしたばかりに、肩が外れました。
example_sentences.english: Simply because I caught a ball, I dislocated my shoulders.

example_sentences.japanese: 体が小さいばかりに、クラスメイトにいじめられた。
example_sentences.english: Simply because I am small, my classmates bullied me.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は練習が大変なばかりに、部活をやめることにした。
example_sentences.english: Simply because practice was difficult, he decided to quit.

example_sentences.japanese: 新人であるばかりに、先輩たちがやりたくない仕事を押し付けられた。
example_sentences.english: Simply because I am new, my senpai made me do all the work they didn't want to.

example_sentences.japanese: 釣りに行きたいばかりに、仕事を休んで海に行った。
example_sentences.english: Simply because he wanted to go fish, he took a day off of work and went to the ocean.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい車が欲しいばかりに、貯金を全部使った。
example_sentences.english: Just because I wanted a new car, I used all my savings.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は驚かされたばかりに、気を失ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: He passed out simply because he got surprised.

example_sentences.japanese: 恋人に会いたいばかりに、インドネシアに旅行した。
example_sentences.english: Simply because I wanted to see my significant other, I traveled all the way to Indonesia.

example_sentences.japanese: 良いリーダーがいなかったばかりに、チームは試合に負けた。
example_sentences.english: Just because they didn't have a good leader, the team lost the match.

example_sentences.japanese: 点検を怠っていたばかりに、タコマナローズ橋は崩壊した。
example_sentences.english: Just because of negligence in inspections, the Tacoma Narrows Bridge crumbled.

example_sentences.japanese: 病院の予約を入れてしまったばかりに、試合に参加できなかった。
example_sentences.english: Unfortunately, just because I made an appointment at the hospital, I couldn't participate in the game.

example_sentences.japanese: おとなしそうに見えた犬の頭を撫でたばかりに噛まれたんだ。まだ手が痛いよ。
example_sentences.english: Just because I patted the head of a docile-looking dog, I got bit. My hand still hurts.

example_sentences.japanese: 私があんなことを言ってしまったばかりに、彼はひどく落ち込んでしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Just because I said those things to him, he got extremely depressed.

example_sentences.japanese: 父親がたまにしか家にいないばかりに親子関係が冷たくなることがある。
example_sentences.english: Just because fathers are only home occasionally, the parent-child bond can become distant.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はスマホをちらりと見たばかりに、事故を起こしたんだ。運転するときは注意が必要だ。
example_sentences.english: Simply because he glanced at his phone, he caused the accident. It is necessary to be careful when driving.

example_sentences.japanese: ある作家のサインがほしいばかりに、作家が普段、どういった行動をとっているかを調べた。
example_sentences.english: Just because I wanted the autograph of a certain author, I investigated what his usual routine is like.

example_sentences.japanese: この鳥は孵化したあと弱かったばかりに、親に見放されたんだ。自然界は怖い...ね？
example_sentences.english: This bird was abandoned by its parents simply because it was weak after hatching. Nature is scary, huh?

example_sentences.japanese: 貰った肉を食べたばかりに、お腹を壊してしまった。
example_sentences.english: Even just with eating the meat that was given to me, I got a stomach ache.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回は許すけど、またやったら許さないからね。
example_sentences.english: I will forgive you this time, but I will not forgive you if you do it again.

general_translation: Something is possible, Sometimes, Occasionally, There are times when
formation: Verb［る］(1) + こと + が(2)ある［い］Adjective + こと + が(2)ある［な］Adjective + な +  こと + が(2)ある(1) Verb［ない］(2) も
casual_structure: Verb［る］(1) + こと + が(2)ある［い］Adjective + こと + が(2)ある［な］Adjective + な +  こと + が(2)ある(1) Verb［ない］(2) も
polite_structure: Verb［る］(1) + こと + が(2)あります［い］Adjective + こと + が(2)あります［な］Adjective + な +  こと + が(2)あります(1) Verb［ない］(2) も
explanation: A grammar point that expresses something as being possible, or occasionally happening. There is that which is (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 頑張ってもうまくいかないことがある。
example_sentences.english: There are times when no matter how hard you try, it doesn't go well.

example_sentences.japanese: この馬は人を蹴ることがあるので、馬の後ろに立たないで下さい。
example_sentences.english: This horse kicks people sometimes, so please don't stand behind him.

example_sentences.japanese: タナカ先生の授業はたまに楽しいことがある。
example_sentences.english: There are times where Mr. Tanaka's classes are fun.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事はだいたい大変だけれども、たまには楽なことがある。
example_sentences.english: Work is usually difficult, but there are times where it is easy.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事は楽しいけど、大変なこともある。
example_sentences.english: Work is fun, but there are times where it gets difficult.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生はいつも怒っているけど、優しいこともある。
example_sentences.english: Our teacher is always angry, but there are times when he is nice.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校に送ってもらうことがある。
example_sentences.english: I sometimes get a ride to school.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達は昼２時まで寝ることがある。
example_sentences.english: There are times when my friend sleeps until two in the afternoon.

example_sentences.japanese: あの番組ならたまに見ることがある。
example_sentences.english: (There are times that ) I sometimes watch that TV program.

example_sentences.japanese: 一日に二、三回ぐらい、ラーメンを食べることがある。
example_sentences.english: There are days where I eat ramen two or three times.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達に日本語を教えることがある。
example_sentences.english: There are times that I teach Japanese to my friend.

example_sentences.japanese: 気になることがありすぎて、夜眠れないことがある。
example_sentences.english: There are times that I can't sleep at night for I feel anxious about too many things.

example_sentences.japanese: 化学物質は、触るだけでも危険なことがある。
example_sentences.english: There are times when chemical substances are dangerous, even if only touched.

example_sentences.japanese: 高級な洋服店だが服が安いこともある。
example_sentences.english: Although this is a high-end Western clothing store, there are also times when the clothes are cheap.

example_sentences.japanese: たまに手を抜くことがあるが、普段は真面目な人だ。
example_sentences.english: There are times that he cuts corners at work, but he is usually a very serious person.

example_sentences.japanese: 「あの時もっと頑張れば良かった」と思うことがある。
example_sentences.english: There are times when I think 'I should have tried harder then.'

example_sentences.japanese: ルームメイトの無作法な振る舞いに注意したいことがよくある。でも、私は気が弱すぎる・・・
example_sentences.english: There are many times when I want to warn my roommate about his rude behavior. However, I am just too timid.

example_sentences.japanese: 週に一回のペースでラーメンを食べることがある。
example_sentences.english: There are times when I eat ramen once a week.

example_sentences.japanese: このラーメンは食べたことがあると思う。
example_sentences.english: I think I have eaten this ramen before.

general_translation: To decide on, Have decided to
formation: Verb［る］+ ことにするVerb［ない］+ ことにする
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ ことにするVerb［ない］+ ことにする
polite_structure: Verb［る］+ ことにしますVerb［ない］+ ことにします
explanation: An expression that shows that the thing which is (A) has been decided upon, or will be done.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はエイプリルフールだからウソしか言わないことにする。
example_sentences.english: Since today is April Fool's, I've decided to only tell lies.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はワクチンを打ったから、明日は仕事を休むことにする。
example_sentences.english: Today I got vaccinated, so I will go with taking the day off tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: タマキさんと箱根に行くことにする。
example_sentences.english: I have decided to go to Hakone with Tamaki-san.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は雨が降っているから、明日行くことにしない？
example_sentences.english: It is raining today, don't you want to make it that we go tomorrow?

example_sentences.japanese: 勝手に僕が行くということにしないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please don't decide that I will go without asking me. (Please don't assume that I want to go)

example_sentences.japanese: あの場所で、記念写真を撮ることにします。
example_sentences.english: We've decided to take the commemorative photo at that place.

example_sentences.japanese: 九時に終わるか分からなかったが、早めに帰ることにしました。
example_sentences.english: I didn't know if it would finish at nine but I decided to go home in advance.

example_sentences.japanese: これ以上言わないことにします。もし何か言ったら彼女を怒らせるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: I have decided not to say anything else. If I say something, it would piss her off.

example_sentences.japanese: この商品、無料で配ることにします。
example_sentences.english: I have decided to hand out this product for free.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日、数分文法を勉強することにした。
example_sentences.english: I have decided to study grammar for a few minutes every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近睡眠不足だから、今日から早く寝ることにした。
example_sentences.english: Starting from today, I have decided to sleep earlier because I have been sleep deprived lately.

example_sentences.japanese: 一本早い電車に乗ることにした。その方が座れるから。
example_sentences.english: I have decided to take the earlier train. That way, I will be able to sit down.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との旅行に行かないで、僕だけ家に残ることにしました。
example_sentences.english: I have decided to stay home alone, and not to go on a trip with friends.

example_sentences.japanese: あまりプロジェクトに気を使わないことにした。疲れてしまうから。
example_sentences.english: I will get completely worn out, so I have decided not to worry about the project too much.

example_sentences.japanese: ビタミン不足だから、毎日野菜ジュースを飲むことにしている。
example_sentences.english: I have decided to drink vegetable juice every day because I am lacking in vitamins.

example_sentences.japanese: やりすぎてしまうから、今後はテレビゲームをしないことにします。
example_sentences.english: I have decided to stop playing video games from now on, because I play too much.

example_sentences.japanese: これからは肉を食べることにする。
example_sentences.english: I have decided to eat meat from now on.

example_sentences.japanese: これからは肉を食べることにしない？
example_sentences.english: Why don't we decide to eat meat from now on?

example_sentences.japanese: これからは肉を食べないことにする。
example_sentences.english: I have decided to not eat meat from now on.

example_sentences.japanese: これからは肉を食べないことにしない。
example_sentences.english: I have decided to not not eat meat from now on.

general_translation: (A) is (Description of A), (A) means that (Description of A)
formation: Phrase + というのは(1) + ［い］Adjective + （という）ことなの(2)だ(3)Phrase + というのは(1) + Verb + （という）ことなの(2)だ(3)Phrase + というのは(1) + ［な］Adjective + な(4)ことなの(2)だ(3)Phrase + というのは(1) + Noun + の(4)ことなの(2)だ(3)(1) って、とは、ということは(2) なん(3) である、でござる(4) という
casual_structure: Phrase + というのは(1) + ［い］Adjective + （という）ことなの(2)だ(3)Phrase + というのは(1) + Verb + （という）ことなの(2)だ(3)Phrase + というのは(1) + ［な］Adjective + な(4)ことなの(2)だ(3)Phrase + というのは(1) + Noun + の(4)ことなの(2)だ(3)(1) って、とは、ということは(2) なん(3) である、でござる(4) という
polite_structure: Phrase + というのは(1) + ［い］Adjective + （という）ことなの(2)です(3)Phrase + というのは(1) + Verb + （という）ことなの(2)です(3)Phrase + というのは(1) + ［な］Adjective + な(4)ことなの(2)です(3)Phrase + というのは(1) + Noun + の(4)ことなの(2)です(3)(1) って、とは、ということは(2) なん(3) であります、でございます(4) という
