explanation: A structure indicating a thing called (A), and then explaining exactly that which it is.

example_sentences.japanese: ハダウェイ：「恋愛とはどういうことなのだろうか。」
example_sentences.english: Haddaway: 'Love, what does it mean?'

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は超一流歌手ということなの？
example_sentences.english: Do you mean that person is the most skilled singer?

example_sentences.japanese: 輸送とは荷物を送ることなの。
example_sentences.english: 'Freight' means to ship a package.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨が上がるというのは雨が止むことなのです。
example_sentences.english: The thing which is 'for rain to rise' means 'to stop raining'.

example_sentences.japanese: 付属品というのはメインの物に付属している物のことなんだ。
example_sentences.english: Accessories are things that come with the main product.

example_sentences.japanese: 漫画家というのは漫画を描く人のことなのだ。
example_sentences.english: Manga artists are people that draw manga.

example_sentences.japanese: つまり、その病気が感染症ではないということなのである。
example_sentences.english: In other words, it means that the disease is not infectious.

example_sentences.japanese: チーターのように走るとは足が速いということなのだ。
example_sentences.english: 'Running like a cheetah' means to be fast.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ザクシャ・イン・ラブ」とは「愛を永遠に」ということなのだ。
example_sentences.english: 'Zawsze in love' means 'forever in love'.

example_sentences.japanese: 頭が切れるというのは頭がいいことなのだ。
example_sentences.english: 'To be sharp' means ' to be smart'.

example_sentences.japanese: 「月に代わって、お仕置きよ!」というのはどういうことなのでしょうか？
example_sentences.english: What does 'in place of the moon, I will punish you' mean?

example_sentences.japanese: 「冬がやってくる」というのはいつでも予想外の事態に対して準備をしておくべきことなのだ。
example_sentences.english: 'Winter is coming' means that one always has to be prepared for the unexpected.

example_sentences.japanese: 干ばつということは食品の価値があがることなのだろう。
example_sentences.english: The drought means that prices of food will probably rise.

example_sentences.japanese: 満身創痍というのは傷だらけのことなのである。
example_sentences.english: 'Manshinsoui (Having wounds all over the body)' means 'to be covered in wounds'.

example_sentences.japanese: 「笑い死に」とは笑うことが原因となって死ぬことなのだ。
example_sentences.english: 'Death by laughter' means to die due to laughter.

example_sentences.japanese: 親愛なる読者。この文章を読むことができるということは日本語がかなり上手だということなのだ。
example_sentences.english: Dear reader, the fact that you are able to read this sentence means that your Japanese is quite good.

example_sentences.japanese: 幽霊船というのは生きた乗組員のいない船舶のことなのである。
example_sentences.english: A ghost ship is (means) a vessel with no living crew.

example_sentences.japanese: つまりそこに一人で行くと危ないということなのか。
example_sentences.english: You mean that it is dangerous to go there alone?

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに怒ることなのですか。
example_sentences.english: Is this something you should get so worked up over?

general_translation: It will end up being, It is the result of, It has been decided that
formation: Verb + ことになる［い］Adjective + ことになる［な］Adjective + な + ことになる
casual_structure: Verb + ことになる［い］Adjective + ことになる［な］Adjective + な + ことになる
polite_structure: Verb + ことになります［い］Adjective + ことになります［な］Adjective + な + ことになります
explanation: A grammar point which expresses that something will end up being the thing which is (A), or result in (A).

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてこんなことになったの？意味がわからないよ。
example_sentences.english: Why did it end up like this? I don't get it.

example_sentences.japanese: なんでも後回しにしているとあとから苦労することになる。
example_sentences.english: If you wait until it is too late, you are going to end up regretting it.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなことをしたらとんでもないことになるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you do something like that, it is going to become a huge deal.

example_sentences.japanese: 出来るだけ早く治療をしないと、後から大変なことになる。
example_sentences.english: If you don't treat it soon, it is going to end up being a bigger issue.

example_sentences.japanese: 大変なことになったぞ。何か作戦を考えなければ。
example_sentences.english: We ended up getting in trouble. We have to figure out a plan.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が会議に出ることになった。
example_sentences.english: It was decided that I will attend the meeting.

example_sentences.japanese: 連絡がなければ、僕が仕事に行くことになります。
example_sentences.english: If we do not hear anything, I will end up going to work.

example_sentences.japanese: 困ったことになったな。もう電池が切れそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I ended up in a jam. It seems that my battery is about to die.

example_sentences.japanese: 来年引っ越すことになった。
example_sentences.english: It was decided that we will move next year.

example_sentences.japanese: 震災のため、アメリカに帰らなければならないことになりました。
example_sentences.english: It was decided that I must return to America because of the earthquake.

example_sentences.japanese: 結局僕がおごることになった。みんな後輩だから。
example_sentences.english: I ended up paying. Since I'm the oldest.

example_sentences.japanese: インフルエンザにかかってしまったので、今日の大会に出れないことになった。
example_sentences.english: Since I got the flu I ended up being unable to attend today's tournament.

example_sentences.japanese: この前のように風邪を引いたら、また入院することになるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you catch a cold like the last time, you will end up going to the hospital again.

example_sentences.japanese: 急に出張することになって、準備が大変だ。
example_sentences.english: It has suddenly been decided that I will go on a business trip and I am having trouble getting ready for it.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日が雨ならば、１週間降り続くことになる。
example_sentences.english: If it rains tomorrow, it will end up being a week straight of rain.

general_translation: Is famous for
formation: Noun + は + Verb + こと(1) + で + 有名（ゆうめい）Noun + は + ［い］Adjective + こと(1) + で + 有名（ゆうめい）Noun + は + ［な］Adjective + な + こと(1) + で + 有名（ゆうめい）Noun + は + Noun + で + 有名（ゆうめい）(1) の
casual_structure: Noun + は + Verb + こと(1) + で + 有名（ゆうめい）Noun + は + ［い］Adjective + こと(1) + で + 有名（ゆうめい）Noun + は + ［な］Adjective + な + こと(1) + で + 有名（ゆうめい）Noun + は + Noun + で + 有名（ゆうめい）(1) の
explanation: A phrase showing that with or for the attribute of (A), something is famous.

example_sentences.japanese: 札幌は雪まつりでゆうめいです。
example_sentences.english: Sapporo is famous for the snow festival.

example_sentences.japanese: ウサイン・ボルトは速く走れることでゆうめいです。
example_sentences.english: Usain Bolt is famous for being able to run fast.

example_sentences.japanese: この学校は野球が強いことでゆうめいです。
example_sentences.english: This school is famous for having a strong baseball team.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は安全なことでゆうめいです。
example_sentences.english: Japan is famous for being safe.

example_sentences.japanese: 岡山は備前焼でゆうめいです。
example_sentences.english: Okayama is famous for Bizen-yaki.

example_sentences.japanese: 大間はマグロでゆうめいだ。
example_sentences.english: Ooma is famous for tuna.

example_sentences.japanese: あの先生は授業がおもしろいことでゆうめいです。
example_sentences.english: That teacher is famous for his interesting classes.

example_sentences.japanese: このうどんはコシが強いことでゆうめいだ。
example_sentences.english: This udon is famous for its strong and chewy noodles.

example_sentences.japanese: この町は温泉でゆうめいです。
example_sentences.english: This town is famous for its hot springs.

example_sentences.japanese: あの会社は残業をさせないことでゆうめいだ。
example_sentences.english: That company is famous for not making employees work overtime.

example_sentences.japanese: このレストランはシェフがハンサムなことでゆうめいです。
example_sentences.english: This restaurant is famous for its handsome chef.

example_sentences.japanese: あの病院は、スタッフがみんな親切なことでゆうめいです。
example_sentences.english: That hospital is famous for its kind staff members.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は憲法に詳しいことでゆうめいです。
example_sentences.english: He is famous for being knowledgeable about the constitution.

example_sentences.japanese: この映画は女優が綺麗なことでゆうめいです。
example_sentences.english: This movie is famous for its beautiful actresses.

example_sentences.japanese: 宮沢賢治は素敵な詩を書いたことでゆうめいです。
example_sentences.english: Kenji Miyazawa is famous for writing beautiful poetry.

example_sentences.japanese: このホテルはシャンデリアが豪華なことでゆうめいです。
example_sentences.english: This hotel is famous for its extravagant chandeliers.

example_sentences.japanese: グランドキャニオンはアメリカでゆうめいな観光地だ。
example_sentences.english: The Grand Canyon is a famous tourist site in America.

example_sentences.japanese: 出雲大社は島根県でゆうめいな神社だ。
example_sentences.english: Izumo Taisha is a famous shrine in Shimane prefecture.

general_translation: There is no need to, Never happens
formation: Verb + ことはない
casual_structure: Verb + ことはない
polite_structure: Verb + ことはありません
explanation: An expression that shows that (A) is a thing that either never occurs, or is not called for.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな急ぐことはない。ぼちぼちやればいい。
example_sentences.english: There is no need to hurry. You should take your time.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに慌てることはない。まだ時間がいっぱいあるからゆっくりやればいいよ。
example_sentences.english: There is no need to rush that much. We still have a lot of time, so it is okay if you pace yourself.

example_sentences.japanese: １０年前に親と喧嘩をしてから、親と話すことはない。
example_sentences.english: Ever since I fought with my parents 10 years ago, I have not talked to them.

example_sentences.japanese: もうあの家に帰ることはないだろう。
example_sentences.english: We will never return to that house, right?

example_sentences.japanese: もう彼に教えることはありません。
example_sentences.english: There is no need to teach him anymore.

example_sentences.japanese: これ以上何も言うことはない。
example_sentences.english: There is no need to say more.

example_sentences.japanese: この抽選で車が当たることはないと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think that winning a car in this lottery never happens.

example_sentences.japanese: その怪我は擦り傷だから、心配することはないよ。
example_sentences.english: That injury is just a flesh wound, so you don't need to worry.

example_sentences.japanese: よくできた作品だ。何も言うことはないな。
example_sentences.english: This is a well done piece. I have nothing to say. (There is no need to say anything)

example_sentences.japanese: 沖縄に住んだら、雪を見ることはない。
example_sentences.english: If you live in Okinawa, you never see snow.

example_sentences.japanese: 君がそんなに責任を感じることはないよ。
example_sentences.english: There is no need to feel so responsible.

example_sentences.japanese: 泣くことはない。君のせいじゃないんだから。
example_sentences.english: There is no need to cry. It's not your fault.

example_sentences.japanese: 落とした鍵を見つけたから、もう心配することはない。
example_sentences.english: Since we found the keys that were dropped, there is no need to worry anymore.

example_sentences.japanese: 恐れることはない。思い切ってやってみるんだ！
example_sentences.english: There is no need to be scared. Give it all of your might!

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに心配した事が無い。
example_sentences.english: There has never been a time where I worried that much.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに心配することはないよ。
example_sentences.english: There is no need to worry that much.

general_translation: Although ~ might say that ~
formation: Verb + と言（い）っても［い］Adjective + と言（い）っても［な］Adjective + （だ） + と言（い）ってもNoun  + （だ） + と言（い）っても
casual_structure: Verb + と言（い）っても［い］Adjective + と言（い）っても［な］Adjective + （だ） + と言（い）ってもNoun  + （だ） + と言（い）っても
explanation: A grammar point highlighting that although, or even if (A) is said, (B) is more accurate.

example_sentences.japanese: プレゼントといっても、たいしたものはない。
example_sentences.english: Although I say that it is a present, it is nothing special.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日走るといっても、１５分しか走らないよ。
example_sentences.english: Although I say I run every day, I only run for 15 minutes.

example_sentences.japanese: 辛いといってもピリ辛だから、あなたでも食べれると思うよ。
example_sentences.english: Even though I say it is spicy, it is only slightly spicy, so I think you should be able to eat it.

example_sentences.japanese: この肉は新鮮だといっても、３日前に買ったからそんなに新鮮ではない。
example_sentences.english: Although I say this meat is fresh, I bought it 3 days ago, so it is not that fresh.

example_sentences.japanese: 新幹線だといってもこだまに乗るから、そんなに早く着かないと思う。
example_sentences.english: Although I say I'm going by shinkansen, I will be riding the Kodama, so I don't think I will get there that fast.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたは天才だといっても過言ではない。
example_sentences.english: Even if someone says you are a genius, it is not an exaggeration.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生っていっても、いろんな人がいるよね。
example_sentences.english: Although you may say 'sensei,' there are different people (types of sensei).

example_sentences.japanese: 楽しいっていっても、サッカーの方が楽しいと思う。
example_sentences.english: Although you might say it is fun, soccer is more fun.

example_sentences.japanese: ほしいっていっても、高くて自分では買えません。
example_sentences.english: Although I might say I want it, it is expensive and I can't buy it for myself.

example_sentences.japanese: 温暖な気候っていっても、冬には雪が降るよ。
example_sentences.english: Although you can say that the climate is warm, it still snows in winter.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は画家といっても、自称画家というだけなんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Although he might say that he is an artist, he is only a self-proclaimed artist.

example_sentences.japanese: 泳ぐのが好きだといっても、平泳ぎしかできないんだけどね。
example_sentences.english: Although I say that I like swimming, I can't do anything but the breaststroke.

example_sentences.japanese: 有名だといっても、日本で知らない人もいる。
example_sentences.english: Although one can say it is famous, it doesn't mean it is known among all Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕の鞄は重いといっても、君のはもっと重い。
example_sentences.english: Although I say that my bag is heavy, yours is heavier.

example_sentences.japanese: この問題は簡単だといっても、解くのに時間はかかる。
example_sentences.english: Although I might say that this problem is easy, it will still take time to solve.

example_sentences.japanese: 魚釣りが趣味といっても、実は得意ではない。
example_sentences.english: Although I say that my hobby is fishing, it doesn't mean I am a good fisher.

example_sentences.japanese: 危険といってもおかしくない。
example_sentences.english: Although some might say that it is dangerous, it's not that strange. (It is safe to say that it is dangerous)

example_sentences.japanese: 難しいといっても、実際にやってみると意外と簡単です。
example_sentences.english: Even though it is said that it is difficult, once you actually try it, it is quite easy.

general_translation: Speaking of, If it were the case that
formation: Noun + と言（い）えば(1)(1) と言（い）うと、と言（い）ったら
casual_structure: Noun + と言（い）えば(1)(1) と言（い）うと、と言（い）ったら
explanation: A hypothetical grammar point that is used when (A) suddenly reminds the speaker of something related.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「夏休み、海に行きたいわ。」  Ｂ：「夏といえばかき氷だよね。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I want to go to the beach during summer vacation.' B: 'Speaking of summer, shaved ice!'

example_sentences.japanese: 夏といえばスイカバーでしょ！
example_sentences.english: If we're talking (about) summer, it's gotta be a Suika-bar, don't you think? (Suika-bars are the best thing when it is summer, don't you think)

example_sentences.japanese: タナカさんというと、先月銀行強盗で捕まった人ですよね。
example_sentences.english: Speaking of Tanaka-san, he is the person that got arrested for robbing a bank last month, right?

example_sentences.japanese: ラーメン？日本といったら寿司の方が人気でしょう。
example_sentences.english: Ramen? If it's Japan (we're talking about), sushi is more popular, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「コーヒーがほしい！」 Ｂ：「コーヒーといえば、新しい喫茶店が開店した。じゃあ、一緒に喫茶店に行こうか？」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I want coffee.' B: 'Speaking of coffee, a new coffee shop just opened. Wanna go?'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「ビットコインの評価は最近下ったみたい...。」 Ｂ：「ビットコインといえば、今、売るべきなの？」
example_sentences.english: A: 'It looks like the value of bitcoin has recently decreased...' B: 'Speaking of bitcoin, should I sell now?'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「最近、アニメは国際的に人気になっていくよ。」 Ｂ：「アニメといえばドラグーンボールの新しいシーズンが放送されているね。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Recently anime is getting popular internationally.'  B: 'Speaking of anime, a new season of 'Dragoon ball' has aired, right?'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「カナダではオーロラや野生動物がよく見られるらしい。」 Ｂ：「オーロラの美しさといったら、言葉では表現できませんなあ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I have heard that you can see auroras and wild animals in Canada.' B: 'Speaking of the beauty of auroras, it cannot be described with words.' (if you were to speak of...)

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「あたしはアメリカの有名人について読むのが好きだわ。」 Ｂ：「アメリカの有名人といえば、トム・クルーズは知っているの？」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I like to read about American celebrities.' B: 'Speaking of American celebrities, do you know Tom Cruise?'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「ドイツの車は世界的に有名ですね。」  Ｂ：「 車といえば日本の中では、トヨタが有名です。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'German cars are known all over the world.'  B: 'Speaking of cars, in Japan, Toyota is famous.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「宇都宮という町、聞いたことがあるの？」  Ｂ：「うん。聞いたことあるよ。宇都宮といえばやっぱり餃子かな。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Have you ever heard about city of Utsunomiya?'  B: 'Yeah! Speaking of Utsunomiya, their gyoza is the best.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「お金は人生でもっとも重要なもの。」  Ｂ：「重要なものといえば、愛もその内の一つだ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Money is the most necessary thing in life.'  B: 'Speaking of necessary things, love is one of them too.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「メアリーさんは今年、卒業したらしい。」 Ｂ：「メアリーといえば、アメリカに帰りたがってると聞いた。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Apparently Mary graduated this year.'  B: 'Speaking of Mary, I heard she wants to go back to the States.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「昨日、水口さんと永代さんと一緒に居酒屋に行った。」Ｂ：「永代さんといえば、亡くなった奥さんの名前を聞くと必ず泣き出すらしい...。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Yesterday I went to a pub with Mizuguchi-san and Eitai-san.' B: 'Speaking of Eitai-san, I heard that whenever he hears his late wife's name, he bursts into tears...'

example_sentences.japanese: 親：「この果物はこの辺では愛の果物という。ハート形のように見えるから。」 子供：「え？そうなの？果物といえば、トマトも果物だ。」
example_sentences.english: Parent: 'This fruit is called 'Fruit of Love' in this area. Because it looks like a heart.' Child: 'Oh, Really? Speaking of fruits, tomatoes are also fruits.'

example_sentences.japanese: 夏と言ったら祭りだから、明日の祭りに一緒に行かない？
example_sentences.english: Speaking of summer, since there is a festival, do you want to go to the festival tomorrow?

example_sentences.japanese: キクチ君といえば、幾つなんだろう？
example_sentences.english: Speaking of Kikuchi-kun, I wonder how old he is.

general_translation: To do for one another, Mutually, With
formation: Verb［stem］+ 合（あ）う
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ 合（あ）う
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ 合（あ）います
explanation: A common expression used to highlight when (A) is done mutually among all involved, or for one another.

example_sentences.japanese: 高校の頃、兄とドッキリをよくしかけあった...
example_sentences.english: During our high school days, my brother and I often pranked one another…

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女と将来の事を話しあう。
example_sentences.english: I am going to talk with my girlfriend about our future.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供たちがおもちゃを取りあうのを見てお兄ちゃんの事を思い出した。
example_sentences.english: The kids were fighting with each other over a toy, and that reminded me of my older brother.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達とポケモンカードを見せあう。
example_sentences.english: My friend and I show each other our Pokemon cards.

example_sentences.japanese: 協力しあったりしながら山をゆっくりと登った。
example_sentences.english: We slowly climbed the mountain while aiding one another (among other things).

example_sentences.japanese: ＥＵで交流しあうことは重要だと考えられている。
example_sentences.english: In the European Union, (to do) mutual cultural exchange is considered important.

example_sentences.japanese: 「友達が苦しんでる時は、たすけあうべきだね。」
example_sentences.english: 'Friends ought to help one another in times of trouble, right?'

example_sentences.japanese: かなださき：「私達、同時に告白しあったんだよ！」
example_sentences.english: Saki Kanada: 'We professed our love for one another at the same time!'

example_sentences.japanese: 私達はそのとき協力しあうべきだったのに。
example_sentences.english: We should have cooperated (with each other) at that time...

example_sentences.japanese: 買い物袋を交代しながらはこびあったので、家に早く帰ることができた。
example_sentences.english: We were able to come home early because we took turns carrying the groceries (for one another).

example_sentences.japanese: お互いにたすけあって、理解できるようになったから、付き合うようになった。
example_sentences.english: Since we were mutually helping one another and came to be able to understand one another we ended up dating.

example_sentences.japanese: この雑誌によるとプレイヤーがきそいあうオンラインゲームは最近なかなか人気になったということだ。
example_sentences.english: According to this magazine, online games in which players compete with one another have gained a lot of popularity recently.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は、サラリーマンが儀式的に名刺を交換しあうことで有名である。
example_sentences.english: Japan is famous for businessmen ceremoniously exchanging business cards with one another.

example_sentences.japanese: よく心がつうじあっていると言っても彼がまだオレをチクったのだ。
example_sentences.english: Although you might say that we understand (one another), he still told on me.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生：「おい、きみたち、授業中にはなしあわないように。」
example_sentences.english: Teacher: 'Hey, you guys, do not talk with one another during class.'

example_sentences.japanese: こういう時こそ、助けあうのが大切だよ。
example_sentences.english: At times like this, it is important to help each other out.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達は夫婦なんだから、どんなことがあっても協力しあわないといけないよ。
example_sentences.english: We are husband and wife, so no matter what happens, we need to cooperate.

example_sentences.japanese: 全チームが賞金をかけて競いあう。
example_sentences.english: Every team competed against each other with the prize money on the line.

general_translation: In accordance with, Matching, Fitting, Suitable for, Adjust or tune to
formation: Noun + に合（あ）わせてNoun + に合（あ）った + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + に合（あ）わせてNoun + に合（あ）った + Noun
explanation: A construction used to show that something is done to fit with (A), or to match (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 合図にあわせて、スタートしてください。
example_sentences.english: In accordance with the signal, please begin.

example_sentences.japanese: 音楽にあわせてギターを弾く練習をしています。
example_sentences.english: I am practicing playing my guitar along with music.

example_sentences.japanese: 相手にあわせて話し方を変えるのは疲れる。
example_sentences.english: It is exhausting to change how you talk in accordance with who you are talking to.

example_sentences.japanese: このソファーにあったテーブルを買おう。
example_sentences.english: Lets buy a table that matches this couch.

example_sentences.japanese: 壁紙にあった家具が欲しい。
example_sentences.english: I want furniture that matches the wallpaper.

example_sentences.japanese: 服装は季節にあわせて、変えるものだよ！
example_sentences.english: You are supposed to change your clothes to match the season.

example_sentences.japanese: 状況にあわせて、やり方を変えてください。
example_sentences.english: Change your approach in accordance with the situation.

example_sentences.japanese: 私にあった服を選んで。
example_sentences.english: Please choose some clothes that suit me. (match)

example_sentences.japanese: あの音楽にあわせて、踊ろうよ。
example_sentences.english: Let's dance (in accordance) with that music.

example_sentences.japanese: 椅子にあった座布団を買おう。
example_sentences.english: I will buy a zabuton that matches the chair(s).

example_sentences.japanese: 相手にあわせて、話し方を調整する。
example_sentences.english: Adjust the way one speaks in accordance with whom one is speaking to.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕の性格にあった仕事が見つかりました。
example_sentences.english: I found work that suits my personality. (match)

example_sentences.japanese: 料理にあった飲み物を選んでもらった。
example_sentences.english: I had them choose a drink that matched the meal.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の家具にあわせてカーテンを選ぶ。
example_sentences.english: To choose curtains that match the current furniture.

example_sentences.japanese: この服にあった靴がなかなか見つかりません。
example_sentences.english: I can't find a pair of shoes that match these clothes.

example_sentences.japanese: 初心者にあった文法の教科書を書こうと思う。
example_sentences.english: I plan to write a grammar textbook suitable for beginners. (match)

example_sentences.japanese: リズムに合わせて歌を歌う。
example_sentences.english: I sing while matching the rhythm. (I sing to the rhythm)

example_sentences.japanese: 合図に合わせてスタートする。
example_sentences.english: To start in accordance with the signal.

general_translation: Concerning, About, Regarding
formation: Noun + についてNoun + について + の + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + についてNoun + について + の + Noun
explanation: A phrase that expresses a topic adhering to (A), and therefore being about it.

example_sentences.japanese: この問題について、誰かに話しましたか。
example_sentences.english: Have you talked to anyone about this problem? (concerning)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女と別れたことについて話したいんだけど時間ある？
example_sentences.english: I want to talk to you about breaking up with my girlfriend, but do you have time?

example_sentences.japanese: 契約のことについて、何か質問はありますか。
example_sentences.english: Do you have any questions regarding the contract?

example_sentences.japanese: 行きたい国について、作文を書いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please write an essay about the country you want to visit.

example_sentences.japanese: 契約についてのパンフレットは明日届くので、しっかりとお読みになってください。
example_sentences.english: The brochure regarding the contract will be delivered tomorrow, so please make sure to read it.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は和製英語についてのレッスンをしたいと思います。
example_sentences.english: Today, I am thinking of giving you a lesson about Wasei Eigo.

example_sentences.japanese: 火災について、訓練をするべきです。
example_sentences.english: There should be training regarding fires. (about)

example_sentences.japanese: 震災についての情報を教えてもらった。
example_sentences.english: I was taught information regarding earthquake disasters. (concerning)

example_sentences.japanese: 原因についてはまだ調査中です。
example_sentences.english: Regarding the cause, we are still investigating. (concerning・about)

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の持ち物についてお伝えします。
example_sentences.english: You will be informed about what to bring tomorrow. (regarding)

example_sentences.japanese: 防災についての講習会に参加してください。
example_sentences.english: Please participate in the training program regarding disaster prevention. (concerning)

example_sentences.japanese: 時間については、後日お知らせします。
example_sentences.english: Regarding the time, we will let you know in the coming days. (concerning・about)

example_sentences.japanese: 詳細について書いてある書類をお渡しします。
example_sentences.english: I will give you the documents about the details. (regarding)

example_sentences.japanese: 今後の人生について考えて、今行動すべきだと思った。
example_sentences.english: Concerning how I will live the rest of my life, I thought I should take action now. (regarding・about)

example_sentences.japanese: その点については、担当の者が説明いたします。
example_sentences.english: Regarding that point, the one in charge will provide an explanation. (about・concerning)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は子供教育について、講演を行います。
example_sentences.english: There will be a lecture today about the education of children. (concerning)

example_sentences.japanese: 問題点についてみんなで話し合ってください。
example_sentences.english: Concerning the problem, please discuss it together. (regarding・about)

general_translation: Figure, Shape, Appearance, Looks, Wearing, Dressed in, Presence
formation: Verb + 姿（すがた）Noun + （の） + 姿（すがた）
casual_structure: Verb + 姿（すがた）Noun + （の） + 姿（すがた）
explanation: An expression highlighting someone having the figure of (A), often in relation to dress or presence.

example_sentences.japanese: この地域には人のすがたが見えない。
example_sentences.english: There is no human presence in this area. (figure)

example_sentences.japanese: 息子が悲しんでいるすがたを見ると、私まで悲しくなってくる。
example_sentences.english: When I see my son in a sad state, it makes even me sad.

example_sentences.japanese: さっき男の人のすがたが見えたけど、気のせいかな。
example_sentences.english: Earlier, I saw a man (his figure), but maybe I was seeing things.

example_sentences.japanese: デパートで息子のすがたが見えなくなって、少しパニックになった。
example_sentences.english: I lost sight of my son's presence at the department store, and it made me panic a little.

example_sentences.japanese: 娘の歩くすがたが夫に似ている。
example_sentences.english: The way my daughter walks looks just like my husband.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬の寝ているすがたはとてもかわいい。
example_sentences.english: The way my dog looks when he is sleeping is so cute.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日初めてお父さんが働いているすがたを見た。
example_sentences.english: Yesterday was the first time I saw my father (his figure) working.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの動くすがたが好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like the way you look when you move. (moving figure)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「あの人は顔も綺麗だし、立ちすがたも美しい。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'That person has a pretty face, and also the way they stand is attractive.' (standing figure)

example_sentences.japanese: 衣料品店、クライアント：「自分のすがたを鏡で見てみるよ。」
example_sentences.english: Clothing store, client: 'I will look at my appearance in the mirror!' (figure)

example_sentences.japanese: ２０１２年に最後に会ってから、あの男のすがたを見ていない。
example_sentences.english: I haven't seen him (his presence) since the last time I met him in 2012. (figure・appearance)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「彼は頭がいいだけでなく、立ってるすがたもイケてる。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'Not only is he smart, but the way he stands is also cool.' (standing figure)

example_sentences.japanese: 新聞記事：「映画会社のパーティーには、華やかな着物すがたの女優たちが出席していた。」
example_sentences.english: Newspaper article: 'Actresses dressed in brilliant kimonos made an appearance at the movie company party.' (appearance・looks)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「彼女の笑うすがたを見かけて、私も嬉しくなった。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'I happened to see the way she laughs, and I also became happy.' (laughing figure)

example_sentences.japanese: 母親が息子に話す：「イズク君、あなたが初めて歩いたすがたを覚えてるわよ。可愛すぎたよ。」
example_sentences.english: Mother speaking to son: 'Izuku-kun, I remember the way you looked, walking for the first time. It was just too cute.' (walking figure)

example_sentences.japanese: 論文：「コンピュータ技術でアイスマンの生きていた時のすがたが復元された。」
example_sentences.english: Essay/thesis: 'The way the iceman looked when he was alive has been restored using computer technology.' (figure/appearance)

example_sentences.japanese: 新聞記事：「マスクすがたの容疑者、警察官の姿を見て逃げる」
example_sentences.english: Newspaper article: 'The mask-wearing suspect escapes at the sight of a policeman' (figure of a masked man)

example_sentences.japanese: ノベル：「高齢者を手伝うボランティアのすがたを見て、泣くほど感動した。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'I was touched to the point of crying after catching the sight of a volunteer helping elderly.' (figure of a volunteer)

example_sentences.japanese: やっとお前の花嫁姿が見れて嬉しいよ。
example_sentences.english: I am so happy that I can finally see you as a bride.

example_sentences.japanese: シンデレラは１２時になった瞬間に元姿に戻った。
example_sentences.english: As soon as it reached 12 o'clock, Cinderella turned back into her original appearance. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: Would or could say that..., Can probably say that..., Fair to say that...
formation: Phrase + と + （も） + 言（い）える + だろうPhrase + と + （も） + いえ よう
casual_structure: Phrase + と + （も） + 言（い）える + だろうPhrase + と + （も） + いえ よう
polite_structure: Phrase + と + （も） + 言（い）える + でしょうPhrase + と + （も） + いえましょう
explanation: An expression indicating that (A) is something which is fair to say, or has the possibility of being said.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らは同時にゴールインしたといえるだろう。
example_sentences.english: One could say that they got to the finish line at the same time.

example_sentences.japanese: この儀式は日本の文化の一つといえる。
example_sentences.english: It is fair to say that this ceremony is part of Japan's culture.

example_sentences.japanese: あのビルは日本一高いビルだといえる。
example_sentences.english: One could say that the building over there is the tallest building in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: このプランは成功したといえるだろう。
example_sentences.english: We could say that this plan was a success, right?

example_sentences.japanese: タナカ選手は国民的アスリートだといえるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Can it not be said that Tanaka is an athlete loved by everyone in the country?

example_sentences.japanese: 船は飛行機ほど速くないが、それでも船旅を好む人は多いといえるだろう。
example_sentences.english: Boats are not as fast as planes are, but it is still fair to say that a lot of people enjoy trips by boat.

example_sentences.japanese: 発明家は、「変人」という評価を一般の人から下されてきたといえるだろう。
example_sentences.english: You can probably say that the inventors were labeled as 'eccentrics' by the common folk.

example_sentences.japanese: ２０世紀にはコンピュータによって生活しやすくなってきたといえるだろう。
example_sentences.english: It is fair to say that life is getting easier due to (the advent of) computers in the 20th century.

example_sentences.japanese: このマニフェストは自然環境の現在の状態についてのひとつの意見だといえるだろう。
example_sentences.english: One could say that this manifesto is one of the opinions about the current state of the natural environment.

example_sentences.japanese: 古い中国語の発音が、現在の日本語に大きく影響しているといえるだろう。
example_sentences.english: You can probably say that the influence of ancient Chinese pronunciation on modern Japanese is vast.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は独自の文化で国際的に有名だといえるだろう。
example_sentences.english: It is fair to say that Japan is internationally famous for its unique culture.

example_sentences.japanese: スマホやタブレットのために子供がいなくなった遊び場は時代の象徴だといえるだろう。
example_sentences.english: You could say that, due to smartphones and tablets, empty playgrounds are a sign of our times.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の長所は働き者であることだといえるだろう。
example_sentences.english: One could probably say that her strong point is being a hard worker.

example_sentences.japanese: 私に言わせれば、彼はポーランドのスティーブン・スピルバーグのような人だったといえるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: If you ask me, I would probably say that he was something like a Polish Steven Spielberg.

example_sentences.japanese: 話している最中に割り込むのは、明らかに失礼だといえるだろう。
example_sentences.english: It is fair to say that interrupting someone when they are in the middle of talking is clearly rude.

example_sentences.japanese: 前会計年度に比べて、今年度は成功だといえるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Compared to the previous fiscal year, it is fair to say that this year is a success.

example_sentences.japanese: 人が話しているときに、携帯を見るのは失礼だといえよう。
example_sentences.english: Let it be said that looking at your phone while someone is talking to you is rude. (Anyone would say this, so don't make me say it to you)

general_translation: Properly, Neatly, Orderly, Sufficiently, Decently
formation: ちゃんと(1) + Phraseちゃんと(1) + した + Nounちゃんと(1) + している(1) きちんと
casual_structure: ちゃんと(1) + Phraseちゃんと(1) + した + Nounちゃんと(1) + している(1) きちんと
explanation: A word highlighting that (A) was done properly, neatly, or in the most correct manner.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻：「ガスをちゃんと閉めたか、わからない。」夫：「心配しないで、僕がちゃんと閉めたよ。」
example_sentences.english: Wife: 'I don't know if I have properly turned the gas off (or not).'Husband: 'Don't worry, I have properly turned it off.'

example_sentences.japanese: ちゃんと宿題した？
example_sentences.english: Did you properly do your homework?

example_sentences.japanese: ちゃんと野菜も食べなさい！
example_sentences.english: Properly eat your vegetables too!

example_sentences.japanese: 今度からはもっとちゃんとした車を買おう。
example_sentences.english: From now on, I should buy a proper car. (From now on, I'm not going to cheap out on a car)

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚式にはきちんとした服装で来てください。
example_sentences.english: Please come to the wedding dressed properly.

example_sentences.japanese: 優しい次長：「昼休みなんだからちゃんと休んでね。」部下：「はい! わかりました、次長！」
example_sentences.english: Gentle vice-director: 'It's lunch, so take a proper break.'Subordinate: 'Yes! Understood, vice-director!'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「悪いことをしたならちゃんと謝るものだ！」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'If you have done something wrong, you are supposed to apologize properly!'

example_sentences.japanese: 母親は子供に言う：「お祖母さんが来る前に部屋をきちんと片付けしなさい！」
example_sentences.english: Mother speaking to her child: 'Clean your room properly before grandma comes!'

example_sentences.japanese: 大人との話、子供を褒める：「あの子は、ちゃんとしてるわね。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between adults, praising a child: 'This child behaves properly, don't they.' (has good manners)

example_sentences.japanese: 親が子供に聞く：「ちゃんと宿題したの？」
example_sentences.english: A parent is asking a child: 'Have you properly done your homework?'

example_sentences.japanese: アルバイトの面接：「独りで暮らせるように、何かちゃんとした仕事を見つけたいのです。」
example_sentences.english: Part-time job interview: 'I want to find a proper job so that I can live by myself.' (decent)

example_sentences.japanese: 書き方について教師が学生に言う：「この言葉読みにくいね。もっときちんと書きましょう。」
example_sentences.english: A teacher speaks to a student about the way of writing: 'This word is hard to read. Let's write it more neatly (properly).'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「ちゃんと朝ごはん食べたの？元気がなさそうだね。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'Did you sufficiently eat breakfast? You don't look so good.' (properly)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女が彼氏に頼む：「ベッドをきちんとしておいてくれる？今ちょっと忙しいから。」
example_sentences.english: A girlfriend asking her boyfriend: 'Could you neatly make the bed? Since I'm a bit busy.' (properly)

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩が後輩にアドバイスする：「あしたの就職の面接にはきちんとした服を着ていった方がいいよ。」
example_sentences.english: A senpai giving advice to a kouhai: 'You should wear proper clothes for tomorrow's job interview.'

example_sentences.japanese: 武道会、アナウンサー：「【水球炭酸拳】の松本対【降竜拳】の西山、決勝です！」観客の一人：「水球炭酸拳って本当にちゃんとした武道なのか？」
example_sentences.english: Martial arts tournament, announcer: 'It is the final fight of the tournament, between Matsumoto of 'Water Polo carbonated fist' and Nishiyama of 'Descending dragon fist!'Member of the audience: 'Water polo carbonated fist' is that even a proper martial art?'

example_sentences.japanese: 社長が来たぞ。ちゃんと立て。
example_sentences.english: The CEO is here. Stand up, quick! (Stand up now, quickly, don't slouch)

example_sentences.japanese: 遊びに行く前にきちんと部屋の掃除をしなさい。
example_sentences.english: You have to clean your room properly before you go out and play.

general_translation: For that reason, Because of that, To that end
formation: そのため + (に)  + Phrase
casual_structure: そのため + (に)  + Phrase
explanation: A structure that indicates that in order to get to that (A), or because of that (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: ５人の家族を養う。そのために僕は働く。
example_sentences.english: I support a family of 5. For that reason I work. (for the sake of that)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では高齢化が進んでいる。そのため、子供が生まれたら政府からお金がもらえる。
example_sentences.english: Japan's population continues to age. For that reason, when a child is born, you receive money from the government.

example_sentences.japanese: ハマダさんはとても釣りが好きです。そのため毎朝仕事に行く前に、釣りに行っています。
example_sentences.english: Hamada-san loves fishing. For that reason, he does it every morning before he goes to work.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜遅くまで仕事をした。そのため寝坊してしまった。
example_sentences.english: I worked until late. Because of that I overslept. (for the sake of that)

example_sentences.japanese: 会社が倒産した。そのために失業した。
example_sentences.english: The company went bankrupt. Because of that I lost my job. (for the sake of that)

example_sentences.japanese: 私は鉄道オタクです。いろんな電車の写真を撮るのですが、そのために徹夜することもあります。
example_sentences.english: I am a railway 'enthusiast'. I take pictures of a variety of trains, because of that I sometimes pull all-nighters. (for the sake of that)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の夢を実現させたい。そのためにできるだけのことはしたいと思っている。
example_sentences.english: I will make her dream a reality. For that reason I want to do all I can (to help). (for the sake of that)

example_sentences.japanese: レポートの提出期限が迫っています。そのためしばらくは遊べません。
example_sentences.english: I am pressed for time in submitting my report. For that reason I will not be able to go out for a while. (for the sake of that)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語教師になりたいです。そのために頑張って勉強しています。
example_sentences.english: I want to become a Japanese language instructor. For that reason I am studying hard. (for the sake of that)

example_sentences.japanese: 調子が悪いのに飛行機に乗った。そのため飛行の最中に気分が悪くなってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Even though I was not feeling well, I boarded the plane. Because of that, I got sick mid-flight. (for the sake of that)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が突然やめると言い出した。そのため計画がパーになった。
example_sentences.english: He suddenly said that he wanted to quit. For that reason we had to abandon the plan. (for the sake of that)

example_sentences.japanese: 食べたかったけど明日は健康診断がある。そのために我慢している。
example_sentences.english: I wanted to eat, but I have a medical check up tomorrow. For that reason I am putting up with it (the hunger). (for the sake of that)

example_sentences.japanese: 私は自転車で通学しています。そのため、雨が降ると大変なのです。
example_sentences.english: I commute to school by bike. For that reason, it is a pain when it rains. (for the sake of that)

example_sentences.japanese: 長年の夢だった世界一周旅行に行ってきます。そのため、しばらく連絡が取りにくいかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: I am taking a trip around the world, a long awaited dream. For that reason I might have difficulty keeping in touch for some time. (for the sake of that)

example_sentences.japanese: 子供達にはなんの不自由もない生活をしてほしい。そのために毎日夜遅くまで仕事をしている。
example_sentences.english: I want my kids to have a life without any struggles. For the sake of that, I work until late at night every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい車が欲しいけど今は住宅ローンで精一杯。そのために車を買うのを我慢している。
example_sentences.english: I want a new car, but I am struggling to pay my mortgage. For that reason, I am holding off on doing it.

general_translation: As a result
formation: Phrase。その結果（けっか） + Phrase
casual_structure: Phrase。その結果（けっか） + Phrase
explanation: A grammar point which highlights something that is a result of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 夜更かしをした。そのけっか、遅刻した。
example_sentences.english: I stayed up till late. As a result, I was late.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校を３ヶ月休んだ。そのけっか、皆と卒業することができなかった。
example_sentences.english: I took three months off from school. As a result, I was not able to graduate with everyone.

example_sentences.japanese: 日焼け止めを塗らずにビーチで一日過ごした。そのけっか凄く日焼けをして、しばらくシャワーに入るのが辛かった。
example_sentences.english: I spent the whole day at the beach without sunscreen. As a result, I got a bad sunburn and it was painful to take a shower for a while.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日朝早くから夜遅くまで練習した。そのけっか、試合で優勝することができた。
example_sentences.english: We practiced every day from early in the morning to late at night. As a result, we were able to win the tournament.

example_sentences.japanese: タナカ君は一年間運動をしないでゲームばっかりしていた。そのけっか２０キロも太った。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka-kun only played video games without exercising for a year. As a result, he gained 20 kilograms.

example_sentences.japanese: 無理をして走った。そのけっか足がつった。
example_sentences.english: I overdid it running. As a result, I got a leg cramp.

example_sentences.japanese: 値上げをした。そのけっか、売り上げが下がってしまった。
example_sentences.english: The price increased. As a result, sales decreased.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の分も買ってきてあげた。そのけっか褒められた。
example_sentences.english: I got one for him too. As a result, I was praised.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動をやめてしまった。そのけっか、五キロも太った。
example_sentences.english: I gave up on exercising. As a result, I gained 5 kilos.

example_sentences.japanese: 仮想通貨にはまった。そのけっか大損した。
example_sentences.english: I got into virtual currency trading. As a result, I lost a lot.

example_sentences.japanese: 高校の頃、五ヶ月間入院をした。そのけっか、留年することになった。
example_sentences.english: During my high school days, I was hospitalized for 5 months. As a result, I ended up repeating a year.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、髪の毛が濡れたままで寝た。そのけっか、風邪を引いた。
example_sentences.english: Last night I went to bed with wet hair. As a result I caught a cold.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語能力試験を受けるまでに彼は毎週日本語の小説を２冊読んだ。そのけっか、読解で満点を取った。
example_sentences.english: Before taking the JLPT, he read two Japanese novels a week. As a result, he got full marks on the reading section.

example_sentences.japanese: クーラーを消し忘れて旅行に行った。そのけっか、電気代がものすごいことになった。
example_sentences.english: I forgot to turn off the air conditioner and went on a trip. As a result, the electricity bill was tremendous.

example_sentences.japanese: 入念に調査をした。そのけっか、大きな問題点が二つあることが分かった。
example_sentences.english: I was very careful in my investigation. As a result, I found two major issues.

example_sentences.japanese: ２ヶ月間ずっと体を鍛え続けていた。そのけっか、筋肉が増えた。
example_sentences.english: I continuously trained for a solid two months. As a result I gained muscle.

general_translation: Compared to, When compared to
formation: Noun + に比（くら）べ（て）(1)(1) に比（くら）べたら、に比（くら）べれば、に比（くら）べると
casual_structure: Noun + に比（くら）べ（て）(1)(1) に比（くら）べたら、に比（くら）べれば、に比（くら）べると
explanation: A grammar point used to make direct comparisons or contrasts between (A) and (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 野球にくらべたら、サッカーの方が好きだ。
example_sentences.english: When compared with baseball, I like soccer more.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京の冬は北海道の冬にくらべて全然寒くない。
example_sentences.english: Tokyo's winter is not cold at all compared to Hokkaido.

example_sentences.japanese: 去年にくらべて今年の冬は暖かい。
example_sentences.english: Compared to last year, this year's winter is warm.

example_sentences.japanese: 大阪の人口は東京の人口にくらべて小さい。
example_sentences.english: Osaka's population is smaller compared to Tokyo.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼も真面目だけど、君は彼にくらべるともっと真面目だ。
example_sentences.english: He is serious too, but you are more serious compared to him.

example_sentences.japanese: 君は彼とくらべて真面目だ。
example_sentences.english: Compared to him, you are serious. (You are serious, while he has other qualities)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本はアメリカとくらべて小さい。
example_sentences.english: Compared to America, Japan is small. (Japan is small, compared to America, which is big, among other things)

example_sentences.japanese: 一学期にくらべて成績がよくなった。
example_sentences.english: My grades have improved compared to first semester.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日にくらべたら今日は暖かい。
example_sentences.english: Compared to yesterday, today is warmer.

example_sentences.japanese: 去年にくらべて今年は雪が多い。
example_sentences.english: There is more snow this year compared to last year.

example_sentences.japanese: 昔にくらべると、今の人は長生きだ。
example_sentences.english: People live longer nowadays compared to those in the past.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩にくらべたら、僕はまだまだ日本語が下手だ。
example_sentences.english: Compared to my superior, I am still poor at Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 以前の家にくらべたら、今の家は快適だ。
example_sentences.english: Compared to our last house, the house we have now is more liveable.

example_sentences.japanese: マニュアル車にくらべたら、オートマの方が運転が楽だ。
example_sentences.english: Compared to manuals, automatic cars are easier to drive.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカにくらべたら、日本の方が安全だと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think that when compared to America, Japan is the safer of the two.

example_sentences.japanese: 他の痛さにくらべて、頭痛は一番辛い。
example_sentences.english: When compared to other types of pain, headaches are the worst.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏にくらべて、ずいぶん涼しくなったが、まだまだ暑い。
example_sentences.english: Compared to summer it is quite cool, but it's still hot.

example_sentences.japanese: 高級肉にくらべると少し味は落ちるが、この肉も十分美味しい。
example_sentences.english: When you compare this meat with expensive meat, it is not as good. However, it is still quite delicious.

example_sentences.japanese: 他の地域に比べたら、この地域は住みやすい。
example_sentences.english: Compared to other areas, this area is very easy to live in.

example_sentences.japanese: 去年に比べれば今年は寒いけど、昨日に比べたら今日は暖かい。
example_sentences.english: If compared to last year, it is colder this year. However if we compare it to yesterday, it is warm today.

example_sentences.japanese: 新型のパソコンに比べるとこのパソコンは遅く感じるけど、そんなに遅くない。
example_sentences.english: If we compare this computer to a new model, it feels slow, but it's not that slow.

general_translation: No matter how
formation: どんな + （に） + Verb［ても］どんな + （に） + ［い］Adjective［ても］どんな + （に） + ［な］Adjective + でもどんな + （に） + Noun + でも
casual_structure: どんな + （に） + Verb［ても］どんな + （に） + ［い］Adjective［ても］どんな + （に） + ［な］Adjective + でもどんな + （に） + Noun + でも
explanation: A grammar point that highlights that no matter how much (A), the result cannot be avoided.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなにがんばっても無理だと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think that it is impossible no matter how hard I try.

example_sentences.japanese: 今はお金が無いからどんなに伊豆に行きたくても行けないんだよ。
example_sentences.english: Right now I have no money, so no matter how much I want to go to Izu, I can't.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩の話しがどんなにつまらなくてもあくびをしてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how boring your senpai's stories are, you should not yawn.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の運転がどんなに上手でもシートベルトはしなくてはならない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how good you are at driving, you must wear a seatbelt.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなにお金持ちでも、働かないとお金が無くなっていく。
example_sentences.english: No matter how rich you are, if you don't work, money will just continue to disappear.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに笑われても、前に進もう。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much they laugh at us, let's keep pushing forward.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに勉強しても、合格できないと思う。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much I study, I don't think that I can pass.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに暇でも、掃除するつもりはない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how bored I am, I won't even think about cleaning.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに苦しくても、僕はぜったいにあきらめない。
example_sentences.english: I will never give up no matter how hard it is.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに忠告しても、あの人は聞いてくれないだろう。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much I warn her, she won't listen to me.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに悲しくても、彼は人前で泣いたりしない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how sad he is, he won't do something like crying in front of people.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに辛くても、現実を受け入れなくちゃ。
example_sentences.english: No matter how hard it is, you have to accept reality.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなにリンゴが嫌いでも、それでも時々リンゴを食べてしまうことがある。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much I hate apples, I still eat them occasionally.

example_sentences.japanese: どんな困難でも、君と一緒なら乗り越えられると思っている。
example_sentences.english: I think we can work through anything together, no matter the hardship.

example_sentences.japanese: 性格が悪いから、どんなにハンサムでも、彼みたいになりたくない。
example_sentences.english: He is not a good person, so no matter how handsome he is, I don't want to be like him.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに綺麗でも何百万円もかかる絵は買いません。
example_sentences.english: No matter how beautiful it is, I won't buy a painting that costs millions of yen.

general_translation: No matter how (much)
formation: いくら + Verb［ても］いくら + ［い］Adjective［ても］いくら + Noun + でもいくら + ［な］Adjective + でも
casual_structure: いくら + Verb［ても］いくら + ［い］Adjective［ても］いくら + Noun + でもいくら + ［な］Adjective + でも
explanation: A phrase that highlights that no matter what number of (A), the result will not change.

example_sentences.japanese: いくらいそいでも土曜日までには終わらない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how quickly I do it, I won't finish before Saturday.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人にいくら言っても、何も変わらないよ。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much you tell him, he won't change.

example_sentences.japanese: いくら新しくても落としたら壊れるに決まってるじゃん。
example_sentences.english: No matter how new it is, of course it is going to break if you drop it!

example_sentences.japanese: あの人のことがいくら嫌いでも、そんな事言ったら可哀そうだよ。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much you dislike them, that is a hurtful thing to say.

example_sentences.japanese: いくら俺でもそんな重いものは持てないよ。
example_sentences.english: No matter if it is me, I can't lift something that heavy. (Even if it is me, who is strong, I cant lift something that heavy)

example_sentences.japanese: 相談ならいくらでも聞いてあげるよ。
example_sentences.english: I'll listen to you vent however much you need.

example_sentences.japanese: お菓子ならいくらでもあるから、好きなだけ持っていきな！
example_sentences.english: As for snacks, I have plenty, so take all you want!

example_sentences.japanese: いくらないても、泣き止まない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much they cry, they won't cry themselves out.

example_sentences.japanese: 文プロを見つけるまでいくら文法を勉強しても、理解ができなかった。
example_sentences.english: Before finding Bunpro, no matter how much I studied grammar I couldn't understand it.

example_sentences.japanese: いくらお金があっても、愛は買えない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much money you have, you can't buy love.

example_sentences.japanese: いくらがんばっても、彼にはかなわない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how hard I try, I can't compete with him.

example_sentences.japanese: いくらご飯を食べても、あの人は全然お腹いっぱいにならない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much he (she) eats, he (she) doesn't get full at all.

example_sentences.japanese: いくらかせいでも、妻がすぐに使ってしまうから困っている。
example_sentences.english: I am having trouble because no matter how much I earn, my wife spends it all.

example_sentences.japanese: いくらしんせつにしても、あの人は全然感謝しない人だ。
example_sentences.english: No matter how nice I am to him (her), he (she) is a completely ungrateful person.

example_sentences.japanese: いくら社長でも、あんな言い方をしてはいけません。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much of a boss you are, you cannot speak in that manner.

example_sentences.japanese: いくらかわいくても、孫になんでも買ってあげるのは良くないですよ。
example_sentences.english: No matter how cute your grandchildren are, it's not good to buy them whatever they want.

example_sentences.japanese: いくら優秀でも、性格が悪い人とは一緒に仕事をしたくありません。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to work with someone who is mean, no matter how amazing they may be.

example_sentences.japanese: いくらちゅうこくしても、彼は考えを変える気がないらしい。
example_sentences.english: No matter how much advice you give him, he doesn't seem to want to change his mind.

example_sentences.japanese: お金はいくら払ってもいいのでその靴を私に下さい。
example_sentences.english: I will pay however much for those shoes, so please let me have them! (Amount only)

example_sentences.japanese: お金はどんなに払ってもいいのでその靴を私に下さい。
example_sentences.english: I will pay whatever sort of money for those shoes, so please let me have them! (Possible amount or type. Dollar, yen, euro, etc)

grammar_point: かは〜によって違（ちが）う
general_translation: Depends on, Changes depending on, Differ depending on
formation: Phrase + かどうか + Noun + によって違（ちが）う(1)WH-Word + A(2) + かは + Noun + によって違（ちが）う(1)A(2)か + B(2)かは + Noun + によって違（ちが）う(1)(1) による(2) ［い］Adjective、［な］Adjective、Verb、Noun
casual_structure: Phrase + かどうか + Noun + によって違（ちが）う(1)WH-Word + A(2) + かは + Noun + によって違（ちが）う(1)A(2)か + B(2)かは + Noun + によって違（ちが）う(1)(1) による(2) ［い］Adjective、［な］Adjective、Verb、Noun
polite_structure: Phrase + かどうか + Noun + によって違（ちが）います(1)WH-Word + A(2) + かは + Noun + によって違（ちが）います(1)A(2)か + B(2)かは + Noun + によって違（ちが）います(1)(1) によります(2) ［い］Adjective、［な］Adjective、Verb、Noun
explanation: A phrase indicating that the general uncertain result of (A) will differ or change depending on (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 音楽が好きか嫌いかは人それぞれによってちがう。
example_sentences.english: It depends on the person, whether they like music or not.

example_sentences.japanese: 川の流れが早いか遅いかは場所によってちがう。
example_sentences.english: Whether the river flows fast or slow depends on the location.

example_sentences.japanese: 銃を簡単に買えるかどうかは国によってちがう。
example_sentences.english: Whether you can easily buy a gun or not depends on the country.

example_sentences.japanese: この技が凄いかどうかは見る人によってちがう。
example_sentences.english: Whether this trick is amazing or not depends on who judges.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本が好きか嫌いかは人によってちがう。
example_sentences.english: Whether they like Japan or not depends on the person.

example_sentences.japanese: お酒を飲んで肌が赤くなるかならないかは体質によってちがう。
example_sentences.english: Whether someone's skin will turn red or not after drinking depends on the person.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日、早く帰れるか帰れないかは仕事の進み具合による。
example_sentences.english: Whether I can go home early or not today will depend on how work goes.

example_sentences.japanese: 納豆を食べられるか食べられないかは人の好みによる。
example_sentences.english: Whether or not a person can eat natto will depend on what they like.

example_sentences.japanese: 果物が高いかどうかは季節によってちがう。
example_sentences.english: Whether fruit is expensive or not changes depending on the season.

example_sentences.japanese: 何が良いかは各人の主観によってちがう。
example_sentences.english: Whether something is good or not depends on each person's personal opinion.

example_sentences.japanese: 海が深いかどうかは場所によってちがうでしょうね。
example_sentences.english: Whether the sea is deep or not differs depending on location, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 何歳で退職できるかは国によってちがう。
example_sentences.english: The age at which one can retire differs depending on the country.

example_sentences.japanese: 入学試験がやさしいか難しいかは学校による。
example_sentences.english: Whether an entrance exam is easy or hard depends on the school.

example_sentences.japanese: 人生に何を求めるかは人による。
example_sentences.english: What one is looking for in life depends on the person.

example_sentences.japanese: スマホの消費電力がどのくらいかはアプリやモデルによってちがうようだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems that the amount of power a smartphone consumes differs depending on the model of phone and the apps that it runs.

example_sentences.japanese: ジョークが面白いかどうかは人によってちがうから相手を傷つける時もある。
example_sentences.english: Whether a joke is funny or not differs depending on the person, so there are also times when you can hurt someone's feelings.

example_sentences.japanese: 割引が適用されるかどうかは商品によってちがう。
example_sentences.english: Whether the discount can be applied or not differs depending on the product.

example_sentences.japanese: 制服があるかないかは学校によりますが、ほとんどの場合、制服があることが普通らしいです。
example_sentences.english: Whether there are school uniforms or not differs depending on the school, but they are pretty ordinary.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べ物が美味しいかまずいかは国によってちがうよ。納豆やピータンがあったりするでしょ。
example_sentences.english: Whether the food is tasty or not differs depending on the country. There are things like natto or century eggs too, right?

general_translation: Quite, Considerably, Pretty, Fairly
formation: かなり + Phraseかなり + の + Noun
casual_structure: かなり + Phraseかなり + の + Noun
explanation: A word showing that (A) is something that is above average in either quantity or quality, but not by a large amount.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話、地図を見て：「ここはかなり遠くの方だね。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends, after looking at the map: 'This place is quite far away, isn't it?'

example_sentences.japanese: 今月もかなりお金を使ったね。
example_sentences.english: This month we used a considerable amount of money again, didn't we?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は一日中仕事をしていたからかなり疲れた。
example_sentences.english: Because I was working all day today, I am pretty tired.

example_sentences.japanese: メキシコまではかなりの距離があるから、船で行くより飛行機で行った方が早くつく。
example_sentences.english: Since there is a considerable distance to Mexico, you will get there quicker if you go by airplane, rather than by boat.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の事故でかなりの人が怪我をした。
example_sentences.english: Quite a lot of people got hurt in the accident yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社の社長：「新しいシステムを導入しよう。」社員：「わかりました。でも、かなり費用がかかりそうですよ。」
example_sentences.english: Company president: 'Let's adopt the new system.'Company employee: 'Understood. However, it seems to be quite expensive.'

example_sentences.japanese: 配送会社、労働者１：「じゃあ、はやくこれ、(トラックに）積んでしまおう。」労働者２：「でもこれ、かなり重いんだけど。」
example_sentences.english: Transport company, worker 1: 'Well then, let's quickly load it on the truck.'Worker 2: 'But it is quite heavy…'

example_sentences.japanese: 文法ちゃん：「ユーザーさんの日本語は、かなり上級レベルだと思う。」
example_sentences.english: Bunpou-chan: 'I think that User-san's Japanese is of quite a high level.'

example_sentences.japanese: 従業員の噂話：「次長は、家ではお孫さんに優しいおじいちゃんらしいよ。そんな風に見えないけどね。会社ではかなり厳しい人だから。」
example_sentences.english: Employees gossiping: 'I heard that the vice-director is a gentle grandpa who is sweet to his grandchild at home. He doesn't look like that though, right? Because he is fairly strict at the company.'

example_sentences.japanese: 日本人の友達：「ポーランドといえば、キュリー夫人を思い出す日本人は、かなり多いだろう。」
example_sentences.english: Japanese friend: 'Speaking of Poland, I guess there are quite a few Japanese people who remember Madam Curie.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話、誰かを褒める：「彼のスペイン語は、かなりの腕前だ。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends, praising someone: 'His Spanish is quite skillful.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「かなり節約したつもりが、もうお金がなくなってしまった。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'My intent was to be quite economical, but my money is already gone.'

example_sentences.japanese: 教科書：「日本の地域によっては、方言はかなり異なります。」
example_sentences.english: Textbook: 'Depending on the region of Japan, the dialect differs considerably.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話、ひなさん：「黒木さんはほかのだれよりかなり忘れられない存在だよね。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends, Hina: 'More than anyone else, Kuroki-san is quite an unforgettable figure.'

example_sentences.japanese: ツイート：「今日はかなり強いコーヒーを飲んだから、今晩は眠れなさそうだ。」
example_sentences.english: Tweet: 'I drank some pretty strong coffee today, so I don't think I'll be able to sleep tonight.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「明日はかなりの確率で雨みたいだから、外に出ないで家にいることにしようかな。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'It looks like it's quite likely to rain tomorrow, so I'll probably stay home the whole day.'

example_sentences.japanese: 初めて作ったの？かなり美味しいよ！
example_sentences.english: You made it for the first time? It's pretty good!

example_sentences.japanese: かなり痛いです。骨が折れていると思いますか？
example_sentences.english: It's quite painful. Do you think a bone is broken?

general_translation: So much...that, (Way) too...
formation: あまり(1) + に (2)+ Adjectiveあまり(1) + に(2) + Adverbあまり(1) + の + Noun(1) あんまり (2) にも
casual_structure: あまり(1) + に (2)+ Adjectiveあまり(1) + に(2) + Adverbあまり(1) + の + Noun(1) あんまり (2) にも
explanation: A structure that expresses an excessive amount of (A) that led to (B).

example_sentences.japanese: あまりに早く着いてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I unfortunately arrived too early.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の仕事はあまりに楽過ぎて仕事をした感じがしない。
example_sentences.english: Work today was so easy that I don't feel like I worked at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝は会社にあまりに遅く着いたため、先輩に怒られた。
example_sentences.english: This morning, I got to the company so late that I was yelled at by my senpai.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はあまりの恐怖に、声をあげて叫んだ。
example_sentences.english: She was so scared that she screamed out loud.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の話しがあまりにもつまらなくて途中からほとんど聞いてなかった。
example_sentences.english: My friend's story was so boring that I stopped paying attention halfway.

example_sentences.japanese: そのケーキはあまりに大きすぎて、食べられない。
example_sentences.english: That cake is too big to eat.

example_sentences.japanese: あまりに寒すぎて、帰ってきてしまった。
example_sentences.english: It was too cold, so I turned back.

example_sentences.japanese: その計画はあまりに非現実的だよ。
example_sentences.english: That plan is too unrealistic!

example_sentences.japanese: あまりに仕事が多すぎて、手に負えない。
example_sentences.english: I have too much work to deal with.

example_sentences.japanese: その言い訳はあまりにも幼稚すぎる。
example_sentences.english: That excuse is way too childish.

example_sentences.japanese: 冬の間、あまりにも高すぎて、野菜が買えない。
example_sentences.english: Vegetables are way too expensive to buy during the winter.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人はあまりに歩くのが速いから、ついていけない。
example_sentences.english: Since he/she walks far too fast, I cannot keep up with him/her.

example_sentences.japanese: あまりに丁寧な言葉遣いというのも、違和感がある。
example_sentences.english: Also using phrases that are too polite feels awkward.

example_sentences.japanese: インフルエンザであまりに多くの社員が休んだから、仕事にならない。
example_sentences.english: We can't get anything done because too many coworkers are out due to the flu.

example_sentences.japanese: あまりに失礼じゃないか。いつも助けてあげているのに。
example_sentences.english: Aren't you being way too rude? To think that I am always helping you out.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らはあまりに忙しそうにみえたから、声をかけるのをやめた。
example_sentences.english: They looked far too busy, so I decided to not talk to them.

example_sentences.japanese: トマトはあんまり好きじゃない。
example_sentences.english: I don't like tomatoes too much.

example_sentences.japanese: この映画はあんまりおもしろくなかったね。
example_sentences.english: This movie wasn't excessively interesting.

general_translation: For that reason, No wonder, As you'd expect, Naturally, Thus, This is why
formation: Verb + (という) + わけだ［い］Adjective + (という) + わけだ［な］Adjective + な(1) + わけだNoun + の(1) + わけだ(1) という
casual_structure: Verb + (という) + わけだ［い］Adjective + (という) + わけだ［な］Adjective + な(1) + わけだNoun + の(1) + わけだ(1) という
polite_structure: Verb + (という) + わけ + です［い］Adjective + (という) + わけ + です［な］Adjective + な(1) + わけ + ですNoun + の(1) + わけ + です(1) という
explanation: A phrase that strongly presents a logical reason or cause for why (A) is so.

example_sentences.japanese: 雪が降っていた。寒いわけだ。
example_sentences.english: It snowed, so as you'd expect, it's cold.

example_sentences.japanese: 事故で電車が遅れたの？だから珍しく遅れて来たというわけだ。
example_sentences.english: The train was late due to an accident? So that's why you came in unusually late.

example_sentences.japanese: 指の骨が折れていたのですね。だから指を動かしたら痛かったというわけですね。
example_sentences.english: You are saying that my finger was broken? So that's why my finger hurt when I moved it.

example_sentences.japanese: やっぱり全然練習してないでしょ？どうりで一年たっても下手なわけだ。
example_sentences.english: As I expected, you didn't practice at all, did you? No wonder you haven't improved even after a year.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は休日か。だから定休日のわけだ。
example_sentences.english: Today is a holiday, isn't it? So that's why they are closed today.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺と一緒にいたくないわけだね？分かったよ。
example_sentences.english: So you are saying that you don't want to be with me, right? I understand.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩たちは後から来るというわけですか？
example_sentences.english: Senpai, so will you be coming later?

example_sentences.japanese: また忘れたの？それで先生に叱られたわけだ。
example_sentences.english: You forgot again? No wonder you were scolded by the teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜更かししてばかりいるの？それじゃあ遅刻するわけだ。
example_sentences.english: Why do you keep staying up late? No wonder you are always late.

example_sentences.japanese: お金を無駄に使っている。貯金がないわけです。
example_sentences.english: You waste your money. No wonder you have no savings.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は医者になりたいから、医学の勉強をするわけだ。
example_sentences.english: Since she wants to be a doctor, this is why she is studying in the medical field.(as you'd expect)

example_sentences.japanese: 道理でうまくいかなかったわけだ。前提がずっと間違っていたのだから。
example_sentences.english: No wonder it didn't turn out well. The premise was wrong all along.

example_sentences.japanese: 人一倍努力している。彼は成功するわけだ。
example_sentences.english: He works twice as hard as others. This is why, he is successful.(as you'd expect)

example_sentences.japanese: 違う人にメールを送っていた。どうりで知らないわけだ。
example_sentences.english: I had sent the email to the wrong person. No wonder you don't know what is going on.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなに高級な素材を使っているの？どうりで高いわけだ。
example_sentences.english: You are using these high-grade materials? No wonder it is expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: みんな態度が悪すぎる。先生もお手上げだったわけだ。
example_sentences.english: Everyone has a terrible attitude. No wonder the teacher gave up.

example_sentences.japanese: 道に迷ったの？それで君は交番に行ったというわけだ。
example_sentences.english: You got lost? Ah, that's why you went to the police station.

example_sentences.japanese: 怒られるのが嫌だから、失敗を隠したってわけだ。
example_sentences.english: No wonder that you hid your failure, since you didn't want to get in trouble.

general_translation: It doesn't mean that, It is not the case, It's not like
formation: Verb + わけではない(1)［い］Adjective + わけではない(1)［な］Adjective + な + わけではない(1)Noun + の(2) + わけではない(1)(1)わけじゃない(2) である
casual_structure: Verb + わけではない(1)［い］Adjective + わけではない(1)［な］Adjective + な + わけではない(1)Noun + の(2) + わけではない(1)(1)わけじゃない(2) である
polite_structure: Verb + わけではありません(1)［い］Adjective + わけではありません(1)［な］Adjective + な + わけではありません(1)Noun + の(2) + わけではない(1)(1)わけじゃありません(2) である
explanation: A grammar point used when (A) is not the case, or not necessarily so.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「北海道といえば、Ｃさんによれば一年中寒いらしい。」 Ｂ：「夏でも寒いわけではない。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Speaking of Hokkaido, according to C it is cold there all year long.' B: 'It doesn't mean it is cold even in summer.'

example_sentences.japanese: 私の家は広いわけではないけど、小さくもない。
example_sentences.english: It is not necessarily that my house is big, but it is not small either.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事が大変なわけではない。忙しいだけ。
example_sentences.english: It's not that my job is difficult, it's just busy.

example_sentences.japanese: 熱のわけではないけど、体がだるい。
example_sentences.english: It's not necessarily that I have a fever, but my body feels heavy.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に住んでいるから日本語を話せるわけではないです。私は日本に来る前に日本語の勉強をしていました。
example_sentences.english: It is not the case that I am able to speak Japanese because I live in Japan. I studied Japanese before I came.

example_sentences.japanese: あの監督は有名だけど、映画を監督して有名になったわけじゃない。
example_sentences.english: That director is famous, but he did not become popular because he directed a movie.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが悪かったって言っているわけじゃない。
example_sentences.english: It's not that I am saying that you were in the wrong. (I am not strictly saying that you were in the wrong)

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「天気予報によると明日は晴れるだろう。」 Ｂ：「雨が降らないわけではない。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'The weather forecast calls for clear skies tomorrow.' B: 'It doesn't mean it won't rain.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「また試合に負けたよ。もう我慢できない！泣いちゃいたい！」 Ｂ：「いつもうまくいくわけではない。失敗はつきものだ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I lost a match again! I can't stand it anymore! I want to cry!' B: 'It is not the case that things will always turn out well. Failures are an unavoidable part of life.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「あなたはデートを忘れていたわ！私は腹が立っているから話しかけないで！」 Ｂ：「遅くなってしまいましたが、忘れていたわけではありませんよ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'You forgot about our date! I am angry, so don't speak to me!' B: 'I may have been late, but that doesn't mean that I forgot.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「Ｂさんは、来年結婚するつもりということだね。」 Ｂ：「まだ決まったわけではないから、内密にお願いします。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'B, I heard you are going to get married next year.' B: 'It is not the case that it is set in stone, so please keep it a secret.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「それは嘘だと思う。」 Ｂ：「まったくの嘘っていうわけではないけど、怪しい情報だな。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I think it is a lie.' B: 'It is not the case that it is an absolute lie, but that information is suspicious.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「では、これから、僕は家の所有者ですね？この家を僕の自由にしていいんですよね？」 Ｂ：「何をしてもいいわけではないですよ。ちゃんとしたルールがあるんです。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'So, from now on I am the house owner, right? I can do whatever I like with it, right?' B: 'It doesn't mean that you can just do whatever you want. There are proper rules.'

example_sentences.japanese: 兄Ａ ：「Ｂくんは俺の古いスマホをもらいたいの？」弟 Ｂ：「必要なわけではないけど、もらえるのなら欲しい。」
example_sentences.english: Older brother, A: 'B, do you want to have my old phone?'  Younger brother, B: 'It is not like I need it, but I won't say no if you give it to me.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「たくさん勉強したのに、結局、試験には落ちた。」 Ｂ：「ただ、完全に落ちたわけではなくて、後日、追試をうけることができる。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Although I studied a lot, in the end I failed the exam.' B: 'But it does not mean that you failed it completely, plus you can retake it in the future.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「Ｃさんは日本に十年以上住んでる。日本語が上手だろうね。」 Ｂ：「日本に長い間住んでも、日本語を話せるわけではないよ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'C has been living in Japan for over ten years. His Japanese is probably amazing, right?' B: 'Even if he has lived in Japan for a long time it doesn't mean he can speak Japanese.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「Ｃのミスで、試合に負けたぞ。」 Ｂ：「Ｃが完全に悪いわけではないが、多少の責任があると思う。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Because of C's mistakes we lost the match!' B: 'It is not like C is completely at fault, but I think that C shares some of the responsibility.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「賞はただのペンだったよ。」Ｂ：「だけど、あのペンはどこでも買えるわけではない。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'The reward was just a pen!' B: 'Yeah, but it is not like you can just buy that pen anywhere.'

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの事が嫌いというわけではない。
example_sentences.english: It's not necessarily so that I dislike you. (But I sure don't love you)

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの事が嫌いというわけがない。
example_sentences.english: I so don't dislike you. (I don't dislike you at all)

general_translation: At the same time as, The instant, The moment, As well as
formation: Verb［る］  + と同時（どうじ）に［い］Adjective  + と同時（どうじ）に［な］Adjective + である + と同時（どうじ）にNoun + （である)  + と同時（どうじ）に
casual_structure: Verb［る］  + と同時（どうじ）に［い］Adjective  + と同時（どうじ）に［な］Adjective + である + と同時（どうじ）にNoun + （である)  + と同時（どうじ）に
explanation: An expression that points out when two or more events take place or coexist at the same time, or same moment.

example_sentences.japanese: 財布とどうじに免許証もなくしてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I lost my wallet and my driver's license at the same time.

example_sentences.japanese: サイレンが鳴ったとどうじに、犯人は逃げた。
example_sentences.english: As the siren went off, the criminal ran away.

example_sentences.japanese: この機械は便利であるとどうじに危険である為、気をつけて使用してください。
example_sentences.english: This machine is useful, but at the same time, it is very dangerous, so please use it with caution.

example_sentences.japanese: その人は博士であるとどうじに宇宙飛行士でもある。
example_sentences.english: That person is a scientist and also an astronaut.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の家は自宅とどうじにオフィスでもある。
example_sentences.english: My place is a house, and at the same time it is also my office.

example_sentences.japanese: 野菜とどうじに肉を鍋に入れてください。
example_sentences.english: Please throw the vegetables and meat into the pot.

example_sentences.japanese: カギとどうじに携帯をどこかに忘れてきた。
example_sentences.english: I lost my keys as well as my phone somewhere.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎朝日の出とどうじに起きる。
example_sentences.english: I wake up with the sunrise every day. (at the same time as)

example_sentences.japanese: 目覚めるとどうじに着替えて出かけた。
example_sentences.english: The moment I woke up, I got dressed and went out. (at the same time as)

example_sentences.japanese: 録画するとどうじにナレーションも入れてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to record the video and, at the same time, narrate.

example_sentences.japanese: 決断力とどうじに慎重さも必要だ。
example_sentences.english: Decisiveness as well as caution is necessary.

example_sentences.japanese: 演奏が始まるとどうじに、彼は眠ってしまった。
example_sentences.english: The moment the performance started, he fell asleep. (at the same time as)

example_sentences.japanese: 道を横断し終わるとどうじに、信号が赤に変わった。
example_sentences.english: The instant I crossed the street, the traffic light turned red. (at the same time as)

example_sentences.japanese: 引っ越すとどうじに髪型を変えてみようと思っています。
example_sentences.english: I am thinking about changing my hairstyle the instant I move. (at the same time as)

example_sentences.japanese: 代引きというのは、商品の受け渡しとどうじに支払うシステムのことです。
example_sentences.english: Cash-on-delivery refers to a system where you pay for goods at the same time you receive them.

example_sentences.japanese: 演技が終わるとどうじに、観客から拍手が起こった。
example_sentences.english: The audience erupted in applause the instant the show was over. (at the same time as)

example_sentences.japanese: 伝承によると、第４代サンドウィッチ伯爵はギャンブルをするとどうじに食事ができるサンドイッチを考案したという話だ。
example_sentences.english: According to folklore, the fourth Earl of Sandwich invented sandwiches in order to eat and gamble at the same time.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨が降り出すとどうじに、雷が鳴りだした。
example_sentences.english: The instant it began raining, thunder started rumbling. (at the same time as)

general_translation: Almost, Nearly, About to, On the verge of
formation: Verb［る］+ ところだったVerb［ない］+ ところだった
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ ところだったVerb［ない］+ ところだった
polite_structure: Verb［る］+ ところでしたVerb［ない］+ ところでした
explanation: A construction indicating the place or situation in which (A) was about to, or on the verge of happening.

example_sentences.japanese: もう少しで船からおちるところだった。
example_sentences.english: I nearly fell off the ship (had I been a little closer to the edge).

example_sentences.japanese: やばい、大事な書類を捨てるところだった。
example_sentences.english: Oh shoot, I was just about to throw away an important document.

example_sentences.japanese: 毒キノコを食べるところだったが、キノコに詳しい友達が止めてくれた。
example_sentences.english: I was about to eat a poisonous mushroom, but a friend that is very knowledgeable about mushrooms stopped me.

example_sentences.japanese: この電車に間に合ってよかった。もう少しで待ち合わせ時間に間に合わないところだった。
example_sentences.english: I am so glad that we made this train. I was about to be late for the meet up.

example_sentences.japanese: 現金が足りなくて家賃が払えないところだった。
example_sentences.english: I was about to not be able to pay my rent because I didn't have cash.

example_sentences.japanese: ちょうど電車が発車するところだった。
example_sentences.english: It was right when the train was about to depart.

example_sentences.japanese: 危うく遅刻するところだった。
example_sentences.english: I was on the verge of  being late.

example_sentences.japanese: もう少しで事故が起こるところだった。
example_sentences.english: I nearly had an accident.

example_sentences.japanese: 好きな声優に会えないところだった。
example_sentences.english: I almost didn't meet my favorite voice actress.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女に誤解されるところだった。
example_sentences.english: She was on the verge of misunderstanding me.

example_sentences.japanese: 今高速に乗るところだったのに...
example_sentences.english: Aw, I was just about to get on the highway....

example_sentences.japanese: 眠りに入るところだったのに、電話で起こされた。
example_sentences.english: I was just about to go to sleep, but was woken up by a phone call.

example_sentences.japanese: もう少しで遅刻するところだったが、ギリギリ間に合いました。
example_sentences.english: I was on the verge of being late, but I made it just in time.

example_sentences.japanese: 店は閉店するところだったが、売ってくれました。
example_sentences.english: The shop was just about to close, but they were kind enough to sell it to me.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車に傘を忘れるところだったが、隣の人が教えてくれた。
example_sentences.english: I was on the verge of forgetting my umbrella on the train, when the person next to me reminded me about it.

example_sentences.japanese: 発見が遅れたら、危うく死ぬところだった。
example_sentences.english: I would have been on the verge of dying had they not found me sooner.

general_translation: I heard/was said, Because, But, Even or also, Even if or even though
formation: Noun + （なん） + だってだって + Phrase
casual_structure: Noun + （なん） + だってだって + Phrase
explanation: A very casual expression used to give reasons, say but, or sometimes even to relay things heard from others.

example_sentences.japanese: 全員合格だってよ。
example_sentences.english: It is said that everyone had passed the exam.

example_sentences.japanese: え〜 行きたくないよ。だって、俺の元カノも誘ったんでしょう？
example_sentences.english: Awwww maaaan I don't want to go. It's because you also invited my ex-girlfriend, right?

example_sentences.japanese: だって、サメとか怖いもん。
example_sentences.english: It's because I'm afraid of things like sharks.

example_sentences.japanese: レムの実家は農家なんだって。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Rem's family owns a farm.

example_sentences.japanese: キリコは明日から一週間休みなんだって。
example_sentences.english: I hear that Kiriko will be on break for a week starting tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: だって、全然知らないんだもん。
example_sentences.english: Because, I have no idea.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼だって落ち込むこともあるよ。
example_sentences.english: Even he gets depressed from time to time.

example_sentences.japanese: 「たけしさん、海外旅行だって？」
example_sentences.english: 'Is it true (what I have heard) that Takeshi is on vacation abroad?'

example_sentences.japanese: 月にだって行けるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: You can probably even go to the moon.

example_sentences.japanese: 今から体育なんだって。
example_sentences.english: I heard that we have P.E. from now.

example_sentences.japanese: 父親だって、たまには一人でのんびりしたいときもある。
example_sentences.english: Even my father wants to occasionally relax by himself.

example_sentences.japanese: アイスクリームだって薬になる。食べ過ぎなければ。
example_sentences.english: Even ice cream, it can do you good. That is, if you don't eat too much.

example_sentences.japanese: めがねちゃん：「どうして遅れたの？」 ヤンキーくん：「だって、 家の手伝いをしなきゃいけなかったんだ。」
example_sentences.english: Megane-chan: 'Why are you late?' Yankee-kun: 'Because I had to help with house work.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「彼は競馬に行ったらしい。」「競馬だって？またお金を全部失うよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I heard that he has gone horse racing.' 'Horse racing you say? He will lose all his money again.'

example_sentences.japanese: それは恋だって。表情を見れば分かります。
example_sentences.english: Like they say, it is love. I can tell just from the look on your face.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達は出かけなかった。だって悪い天気だったから。
example_sentences.english: We didn't go out. Because the weather was bad.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺だって行きたくないよ。
example_sentences.english: Even I don't want to go.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなこと言ったら、誰だって傷つくよ。
example_sentences.english: If you say something like that, anyone would get hurt.

general_translation: I heard that, He or She said that
formation: Verb + んだって［い］Adjective + んだって［な］Adjective + な + んだってNoun + な + んだって
casual_structure: Verb + んだって［い］Adjective + んだって［な］Adjective + な + んだってNoun + な + んだって
explanation: A very casual way to quote something that has been said.

example_sentences.japanese: トムは、また元カノと付き合っているんだって。
