example_sentences.english: (Someone) said that Tom is back with his ex-girlfriend.

example_sentences.japanese: サクラちゃん来年結婚するんだって。うらやましいね。
example_sentences.english: I heard that Sakura-chan is going to get married next year. I am jealous, aren't you?

example_sentences.japanese: タケル君が新しいおもちゃが欲しいんだって。どうしよう？買ってあげる？
example_sentences.english: I heard that Takeru-kun is wanting a new toy. What should we do? Should we buy it for him?

example_sentences.japanese: あの博士は凄い事言っているように聞こえるけど、実は言っていること全部適当なんだって。
example_sentences.english: It sounds like that scientist is saying some amazing stuff, but I heard that everything he says is hot air.

example_sentences.japanese: タクミさんはレスラーみたいな体しているけど、好きなスポーツはフィギュアスケートなんだって。
example_sentences.english: Takumi-san has a body like a wrestler, but I heard that his favorite sport is figure skating.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は真面目なんだって。
example_sentences.english: (Someone) said that he is pretty serious.

example_sentences.japanese: やっと旅行に行けるんだって。お金が貯まったから。
example_sentences.english: (They) said that (they) can finally travel. Because (they) saved up money.

example_sentences.japanese: まだできていないんだって。あんなに時間があったのに…
example_sentences.english: (He) said that it is not ready. Even though (he) had all that time to get it done.

example_sentences.japanese: 本当は嫌なんだって。口では言えないけど。
example_sentences.english: (Someone) said that (he) doesn't actually like it. Although (he) can't tell you to your face.

example_sentences.japanese: 結局食べるんだって。あんなに文句言ってたのに。
example_sentences.english: (She) said that (she) will eat after all. Even though (she) complained so much.

example_sentences.japanese: 飛行機飛ぶんだって。天気悪いけど。
example_sentences.english: They said that the airplane will still take off. The weather isn't great, though.

example_sentences.japanese: 乗物酔いするからバスには乗れないんだって。
example_sentences.english: (They) said that (they) can't use the bus because (they) get motion sickness.

example_sentences.japanese: あのパーティーに、結局一人で行ったんだって。
example_sentences.english: (She) said that (she) just ended up going to that party alone.

example_sentences.japanese: 昔ここに住んでいたから、懐かしいんだって。
example_sentences.english: (They) said that (they) lived here before so this area is nostalgic (for them).

example_sentences.japanese: 来年の春ごろに、彼は故郷に帰るんだって。
example_sentences.english: (Someone) said that he will return to his hometown around next spring.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人には分からないんだって。何回言っても。
example_sentences.english: (Someone) said that person doesn't get it. No matter how many times you tell her/him.

general_translation: (Not) involved with, (Not) concerned with, (No) connection with, (No) relationship with, (Not) related to
formation: Noun + に(1) + 関係（かんけい） + がある(2)Noun + に(1) + 関係（かんけい）+ が(3)ある(2) + Noun(1) と(2) ない(3) の、は
casual_structure: Noun + に(1) + 関係（かんけい） + がある(2)Noun + に(1) + 関係（かんけい）+ が(3)ある(2) + Noun(1) と(2) ない(3) の、は
explanation: A common expression used when a relationship or connection exists, or does not exist with (A).

example_sentences.japanese: その問題は私にはかんけいはないよ。
example_sentences.english: That problem has nothing to do with me. (Has no relation to me)

example_sentences.japanese: 授業にかんけいがない本はしまってください。
example_sentences.english: Please put away books that aren't related to class.

example_sentences.japanese: さっき森の方に逃げた人は事件にかんけいがあると思います。
example_sentences.english: I think the person that ran into the forest earlier is involved in the crime.

example_sentences.japanese: この仕事にかんけいがある資料を全て提出してください。
example_sentences.english: Please submit all documents concerning this work.

example_sentences.japanese: あの工場は川の汚染とかんけいがあるそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that that factory has something to do with the pollution of the river.

example_sentences.japanese: この事件とかんけいがある人を全員ここに連れてきてください。
example_sentences.english: Please bring everyone related to this case over here.

example_sentences.japanese: それとこれはなんのかんけいがあるのだろうか。
example_sentences.english: I wonder what relationship this and that have.

example_sentences.japanese: この被害者とのかんけいがある人を集めてください。
example_sentences.english: Please gather all people that are connected to this victim.

example_sentences.japanese: それは私にかんけいがないです。
example_sentences.english: That, I have no connection to.

example_sentences.japanese: これと事故の間になんらかのかんけいがあるはずだ。
example_sentences.english: There has to be some kind of relation between the accident and this. (has a relationship)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らはそれぞれあいざわさんと不透明なかんけいがあるように見える。
example_sentences.english: It seems that they each have some unclear relationship with Mr. Aizawa.

example_sentences.japanese: 容疑者と直にかんけいがある人物が全員呼び出された。
example_sentences.english: Each person directly related to the suspect was summoned. (has a relationship)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本食にかんけいがある単語で空欄を埋めてください。
example_sentences.english: Fill in the blanks with words that are related to Japanese food. (has a relationship)

example_sentences.japanese: 節のＡと節のＢの間に因果のかんけいがあるとき、「から」や「ので」が使われている。
example_sentences.english: When there is a cause and effect relationship between clause A and clause B, 'kara' and 'node' are used. (has a relationship)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は山にかんけいのある神様が多いことで有名である。
example_sentences.english: Japan is famous for the numerous gods that are related to mountains. (has a relationship)

example_sentences.japanese: 物価が上がれば需要は下がる。このように需要と供給とはかんけいがある。
example_sentences.english: If prices go up, demand goes down. Thus, supply and demand are related. (has a relationship)

example_sentences.japanese: 続行する前に時間や言語とかんけいのあるオプションを設定してください。
example_sentences.english: Please configure options that are related to time and language before proceeding. (has a relationship)

example_sentences.japanese: 最初から日本にかんけいのある名前を犬に付けたかったから、ポチと呼ぶことにした。
example_sentences.english: From the beginning, I wanted to give my dog a name that was related to Japan, so I decided to call him Pochi. (has a relationship)

example_sentences.japanese: ニュースによると前大統領は賄賂の件にかんけいがあって、逮捕されたということだ。
example_sentences.english: According to the news, the former president has been arrested due to (his) involvement in a bribe case. (has a relationship)

example_sentences.japanese: 肺ガンはタバコを吸うことと直接的なかんけいがあると言えるだろう。
example_sentences.english: It can be said that lung cancer has a direct connection to smoking cigarettes.

example_sentences.japanese: この事件にかんけいがない人は帰ってください。
example_sentences.english: People that have no connection to this crime, please go home.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の話とかんけいがないことを言わないで。
example_sentences.english: Please don't say anything that isn't related to my story.

general_translation: Related to, About, Regarding
formation: Noun + に関（かん）してNoun + に関（かん）する +  Noun
casual_structure: Noun + に関（かん）してNoun + に関（かん）する +  Noun
explanation: A phrase that shows that some thought or action is in connection to (A).

example_sentences.japanese: ダンスにかんする本が机の上にあります。
example_sentences.english: There are books related to dance on the desk.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は今地盤汚染に関する研究をしています。
example_sentences.english: He does research related to pollution in the Earth's crust.

example_sentences.japanese: このアプリの使い方にかんする質問はありますか？
example_sentences.english: Do you have any questions concerning how to use this app?

example_sentences.japanese: この農薬にかんして、知っておくべきことはありますか？
example_sentences.english: Is there anything I should know relating to this pesticide?

example_sentences.japanese: 幼稚園にかんしては、全然詳しくないので僕に聞かれても困ります。
example_sentences.english: I am not knowledgeable in regards to kindergartens, so even if you ask me I won't know.

example_sentences.japanese: 過去にかんしては、悲しまなくてもいい。
example_sentences.english: You don't need to be sad about  the past. (related to)

example_sentences.japanese: 環境にかんして、質問はありますか。
example_sentences.english: Do you have any questions related to the environment?

example_sentences.japanese: その件にかんしては改めてご説明いたします。
example_sentences.english: I will provide more details related to that issue at another time.

example_sentences.japanese: 経済にかんしては全然詳しくありません。
example_sentences.english: I am not very knowledgeable in anything related to economics.

example_sentences.japanese: 税金にかんすることは彼に聞くといい。
example_sentences.english: I recommend asking him about matters related to taxes.

example_sentences.japanese: 資金にかんする問題が解決しなかったので困っています。
example_sentences.english: I am at a loss because I didn't solve the problem related to funding.

example_sentences.japanese: 君は将来にかんして悲観的すぎるよ。
example_sentences.english: You are too pessimistic about anything related to your future.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本にかんする情報を集めてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to collect information related to Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 車にかんしては、僕よりも君の方が詳しいと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think you are more knowledgeable in things related to cars than me.

example_sentences.japanese: ビットコインにかんする会議は２０１８年5月5日に行われる。
example_sentences.english: The conference related to bitcoin will take place on May 5th, 2018.

example_sentences.japanese: 公立図書館から中世の音楽にかんする本を借りてきてくれませんか。
example_sentences.english: Could you borrow a book related to medieval music for me from the public library?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が電車の事について話し出すと、永遠に話し続ける。
example_sentences.english: Once on the topic of trains, he will talk forever. (Casual)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が電車の事にかんして話し出すと、永遠に話し続ける。
example_sentences.english: Once the topic is related to trains, he will talk forever. (More formal)

general_translation: In contrast to, While, In regard to, Whereas
formation: Toward・In regard toNoun + に対（たい）して(1)Noun + に対（たい）する + NounIn contrast toVerb + の + に対（たい）して［な］Adjective + な(2) + の + に対（たい）してNoun + （な(2) + の） + に対（たい）して(1) に対（たい）しても、に対（たい）しては(2) である
casual_structure: Toward・In regard toNoun + に対（たい）して(1)Noun + に対（たい）する + NounIn contrast toVerb + の + に対（たい）して［な］Adjective + な(2) + の + に対（たい）してNoun + （な(2) + の） + に対（たい）して(1) に対（たい）しても、に対（たい）しては(2) である
explanation: A structure that expresses some action or thought in relation to (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はみんなにたいして優しい人なんです。
example_sentences.english: He is kind towards everyone.

example_sentences.japanese: 君にたいする気持ちは一生変わらない。
example_sentences.english: My feelings toward you will never change.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は店員にたいする態度が悪い人が苦手です。
example_sentences.english: I don't like people who have a bad attitude towards store employees. (People who target their bad attitude at store employees)

example_sentences.japanese: ああいう風に、先輩にたいしてタメ口を使うのは良くないと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: I don't think it is best to talk to a senpai using casual speech in that manner. (Talking casually toward a senior)

example_sentences.japanese: 何でいつも私にたいしてそういう酷いことを言うの？
example_sentences.english: Why do you always say mean things like that to me? (With me as the target)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の教育制度にたいしてどう思う？
example_sentences.english: What are your thoughts in regards to the Japanese school system?

example_sentences.japanese: 誰にたいしても親切な人になりたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to be nice towards anyone and everyone.

example_sentences.japanese: 父が厳しすぎるのにたいして、母は優しすぎる。
example_sentences.english: My father is too strict, in contrast, my mother is too nice.

example_sentences.japanese: はぐらかさないで質問にたいして答えてください。
example_sentences.english: Regarding the question, please answer it, without dodging.

example_sentences.japanese: 君は僕にたいして冷たい態度を取るよね。
example_sentences.english: You are cold towards me, aren't you?

example_sentences.japanese: 大人にたいしてそんな失礼な態度を取ってはいけません。
example_sentences.english: You must not be so rude toward adults.

example_sentences.japanese: 増税にたいして不満がある人は多い。
example_sentences.english: There are many people who are dissatisfied regarding the tax increase.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は、政治家にたいしていつも批判的だ。
example_sentences.english: That person is always negative towards politicians.

example_sentences.japanese: ルールを守らない人にたいしては厳しく取り締まってください。
example_sentences.english: Please be strict towards people who do not follow the rules.

example_sentences.japanese: イギリス人がビールを好きなのにたいして、フランス人は赤ワインが好きだ。
example_sentences.english: English people like drinking beer in contrast to French people who like red wine.

example_sentences.japanese: この部分にたいして質問が多かった。ちょっと難しかったのかしら...。
example_sentences.english: There were many questions regarding this part. I wonder if it was too difficult...

example_sentences.japanese: このプロジェクトに関して質問がある方は私に直接電話をしてください。
example_sentences.english: If you have any questions concerning this project, please give me a call directly. (Questions in relation to this project)

example_sentences.japanese: 私はサッカーが好きなのにたいして、彼はバドミントンが好き。
example_sentences.english: In contrast to me liking soccer, he likes badminton. (Opposed to me who likes soccer)

example_sentences.japanese: マサミは難しい本を読んだのにたいして、カスミは簡単な本を読んだ。
example_sentences.english: Masami read a difficult book, whereas Kasumi read an easy book.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の仕事は楽なのにたいして、僕の仕事はものすごく大変。
example_sentences.english: His job is carefree, whereas my job is very difficult.

general_translation: To the extent that, So…that, About the only thing that...
formation: Verb + くらい(1)［い］Adjective + くらい(1)［な］Adjective + な + くらい(1)Noun + くらい(1)(1) ぐらい
casual_structure: Verb + くらい(1)［い］Adjective + くらい(1)［な］Adjective + な + くらい(1)Noun + くらい(1)(1) ぐらい
explanation: A fairly casual way to express that (A) happened to the surprising extent of (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 寝ることしか出来ないくらい、疲れている。
example_sentences.english: I am so tired that I can't do anything but sleep.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はもう一生走りたくないくらい走った。
example_sentences.english: Today, I ran so much that I don't want to run again in my whole life.

example_sentences.japanese: わたしも叫びたいくらい、怖かった。
example_sentences.english: I was so scared that I wanted to scream too.

example_sentences.japanese: ５連休が必要なぐらい疲れています。
example_sentences.english: I am tired to the extent that it is necessary for me to have 5 days off.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺もキヨミさんくらいピアノが弾けるようになりたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to be able to play the piano to about the level of Kiyomi-san.

example_sentences.japanese: あの仕事は、泣きたいくらいつらかったよ。
example_sentences.english: That job was rough to the extent that I wanted to cry.

example_sentences.japanese: プロ選手ぐらい上手になりたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to be skilled to the extent that pro athletes are.

example_sentences.japanese: 残っているのはやきとりくらいですが。
example_sentences.english: Yakitori is just about the only thing left...

example_sentences.japanese: みんなを泣かすくらいスパイシーなチリのサラダを作った。
example_sentences.english: I made a chili salad so spicy that it made everyone cry.

example_sentences.japanese: このゲームはお年寄りでもやれるくらい簡単だ。
example_sentences.english: This game is easy to the extent that even elderly can play it.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩ぐらいオシャレになりたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to become stylish to the extent that my senior is.

example_sentences.japanese: ヘリウムの風船は、飛行できるくらいすごく軽い。
example_sentences.english: Helium balloons are so amazingly light, that they can fly.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は何もかもが不思議なくらいうまくいった。
example_sentences.english: Today, just about everything went well, to the extent that it was almost strange.

example_sentences.japanese: 少し日本語を話せるぐらい勉強したことがある。
example_sentences.english: I have studied to the extent that I can speak a little Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 有名人に興味のない彼氏でも彼について知ってるの。そのくらい有名なのよ。
example_sentences.english: Even my boyfriend, that is not interested in celebrities, knows about him. He is THAT famous.

example_sentences.japanese: 兄は久し振りにアメリカから帰った。兄だとわからないくらい変わってしまった。
example_sentences.english: My brother returned home for the first time in a long time from America. He changed, to the extent that I didn't recognize that it was him.

general_translation: About the only, To the extent that
formation: は + Verb + くらい (1) + だは + ［い］Adjective + くらい (1) + だは + ［な］Adjective + な + くらい (1) + だは + Noun + くらい (1) + だ(1) ぐらい
casual_structure: は + Verb + くらい (1) + だは + ［い］Adjective + くらい (1) + だは + ［な］Adjective + な + くらい (1) + だは + Noun + くらい (1) + だ(1) ぐらい
polite_structure: は + Verb + くらい (1) + ですは + ［い］Adjective + くらい (1) + ですは + ［な］Adjective + な + くらい (1) + ですは + Noun + くらい (1) + です(1) ぐらい
explanation: A phrase describing that, in general, (A) is about the extent of something.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が得意なのは料理くらいです。
example_sentences.english: Cooking is about the only thing I'm any good at. (extent)

example_sentences.japanese: 休日の日に家を出るのは、買い物に行くときくらいです。
example_sentences.english: Going out to go shopping is about the only thing I do when I have a day off.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事で忙しいのは、月曜日ぐらいだけです。
example_sentences.english: Monday is about the only time I am busy at work.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は基本的になんでも食べられますよ。食べ物で嫌いなのは茹で玉子ぐらいです。
example_sentences.english: In general, I can eat anything. Boiled eggs are about the only thing I dislike in regards of food.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の夢は家族を作ることぐらいかな。
example_sentences.english: Starting a family is about the extent of my dreams.

example_sentences.japanese: 距離は５キロくらいのものです。
example_sentences.english: The distance is only about 5km.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車は仕事に行くときに使っているくらいなものです。プライベートでは車しか使いません。
example_sentences.english: Commuting to work is about the only time I use the train. In my personal time, I only use my car.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の仲間は、犬と猿と雉くらいです。
example_sentences.english: A dog, a monkey and a pheasant are about the only friends I have. (extent)

example_sentences.japanese: 私が苦手なのは、ネギくらいのものです。
example_sentences.english: Green onion is about the only thing that I do not particularly care for. (extent)

example_sentences.japanese: 私の友人は、君と愛犬くらいだ。
example_sentences.english: As far as my friends go, it’s basically just you and my pet dog. (extent)

example_sentences.japanese: 痛みが続くのは３日間ぐらいだ。
example_sentences.english: It will be only about three days that the pain persists.(extent)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の嫌いな食べ物は、納豆ぐらいだ。
example_sentences.english: Natto is about the only food she dislikes. (extent)

example_sentences.japanese: 私が信用できるのは、あなたぐらいだ。
example_sentences.english: As far as people I can trust, it's basically just you.  (extent)

example_sentences.japanese: 飼い猫が外に出るのは満月の日の夜ぐらいです。
example_sentences.english: A full moon is  about the only time my cat goes outside. (extent)

example_sentences.japanese: 今のあなたに任せられる仕事は、床掃除ぐらいよ。
example_sentences.english: Cleaning the floors is about the only task I can trust you with right now. (extent)

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんが驚いた声を出すのは、はちに刺された時ぐらいです。
example_sentences.english: About the only time Tanaka ever yells out is when he is stung by a bee. (extent)

example_sentences.japanese: そんなにアイスの棒を集めたがる人は、世界で君ぐらいだと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think you're about the only person in the world who wants to collect ice cream sticks that badly. (extent)

example_sentences.japanese: あの癖の強いお婆さんに気に入られているのは、うちの孫ぐらいだ。
example_sentences.english: My grandchild is about the only person that stubborn old granny takes a liking to. (extent)

example_sentences.japanese: バイト先に店長が顔を出すのは、オーナーが視察に来る時ぐらいだ。
example_sentences.english: About the only time the shop manager shows his face at our part-time job is when the owner comes for an inspection. (extent)

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに忙しいといっても、店内が混み合うのは金土の夜ぐらいです。
example_sentences.english: Even if we say we're busy, about the only time the shop gets crowded is on Friday and Saturday nights. (extent)

example_sentences.japanese: 日本海側でくじらが見られる機会は、年に数回あるかないかぐらいだ。
example_sentences.english: There are only a few chances a year to see whales on the Sea of Japan side. (about the only) (extent)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼氏の顔が広いおかげで私も友人が増えたが、心を許せるのは２人ぐらいだ。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to my boyfriend's wide network, I've made more friends too, but I can only truly open up to about two of them. (about the only) (extent)

general_translation: All right, There we go, Now, You see, Well (I don't know, let me see)
formation: さあ + Phrase(1) さ、さぁ、さあ、さー
casual_structure: さあ + Phrase(1) さ、さぁ、さあ、さー
explanation: A short, casual interjection used either to fill silence, or to convey that the following information should be paid attention to.

example_sentences.japanese: 「さあ、仕事を始めよう。」
example_sentences.english: 'Alright, let's start working!'

example_sentences.japanese: さーさー、遠慮をせずにどんどん食べてください。
example_sentences.english: There we go! Please eat a lot without holding back.

example_sentences.japanese: さあ、そろそろ行きますか。
example_sentences.english: Okay then, should we go soon?

example_sentences.japanese: 「さあ、行きましょう。」
example_sentences.english: 'Alright, let's go!'

example_sentences.japanese: 「あの人、誰？」「さあ…」
example_sentences.english: 'Who is that person?''Well… '

example_sentences.japanese: 「足は？」「大丈夫よ。さあ早く…」
example_sentences.english: '(How is) your leg?''It is ok. Now, quickly (keep moving)…'

example_sentences.japanese: 「さ、早く乗ってください。」「うん。」
example_sentences.english: 'Alright, now quickly get on.''Yeah.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「さ、そろそろ帰る時間だぞ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Alright, it's time to go back home now.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「さ、食べて。冷めないうちに。」
example_sentences.english: 'Now, please eat, before it gets cold.'

example_sentences.japanese: 夏休みの後：「さぁ、学校に戻るぞ ！」
example_sentences.english: After summer vacation: 'Well, time to go back to school!'

example_sentences.japanese: 「お腹空いた！」「無駄な時間を過ごしてる暇はないよ。さあ、急いで！」
example_sentences.english: 'I am hungry!''We don't have time to waste. Now, hurry up!'

example_sentences.japanese: 「泥棒はどんなふうに中に入ったのかしら。」「さあ、よくわからないけど…」
example_sentences.english: 'I wonder how the thief got inside?''Well, I don't know, but…'

example_sentences.japanese: 猫を探すとき：「さかもとさんはどこに行ったんだろう？」「さあ、知らないね。あの箱を調べたらどう？」
example_sentences.english: When searching for a cat: 'I wonder where Sakamoto-san went?''Well, I don't know. How about checking in that box over there?

example_sentences.japanese: 「映画館に一緒に行きたいの？」「さあどうしようかな。」
example_sentences.english: 'Do you want to go to the cinema together?''Well, I am not sure…'

example_sentences.japanese: あのさ、昨日は暑さに負けて倒れちゃった。
example_sentences.english: Well, you see… I lost to the heat yesterday and passed out. (Yesterday, I passed out due to the heat)

example_sentences.japanese: さあ、それはどうでしょう？私に聞いてもわからないよ。
example_sentences.english: Well let me see… I don't know about that. Even if you ask me I wouldn't have a clue.

general_translation: Like, You know, You see, Listen, Uhh
formation: Phrase (A) + さぁ(1) + Phrase (B)(1) さあ、さー、さ
casual_structure: Phrase (A) + さぁ(1) + Phrase (B)(1) さあ、さー、さ
explanation: A short, casual interjection used to fill silence, in a similar way to like and you know in English.

example_sentences.japanese: 「今朝さあ、母さんに怒られたよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I got scolded by mom in the morning, you know.'

example_sentences.japanese: あのさ、私さあ、この前さあ、お金貸したじゃん？あれさあ、返してくれない？
example_sentences.english: Hey, um… I, uhh, lent you, like, money before, right? You know… can you give that back to me?

example_sentences.japanese: ね～聞いてよ。彼女がさ、急に別れたいっていって来たんだけどどうすればいいの。
example_sentences.english: Heyyy, listen to this. You know my girlfriend? She suddenly came to me saying that she wants to break up with me, what should I do.

example_sentences.japanese: 来週箱根に行くんだけどさ…どこか美味しいところ知らない？
example_sentences.english: I am going to Hakone next week, soooo… Do you know any good restaurants?

example_sentences.japanese: 夜中に急に娘から電話が来てさあ...本当にビックリしたよ。
example_sentences.english: You know, my daughter suddenly called me in the middle of the night, and… I was really worried.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との会話：「あのさ、俺、彼女ができたんだ！」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'Listen, I got myself a girlfriend!'

example_sentences.japanese: 「あのさぁ、好きな人とかいるの？」
example_sentences.english: 'Listen, do you have someone you like?'

example_sentences.japanese: 「内緒だけどさ、彼宝くじに当たったんだよ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Between us, you see, he won the lottery.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「私さぁ、明日から５連休なんだ！」Ｂ：「いいなぁー」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I have, you see, a 5 day weekend starting from tomorrow.'B: 'Lucky!'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「彼ってさとてもいい父親らしいよ。」Ｂ：「そうなんだぁ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Speaking of him, you see, I heard that he is a very good father.'B: 'Is that so?'

example_sentences.japanese: ちずるちゃん：「すがわらくんさぁ、本気でわたしに告白するつもりあるの？」
example_sentences.english: Chizuru-chan: 'Does Sugawara-Kun, uhh, really plan to confess to me?'

example_sentences.japanese: 怒こっているクライアント：「あのさあ、こっち並んでるんだからさあ、こっちから応対すべきじゃね？」
example_sentences.english: Angry client: 'Listen. We've been waiting in line here, you see, shouldn't you serve us first?'

example_sentences.japanese: 「あのさぁ、昨日帰るときさぁ、あるやつにクラクションを鳴らされてさぁ…びっくりした。」
example_sentences.english: 'Listen, yesterday, when I was going back home, like, some guy, honked at me, you see... It startled me.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との就職についての話、Ａ：「お前さぁ、やる気あるの？」Ｂ：「俺さぁ、就職じゃなくて、進学しようと思ってる。」
example_sentences.english: A conversation among friends about finding a job, A: 'Listen, man, do you feel like doing it?'B: 'You see, I am not looking for a job, I plan to go to uni.'

example_sentences.japanese: 上司が部下に仕事の進捗を聞く：「あのさ、この前お願いした資料だけど、進捗どう？」
example_sentences.english: Superior asking a subordinate about work progress: 'Listen, is there any progress with the documents I requested earlier?'

example_sentences.japanese: 息子（大学生）：「お母さん、来月さぁ、部活の合宿があるんだけど。」母：「うん、それで？」息子：「１万円いるから宜しく」母：「バイトして貯めなさい。」
example_sentences.english: Son (university student): 'Mom, next month, you see, we have a club training camp…'Mother: 'Yes, so what?'Son: 'I need 10,000 yen, so pretty please…'Mother: 'Get a part-time job and save for it!'

general_translation: Casual よ
formation: Phrase + さ(1)(1) さぁ、さあ、さー
casual_structure: Phrase + さ(1)(1) さぁ、さあ、さー
explanation: A short, casual interjection used either to fill silence, or to express that new information has been conveyed.

example_sentences.japanese: 「僕はＮＢＡでやるつもりさ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I intend to play in the NBA.' (emphasis; softer than よ）

example_sentences.japanese: 彼氏がもう私のことを信用できないってさ。
example_sentences.english: My boyfriend told me that he can't trust me anymore. (Added confidence gives the nuance of 'can you believe it!')

example_sentences.japanese: インスタで見たんだけど、キヨミの赤ちゃんが明日生まれるんだってさ！
example_sentences.english: I saw it on instagram, but I heard that Kiyomi is going to give birth tomorrow!

example_sentences.japanese: そんなこと心配ないさ!俺に任せとけ！
example_sentences.english: Such a thing is not necessary! Leave it to me! (Trust it to me in advance, so that it is not a problem later)

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「彼が約束を破ったってさ。」Ｂ：「そんな人じゃないさ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I heard that he broke his word.'B: 'He is not that type of person!' (emphasis; softer than よ）

example_sentences.japanese: 「まぁ、なんとかなるさ。」
example_sentences.english: 'Well, somehow I'll get by.' (emphasis; softer than よ）

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「寒い。寒すぎるよ。」Ｂ：「どうってことないさ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'It's cold. Soo cold.'B: 'This is nothing.' (emphasis; softer than よ）

example_sentences.japanese: 「テレビで台風がやってくるってさ。」
example_sentences.english: 'They say on TV that a typhoon is coming.' (emphasis; softer than よ）

example_sentences.japanese: 「明日までにこのプロジェクトを終えることができるさ。本当さ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I can finish this project by tomorrow. Really.' (emphasis; softer than よ）

example_sentences.japanese: 「君は真剣に練習していないから、いつも負けるのさ。」
example_sentences.english: 'You don't take training seriously, so we lose all the time!' (emphasis; softer than よ）

example_sentences.japanese: 「マルチプルチョイスのテストなど、適当に番号を選ぶだけさ。」
example_sentences.english: 'For multiple-choice tests, I will just randomly choose the numbers.' (emphasis; softer than よ）

example_sentences.japanese: 「二度目の受験だから、前回の轍を踏まなければ合格できるさ。」
example_sentences.english: 'I will take the exam a second time, so if I don't repeat any mistakes, I will pass.' (emphasis; softer than よ）

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「このままだと戻れないんだぞ。現状の深刻さがわからないのか？」Ｂ：「わかっているさ。プラスに考えようとしているだけさ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'If it is like that, we cannot come back! Do you understand the seriousness of the situation?'B: 'I understand. I am just trying to think of it as a positive.' (emphasis; softer than よ）

example_sentences.japanese: クラスメイトＡ：「じゅんいちろうはともちゃんと付き合ってるの？」クラスメートのじゅんいちろう：「そんなことないさ。」
example_sentences.english: Classmate A: 'Hey, I heard that you are going out with Tomo-chan.'Classmate, Junichirou: 'That's not true.' (emphasis; softer than よ）

example_sentences.japanese: 「きっと、勝てるさ。」
example_sentences.english: 'We can surely win!' (emphasis; softer than よ）

example_sentences.japanese: お前さ...
example_sentences.english: You… (Are you freaking serious)

example_sentences.japanese: たかし君も行きたいってさ。どうしよう？彼も招待する？
example_sentences.english: Takashi-kun said he wants to go too. What should we do? Should we invite him too?

example_sentences.japanese: そんなの俺にだってできるさ。分からないけど。
example_sentences.english: Although I am not certain, even I would be able to do something like that.

general_translation: Each, Respectively
formation: それぞれ + Phraseそれぞれ + の + Noun
casual_structure: それぞれ + Phraseそれぞれ + の + Noun
explanation: A word used to indicate each and every individual (A) from within a group.

example_sentences.japanese: それぞれ行きたいところに行きましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's go to each of the places we want to go (respectively).

example_sentences.japanese: それぞれのチームに分かれてから開始してください。
example_sentences.english: Please start once you have divided yourselves into each separate team.

example_sentences.japanese: それぞれ別の行動をした。
example_sentences.english: We each did our own separate things.

example_sentences.japanese: 人それぞれの考え方があるから、しょうがないよ。
example_sentences.english: Each person has different ways of thinking, so there is nothing we can do.

example_sentences.japanese: 皆それぞれ食べたいものを頼んでね。
example_sentences.english: Everyone, please (each) order something you want to eat.

example_sentences.japanese: 生き物はそれぞれ食べるものが違う。
example_sentences.english: Living things each eat different things respectively.

example_sentences.japanese: それぞれ好きな運動をした。
example_sentences.english: We each (respectively) did exercises that we like.

example_sentences.japanese: これからはそれぞれの道を行くことに決めた。
example_sentences.english: We decided that we will each (respectively) go our separate ways from now on.

example_sentences.japanese: 人それぞれ癖というものがあります。
example_sentences.english: Each (respective) person has a habit.

example_sentences.japanese: それぞれが工夫して、いいアイデアを考え出した。
example_sentences.english: Each (respective) participant thought about it and came up with an idea.

example_sentences.japanese: それぞれの役割をちゃんと果たしていけば、もっと上手くいけるはずです。
example_sentences.english: If each (respective) one fulfills their role, it should work out better.

example_sentences.japanese: それぞれの原因を特定しないと、解決できないよ。
example_sentences.english: If we don't find out the cause of each respective problem, it will never be solved.

example_sentences.japanese: それぞれの意見を聞いてから、折り合いをつけましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's hear everyone's (each respective) opinion, and settle the matter.

example_sentences.japanese: お昼はそれぞれ好きなお店で食べましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's each (respectively) have lunch separately in the restaurant you prefer.

example_sentences.japanese: 人にはそれぞれ違う思い出がある。
example_sentences.english: Each (respective) person has different memories.

example_sentences.japanese: それぞれ記入する用紙がありますので、全部記入してください。
example_sentences.english: There is a sheet for each (respective) application, so please fill out all of them.

general_translation: As is, While remaining, Left in a state
formation: Verb［た］(1) + まま［い］Adjective + まま［な］Adjective + な + ままNoun + の + まま(1) Verb［ない］
casual_structure: Verb［た］(1) + まま［い］Adjective + まま［な］Adjective + な + ままNoun + の + まま(1) Verb［ない］
explanation: A grammar point that expresses something left as is, often in some unchanging state.

example_sentences.japanese: コートをきたままだと少し暑いです。
example_sentences.english: I feel a little hot keeping this jacket on.

example_sentences.japanese: うぁ〜、マジかよ。電気とガスを点けたままだった。
example_sentences.english: Whaaat. Are you serious? I left my gas and electricity on.

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋を汚いままにしていたらゴキブリが沢山出てきた。
example_sentences.english: So many cockroaches appeared because I left my room dirty.

example_sentences.japanese: いつまでも元気なままでいてね。
example_sentences.english: Please always stay healthy, okay?

example_sentences.japanese: 今のままだと、一生結婚できないと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: If you are the way you are now, I don't think you'll ever be able to marry.

example_sentences.japanese: 許可を取らないまま駅で撮影をしていたら、警察が来た。
example_sentences.english: While I was filming at the station without getting a permit, the police were called.

example_sentences.japanese: 夕食を食べないまま寝たら、お腹が空いて３時ぐらいに起きてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Because I slept without eating dinner, I woke up around 3 am from hunger.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は窓をあけたまま寝た。
example_sentences.english: Last night I slept with the windows left open.

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒は答えられなくて、だまったままでした。
example_sentences.english: The student couldn't answer and stayed quiet.

example_sentences.japanese: このまま行くと図書館が見えます。
example_sentences.english: If you stay on this course, you will be able to see the library.

example_sentences.japanese: ありのままの君が好きだ。
example_sentences.english: I like you, just as you are.

example_sentences.japanese: 音楽をつけたまま寝るのが好きだよ。
example_sentences.english: I like to sleep with music left turned on.

example_sentences.japanese: およそ千人がたったままで講演を聞いた。
example_sentences.english: About 1000 people listened to the lecture while standing (the whole time).

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、ヒーターをつけたまま出かけたんだ。もう少しで、自分の家を燃やすところだった。
example_sentences.english: While I went out yesterday, I left the heater on. I nearly burned my own house to the ground.

example_sentences.japanese: 車にのったままハンバーガーが買えるのは便利ですね。
example_sentences.english: It's very convenient to be able to buy hamburgers while remaining seated in a car.

example_sentences.japanese: 久しぶりに故郷に帰って、すごく驚いた。十年前、外国へ移住したその日のままだった。
example_sentences.english: After a long time, I had returned to my hometown and was extremely surprised. It was as it had been the day I emigrated, ten years ago.

example_sentences.japanese: 監督：「このチームでは、今のままだと優勝できないから、あることを変更することに決めた。」
example_sentences.english: Coach: 'Since the team can't win the championship staying the way it is, I decided to change things up.'

example_sentences.japanese: ポーランドでは、すわったまま握手することは失礼になります。
example_sentences.english: In Poland, it's rude to shake hands while remaining seated.

example_sentences.japanese: エンジンを点けたままにしておいてください。
example_sentences.english: Please keep your engine on.

example_sentences.japanese: 扇風機を点けたままにして家を出る。
example_sentences.english: I leave my house with my fan turned on. (Often)

example_sentences.japanese: これどこに片付ければいいかわからないからこのまんまでいい？
example_sentences.english: I don’t know where to put this so is it okay if I just leave it here?

general_translation: Accordingly, Now, Therefore, To that end
formation: (Situation) Phrase。そこで + (Solution) Phrase
casual_structure: (Situation) Phrase。そこで + (Solution) Phrase
explanation: A phrase indicating that (A) is the place from which, accordingly, (B). Literally, with that place, (B) is the solution.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は彼女を愛している。そこで、結婚を申し込むことに決めた。
example_sentences.english: I love her. Accordingly, I decided to ask her to marry me.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は雨の中、傘なしで立っている。そこで、私は車から出て彼に私の傘をあげた。
example_sentences.english: He is standing in the rain without an umbrella. As such, I got out of the car and gave him mine.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女と結婚をすることにした。そこで、彼女の親の実家に行って挨拶をすることに決めた。
example_sentences.english: I have decided to marry my girlfriend. To that end, I have decided to go to her parents' place to talk to them.

example_sentences.japanese: うちには泥棒が３回も入っている。そこで、防犯ガラスを買うことにした。
example_sentences.english: Our house has been burgled 3 times already. As such, I have decided to buy an anti-theft window.

example_sentences.japanese: 信号が赤になったのでブレーキをかけた。そこで、後ろの車に私の車をぶつけられた。
example_sentences.english: Because the traffic light turned red, I stepped on the brakes. As such, the car behind me crashed into me. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が泣き始めた。そこで、子供に飴をあげて落ち着かせた。
example_sentences.english: My kid started to cry. As such, I gave them some candy to calm them down.

example_sentences.japanese: この方法ではもう限界だと分かった。そこで、新たな方法を試してみることに決めた。
example_sentences.english: I found out there was a limit to this method. Accordingly, we decided to try another one.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は暗記が苦手だ。そこで、暗記のコツを教えてあげることに決めた。
example_sentences.english: She is not good at memorizing things. Accordingly, I decided to teach her a trick to memorize things effectively.

example_sentences.japanese: この荷物は重い。そこで、仲間を呼んで手伝ってもらうことに決めた。
example_sentences.english: This luggage is heavy. Therefore, I decided to get my friends to help.

example_sentences.japanese: うちには工具箱がありません。そこでお願いなのですが、ドライバーを貸してもらえませんか？
example_sentences.english: We don't have a toolbox. Therefore, I have a favor to ask you, could you please lend me your screwdrivers?

example_sentences.japanese: 一晩中考えたのですが分かりません。そこで質問なのですが、この表現はどういう意味なのですか？
example_sentences.english: I thought about it all night, but I still don't understand. Therefore I have a question, what does this expression mean?

example_sentences.japanese: ストレスが溜まった。そこで、カラオケに行って発散することに決めた。
example_sentences.english: I built up a lot of stress. Accordingly, I decided to release stress with karaoke.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は試験で一位になろうと思う。そこで、勉強時間をもう少し増やすことに決めた。
example_sentences.english: I plan to be the top scorer on the test. Therefore, I decided to slightly increase the amount of time I study.

example_sentences.japanese: お隣にアメリカ人が引っ越してきた。そこで、英語を勉強することに決めた。
example_sentences.english: A person from the U.S moved in next door. Accordingly, I decided to study English.

example_sentences.japanese: 食費がかかりすぎている。そこで、お菓子の量を減らすことに決めた。
example_sentences.english: I am paying too much for food. Accordingly, I decided to reduce the amount of snacks.

example_sentences.japanese: 天気予報で嵐が近づいていると言っていた。そこで、外にある植木鉢を家の中に入れることに決めた。
example_sentences.english: The weather forecast said that a storm is approaching. Accordingly, I decided to put my potted plants inside.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻によれば義理の親が遊びに来るらしい。そこで、近所を案内してあげることに決めた。
example_sentences.english: According to my wife, in-laws are coming to see us. So I decided to show them around the neighborhood.

general_translation: Have no choice but, Only, Just
formation: Verb + しかない
casual_structure: Verb + しかない
polite_structure: Verb + しかありません
explanation: A structure that specifically expresses that no action apart from (A) is possible.

example_sentences.japanese: 人が多いから、並ぶしかない。
example_sentences.english: Because there are a lot of people, we have no choice but to line up.

example_sentences.japanese: こうなったら警察を呼ぶしかない。
example_sentences.english: If it's come to this, there is no choice but to call the police.

example_sentences.japanese: もう電車が来ないから、車で行くしかない。
example_sentences.english: Since trains won't be coming anymore, there is no choice but to go by car.

example_sentences.japanese: この時間帯はピザハット以外どこも開いていないね。こうなったらピザを頼むしかないね。
example_sentences.english: At this hour, nowhere is open other than Pizza Hut. Now that it's come to it, there is no choice but to order some pizza, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 今月は休めないから、コンサートに行くのを我慢するしかない。
example_sentences.english: I can't take a day off this month, so I have no choice but to resist going to the concert.

example_sentences.japanese: 時が来るのを待つしかないですよ。
example_sentences.english: You have no choice but to wait for the time to come.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなにうまくいかないかなあ… もう笑うしかない。
example_sentences.english: To think that it would go this poorly... I have no choice but to laugh!

example_sentences.japanese: 素直に謝るしかないです。
example_sentences.english: I have no choice but to sincerely apologize.

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋はゴミだらけなので掃除するしかない。
example_sentences.english: This room is full of trash. I have no choice but to clean it.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は資源を輸入するしかない。
example_sentences.english: Japan has no choice but to import resources.

example_sentences.japanese: 飲みに行くしかない。だって、私の誕生日だから。
example_sentences.english: We have no choice but to go drinking. Why? Because it's my birthday.

example_sentences.japanese: 迎えに来てもらえないので、歩いて帰るしかない。
example_sentences.english: (They) won't come pick us up so we have no choice but to walk home.

example_sentences.japanese: 私ならほかの仕事をするだろうけど、上司の命令だから、従うしかない。
example_sentences.english: If it was up to me, I would be doing other work but it is an order from my superior, so I have no choice but to obey.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬が外に出たがるから、散歩に連れていくしかない。
example_sentences.english: The dog wants to go out, so I have no choice but to take it for a walk.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らが暴力を振ってくるところだったから身を守るしかなかった。
example_sentences.english: Because they were about to resort to violence, I had no choice but to defend myself.

example_sentences.japanese: 山から降りられるなら降りたいんだ。でも、強い雨が降り始めたから、この雨が止むまで頂上で待っているしかない。
example_sentences.english: If I could go down the mountain, I would go down. However, it started pouring rain, so I have no other choice but to continue waiting at the peak until the rain stops.

example_sentences.japanese: この技で倒れないのなら、必殺技を使うっきゃないな！
example_sentences.english: If I can't defeat them using this move, there is no other choice but to use my special move, is there?

example_sentences.japanese: これほど完璧なチャンスは二度とないから、今やるっきゃないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: An opportunity this perfect will not come around a second time, so I have no other choice but to do it now.

general_translation: It doesn't matter if, I don't mind
formation: Verb［ても］+ かまわない［い］Adjective［ても］+ かまわない［な］Adjective + でも + かまわないNoun + でも + かまわない
casual_structure: Verb［ても］+ かまわない［い］Adjective［ても］+ かまわない［な］Adjective + でも + かまわないNoun + でも + かまわない
polite_structure: Verb［ても］+ かまいません［い］Adjective［ても］+ かまいません［な］Adjective + でも + かまいませんNoun + でも + かまいません
explanation: An expression that highlights (A) as being no problem, or not worth bracing over (giving pause).

example_sentences.japanese: 無視されてもかまわない。
example_sentences.english: It doesn't matter (even) if I am ignored.

example_sentences.japanese: 君がお金を出すなら、ピザでも寿司でも何を頼んでもかまわないよ。
example_sentences.english: If you are going to pay, I don't mind whether you order pizza, sushi, or anything else.

example_sentences.japanese: 運転手さん、遅くてもかまいませんので、安全運転でお願いします。
example_sentences.english: Chauffeur, I don't care if it's slower, please drive safely.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事はどんなに大変でもかまいません、仕事が出来ればうれしいです。
example_sentences.english: I don't care how busy work is, I am happy so long as I can do my job.

example_sentences.japanese: アルバイト募集中。未経験者でもかまいません。
example_sentences.english: Hiring part time workers. It doesn't matter if you are not experienced.

example_sentences.japanese: その写真なら、みてもかまいません。
example_sentences.english: If it is that picture, I don't mind if you look at it.

example_sentences.japanese: 欲しい人がいればあげてもかまわない。
example_sentences.english: If someone wants it, I don't mind (even if) giving it.

example_sentences.japanese: 答えたくなければ、こたえなくてもかまいません。
example_sentences.english: If you don't want to answer, it doesn't matter (even) if you don't answer.

example_sentences.japanese: 暇な時はゲームをやってもかまわない。
example_sentences.english: It doesn't matter (even) if you play games when you have free time.

example_sentences.japanese: うまくいかなくてもかまわない。やってみることが大切だ。
example_sentences.english: It doesn't matter (even) if it won't go well. It's important to try.

example_sentences.japanese: ぬれてもかまいません。革靴ではないですから。
example_sentences.english: I don't mind (even if) they get wet. These are not leather shoes.

example_sentences.japanese: おそくなってもかまわないので、ぜひ遊びに来てください。
example_sentences.english: It doesn't matter (even) if it is late, so please come for a visit.

example_sentences.japanese: わらわれてもかまわない。僕はあきらめないぞ。
example_sentences.english: I don't mind if I am laughed at. I won't give up.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の家だから服をきなくてもかまいません。
example_sentences.english: It doesn't matter (even) if you don't wear clothes because it is your own house.

example_sentences.japanese: お金がなくてもかまわない。だって、彼のことが大好きだから。
example_sentences.english: It doesn't matter (even) if he doesn't have money, because I love him.

example_sentences.japanese: 費用はいくらかかってもかまわない。とにかく買ってきてくれ。
example_sentences.english: It doesn't matter how much it costs. Just go buy it for me. (even if)

general_translation: Whether ~ or not
formation: Verb［ても］(A) + Verb［なくても］(A)
casual_structure: Verb［ても］(A) + Verb［なくても］(A)
explanation: A common phrase indicating that even with (A), or even not with (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: つれてもつれなくても、釣りは楽しいらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard fishing is fun whether you are able to catch any fish or not.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人がいてもいなくても、仕事の量は変わらないから、首にしてもいいと思う。
example_sentences.english: Whether or not he is here doesn't change the workload, so I think it would be good if we fired him.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は運動しても運動しなくても痩せられないから、もう運動はしない。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether or not I exercise, I can't lose weight, so I will not exercise anymore.

example_sentences.japanese: ここの居酒屋ではビールを頼んでも頼まなくても、ビールを持ってくる。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of whether you order beer or not, they will bring you one at this izakaya.

example_sentences.japanese: いってもいわなくても、彼はちゃんと仕事ができるよ。
example_sentences.english: Whether you tell him or not, he will get the job done.

example_sentences.japanese: お金をもっていてももっていなくても、幸せになることは可能です。
example_sentences.english: You can be happy whether you have money or not.

example_sentences.japanese: あえてもあえなくても、１８時には解散して帰りましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's finish up and go home by 6pm, whether we can meet (them) or not.

example_sentences.japanese: 助手がいてもいなくても、やることはたいして変わらない。
example_sentences.english: Whether I have an assistant or not, there won't be much difference in what I do.

example_sentences.japanese: あの授業はいってもいかなくてもいいらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that it is alright whether or not you go to that class.

example_sentences.japanese: かってもかわなくてもいいので、一度見てもらえませんか？
example_sentences.english: It doesn't matter whether you buy it or not, why don't you take a look?

example_sentences.japanese: 担当になってもならなくても、私はあなたの味方です。
example_sentences.english: Whether you get to be in charge or not, I support you.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強してもしなくても、試験の結果は変わらない。
example_sentences.english: Whether I study or not, the exam results won't change.

example_sentences.japanese: 試験にうかってもうからなくても、勉強していたら自分の身になる。
example_sentences.english: Whether you pass the exam or not, you will still be better off if you studied for it.

example_sentences.japanese: この単位がとれてもとれなくても、卒業できるだけの単位は取れている。
example_sentences.english: Whether I get this credit or not, I will still have the necessary credits to graduate.

example_sentences.japanese: そろそろ家を出るから、食欲があってもなくても、今食べておいた方がいい。
example_sentences.english: Because we are leaving the house soon, you should eat something, whether you have an appetite or not.

general_translation: Don't, Mustn't, Shouldn't have
formation: Verb + んじゃない
casual_structure: Verb + んじゃない
explanation: A slightly slangy expression used to prohibit an action by framing it as something that is not done.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕をバカにするんじゃない！
example_sentences.english: Don't make a fool of me!

example_sentences.japanese: 親に向かってそんなこと言うんじゃない。
example_sentences.english: Don't say something like that directed at your parents!

example_sentences.japanese: そこら辺のキノコを食べるんじゃない！
example_sentences.english: Don't eat the mushrooms from around there!

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は混んでるからパパから離れるんじゃないぞ！
example_sentences.english: It's crowded today, so don't get separated from your dad!

example_sentences.japanese: 勝手にお友達のものを取るんじゃありません。
example_sentences.english: You shouldn't just freely take your friend's things.

example_sentences.japanese: 乳児にハチミツをあげるんじゃありません。
example_sentences.english: Don't give honey to infants.

example_sentences.japanese: いつまでもケラケラしながら話してんじゃない！
example_sentences.english: Don't keep laughing while you're talking!

example_sentences.japanese: 一日中ダラダラしてんじゃない！いい加減、仕事でも探してこい！
example_sentences.english: Don't laze around all day! Get your act together and find a job!

example_sentences.japanese: 先生：「カンニングをするんじゃない！」
example_sentences.english: Teacher: 'Don't cheat!'

example_sentences.japanese: 嘘をつくんじゃない。
example_sentences.english: You shouldn't lie.

example_sentences.japanese: あなた、仕事をサボるんじゃありません。
example_sentences.english: Hey, don't skip work.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ子供ですよ。門限を破るんじゃありません。
example_sentences.english: You're still a kid. Don't break curfew!

example_sentences.japanese: 生意気を言ってんじゃない。
example_sentences.english: Don't say cheeky things!

example_sentences.japanese: 見栄を張ってんじゃない。逆にカッコ悪いぞ。
example_sentences.english: Don't show off. On the contrary, it's uncool!

example_sentences.japanese: 大学を中退するんじゃなかった…。
example_sentences.english: I shouldn't have dropped out of university…

example_sentences.japanese: 事故を起こした…スピードを出すんじゃなかった。
example_sentences.english: I shouldn't have sped up… It caused an accident.

example_sentences.japanese: パチンコに行ってお金を無駄にするんじゃない！
example_sentences.english: Don't go to pachinko and waste money!

example_sentences.japanese: もう体はボロボロだ。違法な薬物をやるんじゃなかった…。
example_sentences.english: My body is wrecked. I shouldn't have taken illegal drugs…

example_sentences.japanese: 上級生：「下級生が調子に乗ってんじゃない！」
example_sentences.english: Upperclassmen: 'Lowerclassmen, don't get carried away!'

example_sentences.japanese: こんな安い車を買うんじゃなかった。
example_sentences.english: I shouldn't have bought a cheap car like this.

example_sentences.japanese: あんな怪しい話に乗るんじゃなかった。
example_sentences.english: I shouldn't have gotten swept up in such a suspicious story.

example_sentences.japanese: 本当は彼も来たかったんじゃない？
example_sentences.english: Really though, didn't he want to come too?

general_translation: There is no way, There is no reason, It is impossible, Cannot be
formation: Verb［る］(1) + わけがない［な］Adjective + な + わけがない［い］Adjective + わけがない(1) Verb［た］
casual_structure: Verb［る］(1) + わけがない［な］Adjective + な + わけがない［い］Adjective + わけがない(1) Verb［た］
polite_structure: Verb［る］(1) + わけがありません［な］Adjective + な + わけがありません［い］Adjective + わけがありません(1) Verb［た］
explanation: A grammar point that expresses (A) as being impossible, or that it cannot be so.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が嘘をつくわけがない。
example_sentences.english: There is no way he would lie.

example_sentences.japanese: キムラシェフが作ったパスタだよ、不味いわけがないじゃん！
example_sentences.english: This pasta is made by Chef Kimura, there is no way this would taste bad!

example_sentences.japanese: このステーキ２キロもあるの？！こんなの一人で食べれるわけがない！
example_sentences.english: This steak weighs 2kg?! I SO can't eat something like this alone!

example_sentences.japanese: このアパートは線路の隣にあるから静かなわけがない。
example_sentences.english: This apartment is next to the train track, so there is no way it is quiet.

example_sentences.japanese: あんな大ニュース、知らないわけがない。
example_sentences.english: There is no way not to know this. It is such big news!

example_sentences.japanese: 日本人ならそんなことを言うわけがない。
example_sentences.english: There is no way that a Japanese person would say that.

example_sentences.japanese: あれだけ着込んだら寒いわけがない。
example_sentences.english: There is no reason why you would feel cold, wearing all those extra clothes.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなやり方でうまくいくわけがない。
example_sentences.english: With the way you're doing it, it is impossible for it to go well.

example_sentences.japanese: あんなにたくさんのプレゼントをもらったのだから、忘れるわけがない。
example_sentences.english: Since I received so many presents, there's no way that I could forget about it.

example_sentences.japanese: みんなが当たるわけがない。くじ引きとはそういうものだ。
example_sentences.english: It is impossible for everyone to be a winner. That is how lotteries are.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの子猫がこんなに魅力的なわけがない。
example_sentences.english: My kitten cannot be this charming.

example_sentences.japanese: あんなに時間があるんだから、宿題ができないわけがない。
example_sentences.english: Because you have all that time, there is no way for you to not be able to do the homework.

example_sentences.japanese: 翼があるんだから、飛べないわけがない。
example_sentences.english: It has wings, so there is no reason that it would not be able to fly.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本にいるだけで、日本語を学べるわけがない。
example_sentences.english: There is no way you can learn Japanese from just being in Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 手を繋いでいるので、子供が勝手にどこかに行くわけがない。
example_sentences.english: I am holding my kid's hand, so there is no way that he would just run off somewhere.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいつも遊んでいるが、暇なわけではない。
example_sentences.english: He is always going out, but it is not necessarily so that he has a lot of free time.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいつも仕事をしているから、暇なわけがない。
example_sentences.english: Since he is always working, he SO does not have any free time.

general_translation: If it were the case that, Assuming that...
formation: Verb + としたら(1)［い］Adjective + としたら(1)［な］Adjective + （だ） + としたら(1)Noun + （だ） + としたら(1)(1) とすると、とすれば
casual_structure: Verb + としたら(1)［い］Adjective + としたら(1)［な］Adjective + （だ） + としたら(1)Noun + （だ） + としたら(1)(1) とすると、とすれば
explanation: A structure that goes off the assumption that (A) were true, and then expresses some hypothetical result.

example_sentences.japanese: 付き合うとしたら、田中さんと山田さんどっちがいい？
example_sentences.english: If you were to date Tanaka or Yamada, who would you choose?

example_sentences.japanese: 来週出かけるとしたらどこに行きたい？
example_sentences.english: If we were to go out next week, where would you want to go?

example_sentences.japanese: 歯が痛いとすれば、虫歯かもしれません。
example_sentences.english: If your tooth hurts, you might have a cavity.

example_sentences.japanese: この壁が真っ直ぐだとすると、こっちの壁は斜めっていうこと？
example_sentences.english: Assuming that this wall here is straight, does that mean that this one here is slanted?

example_sentences.japanese: 通勤手段が車だとしたら、交通費は出ません。
example_sentences.english: Assuming that your mode of transportation is your car, transportation will not be compensated.

example_sentences.japanese: 無料だとすれば、人が大勢来る。
example_sentences.english: If we suppose it was free, lots of people would come.

example_sentences.japanese: 留学に行くとすると、論文が必要。
example_sentences.english: Assuming that you study abroad, an essay is necessary.

example_sentences.japanese: 買い物に行かないとしたら、晩御飯はどうする？
example_sentences.english: Assuming that I don't go shopping, what will be done about dinner?

example_sentences.japanese: もし会えるとしたら、明日か明後日だね。
example_sentences.english: Assuming that we can meet, it will be either tomorrow or the day after.

example_sentences.japanese: 突然、終わってしまうとすれば、君はどうするの？
example_sentences.english: Assuming it suddenly ended, what would you do?

example_sentences.japanese: それが原因だとすれば、修理できると思うよ。
example_sentences.english: Assuming that is the cause, I think you can fix it.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の試合に勝ったとすれば、決勝に進める。
example_sentences.english: If I win tomorrow's match, I would advance to the finals.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年受からなかったとしたら、来年の受験はどうするつもりなの？
example_sentences.english: Supposing you didn't pass the entrance exam this year, what do you intend to do next year?

example_sentences.japanese: もし勉強しなかったとしたら、明日のテストは悲惨なことになるかなぁ？
example_sentences.english: Assuming that I hadn't studied, I wonder if it would mean that tomorrow's test would be a disaster?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日中に結論が出ないとすれば、明日の発表に間に合いませんよ。
example_sentences.english: Assuming that you don't reach a conclusion by today, you won't make it in time for tomorrow's presentation.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の記憶が間違いないとすれば、あの角を曲がった辺りにスーパーがあるはずです。
example_sentences.english: Assuming that my memory is correct, there should be a supermarket around that corner.

general_translation: As (i.e. in the role of), For
formation: Noun + としてNoun + として + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + としてNoun + として + Noun
explanation: A grammar point that expresses something, considering either the viewpoint or role of (A). Going off that it's (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちは先生としての彼を尊敬します。
example_sentences.english: We look up to him as our teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 動物を傷つける奴は人間として失格だ。
example_sentences.english: People who hurt animals are a failure as humans.

example_sentences.japanese: ミキは友達としては最高だ。
example_sentences.english: As a friend, Miki is awesome.

example_sentences.japanese: このゲーム機はＤＶＤプレイヤーとしても使えます。
example_sentences.english: You can use this game console as a DVD player.

example_sentences.japanese: これは会社としての目標です。
example_sentences.english: This is the goal as a company.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻としての役割をよく果たしてくれている。
example_sentences.english: She does well as a wife.

example_sentences.japanese: 挨拶は礼儀として必要です。
example_sentences.english: As a courtesy, greetings are important.

example_sentences.japanese: ジョチはチンギス・カンの長男として生まれた。
example_sentences.english: Jochi has been born as the first son of Genghis Khan.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の嫁さんは母として、そして妻として、本当にいい人だ。
example_sentences.english: As both a mother and as a wife, my wife is really a great person.

example_sentences.japanese: それは事実として受け止めるけど、感情的には納得できない。
example_sentences.english: I will accept that as a fact, but it hardly satisfies me emotionally.

example_sentences.japanese: これは私の想い出の品として大切に持っていてください。
example_sentences.english: Please keep it as a memento of me.

example_sentences.japanese: ここに来た証として、私たちの名前を書いておきましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's write down our names as proof that we were here.

example_sentences.japanese: このカンファレンスは日本文化を広めることを目的として行われます。
example_sentences.english: This conference will be held with the role of spreading Japanese culture.

example_sentences.japanese: マルボルク城は中世で最大の城の一つとして知られている。
example_sentences.english: Castle Malbork is known as one of the biggest castles from the Middle Ages.

example_sentences.japanese: 条件として悪くはないが、今はお金がないから契約できません。
example_sentences.english: For terms and conditions, they aren't bad, but because I don't have money now I can't enter the contract.

example_sentences.japanese: 文法は日本語の一番難しいところとして、学ぶ方法がなかなか見つからない。
example_sentences.english: For (something that is considered to be) the most difficult aspect of Japanese, it is hard to find resources for grammar.

example_sentences.japanese: タナカさんは友達としてはいい人なんだけど、先輩としてはよくない。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka-san is a nice person as a friend, but not as a senpai.

general_translation: (Even) considering, (Even) for
formation: Verb + にしてはNoun + にしては
casual_structure: Verb + にしてはNoun + にしては
explanation: A structure that goes off the consideration that (A) is a general truth, before elaborating that even for (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 子供にしては静かな方だ。
example_sentences.english: Considering (she) is a child, (she) is a quiet one.

example_sentences.japanese: 中卒にしては頭がいいけど、大卒の同級生と比べるとそうでもない。
example_sentences.english: He's smart considering he's only a middle school graduate, but compared to people his age who graduated from college, he's nothing special.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は俳優にしてはあまりイケメンじゃない。
example_sentences.english: Considering he is an actor, he is not very attractive.

example_sentences.japanese: 始めたばかりにしては結構じょうずだね。
example_sentences.english: Considering you have just started, you are considerably good.

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎にしてはコンビニがいっぱいあるね。
example_sentences.english: Considering that this is the countryside, there are many convenience stores.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は毎日漢字の勉強をしているにしては全然漢字を読めない。
example_sentences.english: For someone that studies kanji every day, he can't read it at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 新人にしてはよく働くけど、他と比べるとあまり働いていない。
example_sentences.english: For a new worker he works a lot, but compared to others, he doesn't work that much.

example_sentences.japanese: 力士にしては結構細いですね。
example_sentences.english: Considering he is a sumo wrestler, he is quite thin.

example_sentences.japanese: 猫にしては大きすぎませんか？
example_sentences.english: (Even) for a cat, isn't it too big?

example_sentences.japanese: うどんにしては随分細い麺だな。
example_sentences.english: Considering it's udon, these noodles are quite thin.

example_sentences.japanese: 昔話にしては、随分現実的な話ですね。
example_sentences.english: (Even) considering it is an old folk tale, it is quite a realistic story.

example_sentences.japanese: 夢にしてはかなりリアルだったから、泣いてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: It was quite realistic (even) for a dream, so I ended up crying. (even considering)

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎にしてはいい方ですよ、うちの家は。
example_sentences.english: Considering it's in the countryside, my house is decent.

example_sentences.japanese: （彼女は）政治家にしてはかなり若いから、少し不安ですね。
example_sentences.english: Considering (she) is a politician, (she) is quite young, so I am a bit anxious.

example_sentences.japanese: 初めてにしては随分上手に仕事をするね。
example_sentences.english: Considering it is your first time, you do quite well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は１０年間日本に住んでいるにしては、全く日本語をしゃべれない。
example_sentences.english: (Even) considering he has lived in Japan for 10 years, he can't speak a word of Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が初めて絵を描いたにしてはよくできたと思うんだけど…
example_sentences.english: Considering that (this) is the first time he has drawn a picture, I think that he did a good job...

example_sentences.japanese: ２月にしては暖かすぎる。こんな天気は異常だ。
example_sentences.english: Considering it is February, it's too warm. This kind of weather is out of the ordinary.

general_translation: Even though, Even if, Even when, Also
formation: Verb + にしても［い］Adjective + にしても［な］Adjective + にしてもNoun + にしても
casual_structure: Verb + にしても［い］Adjective + にしても［な］Adjective + にしてもNoun + にしても
explanation: A phrase that expresses that even if you go off the assumption that (A), (B) is still true.

example_sentences.japanese: テスラモデルＳにしても、この値段は高すぎる。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is a Tesla Model S, this price is too expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: パーティーに行くにしても、私はシャイだから一人で飲むことになる。
example_sentences.english: Even if I did go to a party, I am shy so I'd just end up drinking alone.

example_sentences.japanese: 冗談にしても、言っていいことと言ってはいけないことがある。
example_sentences.english: Even if it's a joke, there are things that are fine to say and things that you can't say.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事で忙しいにしても、連絡はしてください。
example_sentences.english: Even if you are busy with work, please at least contact me.

example_sentences.japanese: 今は怠惰な私にしても、元々こうだったわけではない。
example_sentences.english: Even though I'm being lazy now, this isn't what I was like originally.

example_sentences.japanese: ハイキングをするときは、どこに行くにしてもベルを持って行った方がいい。
example_sentences.english: No matter where you go hiking, you should take a bell with you.

example_sentences.japanese: もし近所のルールを守っていない人を見つけたら、誰に注意するにしても注意をしなければいけない。
example_sentences.english: In the case that you see someone not following the rules of the neighborhood, even if you're warning someone you don't know, you need to warn them.

example_sentences.japanese: ジュースがいっぱいの樽を頼むにしても、まだ足りないと思います。
example_sentences.english: Even if we order a barrel full of juice, I still think it won't be enough.

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪にしても、楽しい英語の勉強はできるはずだ。
example_sentences.english: Even if I were to have a cold, I would surely be able to study English, which is fun.

example_sentences.japanese: 言うにしても言い方というものがあるでしょ。
example_sentences.english: Even if you (decide to) say something, there is still something called manner of speech.

example_sentences.japanese: 分からないにしても、少しくらいは調べてくれてもいいじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: Even if you don't know, you can do a bit of research, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 理想を語るにしても、少しは現実を見てほしい。
example_sentences.english: Even if you are talking about ideals, I want you to take a look at reality.

example_sentences.japanese: すぐ始めるにしても、肝心の山田さんがいないと始められない。
example_sentences.english: Even if we were to start immediately, we cannot start when Mr. Yamada, who is essential, is not here.

example_sentences.japanese: 負けるにしても、全力で試合に臨むべきだ。
example_sentences.english: Even if you were to lose, you should still confront the match with your full strength.

example_sentences.japanese: 車を買うにしても、車庫が少し狭いから、小さいのを選ばなければ。
example_sentences.english: Even if I (decide to) buy a car, the garage is a bit small, so I have to choose a small one.

example_sentences.japanese: 勇者の生死は不明だ。いずれにしても、誰かが世界を救わなければいけないのだ。
example_sentences.english: The hero's life or death is uncertain. But in any case, someone has to save the world.

example_sentences.japanese: どこで暮らすにしても故郷を忘れる日は一日もなく、たまに泣いてしまいます。
example_sentences.english: Even if I were to live somewhere else, there would be not a single day that I forget my hometown, and I'd sometimes cry.

example_sentences.japanese: 何をするにしても手段が大切であり、手段を間違えると何も達成できません。
example_sentences.english: Even if you were to do something, the method is important, so if you make a mistake with the method then you won't achieve anything.

example_sentences.japanese: このプロジェクトが難しいとしても、クライアントのためにやらないといけない。
example_sentences.english: Even if this project is hard, we have to do it for the client. (Even though it is hard, we must do it for the client)

example_sentences.japanese: このプロジェクトが難しいにしても、締め切りまでには終わらせないといけない。
example_sentences.english: Even if this project is hard, we must finish it by the deadline. (Even if we go off that fact that it is hard, it must be finished by the deadline)

grammar_point: と言（い）うのは事実（じじつ）だ
general_translation: It is a fact that ~, There is no doubt that
formation: Phrase + (という) + のは事実（じじつ） + だ
casual_structure: Phrase + (という) + のは事実（じじつ） + だ
polite_structure: Phrase + (という) + のは事実（じじつ） + です
explanation: A structure highlighting that that which can be said is (A), is the truth.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が俳優だというのはじじつだ。
example_sentences.english: It is a fact that he is an actor.

example_sentences.japanese: この人が私の母親を殺したというのはじじつだ。
example_sentences.english: It is a fact that this person killed my mother.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女が弁護士だというのはじじつだ。
example_sentences.english: It is a fact that she is a lawyer.

example_sentences.japanese: 赤信号を無視したのは事実だ。
example_sentences.english: It is true that I ignored the red light.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女と仲直りしたのは事実だ。
example_sentences.english: It is a fact that I worked it out with my girlfriend.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女が二十歳だというのはじじつだ。
example_sentences.english: It is a fact that she is 20 years old.

example_sentences.japanese: 地球が丸いというのはじじつだ。
example_sentences.english: It is a fact that the earth is round.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼に前科があるというのはじじつだ。
example_sentences.english: It is a fact that he has a criminal history.

example_sentences.japanese: 父が病気だというのはじじつです。
example_sentences.english: It is a fact that my dad is ill.

example_sentences.japanese: 車が環境に良くないというのはじじつだ。
example_sentences.english: It is a fact that cars are not good for the environment.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕が１日１食生活をしているというのはじじつです。
example_sentences.english: It is a fact that I only eat once a day.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が来年引っ越すというのはじじつです。
example_sentences.english: It is a fact that I am moving next year.

example_sentences.japanese: あの政治家が賄賂を受け取ったというのはじじつだ。
example_sentences.english: There is no doubt that that politician received a bribe. (It is a fact that...)

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい細菌が発見されたというのはじじつだ。
example_sentences.english: It is a fact that a new bacterium has been discovered.

example_sentences.japanese: 盗難被害にあったというのはじじつだ。
example_sentences.english: There is no doubt that I have been robbed. (It is a fact that...)

example_sentences.japanese: 食料が不足しているというのはじじつだ。
example_sentences.english: There is no doubt that they do not have sufficient food. (It is a fact that...)

general_translation: Speaking in terms of, From the point of view of
formation: Noun + から言（い）うと(1)(1)から言（い）えば、 から言（い）って
casual_structure: Noun + から言（い）うと(1)(1)から言（い）えば、 から言（い）って
explanation: A phrase that speaks from (A), before explaining some point of view.

example_sentences.japanese: 法律からいうと、それは違反です。
example_sentences.english: Speaking in terms of the law, that is a crime.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の経験からいうと、このやり方が一番効率がいい。
example_sentences.english: Speaking from my experience, this way of doing it is the most efficient.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の立場からいえば、彼は絶対いつか成功する。
example_sentences.english: Speaking from my position, he will make it big one day.

example_sentences.japanese: この結果からいって、この計画はあまりよくありませんでした。
example_sentences.english: Speaking from these results, this plan was not that great.

example_sentences.japanese: 結論からいうと、失敗です。
example_sentences.english: Speaking in terms of results, it is a failure.

example_sentences.japanese: 値段からいうと、このコーヒーは高すぎるよ。
example_sentences.english: Speaking in terms of price, this coffee is too expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: 物価からいうと、この地域は住みやすいですね。
example_sentences.english: Speaking in terms of prices in general, this region is easy to live in.

example_sentences.japanese: 景色からいうと、あの山は最高だよ。
example_sentences.english: Speaking in terms of scenery, that mountain is the best.

example_sentences.japanese: 場所からいうと、あの家は悪くないと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: Speaking in terms of location, I think that that house is not too bad.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の経験からいうと、ゼミでは先生と仲良くなるべきだ。
example_sentences.english: From my experience's point of view, you ought to get along with teachers at seminars.

example_sentences.japanese: 成績からいうと入社は厳しいが、その人柄でなんとかなるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Speaking in terms of his grades, getting a job at a company will be hard, but his personality might land him a position somewhere.

example_sentences.japanese: 使いやすさからいうと、こっちのパソコンの方がいいと思います。
example_sentences.english: Speaking in terms of ease of use, I think this computer is better.

example_sentences.japanese: 実力からいうと、間違いなくメダルは取れると思う。
example_sentences.english: Speaking in terms of real ability, there is no doubt that he is capable of getting a medal.

example_sentences.japanese: 消費者の立場からいうと、値上げは好ましくないと言うことになる。
example_sentences.english: From a consumer standpoint perspective, price increases are not going to be favorable.

example_sentences.japanese: 飲みやすさからいうとこのピザ屋さんのワインより、昨日飲んだワインの方が美味しい。
example_sentences.english: Speaking in terms of palatableness, the wine we had last night is better than the wine at this pizzeria.

example_sentences.japanese: タクミからいうと、後輩のタケシ君は次の試合で勝てそうなの？
example_sentences.english: Speaking as Takumi, do you think your kouhai, Takeshi-kun can win in the next competition? (Unnatural)

example_sentences.japanese: タクミの立場からいうと後輩のタケシ君は次の試合で勝てそうなの？
example_sentences.english: Takumi, speaking from your position, do you think your kouhai, Takeshi-kun is going to win at the next competition? (Natural)

example_sentences.japanese: サトミの視点からいうと、あの人たちは採用しない方がいいという事ですか？
example_sentences.english: Satomi, from your point of view, are you saying that we should not recruit those people? (Natural)

example_sentences.japanese: 家のレイアウトから言うと、この家は３０年前に建てられた家だと思う。
example_sentences.english: Speaking from the layout of this house, I think it was built 30 years ago. (Not incorrect, but a little unnatural)

general_translation: To, For, Concerning
formation: Noun + に取（と）って
casual_structure: Noun + に取（と）って
explanation: A phrase that often gives someone's opinion, or their take on (A).

example_sentences.japanese: それは会社にとってもいいアイデアですね。
example_sentences.english: That is also a great idea for the company.

example_sentences.japanese: タケミにとって一番大切な人は誰ですか？
example_sentences.english: Takemi, who is the most important person to you?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は私にとって親みたいな存在です。
example_sentences.english: He is like a parent to me.

example_sentences.japanese: この石はタケル君にとって、宝物です。
example_sentences.english: To Takeru, this rock is a treasure.

example_sentences.japanese: 君にとって友達を作ることは簡単だ。
example_sentences.english: It is easy for you to make friends.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰にとっても親は大切です。
example_sentences.english: Parents are important for everyone.

example_sentences.japanese: 君にとっては簡単でも、僕には難しいよ。
example_sentences.english: It might be easy for you but it's difficult for me.

example_sentences.japanese: お父さんにとって、仕事は大切だ。
example_sentences.english: Your father's job is important to him.

example_sentences.japanese: このガソリンは安いけど、車にとってはよくないと思うな。
example_sentences.english: This gasoline is cheap but I don't think it's good for the cars.

example_sentences.japanese: 人生にとって大切なことは何かを考えています。
example_sentences.english: I am thinking of what is important for my life.

example_sentences.japanese: 人間にとって必要なのは、「愛すること」と「愛されること」だと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think it is necessary for humans 'to love' and 'to be loved'.

example_sentences.japanese: 動物にとって、動物園で暮らすのはかわいそうなことなのかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Living in a zoo might be cruel for animals.

example_sentences.japanese: 私にとって、君は化粧をする必要がないくらい美しいよ。
example_sentences.english: For me, you're so beautiful that it's not necessary for you to put on makeup.

example_sentences.japanese: 政治家にとっていいことが、国民にとっていつもいいことなわけではない。
example_sentences.english: What is good for politicians, is not always good for citizens.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供にとって、両親共働きというのはあまり良くないのかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: Both parents working, might not be a very good solution for children.

example_sentences.japanese: 私にとって一番大事な友達はあなたです。
example_sentences.english: You are the most important friend to me.

example_sentences.japanese: 私にとってあの会社は人を働かせすぎだと思います。
example_sentences.english: To me, I think that company makes people work too much.

general_translation: From the fact that
formation: Verb + ことから ［い］Adjective + ことから ［な］Adjective + な + ことから   Noun + の + ことから
casual_structure: Verb + ことから ［い］Adjective + ことから ［な］Adjective + な + ことから   Noun + の + ことから
explanation: A phrase that expresses the thing which is (A) as a fact, and then explains further from that.

example_sentences.japanese: 以上のことから、この結論に至りました。
example_sentences.english: From (the facts) above, we arrived at this conclusion.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな早い時間に妻が寝ていることから、今日は色々と大変だったと気づいた。
example_sentences.english: From the fact that my wife is sleeping at such an early time, I noticed that she was busy with many things today.

example_sentences.japanese: 家の家具が全部新しいことから、彼はここに引っ越してきたばかりだと分かった。
example_sentences.english: From the fact that all his furniture is new, I realized that he has just moved here.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が静かなことから、何か悪いことをしていると分かった。
example_sentences.english: From the fact that my kids were quiet, I knew that they were doing something bad.

example_sentences.japanese: これらのことからイベントを中止することに決めました。
example_sentences.english: From these facts, we have decided to cancel the event.

example_sentences.japanese: 「お父さん」と呼ばれていることから、子供がいるのだと分かった。
example_sentences.english: From the fact that he is being called 'dad', I discerned that he has children.

example_sentences.japanese: 指輪をしていることから、既婚者だと分かった。
example_sentences.english: I realized that he is married from the fact that he is wearing a ring.

example_sentences.japanese: 野球がとても上手なことから、将来は有名になりそうだ。
example_sentences.english: From the fact that he is really good at baseball, it seems like he will be famous one day.

example_sentences.japanese: 田代島は猫が多いことから、猫の島と呼ばれるようになった。
example_sentences.english: From the fact that there are many cats in Tashirojima, it came to be called 'Cat Island'.

example_sentences.japanese: フィルが一生懸命文法を勉強し始めたことから、彼が日本語の能力を高めようと思っていることに気がついた。
example_sentences.english: From the fact that Phil began intensely studying grammar, I realized that he was set on improving his Japanese language ability.

example_sentences.japanese: この城の城壁は白い鳥の翼のように見えることから、白鳥城と呼ばれるようになった。
example_sentences.english: From the fact that this castle's walls look like a white bird's wings, it has come to be called 'white bird castle'.

example_sentences.japanese: この靴は歩いてもあまり音がしないことから、英語でスニーカーと呼ばれている。「トゥ スニーク」というのは日本語で忍び寄るということです。
example_sentences.english: From the fact that these shoes produce little sound, they are called 'sneakers' in english. 'To sneak' is 'しのびよる' in Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯行現場で凶器が見つかったことから、被告は２５年の懲役を宣告された。
example_sentences.english: From the fact that a murder weapon was found at the crime scene, the defendant was sentenced to 25 years in prison.

example_sentences.japanese: 無理して学校へ行くことで体調を崩すことがある。このことから、学校へ行くことがいつも正しいとは言えない。
example_sentences.english: There are times where insisting on going to school can lead to health deterioration. From this fact, you cannot say that it is always right to go to school.

example_sentences.japanese: この種のゲームは机の上で行われることから、英語でテーブルトップゲームと呼ばれている。
example_sentences.english: From the fact that this kind of game is played on the top of the table, it is called a 'tabletop game' in English.

example_sentences.japanese: いい先生から数学を学んだことから、私も数学の先生になりたいと思うようになった。
example_sentences.english: From the fact that I learned math from a good teacher, I too came to want to be a math teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: コーヒーが冷たいことから、コーヒーが淹れられたのは結構前だと分かる。
example_sentences.english: From the fact that the coffee is cold, you can tell that it was poured quite a while ago.

example_sentences.japanese: コーヒーが冷たいことだから、コーヒーが淹れられたのは結構前だと分かる。
example_sentences.english: Since coffee is a cold thing, you can tell that it was poured quite a while ago. (Unnatural Japanese)

general_translation: ...is more of a... than a..., Rather than saying that...
formation: Verb + というより［い］Adjective + というより［な］Adjective + （だ） + というよりNoun + （だ） + というより
casual_structure: Verb + というより［い］Adjective + というより［な］Adjective + （だ） + というよりNoun + （だ） + というより
explanation: A grammar point that presents (A) and then makes another more correct statement. Rather than saying (A), (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は暖かいというより暑い。
example_sentences.english: It is hot rather than warm today.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は暇だというより、なにをすればいいか分からないだけだ。
example_sentences.english: Rather than having nothing to do, I just don't know what I should be doing.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は仕事をしているというより、仕事をさせられている感じがする。
example_sentences.english: Rather than saying that he is working, it seems like he is being made to work.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の天井が低いというより、あなたの身長が高いだけだと思う。
example_sentences.english: Rather than Japanese ceilings being low, I think you are just tall.

example_sentences.japanese: ここは公園というより、小さい広場みたいな物だ。
example_sentences.english: Rather than calling this a park, it is something more like a small field. (だ used at the end rather than following 'park', as 'field' is the actual state that the speaker considers true)

example_sentences.japanese: あの人はかわいいというより綺麗。
example_sentences.english: That person is beautiful rather than cute.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は聡明というよりずる賢い人です。
example_sentences.english: Rather than saying that he is wise, he is cunning.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は技術者というより芸術家だ。
example_sentences.english: He is more of an artist than an engineer.

example_sentences.japanese: これは悲しさというより後悔に近い。
example_sentences.english: Rather than saying that this is sorrow, it is closer to regret.

example_sentences.japanese: それは理由というより言い訳ですよね？
example_sentences.english: Rather than calling it a reason, it's an excuse, right?

example_sentences.japanese: これはサッカーというよりフットサルのコートみたいだ。
example_sentences.english: This appears to be more of a futsal court than a soccer pitch.

example_sentences.japanese: 「嫌い」というより「好きではない」と言った方が正確だ。
example_sentences.english: Rather than saying 'I hate it', it is more accurate to say 'I don't like it'.

example_sentences.japanese: これは草というより、竹みたいだ。
example_sentences.english: Rather than saying that this is grass/weeds, it looks like bamboo.

example_sentences.japanese: 来月というより来年と言った方がいいかな。
example_sentences.english: Rather than saying next month, maybe it is better to say next year.

example_sentences.japanese: オニズカさんは先生というより友達だと思っています。
example_sentences.english: I think of you (Onizuka-san) as more of a friend than a teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日というより、一週間に五回運動をすると言った方が正しい。
example_sentences.english: Rather than saying every day, I would say it's more correct to say that I exercise 5 days a week.

example_sentences.japanese: マサミさんは綺麗というより、かわいい。
example_sentences.english: Masami is more cute than beautiful.

example_sentences.japanese: その話がつまらないというより、興味がないだけ。
