example_sentences.english: It's not that the story is boring, it's just more that I have no interest in it.

general_translation: Not only but also, Let alone, Not to mention, Of course
formation: Noun (A) + はもちろん + Noun (B) + も(1)(1) さえ
casual_structure: Noun (A) + はもちろん + Noun (B) + も(1)(1) さえ
explanation: A phrase indicating that (A) is of course true in general, but even the more surprising (B) is true too.

example_sentences.japanese: 平日はもちろん、土日も働いている。
example_sentences.english: I work not only on weekdays, but also weekends.

example_sentences.japanese: パソコンのことはもちろん、電化製品の事ならなんでも聞いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please ask me anything, not only about computers but also other electronics.

example_sentences.japanese: 数学はもちろん、学校の科目を全て一人で教えることができる人を探している。
example_sentences.english: We are looking for someone not only who can teach math, but every subject in this school by themselves.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は日本語はもちろん、韓国語も話すことができます。
example_sentences.english: Not only can she speak Japanese, but she can also speak Korean.

example_sentences.japanese: この作家の本はもちろん、歌もうまいから人気がある。
example_sentences.english: This author is popular, not only because of his book, but also because he is a good singer.

example_sentences.japanese: ここのそば屋はそばはもちろん、カレーも美味しい。
example_sentences.english: This soba restaurant not only has delicious soba, but also delicious curry.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は、英語はもちろん、日本語も話せる。
example_sentences.english: He is not only able to speak in English, but also in Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は、スマホはもちろん、ガラケーも持っていません。
example_sentences.english: Not only a smartphone, dad doesn't even have a flip-phone.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強はもちろん、運動もできるのだからすごい人だ。
example_sentences.english: He is an amazing person because he is not only good in academics, but also in sports.

example_sentences.japanese: 椅子はもちろん、家具全般取り扱っています。
example_sentences.english: I will not only handle the chairs, but also all of the furniture.

example_sentences.japanese: あの高級車はシートやフロントガラスはもちろんドアミラーも温められます。
example_sentences.english: In that high-class car, not only are the seats and the windshield heated, but also the side mirrors.

example_sentences.japanese: チョコやあんこはもちろん、甘いものならなんでも好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like not only chocolate or bean-paste, but also anything that is sweet.

example_sentences.japanese: パーティーに、家族はもちろん、友達も誘って来てください。
example_sentences.english: Please invite not only your family, but your friends as well to the party.

example_sentences.japanese: 現在のテレビは、映画を観ることはもちろんネットサーフィンもできる。
example_sentences.english: On modern TVs you can not only watch movies but you can also surf the internet.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい仕事を探す時は、給料はもちろん、それ以外の条件も考えます。
example_sentences.english: When I look for a new job, I consider not only salary, but also other conditions.

example_sentences.japanese: 人生いい時はもちろん、悪い時も助け合って生きていこう。
example_sentences.english: Let's live our lives by helping each other not only during the good times, but also during the hard times.

general_translation: Not only...but also..., Starting with
formation: Noun + をはじめ(として)Noun + をはじめとする + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + をはじめ(として)Noun + をはじめとする + Noun
explanation: A phrase that expresses logical or planned progressions that start from (A).

example_sentences.japanese: スーツをはじめ、シャツや靴も新しくした。
example_sentences.english: Starting with a suit, I also upgraded my shirts and shoes.

example_sentences.japanese: この会社は車をはじめ、ロケットなども作っている。
example_sentences.english: Not only does this company make cars, but it also makes rockets.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の近所には、公園をはじめ、博物館など、プラネタリウムがある。
example_sentences.english: Not only is there a park in my neighborhood, but also a museum, and a planetarium.

example_sentences.japanese: ストリートファッションはアメリカをはじめとして、世界中に進出していく。
example_sentences.english: With America as the starting point, street fashion spread all over the world.

example_sentences.japanese: この商品には卵をはじめとする多くのアレルゲンが含まれている。
example_sentences.english: Starting with eggs, there are many allergens in this product. (Eggs being the primary allergen)

example_sentences.japanese: 小説をはじめ、本なら何でも読みます。
example_sentences.english: Starting with short novels, I read all kinds of books.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬をはじめ、様々な動物を飼うようになった。
example_sentences.english: Starting with dogs, I have come to raise various animals.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京をはじめ、国内観光ツアーに行きます。
example_sentences.english: I am going on a countrywide tour starting in Tokyo.

example_sentences.japanese: ヨーロッパをはじめ、世界中を旅行してみたいです。
example_sentences.english: Starting in Europe, I want to travel the world.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生をはじめ、生徒たちにも教えてあげてください。
example_sentences.english: Please teach teachers, as well as students.

example_sentences.japanese: パソコンをはじめ、その他の機器も導入するつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: I plan to set up various devices, starting with computers.

example_sentences.japanese: この国はミサイルをはじめ、核兵器まで開発している。
example_sentences.english: This country is developing arms, starting with missiles and moving to nuclear weapons.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長をはじめ、社員も皆同じ目標を持ってがんばっています。
example_sentences.english: Starting with the company president, the employees are also doing their best with common, firm goals in mind.

example_sentences.japanese: 担任の先生をはじめ、先生方には本当にお世話になりました。
example_sentences.english: Starting with my homeroom teacher, I would like to thank my teachers for taking care of me.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語をはじめ、韓国語と中国語も学びたい。
example_sentences.english: Starting with Japanese, I would also like to learn Korean and Chinese.

example_sentences.japanese: 漫才をはじめとする日本のいろいろな「お笑い」に興味を持ち始めた。
example_sentences.english: I have taken interest in various kinds of Japanese comedy, starting with 'manzai'.

general_translation: For the first time, Not until, Only after, Only when, Only because
formation: Verb［て］+ はじめて
casual_structure: Verb［て］+ はじめて
explanation: An expression that highlights that not until after the first time of (A), did (B) happen.

example_sentences.japanese: うしなってはじめて、その価値が分かりました。
example_sentences.english: Only after I lost it, did I understand its value.

example_sentences.japanese: 好きなバンドのコンサートに行ってはじめて、歌手の人が男の人だと気づいた。
example_sentences.english: It wasn't until I went to a concert of my favorite band that I realized the singer was a man.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生になってはじめて、先生の大変さが分かった。
example_sentences.english: It was only upon becoming a teacher, that I understood how hard it is to be one.

example_sentences.japanese: 駅にある時刻表を見てはじめて、土日には電車が来ないことを知った。
example_sentences.english: I didn't know that trains don't come during the weekends, until I saw the train schedule.

example_sentences.japanese: やってみてはじめて、難しさを痛感しました。
example_sentences.english: Only after I tried it, did I fully realize the degree of difficulty.

example_sentences.japanese: 話をきいてみてはじめて、君の苦労を知った。
example_sentences.english: Only after I heard your story, did I understand what you had been through.

example_sentences.japanese: テレビをみてはじめて、地震があったことを知った。
example_sentences.english: It wasn't until I saw what was on TV, that I became aware of the fact that an earthquake had occured.

example_sentences.japanese: 指摘されてはじめて、寝癖がついていることに気づいた。
example_sentences.english: Only after it was pointed out, did I notice that I had bed hair.

example_sentences.japanese: 時計をみてはじめて、寝坊したことに気づいた。
example_sentences.english: Only after I saw the clock, did I notice that I had overslept.

example_sentences.japanese: 親になってはじめて、親の大変さが分かりました。
example_sentences.english: It wasn't until I became a parent, that I understood the hardships of parenthood.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を勉強してはじめて、他の国の言語で話す面白さを知った。
example_sentences.english: I didn't know how fun it was to speak in other languages until I started studying Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 実物をみてはじめて、その素晴らしさを実感できました。
example_sentences.english: Only after I had seen the real thing, did I actually realize how amazing it was.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬をかってはじめて、ペットを飼うには責任が伴うことを知った。
example_sentences.english: It wasn't until I got a dog that I understood the responsibility required to keep a pet.

example_sentences.japanese: 京都をおとずれてはじめて、京都が歴史の古い町だと分かった。
example_sentences.english: Only after visiting Kyoto did I understand that it is a city with a long history.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本にきてはじめて、日本文化に興味を持った。
example_sentences.english: I didn't have any interest in Japanese culture until I came to Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: カレンダーを見て始めて今日は休日だってことを知った。
example_sentences.english: Commencing with checking the calendar, I noticed that today is a holiday. (Unnatural kanji choice)

example_sentences.japanese: カレンダーを見てはじめて今日が休日だってことを知った。
example_sentences.english: Only after checking the calendar did I notice that it is a holiday today.

general_translation: Even
formation: Noun + (で) + さえNoun + Particle + さえVerb + こと(1) + さえ + (する)Verb［stem］+ さえ + (する)Verb［て］+ さえ +(いる)(1) の
casual_structure: Noun + (で) + さえNoun + Particle + さえVerb + こと(1) + さえ + (する)Verb［stem］+ さえ + (する)Verb［て］+ さえ +(いる)(1) の
explanation: A structure that shows that the very surprising (A) can even be included in a group.

example_sentences.japanese: 富士山の頂上は夏でさえ寒い。
example_sentences.english: It is cold on the summit of Mt. Fuji even in summer.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなの放っておいてさえいたら、すぐ直るよ。
example_sentences.english: Even if you leave it as it is, it will get well quickly.

example_sentences.japanese: 上級者の彼でさえ出来ないのに、あなたが出来るわけがないでしょう。
example_sentences.english: Even someone in the advanced class level can't do it, there is no way you can do it.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は親にさえ知らせずに彼氏と結婚をした。
example_sentences.english: She got married to her boyfriend, without even telling her parents.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はストレスのせいで、晩飯を食べることさえ出来なくなった。
example_sentences.english: Due to him being stressed, he couldn't even eat dinner.

example_sentences.japanese: タナカ君は酷くない？彼女を傷つけたのに、謝りさえしなかったらしいよ。
example_sentences.english: Don't you think Tanaka-kun is a jerk? He hurt his girlfriend, but I heard he didn't even apologize.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな初歩的なことは、子供でさえ知っている。
example_sentences.english: Even children know things that basic.

example_sentences.japanese: 小さい戦いさえ、私はしたことがない。
example_sentences.english: I've never even been in a small fight.

example_sentences.japanese: あのことについてさえ知っているんです。
example_sentences.english: I even know about that thing.

example_sentences.japanese: 家族さえも応援してくれないんです。
example_sentences.english: Even my family doesn't support me.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼からさえプレゼントをもらったわよ！
example_sentences.english: I got a present even from him!

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のいたずらがひどすぎて、同情する余地さえない。
example_sentences.english: His prank went too far, I don't even feel sorry for him.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻は僕の声さえ聞こえないほど集中してテレビを見ている。
example_sentences.english: My wife is so focused on watching TV that she can't even hear my voice.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は親友の僕の意見さえ無視するほど傲慢になってしまった…
example_sentences.english: He has become so arrogant that he even ignores advice from his best friend (me).

example_sentences.japanese: 「タダであげる」と言われても、こんな読む価値さえない本はいりません。
example_sentences.english: I don't need a book that is not even worth reading, even if I am told 'I'll give it to you for free'.

example_sentences.japanese: このペット型ロボットは走れるだけではなく、飛びさえするそうだ。
example_sentences.english: I heard that this pet robot can not only run but even jump.

example_sentences.japanese: 祖父は若い頃、戦時中に遠くまで戦闘に向かった。日本にさえ戦いに行ったことがある。
example_sentences.english: When my grandfather was young, he fought in far off lands during the war. He even went to Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: このレベルはプロでさえ難しいというのに、よくできたね。
example_sentences.english: I am impressed you were able to do this, let alone that it is difficult even for professionals.

example_sentences.japanese: トムがこんなに漢字を知っているのは凄いと思うよ。日本人でさえ漢字は難しいのに。
example_sentences.english: Tom, I think it is impressive that you know this many kanji. Not to mention that it is difficult even for Japanese people.

general_translation: If only…then, As long as..., Provided..., Only thing ... needs for ... is ...
formation: Verb［stem］+ さえ + すればVerb［て］+ さえ + いればNoun + さえ + Verb［ば］［い］Adjective［く］+ さえ + あればNoun + さえ + ［い］Adjective［ば］［な］Adjective + （で） + さえ + あれば
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ さえ + すればVerb［て］+ さえ + いればNoun + さえ + Verb［ば］［い］Adjective［く］+ さえ + あればNoun + さえ + ［い］Adjective［ば］［な］Adjective + （で） + さえ + あれば
explanation: A strong, hypothetical phrase that expresses (A) as being all that is required for (B).

example_sentences.japanese: この薬を毎日飲みさえすれば、すぐに治りますよ。
example_sentences.english: As long as you drink this medicine every day, it will heal quickly.

example_sentences.japanese: もっと若い頃からお金を貯めてさえいれば、今頃デカい家を買えてたかも。
example_sentences.english: If only I had saved up money since I was young, by now, I would have been able to buy a big house.

example_sentences.japanese: あの背が高い人さえ横にずれてくれれば、ちゃんと見えるのにな。
example_sentences.english: If only that tall person moved to the side, (then) I would be able to see.

example_sentences.japanese: タナカさんは若くさえあれば、あんな人でも雇う。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka-san will hire anyone, so long as they are young.

example_sentences.japanese: 家の前の道さえ広ければＳＵＶが買えたのに。
example_sentences.english: I would have been able to buy an SUV, if only the street in front of my house was bigger.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は静かでさえあればどこでも寝れます。
example_sentences.english: As long as it is quiet, I can sleep anywhere.

example_sentences.japanese: バンドメンバー募集中。ギターさえ弾けたら誰でもオッケーです。
example_sentences.english: Looking for a new band member. Anyone is okay, so long as you can play the guitar.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本で英語さえ話せたら、どこでも働けます。
example_sentences.english: As long as you can speak English in Japan, you can work anywhere.

example_sentences.japanese: 妹は暇さえあれば、運動する。
example_sentences.english: As long as my little sister has free time, she will exercise.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は自分さえよければ、いいと思っている。
example_sentences.english: He thinks that as long as it is good for him, it is good (for everyone). (only if)

example_sentences.japanese: 天気さえよければテニスできるのに…
example_sentences.english: If only the weather was good, then I would be able to play tennis, but...

example_sentences.japanese: 君さえいれば、他には何もいらない。
example_sentences.english: I don't need anything else, as long as I have you. (if only you exist)

example_sentences.japanese: 機会さえあれば、会えるのに…
example_sentences.english: If only there was a chance, then I would meet him...

example_sentences.japanese: インターネットさえあれば、だいたいのことは調べられますよ。
example_sentences.english: As long as you have an internet connection, then you can look up almost everything. (if only)

example_sentences.japanese: 参加の意志さえあれば、軍隊に入ることができる。
example_sentences.english: As long as you are willing to join the army, you can get in. (if only...)

example_sentences.japanese: 責任を持った生活さえできればボランティアになることができる。
example_sentences.english: As long as someone can be responsible, then that person can be a volunteer. (if only ~ then)

example_sentences.japanese: 雨さえふらなければ、あの試合は僕たちの勝ちだったのに…
example_sentences.english: If only it hadn't rained, then we would have won the match.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強さえすれば、もう少しいい点が取れますよ。
example_sentences.english: As long as you study, you will improve your score a little. (if only ~ then)

example_sentences.japanese: 死体さえ発見できれば、警察が解決をする。
example_sentences.english: Provided the police can find the body (then) they will solve the case. (if only..)

example_sentences.japanese: 生きてさえいれば、きっとまた出会えるさ。
example_sentences.english: As long as we are alive, we will surely see each other again. (if only ~ then)

general_translation: Used to
formation: Verb［た］+ ものだ
casual_structure: Verb［た］+ ものだ
polite_structure: Verb［た］+ ものです
explanation: A strong expression that says that which is (A) used to be a certain way in the past, often with a nuance of being nostalgic or reminiscing.

example_sentences.japanese: 若い頃は、いろんな苦労をしたものだ。
example_sentences.english: I used to have lots of hardships when I was young.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の頃はよく先生に怒られたものだ。
example_sentences.english: I used to get yelled at by the teacher often when I was still a kid.

example_sentences.japanese: 昔はよく親父と釣りに行ったものだ。
example_sentences.english: I often used to go fishing with my father in the past.

example_sentences.japanese: 若い頃は色々と苦労したものだ。
example_sentences.english: When I was young, I used to suffer a lot.

example_sentences.japanese: 小学生の頃は毎日学校に行ったものだ。
example_sentences.english: I used to go to school everyday when I was an elementary student. (Unnatural, as this is a normal event)

example_sentences.japanese: 昔は毎日のように親父とけんかをしたものだ。
example_sentences.english: In the past I fought with my father every day. (Natural, as this is a meaningful event)

example_sentences.japanese: 多分子供の頃に食べたことがある。
example_sentences.english: I may have eaten this when I was a kid. (Unimportant)

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の頃はよく、神社で遊んだ事がある。
example_sentences.english: When I was a kid, I played at the shrine a lot. (Potentially important, but not in this speaker's opinion)

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の頃はよく海に泳ぎにいったものだ。
example_sentences.english: I used to go swimming in the ocean a lot when I was a child.

example_sentences.japanese: 昔はよく、車を運転して遠くにでかけたものだ。
example_sentences.english: A long time ago, I often used to go out and take long drives.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の頃は授業中、よく居眠りをしたものだ。
example_sentences.english: When I was a child, I used to nod off a lot in the middle of class.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が子どもの頃、よく父に映画を見に連れていってもらったものだ。
example_sentences.english: Dad used to take me to the movies when I was a child.

example_sentences.japanese: 小学生の頃は雪が降るたびに、必ず雪だるまをつくったものだ。
example_sentences.english: I used to make a snowman every time it snowed when I was in elementary school.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供のころ、父親と様々な教科書を読みながら田舎をあるいたものだ。
example_sentences.english: As a child, I used to walk through the countryside while reading various textbooks with my father.

example_sentences.japanese: 昔は井戸から水をくんだものだが、今は水道を出すだけでいい。
example_sentences.english: People used to take their water from wells, but now you can just get it (directly) from the water supply.

example_sentences.japanese: 昔、母親は寝る前にはほとんど毎晩絵本を読んでくれたものだ。
example_sentences.english: Long ago, my mom used to read me picture books almost every night before going to bed.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏休みは友達のクリスと彼の別荘に行っていろいろあそんだものだ。
example_sentences.english: During summer vacation I used to go with my friend Chris to his summer house and would play a lot.

example_sentences.japanese: 今はこの場所はガソリンスタンドになっているけど、昔はここには図書館があってよくそこで本をよんだものだ。
example_sentences.english: This place is a gas station now, but in the past there was a library here and I often used to read there.

example_sentences.japanese: この庭には１５年前までは桜があって、昔は家族で花見をしたものだ。
example_sentences.english: A cherry tree was in this garden until 15 years ago, and in the past I used to look at it with my family.

general_translation: Well, Well then
formation: さて + (New Topic) Phrase
casual_structure: さて + (New Topic) Phrase
explanation: A short sentence starter typically used to change topic, or start talking about more important matters.

example_sentences.japanese: さて、順番に並べましたか。
example_sentences.english: Well then, have you lined up in order?

example_sentences.japanese: さて、そろそろ出ますか。
example_sentences.english: Well then, let's head off soon.

example_sentences.japanese: さて、とりあえず乾杯しましょう。
example_sentences.english: Well, first things first, let's have a toast.

example_sentences.japanese: さて、出発してもいいでしょうか。
example_sentences.english: Well then, may I take off?

example_sentences.japanese: さて、行きましょうか。
example_sentences.english: Well then, shall we go?

example_sentences.japanese: さて、準備はできましたか。
example_sentences.english: Well then, are you ready?

example_sentences.japanese: さて、次のテーマは何にしますか？
example_sentences.english: Well then, what would you like for the next theme?

example_sentences.japanese: さて、そろそろお昼にしましょうか？
example_sentences.english: Well then, shall we have lunch now?

example_sentences.japanese: さて、雑談はこれくらいにして、本題に入りましょうか？
example_sentences.english: Well then, enough chit chat. Shall we get straight to the point?

example_sentences.japanese: さて、冗談はそれくらいにして、真面目に答えてもらえますか？
example_sentences.english: Well, can you please stop joking now and give me a serious answer?

example_sentences.japanese: さて、そろそろ実験を始めるときだ。
example_sentences.english: Well, it is about time to start the experiment.

example_sentences.japanese: さて、手紙に何を書きましょう？思いつきましたか？
example_sentences.english: Well, what should we write on the letter? Did you come up with anything?

example_sentences.japanese: さて、今日はどんなお弁当だろう？楽しみだ。
example_sentences.english: Well then, what is my lunchbox like today? I am excited.

example_sentences.japanese: さて、お金がいくら溜まったか数えてみよう。
example_sentences.english: Well, let's count how much money we have saved.

example_sentences.japanese: 扨、この問題の答えが分かる人はいますか。
example_sentences.english: Now, is there anyone here that knows the answer to this question?

example_sentences.japanese: 偖、その荷物をこの箱の上においてください。
example_sentences.english: Now, please place that luggage on top of this box.

general_translation: Rather, Instead, Over
formation: むしろ + (Preferred Choice) Phrase
casual_structure: むしろ + (Preferred Choice) Phrase
explanation: A phrase used to say rather than (A), (B), often with the nuance that (B) is preferable.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼よりもむしろあなたに来てほしい。
example_sentences.english: I'd rather you come than him.

example_sentences.japanese: 何でそっちが怒ってるの？むしろこっちが怒りたいよ。
example_sentences.english: Why are you mad? I want to be the one that is mad instead. (It would be preferable if I was mad, because you're the one that is wrong)

example_sentences.japanese: むしろ、安い方を買った方がいいとおもう。
example_sentences.english: Buying a cheaper one would be better instead.

example_sentences.japanese: 車をリースするより、むしろ中古の車を買った方が安く済む。
example_sentences.english: Instead of leasing a car, it would be cheaper if you bought a used one.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺はＭＭＯよりむしろシングルプレイヤーのゲームの方が好きだ。
example_sentences.english: Rather than MMOs, I like single player games more.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕はコーヒーよりむしろ紅茶が飲みたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to drink tea rather than the coffee.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日よりむしろ今日行きたいんですが、駄目ですか？
example_sentences.english: I want to go today rather than tomorrow. Is that OK?

example_sentences.japanese: 韓国に行くよりむしろ日本に行きたい。
example_sentences.english: Rather than going to Korea, I'd go to Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: 事態はむしろ好転してきたように思える。
example_sentences.english: Rather, I think that the situation is changing for the better.

example_sentences.japanese: 都会よりむしろ田舎の方が好きだ。
example_sentences.english: I prefer the countryside over the city.

example_sentences.japanese: 友人にするなら、賑やかな人よりむしろ無口なくらいの人がいい。
example_sentences.english: Rather than a lively person as a friend, a silent person is better.

example_sentences.japanese: 一緒に悪口を言うより、むしろ悪口を言われる方がいい。
example_sentences.english: Instead of bad-mouthing together, you both should be the ones getting insulted.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行は楽しかったと言うより、むしろ疲れてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Rather than saying that the trip was exciting, I would say that it was tiring.

example_sentences.japanese: この問題は、力よりむしろ頭を使わないと解決しません。
example_sentences.english: This problem cannot be solved with physical strength, rather it requires that you use your head.

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪を予防したいなら、病院に行くよりむしろ家に一人でいる方がいい。
example_sentences.english: If you want to protect yourself from catching a cold, you should stay at home rather than go to the hospital.

example_sentences.japanese: 先に出発する電車に乗るより、むしろ次の急行電車に乗った方が早く着く。
example_sentences.english: You will arrive more quickly if you catch the next express train rather than the train that departs earlier.

example_sentences.japanese: むしろ、そっちに謝ってほしいよ。
example_sentences.english: Preferably, I want you to apologize. (Rather than me, it would be better if you apologized)

example_sentences.japanese: むしろ、先生に聞いてみた方がいいんじゃない？
example_sentences.english: Preferably, wouldn't it be better to ask the teacher? (The teacher will give a much more preferable answer than me)

general_translation: In short, To sum up, In other words
formation: Phrase (A)。つまり + (Summary) Phrase (B)
casual_structure: Phrase (A)。つまり + (Summary) Phrase (B)
explanation: A phrase used for summarizing that packs information into something smaller.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日何時でも良いんだって。つまり、夜遅くなっても良いらしい。
example_sentences.english: They said anytime tomorrow is good. To sum up, it seems that even late at night is ok.

example_sentences.japanese: ハマサキさんはまた何も言わずに休んだのですか？つまり、また無断欠勤という事ですね。
example_sentences.english: Hamasaki-san didn't come to work without saying anything again? In other words, he ditched work again, didn't he?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼氏と本当に別れたの？つまり、もうあんな奴と関わらなくていいということ？
example_sentences.english: Did you really break up with your boyfriend? In other words, that means we don't have to deal with him anymore?

example_sentences.japanese: また誰か辞めたんですか？つまり、今すぐ新しい人を見付けないといけないという事ですね。
example_sentences.english: Someone quit again ? In other words, we need to find a new person as soon as possible, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいつも約束を破る。つまり、私のこと好きじゃないよね。
example_sentences.english: He's always breaking his promises to me. In other words it seems that he isn't fond of me, right?

example_sentences.japanese: この車は電気自動車です。つまり、ガソリンが要らないです。
example_sentences.english: This is an electric car. In other words it doesn't need gasoline.

example_sentences.japanese: つまりそれはどういうことですか？もっと簡単に説明してください。
example_sentences.english: To sum up, what do you mean? Please explain it in a more simple manner.

example_sentences.japanese: 今は失業しています。つまり、あまりお金がないということです。
example_sentences.english: He is unemployed now. In other words he doesn't have very much money.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「 問題が起きました。」Ｂ：「つまり、何が言いたいんですか？」
example_sentences.english: A: 'We have a problem.' B: 'In short, what are you trying to say?'

example_sentences.japanese: 長々と説明したけど、結論を言うと、つまりそれは失敗だったということだ。
example_sentences.english: I gave a very long explanation but, in short, we concluded that it was a failure.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「言われたようにバッグにお金を入れてゴミ箱に置いてきたんだ。でも約束してた場所に誰もいなかったんだよ。」 Ｂ：「つまりあの人たちに騙されたということなの？」
example_sentences.english: A: 'He did as he was told to, he put money into a bag, and then left it in the trash can. However, there was no one at the agreed upon spot.' B: 'To sum up, that means he was tricked by those people?'

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は仕事です。つまり、一緒に行くのは無理だということです。
example_sentences.english: I have work tomorrow. In other words, we can't go together.

example_sentences.japanese: この手紙では彼らがそのことに関心がないと書かれている。つまり不採用ということだ。
example_sentences.english: In this letter, it is written that they are not interested. In short, it means I was rejected.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「君...取引は駄目だったよ。」 Ｂ：「つまりそれは僕のせいだと言いたいの？」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Hey, the deal was a failure!' B: 'To sum up, you are saying that I am to blame?'

example_sentences.japanese: 右からでも左からでもあの道に出る。つまり、どちらから行っても同じだよ。
example_sentences.english: You'll reach that road whether you go from the right or from the left. In short, it'll be the same no matter what direction you go from.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたは昨日一日中家でゲームをして、家の事は何もしなかったってことですね。つまり一日中ダラダラしていたという事ですね。
example_sentences.english: You are saying that you were at home playing video games without doing any chores yesterday. Condensed, you were being lazy. (In short)

general_translation: In other words, That is, Namely
formation: すなわち + Phrase
casual_structure: すなわち + Phrase
explanation: A structure showing that something is namely (A), by offering summarized information which is in concordance with what was previously stated.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は肉を食べない。すなわち菜食主義者だ。
example_sentences.english: I don't eat meat. In other words, I am a vegetarian.

example_sentences.japanese: この人は私の妻のお母さんです。すなわち、義理の母です。
example_sentences.english: This person is my wife's mother. In other words, my mother in law.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はゲームしてお金を稼いでいます。すなわち、プロゲーマーです。
example_sentences.english: I get paid for playing video games. In other words, I am a professional gamer.

example_sentences.japanese: 和食、すなわち焼き魚やお味噌汁のようなものが食べられるお店に行きたいんです。
example_sentences.english: I want to go to a restaurant where I can eat Japanese food, namely grilled fish, miso soup and the like.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は学校の先生、すなわち教育者だ。
example_sentences.english: He is a school teacher, that is, an educator.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は私の母の弟の息子、すなわち従兄弟です。
example_sentences.english: He is my mother's brother's son. In other words, he is my cousin.

example_sentences.japanese: ５割引きの商品とは、すなわち元の値段の半額ということだ。
example_sentences.english: A product that is 50% off is, in other words, half off.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は将来、子供たちに物事を教える職業に就きたいです。すなわち、学校の先生になりたいのです。
example_sentences.english: In the future, I'd like to take up the profession of teaching various things to kids. Namely, I'd like to become a school teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の議会は二院制、すなわち衆議院と参議院です。
example_sentences.english: The National Diet of Japan consists of two Houses, namely the House of Representatives and the House of Councilors.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は私の弟の妻、すなわち義理の妹です。
example_sentences.english: She is my brother's wife, that is, my sister in law.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はこの会社で最も偉い人、すなわち社長だ。
example_sentences.english: He is the most important person in the company. In other words he is the CEO.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人はお金をもらわずにこの辺りの掃除をしている。すなわちボランティアだ。
example_sentences.english: That person cleans around here without receiving money. In other words, that person is a volunteer.

example_sentences.japanese: オレは歌を歌ってお金をもらっている。すなわちミュージシャンだ。
example_sentences.english: I earn money by singing songs. In other words, I am a musician.

example_sentences.japanese: この会社では、兼業、すなわち二つの仕事をかけ持ちして働くことを禁止しています。
example_sentences.english: In this company, you are not allowed to have a side job, that is, to work for two companies at the same time.

example_sentences.japanese: この車はもう動かないです。すなわち廃車です。
example_sentences.english: This car does not run anymore. In other words, it is a decommissioned car.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は僕の父の弟です。つまり叔父です。
example_sentences.english: He is my father's brother. In other words, he is my uncle.

general_translation: All the more, On the contrary, Conversely
formation: Phrase (A) + かえって + Phrase (B)
casual_structure: Phrase (A) + かえって + Phrase (B)
explanation: A word used to express that rather than (A), (B). Can be seen as revoking or taking back the initial (A), due to (B) being more correct.

example_sentences.japanese: 欲張るとかえって損をしますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you are greedy, you'll lose all the more.

example_sentences.japanese: 手伝ってくれてるのはありがたいけど、かえって邪魔になってるからあっちに行ってくれる？ごめんね。
example_sentences.english: I am grateful that you are helping me, but putting that aside, since you are in the way, can you go over there please? I'm sorry.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんを元気にするつもりだったけど、かえって怒らせてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I was supposed to make my mom happy, but rather than that I actually made her angry.

example_sentences.japanese: 「やれ」と言われると、かえってやる気がなくなる。
example_sentences.english: If someone says 'do it', on the contrary, I'll lose motivation.

example_sentences.japanese: 情けがかえって仇となることもある。
example_sentences.english: On the contrary, there are times when pity can backfire.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕がいるとかえって邪魔になると思うんです。
example_sentences.english: On the contrary, if I stick around I think that I'll just get in the way.

example_sentences.japanese: お手伝いのつもりでしょうが、かえって迷惑です。
example_sentences.english: I realize that you are trying to help, on the contrary you are getting in the way.

example_sentences.japanese: 近道をするつもりが、かえって遠回りしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I intended to take a shortcut, but on the contrary I accidentally took a detour.

example_sentences.japanese: 手術をしたらかえって悪化する場合もあります。
example_sentences.english: On the contrary, if you have an operation your condition could worsen.

example_sentences.japanese: 言い訳するとかえって悪い印象を与える。
example_sentences.english: You'll make all the more of a bad impression if you make excuses.

example_sentences.japanese: 失敗しても正直に告白すればかえって評価が上がる。
example_sentences.english: Contrary to expectations, if you honestly confess your feelings, even if you fail, it will be highly appreciated.

example_sentences.japanese: 笑わせるつもりだったけど、かえって泣かせてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I intended to make her laugh, but on the contrary I unfortunately made her cry.

example_sentences.japanese: 安い家具を買ったらすぐ壊れて、かえって高くついた。
example_sentences.english: I bought cheap furniture that broke almost immediately so, contrary to my expectations, it got costly.

example_sentences.japanese: 見え透いたお世辞は、かえって印象が悪くなるからやめておいた方がいい。
example_sentences.english: On the contrary, obvious compliments will make a rather bad impression. So it is better to stop.

example_sentences.japanese: 「宿題やれ！」って言われると、かえってやりたくなくなる。
example_sentences.english: When someone tells me to do my homework, taking a step back from that, it makes me not want to do it even more.

example_sentences.japanese: 遅く走った方が安全だと思うかもしれないけどかえって危ないから、高速道路ではスピードを落とさないで。
example_sentences.english: You might think that it is safer to drive slower on a highway, but taking a step back from that, it is actually dangerous. So, please don't slow down on the highway.

general_translation: It is entirely as if, It is just as though
formation: まるで + Verb + みたい(1) + だまるで + ［い］Adjective + みたい(1) + だまるで + ［な］Adjective + みたい(2) + だまるで + Noun + みたい(3) + だ(1) よう(2) なよう(3) のよう
casual_structure: まるで + Verb + みたい(1) + だまるで + ［い］Adjective + みたい(1) + だまるで + ［な］Adjective + みたい(2) + だまるで + Noun + みたい(3) + だ(1) よう(2) なよう(3) のよう
polite_structure: まるで + Verb + みたい(1) + ですまるで + ［い］Adjective + みたい(1) + ですまるで + ［な］Adjective + みたい(2) + ですまるで + Noun + みたい(3) + です(1) よう(2) なよう(3) のよう
explanation: A structure that expresses something as being completely the manner of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの顔はまるで幽霊を見たようだ。
example_sentences.english: Your face totally looks as though you saw a ghost.

example_sentences.japanese: このゲームはものすごくリアルだ。まるで映画を見ているようだ。
example_sentences.english: This game is very realistic. It is as if I am watching a movie.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は私の母親と同じ年だけど運動神経がいい。まるで２０代のようだ。
example_sentences.english: That person is the same age as my mother, but is very athletic. It is as though she's in her twenties.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人の仕事の仕方はまるで楽みたいだ。
example_sentences.english: How that person works looks as if it is super easy.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は弟にそっくりだ。まるで兄弟みたいだ。
example_sentences.english: He looks very similar to my younger brother. It is as if they are siblings.

example_sentences.japanese: 全部の家事をしてくれたの？まるで天使のようだ！
example_sentences.english: You did all the housework? You are just like an angel.

example_sentences.japanese: あの二人は仲がいい。まるで兄弟のようだ。
example_sentences.english: Those two really get along well. It is just as though they are siblings. (entirely)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は、まるで山のように積まれた本を見て驚いた。
example_sentences.english: He was surprised to see books stacked just as if they were a mountain. (entirely)

example_sentences.japanese: こんな日がくるなんて、まるで夢のようだ。
example_sentences.english: To think such a day would come, It is just as though I am in a dream. (entirely)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の風はまるで台風のようだ。
example_sentences.english: The wind today is entirely as if there is a typhoon. (totally)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の瞳はまるで 夜空の星のように煌めいていた。
example_sentences.english: Her eyes sparkled just as if they were stars in the night sky. (completely)

example_sentences.japanese: あいつ！あたしの家、まるでホテルみたいに扱うのよ。彼を追い出したい、どうすればいいかな？
example_sentences.english: That son of a gun! He treats my house just as though it is a hotel! I want to kick him out, but how? (entirely)

example_sentences.japanese: この問題はまるで東京大学の入学試験のようだ。
example_sentences.english: This question is entirely as if it were from the Tokyo university entrance exam.

example_sentences.japanese: 冬なのにこんなに暖かくて、蝶々まで飛んでいる。まるで春がきたみたいだ！
example_sentences.english: Although it is winter, it is so warm that even butterflies are flying. It is entirely as if spring has come. (completely)

example_sentences.japanese: あの家には子供が４人いるので、まるで動物園のようだ。
example_sentences.english: Since there are four kids living in that house, it is entirely as if it were a zoo.

example_sentences.japanese: ひとみはほんの高校生だけど、まるで経験豊富な大人のように演説した。私ばかりでなく彼女のご両親を含めてみんな彼女の能力にびっくりした。
example_sentences.english: Although Hitomi is just a high school student, she talked just as though she was a person with a lot of experience. (entirely)Not just me, but everyone, including her parents, were surprised at her ability.

example_sentences.japanese: お客さんと話すときにはちゃんと目を見て話せ！目を見ていないとまるでお客さんの話を聞いていないみたいじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: Look at the customers eyes when you talk to them! If you don't make eye contact, it is as though you are not listening to what they are saying.

example_sentences.japanese: なんだそのフォームは？まるでなってないぞ！
example_sentences.english: What is that form? That is completely unacceptable. (Natural, but different meaning)

general_translation: Have a feeling that
formation: Verb +  （ような） + 気（き）がする［い］Adjective + （ような） + 気（き）がするNoun + （の + ような ）気（き）がする［な］Adjective + （な(1) + ような） + 気（き）がする(1) の
casual_structure: Verb +  （ような） + 気（き）がする［い］Adjective + （ような） + 気（き）がするNoun + （の + ような ）気（き）がする［な］Adjective + （な(1) + ような） + 気（き）がする(1) の
polite_structure: Verb +  （ような） + 気（き）がします［い］Adjective + （ような） + 気（き）がしますNoun + （の + ような ）気（き）がします［な］Adjective + （な(1) + ような） + 気（き）がします(1) の
explanation: A phrase that expresses the slight manner of feeling about (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 分かるようなきがする。
example_sentences.english: I have a feeling that I understand.

example_sentences.japanese: あいつと話した感じでは元気なようなきがするけど…
example_sentences.english: Based on talking to him, he seemed like he was doing well, but…

example_sentences.japanese: 前にいる人は警察のようなきがする。
example_sentences.english: I have a funny feeling that the person in front of us is a cop.

example_sentences.japanese: あの技はなんか簡単そう。俺でも出来るようなきがする。
example_sentences.english: That technique looks easy. I feel like I would be able to do it.

example_sentences.japanese: そこへ一人で行くのは危ないようなきがする。ガイドと一緒に行った方がいいと思う。
example_sentences.english: I have a feeling that it would be dangerous to go there alone. I think it would be better to go with a guide.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人に騙されたようなきがする。
example_sentences.english: I have a feeling that I was deceived by that person.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回は合格するようなきがしています。
example_sentences.english: I have a feeling that I will pass this time.

example_sentences.japanese: 道を間違えたようなきがします。
example_sentences.english: I have a feeling that I went the wrong way.

example_sentences.japanese: この問題、分かったようなきがするぞ。
example_sentences.english: I have a feeling that I know the answer of this question.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は気が変わるようなきがする。
example_sentences.english: I have a feeling that he will change his mind.

example_sentences.japanese: この気持ち、届かないようなきがする。
example_sentences.english: I have a feeling that he won't get what you are feeling.

example_sentences.japanese: あの二人は結婚してもうまくいかないようなきがする。
example_sentences.english: I have a feeling that even if they get married, it won't turn out well.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたに以前どこかで会ったことがあるようなきがするのですが…
example_sentences.english: I have a feeling that we have met somewhere before...

example_sentences.japanese: 文法を勉強すればするほど、しゃべることができるようなきがする。
example_sentences.english: I have a feeling that the more you study grammar, the easier it becomes to speak with people.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社の意見は僕の考えとは違うようなきがする。
example_sentences.english: I have a feeling that the company's opinion differs from mine.

example_sentences.japanese: そこまでしてもらうのは悪いようなきがして…
example_sentences.english: I have a bad feeling having them go to that extent...

general_translation: Not ~ at all, Cannot ~ at all
formation: とても + Verb［ない］
casual_structure: とても + Verb［ない］
explanation: An expression meaning not at all (A), or (A) is impossible. Literally, in every way, not (A).

example_sentences.japanese: とても考えられない。
example_sentences.english: I cannot think of it at all.

example_sentences.japanese: その考え方はとても理解できない。
example_sentences.english: I cannot understand that way of thinking at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいつも嘘ばかり言うから、彼の言う事はとても信じられない。
example_sentences.english: He always just lies, so I cannot trust what he says at all.

example_sentences.japanese: とても観光できない。
example_sentences.english: I cannot do any sight-seeing at all.

example_sentences.japanese: とても観察できない。
example_sentences.english: I cannot do any observations at all.

example_sentences.japanese: とても完成させられない。
example_sentences.english: I cannot complete it at all.

example_sentences.japanese: とても記憶できない。
example_sentences.english: I can't memorize anything at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕にはとても車は買えません。
example_sentences.english: I cannot buy a car at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 君の能力にはとても敵わない。
example_sentences.english: I am no match for your abilities at all.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなうまい話、とても信じられません。
example_sentences.english: It's too good to be true, I cannot believe it at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の僕の力ではとても歯が立たない。
example_sentences.english: I have no chance at all of beating him/her with my current ability.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は寒がりだから、北海道の寒さにはとても耐えられません。
example_sentences.english: I am sensitive to the cold, so I can't stand Hokkaido's chill at all.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなにたくさん出されても、とても食べ切れないよ。
example_sentences.english: Even if all of these foods are provided, there is no way at all that I will be able to eat it all.

example_sentences.japanese: 君の考えはとても理解できない。
example_sentences.english: I can't understand your thinking at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼に子供ができたの！？彼が親になることを想像するのはとても無理だ。
example_sentences.english: He has a baby coming? I cannot imagine him becoming a parent at all.

example_sentences.japanese: どこの航空会社も今はチケットを売っていないから、旅行をするのがとても無理だ。
example_sentences.english: No airline company is selling airline tickets, so it is not possible to travel at all.

general_translation: Not really, Not particularly, It's not like...
formation: 別（べつ）に + Verb［ない］別（べつ）に + ［い］Adjective［ない］別（べつ）に + ［な］Adjective + ではない(1)別（べつ）に + Noun + ではない(1)(1) じゃない
casual_structure: 別（べつ）に + Verb［ない］別（べつ）に + ［い］Adjective［ない］別（べつ）に + ［な］Adjective + ではない(1)別（べつ）に + Noun + ではない(1)(1) じゃない
explanation: An expression that shows that (A) is not really the case, or not exclusively the case.

example_sentences.japanese: トムが悪いとはべつにいっていないよ。
example_sentences.english: I'm not really saying that Tom is bad. (not particularly)

example_sentences.japanese: 私はべつに構わないけど、お父さんはそういうの気にするから、お父さんの前ではそういう事言わないでね。
example_sentences.english: I actually don't mind, but my dad cares a lot about things like that, so please don't say such things in front of him.

example_sentences.japanese: べつに痛くないよ。少しチクってするだけ。
example_sentences.english: It's not really painful. It just stings a little.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの事はべつに嫌いではないよ。ただあなたと何について話せばいいか分からないだけ。
example_sentences.english: It's not that I don't like you at all. It's just that I don't know what to talk about with you.

example_sentences.japanese: パーティーってみんな言っているけど、べつにそんなに大したものではないよ。
example_sentences.english: Everyone is calling it a party, but it is actually not that big of a deal.

example_sentences.japanese: それはべつに悪いことではないよ。
example_sentences.english: That's not particularly a bad thing.

example_sentences.japanese: べつに夢がないわけではないよ。
example_sentences.english: It is not that I don't really have a dream.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はそんなに音楽がうるさくても、べつにきにしない。
example_sentences.english: Even if the music is that loud, I don't particularly care.

example_sentences.japanese: べつにたのしくないわけではない。少し疲れているだけだ。
example_sentences.english: It is not like I am not particularly having fun. I am just a bit tired.

example_sentences.japanese: べつにもんだいない。時間が解決してくれるよ。
example_sentences.english: That's not particularly a problem. It will sort itself out in time.

example_sentences.japanese: べつに深い意味はないですよ。考えすぎです。
example_sentences.english: No, I didn't mean anything in particular. You think too much.

example_sentences.japanese: べつに何でもないです。気にしないでください。
example_sentences.english: It's nothing in particular. Don't worry about it.

example_sentences.japanese: べつに自慢しているわけじゃない。事実を話しただけだ。
example_sentences.english: It is not like I am boasting. I just told you the truth. (not particularly)

example_sentences.japanese: べつに怒っているわけではないですよ。元々ああいう顔なんです。
example_sentences.english: It is not like I am particularly angry. This is my neutral face expression.

example_sentences.japanese: べつに君だけに言ったわけではない。みんなに言ったんだ。
example_sentences.english: It is not like I said it just to you. I said it to everyone. (not particularly)

example_sentences.japanese: べつに自分が汗だらけになってもかまわないが、他の人の汗は嫌です。
example_sentences.english: I don't particularly mind being drenched in sweat, but I don't like other people's sweat.

example_sentences.japanese: 別にケーキが嫌いというわけではない。今は食べたくないだけ。
example_sentences.english: It is not that I dislike cakes. I just don't want one right now.

example_sentences.japanese: 別にケーキが嫌いというわけがない。今は食べたくないだけ。
example_sentences.english: It is not that I SO don't not like cakes. I just don't want any right now. (Grammatically correct, but very confusing for the listener)

general_translation: Not only…but also, As well as
formation: Verb + ばかりではなく(1)［い］Adjective + ばかりではなく(1)［な］Adjective + な + ばかりではなく(1)Noun + ばかりではなく(1)(1) ばかりか
casual_structure: Verb + ばかりではなく(1)［い］Adjective + ばかりではなく(1)［な］Adjective + な + ばかりではなく(1)Noun + ばかりではなく(1)(1) ばかりか
explanation: A slightly formal way to express that something is not just (A), but also (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 田中さんはサッカーばかりでなく水泳も上手です。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka is good at soccer as well as swimming.

example_sentences.japanese: この池は綺麗なばかりではなく、ワニが沢山いるので危ないです。
example_sentences.english: This pond is more than just beautiful, there are a lot of alligators, so it is dangerous too.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は仕事ばかりではなく、家事もちゃんとやっています。
example_sentences.english: Not only does he work, but he also takes care of the housework properly.

example_sentences.japanese: 都内にある安いアパートは古いばかりではなく、だいたい小さくて汚い。
example_sentences.english: Cheap apartments in metropolitan areas aren't only old, but they are usually small and dirty.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は宝くじに当たって、車ばかりではなく、ボートとバイクも買った。
example_sentences.english: He won the lottery, and not only did he buy a car, but he also bought a bike and a boat.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語は漢字ばかりでなく、ひらがなとカタカナもある。
example_sentences.english: Japanese not only has Kanji, but also has Hiragana and Katakana too.

example_sentences.japanese: 悪いことばかりではなく、楽しいことを考えてみよう。
example_sentences.english: Try not to think only of bad things, but fun things as well!

example_sentences.japanese: 自分ばかりでなく、家族にも迷惑をかけてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I have inconvenienced not only myself, but also my family.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強ばかりでなく、運動もした方がいいと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think you should not only study, but also exercise.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分のことばかりではなく、一緒に働く人のことも考えて行動してください。
example_sentences.english: Please behave in a manner that allows you to not only think about yourself, but also about the people working around you.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼には短所ばかりでなく長所もあります。
example_sentences.english: He has weaknesses as well as strengths.

example_sentences.japanese: 成績ばかりでなく、人柄も評価してください。
example_sentences.english: Please also evaluate people's personalities not only their grades.

example_sentences.japanese: 山田さんがアメリカに行ったことは、友達ばかりでなく、家族も知らなかった。
example_sentences.english: Not only did Yamada's friends not know that she went to America but her family didn't know either.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生ばかりでなく、生徒たちも皆反対している。
example_sentences.english: Not only teachers, but students are against it as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 成功例ばかりでなく、失敗例からもいろいろと学べる。
example_sentences.english: You can learn a lot from instances of success, as well as (instances of) failures.

example_sentences.japanese: 違いばかりでなく、共通点を探してみよう。
example_sentences.english: Let's not only look for differences, but also common points.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は友達だけでなく、家族にも内緒で海外へ引っ越した。
example_sentences.english: Not only did he not tell his friends, but he didn't even tell his family about moving abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はバスケだけでなく、水泳もするそうです。
example_sentences.english: Not only can she play basketball, but I heard that she can swim too.

general_translation: Not A but B, Conjunctive
formation: Verb + の + ではなく（て）(1)［い］Adjective + の + ではなく（て）(1)［な］Adjective + ではなく（て）(1)Noun + ではなく（て）(1)(1) じゃなく（て）
casual_structure: Verb + の + ではなく（て）(1)［い］Adjective + の + ではなく（て）(1)［な］Adjective + ではなく（て）(1)Noun + ではなく（て）(1)(1) じゃなく（て）
explanation: A phrase used to express that in general, it is not (A), but actually (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は兄弟ではなくて従兄弟です。
example_sentences.english: He is not my sibling, but my cousin.

example_sentences.japanese: 事故を起こしたら逃げるのではなくて、警察に電話をしてください。
example_sentences.english: When you get into an accident, don't run, but call the police please.

example_sentences.japanese: 赤いのではなくて、青いのをください。
example_sentences.english: Please give me the blue one, not the red one.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は暇ではなくて忙しいです。
example_sentences.english: I'm not free today, but busy.

example_sentences.japanese: メールではなくて、ファックスで送ってください。
example_sentences.english: Please send it via fax, and not email.

example_sentences.japanese: その建物は刑務所ではなくて、学校です。
example_sentences.english: That building is not a prison, but a school.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は正社員でなくて、アルバイトです。
example_sentences.english: He is not a full time worker, but a part time worker.

example_sentences.japanese: 魚じゃなくて肉が食べたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to eat meat, not fish.

example_sentences.japanese: 科学ではなくて化学です。
example_sentences.english: Not science, but chemistry.

example_sentences.japanese: 火曜日ではなくて水曜日です。
example_sentences.english: It's not Tuesday, but Wednesday.

example_sentences.japanese: あの選手は天才ではなくて、努力家だ。
example_sentences.english: That player is not a genius, but a hard worker.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は歌手ではなくて俳優だ。
example_sentences.english: He is not a singer, but an actor.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は医者ではなくて薬剤師です。
example_sentences.english: I am not a doctor, but a pharmacist.

example_sentences.japanese: これは夢じゃなくて現実だ。
example_sentences.english: This is not a dream, but reality.

example_sentences.japanese: それは僕のアイデアじゃなくて、あの人のアイデアだ。
example_sentences.english: That is not my idea, but that person's.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は土曜日じゃなくて日曜日ですよ。
example_sentences.english: Today is not Saturday, but Sunday.

example_sentences.japanese: 観光じゃなくて仕事です。
example_sentences.english: It's not sightseeing, but work.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが約束したのは明日ではなくて今日ですよ。
example_sentences.english: What you promised was not tomorrow, but today!

example_sentences.japanese: このラーメンは不味いのではなく、味が薄いだけです。
example_sentences.english: It is not﻿﻿ that this ramen tastes bad, but it is bland.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は高いのではなく安いのを買った。
example_sentences.english: I bought the cheap one, not the expensive one.

general_translation: Not only ~ but ~ also, Not just ~ but ~ also
formation: Noun + だけ + でなく（て）(1) + Noun + も(1) じゃなく（て）
casual_structure: Noun + だけ + でなく（て）(1) + Noun + も(1) じゃなく（て）
explanation: An expression which states that not only (A), but also (B), when emphasizing (B).

example_sentences.japanese: アイスクリームだけじゃなくて、プリンも買いました。
example_sentences.english: I didn't just buy ice cream, I also bought pudding.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカだけではなく、韓国とチリにも行った事があります。
example_sentences.english: Not only the US, I have also been to Korea and Chile.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本は地震だけでなく、台風も多いです。
example_sentences.english: Not only are there earthquakes in Japan, there are also many typhoons.

example_sentences.japanese: 漫画は子供だけではなくて、大人にも人気があります。
example_sentences.english: Not only is manga popular amongst children, it is popular among adults too.

example_sentences.japanese: お年玉は子供だけじゃなく、大人ももらえたらいいのにね。
example_sentences.english: Don't you think it would be nice if adults also got money during new years and not just kids?

example_sentences.japanese: 遊園地だけじゃなくて動物園にも連れて行ってほしい。
example_sentences.english: Not only the amusement park, I also want you to take me to the zoo.

example_sentences.japanese: 机だけじゃなくて、椅子もほしい。
example_sentences.english: I don't just want a desk, I want a chair too.

example_sentences.japanese: 市場だけでなく、スーパーにもいきませんか。
example_sentences.english: Won't you not only go to the market, but the store too?

example_sentences.japanese: 君だけじゃなく、僕も悪かったと思っている。
example_sentences.english: It's not only you, I think that I am also to blame.

example_sentences.japanese: 体だけじゃなく、心も疲れてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I am tired not only physically but mentally as well.

example_sentences.japanese: 人間だけじゃなく、動物も涙を流すらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that not only humans, but animals cry too.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は強いだけではなく、とても優しい人だ。
example_sentences.english: He is not only strong, but also very kind.

example_sentences.japanese: 車だけじゃなく、船も運転できます。
example_sentences.english: I can not only drive a car, but can also a boat.

example_sentences.japanese: 鳥だけじゃなくて、猫にも餌をあげています。
example_sentences.english: I feed not only birds, but also cats.

example_sentences.japanese: 原因はそれだけじゃなく、他にもあると思います。
example_sentences.english: That is not the only reason, I think there is something else too.

example_sentences.japanese: 私だけじゃなく、何人もの社員が反対しています。
example_sentences.english: Not only me, but many employees disagree too.

example_sentences.japanese: 実は、それだけじゃなくて、もっと悪い報告もあるんです…
example_sentences.english: To be honest, it's not only that, (but) I have something even worse to tell you...

general_translation: To emphasize '~only', Nothing but
formation: Noun + だけしか + ない
casual_structure: Noun + だけしか + ない
polite_structure: Noun + だけしか + ありません
explanation: A strong expression highlighting that only (A) and nothing but (A) exists. Sometimes with the nuance of pity.

example_sentences.japanese: この時間、医師は一人だけしかいません。
example_sentences.english: At this time of day, there is only one doctor present.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は野菜だけしか食べられません。
example_sentences.english: He can only eat vegetables.

example_sentences.japanese: 土曜日だけしか空いてる日がないから、出来たら土曜日がいい。
example_sentences.english: I have no days except for Saturdays that are free, so if possible, it would be better if it was a Saturday.

example_sentences.japanese: この中ではタケシだけしか下手じゃない。他はみんな結構うまい。
example_sentences.english: In this group, Takeshi is the only one that isn't good. Everyone else is considerably skilled.

example_sentences.japanese: 何でこのコップだけしか５００円ではないの？
example_sentences.english: Why is this cup the only one that is not 500 yen?

example_sentences.japanese: 私は日本語だけしか話せないです。
example_sentences.english: I can only speak Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 椅子はここにあるものだけしかありません。
example_sentences.english: The chairs here are the only chairs.

example_sentences.japanese: 私には従兄弟が一人だけしかいません。
example_sentences.english: I only have one cousin.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は日本語だけしかできません。
example_sentences.english: I can only speak Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 現金は今１０００円だけしかありません。
example_sentences.english: I only have 1000 yen in cash.

example_sentences.japanese: 少しだけしかありませんが、お菓子を食べませんか？
example_sentences.english: I only have a few, but would you like some snacks?

example_sentences.japanese: 風の音だけしか聞こえません。
example_sentences.english: I can't hear anything but the sound of the wind.

example_sentences.japanese: あの先生は人の表面だけしか見ない人だ。
example_sentences.english: That teacher is a person who only judges people by their outward appearance.

example_sentences.japanese: 命は一人に一つだけしかありません。
example_sentences.english: Each person has but only one life.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかく並んだのに、欲しいものはこれだけしか買えませんでした。
example_sentences.english: Even though I went through all the trouble of getting in line, these are the only things I could buy out of what I wanted.

example_sentences.japanese: ミシェル：「一度だけしか言わないので、ちゃんと聞いてください。」
example_sentences.english: Michelle: 'Listen very carefully, I will only say this once.'

example_sentences.japanese: 握手会に行ったのに、声優の後ろ姿だけしか見えませんでした。
example_sentences.english: Although I went to a handshake event, I saw nothing but the voice actress' back.

example_sentences.japanese: 日曜日しかだけ休みが取れない。
example_sentences.english: I can take only breaks on Sunday. (Unnatural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 日曜日だけしか休みが取れない。
example_sentences.english: I can only take breaks on Sunday. (Natural Japanese)

example_sentences.japanese: 日曜日だけしか休みが取れない。
example_sentences.english: I can only take breaks on Sunday. (Natural Japanese)

grammar_point: は言（い）うまでもない ①
general_translation: It goes without saying (that), (It is) needless to say, I don't need to remind you
formation: Phrase + は + 言（い）うまでもないVerb + ということ(1)は + 言（い）うまでもない［い］Adjective + ということ(1)は + 言（い）うまでもない［な］Adjective + ということ(2)は + 言（い）うまでもないNoun + は + 言（い）うまでもない(1) こと、の、というの(2) というの、なこと、なの、
casual_structure: Phrase + は + 言（い）うまでもないVerb + ということ(1)は + 言（い）うまでもない［い］Adjective + ということ(1)は + 言（い）うまでもない［な］Adjective + ということ(2)は + 言（い）うまでもないNoun + は + 言（い）うまでもない(1) こと、の、というの(2) というの、なこと、なの、
polite_structure: Phrase + は + 言（い）うまでもありませんVerb + ということ(1)は + 言（い）うまでもありません［い］Adjective + ということ(1)は + 言（い）うまでもありません［な］Adjective + ということ(2)は + 言（い）うまでもありませんNoun + は + 言（い）うまでもありません(1) こと、の、というの(2) というの、なこと、なの、
explanation: A structure highlighting that in general, even going so far as to say (A) is not required, as it should be commonly known.

example_sentences.japanese: 困っている人を助けるべきというのはいうまでもない。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that one should help people in need.

example_sentences.japanese: 師匠の戦い方が凄いということはいうまでもない。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying how amazing the master's fighting style is.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は歌うのが上手い。ピアノもいうまでもない。
example_sentences.english: She is very good at singing. Needless to say, the piano too.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の成績がクラスで一番なのはいうまでもない。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that his grades are the best in the whole class.

example_sentences.japanese: ガソリンの値段が上がれば、電気自動車の数が増えることはいうまでもない。
example_sentences.english: If the gas prices go up, it goes without saying that the amount of electric cars will increase.

example_sentences.japanese: エネルギーの無駄使いをやめれば、電気代が下がることはいうまでもない。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that if you stop wasting electricity, the electricity bill will go down.

example_sentences.japanese: ともちゃんの大阪での知名度が高いことはいうまでもない。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that Tomo-chan's popularity in Osaka is high.

example_sentences.japanese: 「にせあい」がこの世代の最良の漫画の一つであることはいうまでもないだろう。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that 'False love' is one of the best manga of this generation.

example_sentences.japanese: 生きるのに酸素が必要なことはいうまでもない。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that oxygen is essential to live.

example_sentences.japanese: さだおさんは中国語がペラペラだ。英語はいうまでもない。
example_sentences.english: Sadao-san is fluent in Chinese. Needless to say (he is also fluent in) English.

example_sentences.japanese: 大統領が自分の仕事で忙しいのはいうまでもない。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that the president is busy with his work.

example_sentences.japanese: バイクを運転するのがどんなに危ないかいうまでもないでしょうね。
example_sentences.english: I suppose I don't have to remind you how dangerous riding a motorbike is. (I don't have to tell you)

example_sentences.japanese: 昔と比べ、子供向けのおもちゃの電子化が進んだことはいうまでもない。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that computerization of toys for children has progressed compared to in the past.

example_sentences.japanese: 江戸時代以前の日常生活が大変だったというのはいうまでもない。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that daily life before the Edo period was hard.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「レオンはプロだそうだよ。」Ｂ：「うん、それはいうまでもないね。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I heard that Leon is a professional.'B: 'Yeah, it goes without saying.'

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女が約束を守る人であることはいうまでもない。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that she is a person that keeps promises.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の日本語がうまいのは言うまでもないが、日本語が上手いのは日本に３０年住んでいるからである。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that his Japanese is very good, but he is good at Japanese because he has been living in Japan for 30 years.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で山を登るのが危ないというのは言うまでもないが、気をつけて行けばそれほど危なくない。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that it is dangerous to climb a mountain on your own, but if you go cautiously, it is not that dangerous.

general_translation: Never, By no means
formation: 決（けっ）して + Verb［ない］決（けっ）して + ［い］Adjective［ない］決（けっ）して + ［な］Adjective + ではない(1)決（けっ）して + Noun + ではない(1)(1) じゃない
casual_structure: 決（けっ）して + Verb［ない］決（けっ）して + ［い］Adjective［ない］決（けっ）して + ［な］Adjective + ではない(1)決（けっ）して + Noun + ではない(1)(1) じゃない
explanation: A grammar point that strongly implies that something is decisively not the case

example_sentences.japanese: 嘘をついたらけっしてゆるさない。
example_sentences.english: I will never forgive you if you lie to me.

example_sentences.japanese: この道はものすごく危ないので、けっしてグループから離れないで下さい。
example_sentences.english: This road is very dangerous, so please under no circumstances leave the group.

example_sentences.japanese: けっして痛くないとは言えないです。
example_sentences.english: By no means, can I say that it does not hurt.

example_sentences.japanese: この乗り物はけっして危険ではないです。
example_sentences.english: This ride is by no means dangerous.

example_sentences.japanese: この子はけっして悪い人ではないけど、時々失礼なときがある。
example_sentences.english: By no means do I think that this kid is bad, but they are rude at times.

example_sentences.japanese: 何があっても、けっしてあきらめない。
example_sentences.english: I will never give up, no matter what happens.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はけっして妥協しない人だ。
example_sentences.english: He is a person that never compromises.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人はけっして嘘をつかない。
example_sentences.english: That person never tells lies.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたのことはけっしてわすれません。
example_sentences.english: I will never forget you.

example_sentences.japanese: けっして損はさせないから、私を信用してください。
example_sentences.english: Please trust me because I will never let you lose out.

example_sentences.japanese: 何を手に入れても、けっして満足しない。
example_sentences.english: I will never feel satisfied no matter what I get.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな決定はけっしてみとめない！
example_sentences.english: I will never approve such a decision!

example_sentences.japanese: あの人に冗談を言っても、けっしてわらわない。
example_sentences.english: Even if you tell a joke, he never laughs.

example_sentences.japanese: 何回友達に行こうと誘われても、けっして行かない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how many times my friends pressure me to go, I will never go.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は少し偏屈だが、けっして悪い人ではない。
example_sentences.english: He is a bit eccentric, but he is by no means a bad person.

example_sentences.japanese: トムはけっして頭が悪いわけではない。単なる怠け者なだけだ。
example_sentences.english: Tom is by no means dumb, he is simply lazy.

example_sentences.japanese: この宝石を決して渡すものか！
example_sentences.english: There is no way I will hand over this treasure!

example_sentences.japanese: お前に決してお金を貸すものか！
example_sentences.english: There is no way I will lend you money!

grammar_point: 訳（わけ）には行（い）かない
general_translation: Cannot afford to, No way, Impossible to do
formation: Verb + わけにはいかない
casual_structure: Verb + わけにはいかない
polite_structure: Verb + わけにはいきません
explanation: A strong expression that states (A) as being impossible, or unable to proceed if so.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕はその問題を黙って見過ごすわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: I cannot afford to silently overlook that problem.

example_sentences.japanese: この料理は妻が頑張って作ってくれたやつだから、不味くても残すわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: This food is something that my wife tried her best to make for me, so even if it tastes bad, there's no way that I can leave it.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日は人手が足りないから、休むわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: Since we are short-handed tomorrow, I cannot afford to take a day off.

example_sentences.japanese: このジャケットが欲しいけど、今月はお金を使い過ぎたから買うわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: I want this jacket, but because I spent too much money this month, it cannot be so that I buy it.

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩に誘われたから、断るわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: I was invited by my senpai, so there is no way that I can decline the offer.

example_sentences.japanese: まだやるべきことがあるから、死ぬわけにはいかないんだ！
example_sentences.english: I can't afford to die, because there are still some things I have to do!

example_sentences.japanese: 大統領に頼まれたので断るわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: Since I was asked by the president I can't afford to say no.

example_sentences.japanese: それは捨てるわけにはいきません。大切な人からもらったんです。
example_sentences.english: I can't afford to throw it away. I got it from my special someone.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ許すわけにはいきません。ちゃんと反省してないでしょ。
example_sentences.english: I can't afford to forgive you yet. You haven't taken the time to properly reflect on what you have done.

example_sentences.japanese: ダイエット中だから、こんな美味しいケーキ、食べるわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: I am on a diet, so I cannot afford to eat this delicious cake.

example_sentences.japanese: ３０分遅刻したから、これ以上お客さんを待たせるわけにはいきません。
example_sentences.english: Since I was 30 minutes late, I cannot afford to keep my customers waiting anymore.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はまだ初心者だから、あの仕事を一人でやらせるわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: I can't afford to let him do that job alone, because he is still a newbie.

example_sentences.japanese: 引退するし、このチームの選手として最後の勝負だから、負けるわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: Because I am retiring and this is my last game as a team member, I can't afford to lose.

example_sentences.japanese: 前に一度、彼女との約束を破ったから、今度は破るわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: I broke a promise with her once before, so this time I cannot afford to break another.

example_sentences.japanese: 前回の日本語能力試験に不合格だったので、次は失敗するわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: I failed the JLPT last time, so I cannot afford to fail it a second time.

example_sentences.japanese: 硬貨を持ってないから、何も買うわけにはいかない。
example_sentences.english: I don't have any hard currency on me, so I cannot afford to buy anything.

grammar_point: う・よう + としない
general_translation: Not willing to, Not make an effort to, To not attempt or try to, Volitional + としない
formation: Verb［おう］ + としない
casual_structure: Verb［おう］ + としない
polite_structure: Verb［おう］ + としません
explanation: A phrase that highlights that someone does not have the strong will to attempt (A), or will not make an effort.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は好きな男をあきらめようとしない。
example_sentences.english: She is not willing to give up on the man she likes.

example_sentences.japanese: 家になかなか帰ろうとしない。
example_sentences.english: He isn't quite trying to go home. (It doesn't seem like he is going to leave anytime soon)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は怒っているから、誰の話も聞こうとしない。
example_sentences.english: Since he is angry, he is not willing to listen to what anyone has to say.

example_sentences.japanese: 皆に嫌われているのに、性格をかえようとしないの？
example_sentences.english: Even though you're disliked by everyone you won't try to change your personality?

example_sentences.japanese: こんなに天気がいいのに、うちの息子は外にでようとしない。
example_sentences.english: Although it's nice outside, my son is not willing to go outside.

example_sentences.japanese: これだけ説明してもしんじようとしないならもういいよ。
example_sentences.english: If you are not willing to believe me, even after I took the time to explain things to you, then so be it.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は現実をみようとしない。逃げてばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: He is not willing to face (see) reality. He is just running from it.

example_sentences.japanese: 隠蔽しようとしないで、正直に言ってください。
example_sentences.english: Do not attempt to conceal anything, just speak honestly.

example_sentences.japanese: 何度失敗しても、彼は望みをすてようとしない。
example_sentences.english: He is not willing to throw away his dreams, no matter how many times he fails.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は怒って、昨日から食事をしようとしない。
example_sentences.english: He got pissed off and has not been willing to eat since yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ話し足りないからなのか、車からおりようとしない。
example_sentences.english: He is not willing to get out of the car, perhaps because he is not yet finished with the conversation.

example_sentences.japanese: 誘ってもこようとしないから、誘われなくなっちゃったんだよ。
example_sentences.english: You are not being invited, because even if we invite you, you would not make the effort to come.

example_sentences.japanese: 何回言われても復習しようとしないから、全然上達しないんですよ。
example_sentences.english: You are not making any progress at all! No matter how many times you are told, you are not willing to review.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は自分が悪いことをしても、決してみとめようとしない。
example_sentences.english: Even if he does something bad, he will not make an effort to admit it.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分から買って食べようと思わないけど、誰かに貰ったら食べるかも。
example_sentences.english: I don't think I would eat it if I had to buy it myself, but I might if someone gave it to me.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は性格を変えようと思わない。
example_sentences.english: I think I shan't change my personality.

general_translation: Perhaps, Maybe, Possibly
formation: もしかしたら(1) + Phrase +（かもしれない）(1) もしかして、もしかすると
casual_structure: もしかしたら(1) + Phrase +（かもしれない）(1) もしかして、もしかすると
explanation: A strong way to further emphasize a hypothetical situation.

example_sentences.japanese: もしかしたら…病気かもしれないんだ…
example_sentences.english: I might be ill...

example_sentences.japanese: もしかしたら、行けるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Maybe, I will be able to go.

example_sentences.japanese: もしかして仕事があるかもしれないから、今ははっきりしたことが言えない。
example_sentences.english: I may have to work, so I can't say anything for certain.

example_sentences.japanese: もしかすると、アンちゃんも来るかもしれないけど皆は大丈夫？
example_sentences.english: Maybe Ann-chan might come, but are you all okay with that?

example_sentences.japanese: もしかしたら明日も休むかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Perhaps I will take a day off tomorrow.

example_sentences.japanese: もしかしたら昨日だったかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Perhaps it could have been yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: もしかしたら採用されるかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: I might be hired.

example_sentences.japanese: もしかしたら今晩雪になるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Perhaps it will snow tonight.

example_sentences.japanese: もしかしたら気が変わって、来てくれるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: He/she might change his/her mind and come.

example_sentences.japanese: 「もしかしたら嫌われてるのかな？」なんて思ってしまうことがある。
example_sentences.english: I sometimes think 'maybe I am disliked?'

example_sentences.japanese: もしかしたら彼のことを誤解していたのかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: Perhaps I misunderstood him.

example_sentences.japanese: もしかしたら有名人がここに来るかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Maybe a famous person will come here.

example_sentences.japanese: もしかしたら間違っているかもしれないので、確認してもらえますか？
example_sentences.english: Since there is a chance I might be wrong, can I have you check it, please?

example_sentences.japanese: 今度そっちに行くから、もしかしたら会えるかもしれないね。
example_sentences.english: Next time I'll go there, so we might be able to meet.

example_sentences.japanese: もしかしたら見終わったの？一緒に見ようと言っていたのに！
example_sentences.english: Did you perhaps already watch it? We said that we were going to watch it together!

example_sentences.japanese: もしかしたら彼は駅で、今も待っているかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: It is possible that he is still waiting at the station.

example_sentences.japanese: もしかしたら相談するかもしれないので、その時はよろしくお願いします。
example_sentences.english: I might consult you on that matter, so I will be counting on you when that time comes.

general_translation: Even if…is the case, Supposing that
formation: たとえ + Verb［ても］たとえ + ［い］Adjective［ても］たとえ + ［な］Adjective + でもたとえ + Noun + でも
casual_structure: たとえ + Verb［ても］たとえ + ［い］Adjective［ても］たとえ + ［な］Adjective + でもたとえ + Noun + でも
explanation: A phrase that presents that even if one supposed that (A) were true, (B).

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ雪が降らなくても、スノーボードをしに行く。
example_sentences.english: Even if it doesn't snow, I'm going snowboarding.

example_sentences.japanese: 空手ではたとえ試合で勝っても、ガッツポーズをしてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: Even if you win in a karate competition, you should not celebrate visibly.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ暑くても、虫が入ってくるのでこの窓は開けないで下さい。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is hot, bugs will come in, so please do not open this window.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ好きでも、そんなことをされたら、嫌いになる。
example_sentences.english: Even if I like them, if someone does such a thing, I will start to dislike them.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ電車でも３０分はかかる。
example_sentences.english: Even by train, it will take at least 30 minutes.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ来年までに完成したとしても、中に入る店が決まっていないから来年中にはオープンされないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even if it is completed by next year, the shops that it is going in have not been decided, so it is unlikely that they will open next year.

example_sentences.japanese: もし今年中にモールの工事が終わったら、来年の頭にはオープンするはず。
example_sentences.english: If the construction for the mall finishes within this year, it should open at the beginning of next year.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ笑われても、正しいことをしたいんだ。
example_sentences.english: I want to do the right thing, even if they laugh at me.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ叱られても、譲れないことがある。
example_sentences.english: Even if (I am) reprimanded, there are things that are non-negotiable.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえあなたが行かなくても、僕は行きます。
example_sentences.english: Even if you don't go, I will.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ嬉しくても、笑ってはいけない時もある。
example_sentences.english: There are times when you cannot laugh, even if you are happy.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ忙しくても、責任はちゃんと果たさなければいけない。
example_sentences.english: Even if you are busy, you will get in trouble if you don't fulfill your responsibilities.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ最後の一人になっても、僕は諦めない。
example_sentences.english: I won't give up even if I am the last one standing.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえあなたが何をしても、僕はあなたのことを嫌いにはならない。
example_sentences.english: No matter what you do (even if it is something bad), I won't hate you.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ子供でも、それくらいの仕事なら自分でさせた方がいいと思います。
example_sentences.english: Even if they are just kids, I think you should make them do that kind of work by themselves.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ短い時間でも、給料はちゃんと払いますよ。
example_sentences.english: I will certainly pay you a salary, even if you only worked for a short time.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえコーヒーを５杯飲んでも、眠気は取れないだろう。
example_sentences.english: Even if I were to drink 5 cups of coffee, I probably couldn't get rid of this sleepiness.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ太ったとしても、彼が力士になることはないだろう。彼は相撲向きではないから。
example_sentences.english: Even if he were to gain weight, he will never become a sumo wrestler. He's just not cut out for it.

general_translation: Extremely, Especially, To my ...
formation: Verb + ことに［い］Adjective  + ことに［な］Adjective + な + ことに
casual_structure: Verb + ことに［い］Adjective  + ことに［な］Adjective + な + ことに
explanation: A phrase that expresses the extremely or particularly high emotional response of (A), caused by something unexpected.

example_sentences.japanese: 幸せなことに、来年結婚します。
example_sentences.english: I am extremely happy about getting married next year.

example_sentences.japanese: ビックリしたことに、久しぶりに小学生時代の友達から電話がかかってきた。
example_sentences.english: To my surprise, I got a phone call from a friend from elementary school after such a long time.

example_sentences.japanese: 珍しいことに、彼がいいレストランに連れていってくれた。
example_sentences.english: In a particularly rare occurance, he took me to a good a restaurant.

example_sentences.japanese: 残念なことに、その商品はもう販売中止になりました。
example_sentences.english: Unfortunately, that product is no longer being sold.

example_sentences.japanese: 不思議なことに、最近物事がすべてうまくいく。
example_sentences.english: By some extreme oddity, lately everything seems to be going well.

example_sentences.japanese: 嬉しいことに、みんなが協力してくれるようになりました。
example_sentences.english: I am extremely happy that everyone started to cooperate with me.

example_sentences.japanese: 嬉しいことに日本語能力試験に合格しました。
example_sentences.english: I am especially happy about passing the JLPT.

example_sentences.japanese: 驚いたことに、六ヶ月で赤ちゃんが初めて歩いた。
example_sentences.english: To our extreme surprise, the six month old baby took its first steps.

example_sentences.japanese: 不幸なことに、彼は奥さんがなくなり失意のあまり、辞職した。
example_sentences.english: Sadly, he was so heartbroken after his wife's death that he resigned.

example_sentences.japanese: 不幸なことに、事故で何人もの人が亡くなってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: By some extreme misfortune, many people died in the accident.

example_sentences.japanese: 喜ばしいことに、何年も前に書いた小説が賞を取りました。
example_sentences.english: To my extreme delight, the novel I wrote many years ago won the prize.

example_sentences.japanese: おかしいことに、悪いことをしたのは僕ではないのにメンバーから外された。
example_sentences.english: What was especially strange was that they removed me as a member, even though I didn't do anything wrong.

example_sentences.japanese: 腹立たしいことに、突然大雪が降って、渋滞になった。
example_sentences.english: To my extreme dismay, suddenly heavy snow started falling and caused a traffic jam.

example_sentences.japanese: 驚くべきことに、彼は交通事故で怪我をしたあと、怪我を克服してオリンピックで金メダルを手にしたんだ。
example_sentences.english: To our extreme surprise, after he was injured in a traffic accident, he overcame his injury and won the gold medal at the olympics.

example_sentences.japanese: 信じられないことに、毎日、彼は早起きして勉強している。
example_sentences.english: To my extreme disbelief, he wakes up early every day and studies!

example_sentences.japanese: 幸いなことに、近所の人が私の猫を見つけて家まで届けてくれた。
example_sentences.english: Fortunately, my neighbor found our cat for us, and brought her home.

general_translation: How…, What..., God knows...
formation: Verb + ことか［い］Adjective + ことか［な］Adjective + な + ことかNoun + である + ことか
casual_structure: Verb + ことか［い］Adjective + ことか［な］Adjective + な + ことかNoun + である + ことか
explanation: A phrase that expresses (A) as being a particularly large amount that shocks even the speaker.

example_sentences.japanese: これをどれだけ待っていたことか。
example_sentences.english: God knows how long I have waited for this!

example_sentences.japanese: あの人のコンサートには何回いったことか。
example_sentences.english: God knows how many times I have gone to that person's concert.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの犬はどんなに可愛いことか。こんなに可愛いワンチャンは他にはいないはず。
example_sentences.english: How can I explain how cute my dog is? There is no other dog as cute as her.

example_sentences.japanese: なんて暇なことか。こんなに暇なのは久しぶりだ。
example_sentences.english: God knows how bored I am. It's been a long time since I've been this bored.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子を一人で電車に乗せるのがどれだけ心配であることか。
example_sentences.english: God knows how worried I am to let my kid on the train by himself.

example_sentences.japanese: 文プロがあってどんなに便利なことか！
example_sentences.english: How convenient it is to have Bunpro!

example_sentences.japanese: 君に会えてどんなに嬉しかったことか。
example_sentences.english: How happy I was after meeting you!

example_sentences.japanese: 君に会える日を、どんなに夢見たことか。
example_sentences.english: How much I have dreamed of the day I could finally meet you!

example_sentences.japanese: このプロテインのなんと美味しいことか！すごく飲みやすい。
example_sentences.english: How delicious this protein is! It goes down like nothing.

example_sentences.japanese: 何たることか、前回と同じ間違いをしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: What the...! I made the same mistake as last time.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供のころ、この喫茶店に行ったことがある。あの時のドーナツは、何とうまかったことか。
example_sentences.english: When I was a child, there was a time we went to this coffee shop. God knows how delicious these donuts were!

example_sentences.japanese: 彼に何回「気を付けて」と言ったことか。今、同情する余地がない。
example_sentences.english: God knows how many times I told him 'be careful!'. Now I don't even feel sorry for him.

example_sentences.japanese: 何たることか！？これは私がずっと探していた石ではないか！
example_sentences.english: What the...!? Is this not the stone that I have been searching for!
