example_sentences.japanese: 文法を勉強するためのサイトを今まで何度、試したことか！
example_sentences.english: Until now, god knows how many sites I have tried learning grammar on!

example_sentences.japanese: みんなに「頭がいい」と褒められるが、ここまで文法を理解するのにどんなに時間がかかったことか！
example_sentences.english: Everyone tells me how smart I am, but in order to understand grammar to this degree, how many hours it took!

example_sentences.japanese: この男、こんな姿になるまでに、何回ジムに行ったことか。
example_sentences.english: How much he must have gone to the gym to get a body like that!

example_sentences.japanese: どれだけお前の事を愛していたことか！それでも俺はお前に裏切られた！
example_sentences.english: God knows how much I loved you! Still, you betrayed me.

example_sentences.japanese: 知らない人にありがとうと言われるのがどれだけ嬉しいことか。
example_sentences.english: God knows how nice it feels to have a stranger thank you.

general_translation: Why? Well..., Why? Because..., If you ask me why..., The reason why is..., It is because...
formation: どうして(1) + Phrase (A) + かというと(2) +  Phrase (B) + からだ(3)Phrase (A)。どうして(1) + かというと(2) + Phrase (B) + からだ(3)どうして(1) + Verb + （の） + かというと(2)(1) なぜ(2) かといえば(3) のだ、ためだ
casual_structure: どうして(1) + Phrase (A) + かというと(2) +  Phrase (B) + からだ(3)Phrase (A)。どうして(1) + かというと(2) + Phrase (B) + からだ(3)どうして(1) + Verb + （の） + かというと(2)(1) なぜ(2) かといえば(3) のだ、ためだ
polite_structure: どうして(1) + Phrase (A) + かというと(2) +  Phrase (B) + からです(3)Phrase (A)。どうして(1) + かというと(2) + Phrase (B) + からです(3)どうして(1) + Verb + （の） + かというと(2)(1) なぜ(2) かといえば(3) のです、ためです
explanation: A hypothetical structure indicating that if someone were to ask the question of (A), (B). Used for giving reasons.

example_sentences.japanese: なぜ彼はそれをしたのかというといまだに私自身もわからない。
example_sentences.english: If you ask me why he did that, well, even now I don't know.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして明日のパーティーに行きたくないかというと、元カレが来ると聞いたからです。
example_sentences.english: The reason why I don't want to go to tomorrow's party is because I heard that my ex-boyfriend is coming.

example_sentences.japanese: なぜこの計画で進めようと思ったかというと、以前この計画に似たプランが成功したからです。
example_sentences.english: The reason why we have decided to continue with this plan is because a similar plan succeeded last time.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてそのブランドのスマホは買いたくないかっていうと、前に一回買ったけど二週間で壊れたんだよね.
example_sentences.english: If you ask me why I don't want to buy that brand of smartphone, it is because I bought one before and it broke in (just) two weeks.

example_sentences.japanese: キリンには長い首がある。なぜかというと、その長い首を使って高い木の上にある葉を食べるためだ。
example_sentences.english: Giraffes have long necks. The reason why is because by using their long necks they can eat leaves on the top of trees.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてバスを使うよりは自転車を使うようにしているかというと、自転車はより安いばかりではなくて交通渋滞の中でもより速いからです。
example_sentences.english: If you ask me why I do my best to bike (to work) rather than take a bus, it is because bicycles are not only cheaper but also faster in traffic.

example_sentences.japanese: 法律によって犬や猫にチップをつけることが要求されています。なぜかというとペットが捨てられた場合にすぐにオーナーがわかるようにするためです。
example_sentences.english: The law requires that dogs and cats be microchipped. Why? Because in the event that the pet is abandoned, the microchip will allow the owner to be quickly identified.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「どうしてそんなことを言うの？」Ｂ：「どうしてかというと、あーの、えーと、Ａさんのことが心配だからです。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Why are you saying this?'B: 'If you ask me why, hmm...uhhh... It's because I am worried about you.'

example_sentences.japanese: なぜアイスクリームトラックが音楽を流しているのかといえば、それはお客さんにその地域でアイスクリームを売っていることを知らせるためです。
example_sentences.english: If you ask me why ice cream trucks are playing music, it is because it lets customers know they are selling in the area.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてそれはグラファイトからできているかというと、答えは単に値段がかなり安いからです。
example_sentences.english: If you ask me why it is made from graphite, well the answer is simple, because it is quite cheap.

example_sentences.japanese: ニューヨークは驚きだらけの街だ。なぜかというと毎日地下鉄で有名人に会う可能性が高いからです。
example_sentences.english: New York is a city full of surprises. If you ask me why, it is because there is a high chance of meeting famous people on the metro every day.

example_sentences.japanese: なぜこれほど両親に感謝しているのかというと食べ方を始めとして知っていることすべて教えてくれたからだ。
example_sentences.english: If you ask me why I am so grateful to my parents, it is because they taught me everything I know, starting with how to eat.

example_sentences.japanese: なぜそのようにするべきかというと、それが効果的だから、それだけの話です。
example_sentences.english: If you ask me why we have to do it like that, it is because it is effective, and that's all.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいノートパソコンを買うべきかどうか迷っている。どうしてかというと、今持ってるのもまだきちんと動くけど新しいのがより速いから。
example_sentences.english: I am not sure if I should buy a new laptop or not. Why? Because, while the one I have now still works fine, the new one would be faster.

example_sentences.japanese: どうして冬でも冷房をかけているかと言えば、お客さんに汗をかかずに買い物をさせる為です。
example_sentences.english: If you ask me why we keep the air conditioning on even in the winter, it is because we want the customers to shop without sweating.

example_sentences.japanese: なぜ安い方を選んだかといったら、安いやつも、高いやつもついている機能が同じだからです。
example_sentences.english: If you ask me why I picked the cheaper one, it is because both the cheaper one and the expensive one have the same functionality.

general_translation: If you ask me..., If I had to say, If I were to say, If I were to choose one, I'd rather
formation: Question Word + (の(1)) + かというと(2)Question Word + Phrase + (の(1)) + かというと(2)(1) ん(2) かといえば
casual_structure: Question Word + (の(1)) + かというと(2)Question Word + Phrase + (の(1)) + かというと(2)(1) ん(2) かといえば
explanation: A hypothetical expression, highlighting that if you were to ask or say (A) to the speaker, their reply would be (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 一方、自分にとってどちらかというと丈夫な車のほうが優れていると思う。
example_sentences.english: On the other hand, if you ask me, I think that sturdy cars are superior.

example_sentences.japanese: どの街に住みたいかというと 、両親が住んでいる街に住みたいと思っています。
example_sentences.english: If I were to say which city I wanted to live in, I think it would be the city that my parents do.

example_sentences.japanese: 何で日本に引っ越して来たかというと 、私の家族が日本に住んでいるからです。
example_sentences.english: If I were to say why I moved to Japan, it is because my family lives here.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰と旅行に行きたいかというと 、大親友と行きたい。
example_sentences.english: If I were to say who I wanted to travel with, it would be my best friend.

example_sentences.japanese: イオさん：「どっちのほうがいいの？」ツミキさん：「どどどっちかっていうと、こっちのほう...」
example_sentences.english: Io: 'Which do you like more?'Tsumiki: 'If, if, if I were to say, I like this more...'

example_sentences.japanese: イチカさん：「ミクちゃんは好きな人がいるみたいに見えるよ。」イツキさん：「誰が好きかっていうときっとフウタロウくんでしょう。」
example_sentences.english: Ichika: 'It looks like Miku has a crush on someone.'Itsuki: 'If I were to say on who, then it would be Futaro.'

example_sentences.japanese: ヨツバさん：「その犬はどのくらい大きいの？」フウカさん：「どのくらい大きいかというと....えーと....こんなに大きいくらいでしょう。」
example_sentences.english: Yotsuba: 'How big was that dog?'Fuuka: 'If you ask me how big, hmmm, I think about this big?'

example_sentences.japanese: 何でこんなことになったかというと、すべてが始まったのは一週間ほど前に学校から帰っていた時...
example_sentences.english: If I were to say why it turned out like this, well, it all started around 1 week ago when I was coming back from school...

example_sentences.japanese: オティス：「人生で最も大切にしているのは何かというと、それは人でしょう。私が一人ぼっちだった時助けてくれた人たちのことです。」
example_sentences.english: Otis: 'If I were to say what do I value in life the most, that would be: people. (Specifically) the people who helped me when I was all alone.'

example_sentences.japanese: コウさん：「明日、用事ある？一緒にどこかに行く？」ニノさん：「用事があるわけではないけど、どちらかっていうと家でゆっくりしたい。」
example_sentences.english: Kou: 'Do you have plans for tomorrow? Do you want to go somewhere together?'Nino: 'It is not like I have plans, but if I were to choose one, I'd rather take it easy at home.'

example_sentences.japanese: 何を晩ご飯に食べたいかっていうと...よく分からない...焼きそばかもしれん...
example_sentences.english: If I were to say what I want for dinner... I don't know... yakisoba, maybe...

example_sentences.japanese: ３ヶ月後に日本語能力試験を受ける予定です。合格したら何をするかといえば、日本に旅行に行くかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: I plan to take the JLPT in three months. If I were to say what I would do if I passed, perhaps I would take a trip to Japan.

example_sentences.japanese: ブンポウちゃん：「いつあたしを好きになった？」ユーザーくん：「いつかというと、窓を開けっぱなしにして君がすごく怒った日だろう。」
example_sentences.english: Bunpou-chan: 'When did you fall in love with me?'User-kun: 'If I were to say when it would probably be the day when I left the window open and you got really angry.'

example_sentences.japanese: どんな人なのかというと一見怖そうなのに実は天使のように優しい人です。
example_sentences.english: If I were to say what kind of person he is, it would be a person that looks scary at first glance, but in reality, is as kind as an angel.

example_sentences.japanese: それがどのように起こったかというと、労働者が安全第一というルールに従わなかったためだ。
example_sentences.english: If I were to say how it happened, it was because workers didn't follow the safety-first rule.

example_sentences.japanese: 何でこんな事になったかといえば、私がきちんと確認をしなかったからです。
example_sentences.english: If I were to say why something like this happened, well, it is because I did not check properly.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰が一番上手かといったらＢ組のタカハシさんです。
example_sentences.english: If I were to say who was the best, it would be Takahashi-san from class B.

general_translation: In, Of, According to
formation: Noun + で言（い）うと
casual_structure: Noun + で言（い）うと
explanation: A hypothetical grammar point which says something in terms of (A). If said with (A), then it's (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 統計でいうと、客の７０％が観光客だ。
example_sentences.english: According to statistics, 70% of customers are tourists. (speaking of)

example_sentences.japanese: このバイクは、車でいうとランボルギーニみたいなものだ。
example_sentences.english: If we say it's a car, this bike is something like a Lamborghini.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本でいうとパンみたいなもの？
example_sentences.english: If we say Japan, is it something like bread? (Would this be considered bread in Japan)

example_sentences.japanese: 一言でいうと彼は本当に凄い人だ。
example_sentences.english: If said in a word, he is an amazing person.

example_sentences.japanese: 「What's up」は日本語でいうと、「元気」に当たる。
example_sentences.english: If said with Japanese, 'what's up' is equivalent to 'Genki'.

example_sentences.japanese: コンピューターでいうとＲＡＭに当たる。
example_sentences.english: If speaking about computers, it is equivalent to RAM.

example_sentences.japanese: この年をとっていそうな猫は人間の年齢でいうと８４歳ぐらいです。
example_sentences.english: This old-looking cat is about 84 years old in human years. (in terms of)

example_sentences.japanese: つまり、「hmmm」は日本語でいうと「うーん」に当たります。
example_sentences.english: To sum up, 'Hmm' corresponds to 'うーん' in Japanese. (in terms of)

example_sentences.japanese: わかりやすい言葉でいうと俺は上司だが、君は部下だ。
example_sentences.english: To put it in simple words, I am the superior and you are the subordinate. (in terms of)

example_sentences.japanese: 「I am batman」って日本語でいうとどうなる？
example_sentences.english: What is 'I am batman' in Japanese? (in terms of)

example_sentences.japanese: 一言でいうと、俺は会社を辞めようと思う。
example_sentences.english: In short, I plan to quit the company. (in terms of)

example_sentences.japanese: １００円は今のアメリカ通貨でいうと約１ドルです。
example_sentences.english: 100 yen is about one dollar in USD. (in terms of)

example_sentences.japanese: この車を早く修理できる。一言でいうと彼はプロなのだ。
example_sentences.english: He can repair this car quickly. In a word, he is professional. (in terms of)

example_sentences.japanese: 魚のえらというのは人でいうと肺にあたる器官だ。
example_sentences.english: Fish gills are organs that correspond to lungs in humans. (in terms of)

example_sentences.japanese: 「お盆」というのは、西洋の行事でいうと「ハロウィン」に近いのかも知れない。
example_sentences.english: 'Obon' may be similar in practice to the Western 'Halloween.' (in terms of)

example_sentences.japanese: バイナリの１００１は十進数でいうと、９に当たります。
example_sentences.english: The binary 1001 corresponds to 9 in decimal. (in terms of)

example_sentences.japanese: そのテレビは５０インチです。メートル法でいうとおよそ１２７センチです。
example_sentences.english: That TV is 50 inches. That is about 127 centimeters in the metric system. (in terms of)

example_sentences.japanese: 西暦の２０１９年は、令和でいうと元年に当たります。
example_sentences.english: The year 2019, on the western calendar, corresponds to the first year of Reiwa. (in terms of)

example_sentences.japanese: 一言で言うと彼とはもう会わないことにした。
example_sentences.english: To sum it up, I have decided to never see him again.

general_translation: One at a time, Per, Each, Gradually
formation: 1. Number + Counter + ずつ (Per/Each/At time)2. 少（すこ）し(1) + ずつ (Little by little) 3. いくらか + ずつ (Some … every)(1) ちょっと、わずか
casual_structure: 1. Number + Counter + ずつ (Per/Each/At time)2. 少（すこ）し(1) + ずつ (Little by little) 3. いくらか + ずつ (Some … every)(1) ちょっと、わずか
explanation: A suffix which indicates each (A), with the nuance of (A) being an individual allotment of something.

example_sentences.japanese: それぞれのテストを２回ずつチェックした。
example_sentences.english: I have checked each test two times each.

example_sentences.japanese: メニューに載ってるもの一つずつちょうだい。
example_sentences.english: Give me one of each thing on the menu!

example_sentences.japanese: 一人ずつゆっくりとお入りください。
example_sentences.english: Please enter slowly, one person at a time.

example_sentences.japanese: このお酒は強いので少しずつ飲んでください。
example_sentences.english: This alcohol is strong, so please drink a little at a time.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎月いくらかずつお金を貯めて旅行に行く。
example_sentences.english: Every month, I want to save up some money, and go on a trip.

example_sentences.japanese: 静かにして下さい！一人ずつお願いします！
example_sentences.english: Please be quiet! One person at a time, please!

example_sentences.japanese: １０ずつに分けて数えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please divide (it) into 10's and count. (10 at a time)

example_sentences.japanese: 一人ずつ入場できる。
example_sentences.english: One person can enter at a time.

example_sentences.japanese: 生徒は１０人ずつのグループに分かれてバスに乗った。
example_sentences.english: The students were broken up into groups of 10 each and got on the buses. (10 at a time)

example_sentences.japanese: 名探偵ゴナン：「この謎の解明に少しずつ近づいている。」
example_sentences.english: Detective Gonan: 'We are gradually getting closer to solving this mystery.'

example_sentences.japanese: 地球温暖化のため、気温は年ごとに０．００８度ずつ上がっています。
example_sentences.english: Due to global warming, the atmospheric temperature is rising (gradually) by 0.008°C per year.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語能力試験のために文法項目を一日に一つずつ学ぶつもりです。
example_sentences.english: I plan to study one grammar point per day for the JLPT. (one at a time)

example_sentences.japanese: 念のため、毎月いくらかずつ貯金することにしている。
example_sentences.english: I made it a rule to save a little money each month, just in case. (incrementally・gradually)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達のおかげで、わずかずつですが、日本語で会話できるようになっています。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to my friends, although only a little bit gradually, I have  come to the point where I can hold a conversation in Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日３〜４回、赤い薬と青い薬を一つずつを飲むようにしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please make sure to take the blue and red pill (one each) 3~4 times per day. (one at a time)

example_sentences.japanese: 店員：「赤のと青のがあります。どちらがいいでしょうか？」買い手：「ひとつずつお願いします。」
example_sentences.english: Shop clerk: 'We have red ones and blue ones. Which one would you like?'Buyer: 'One of each, please.'

example_sentences.japanese: 一グループずつ前に出て来てください。
example_sentences.english: Please come to the front one group at a time. (Group = allotment)

example_sentences.japanese: パーティーに来る人は一人一つずつ食べ物を持って来てください。
example_sentences.english: Whoever is coming to the party, please bring your own portion of food. (Portion = allotment)

general_translation: By far, Way, Far...er, Far...more
formation: ずっと + Phrase
casual_structure: ずっと + Phrase
explanation: A casual expression highlighting that (A) is far more than anything else, due to its degree continuing on and on, unwaveringly.

example_sentences.japanese: この車は私のよりずっとよく見える。
example_sentences.english: This car looks way better than mine.

example_sentences.japanese: さっき見た鳥よりずっと大きかったよ！
example_sentences.english: It was much bigger than the bird we saw earlier.

example_sentences.japanese: それよりずっと昔だよ。
example_sentences.english: It was way more before that. (That happened way before that)

example_sentences.japanese: 「でも勇者さまはずっと強いし...」
example_sentences.english: 'But our hero is far stronger and...'

example_sentences.japanese: 僕よりもずっと年上だということ、信じられないよ。
example_sentences.english: I can't believe that he is far older than (even) me.

example_sentences.japanese: 太陽のほうが地球よりずっと大きいです。
example_sentences.english: The sun is far larger than Earth.

example_sentences.japanese: コンピュータは以前に比べてずっと使いやすくなった。
example_sentences.english: Computers have become much easier to use than before.

example_sentences.japanese: このシャンプーのほうがずっと安いけど、ボトルが小さい。
example_sentences.english: This shampoo is much cheaper, but the bottle is small.

example_sentences.japanese: 「薬を飲んだほうがいいですよ。ずっと気分がよくなるでしょう。」
example_sentences.english: 'You should take medicine! You will feel way better.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「さかもとくんは他のクラスメイトたちよりも、ずっと大人らしいね。」
example_sentences.english: 'Sakamoto-kun is far more mature than (even) his other classmates, don't you think?'

example_sentences.japanese: アムステルダムに比べて東京のほうがずっと混雑している都市です。
example_sentences.english: Tokyo is far more crowded when compared to Amsterdam.

example_sentences.japanese: その道よりこっちの道のほうがずっと早く行けるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: This street is probably much faster than that street.

example_sentences.japanese: 「この建物はここから、思ったよりもずっと大きく見えます。」
example_sentences.english: 'This building looks far bigger from here (even more) than I thought (it would).'

example_sentences.japanese: 漫画の主人公：「これから、ずっとずっと強くなるぞ。」
example_sentences.english: Manga main character: 'From now on I am going to become far, far stronger.'

example_sentences.japanese: ずっと運動していなかったから体が全然動かない。
example_sentences.english: I haven't exercised for an extremely long interval, so my body does not move at all.

example_sentences.japanese: そんな変な奴よりこっちの方がずっとすごいよ！
example_sentences.english: This one is so much better by a lot, compared to that weird thing!

general_translation: Completely covered in, Full of
formation: Noun + だらけNoun + だらけ + の + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + だらけNoun + だらけ + の + Noun
explanation: A grammar point expressing that (A) is covered in (B), often lots of individual small things.

example_sentences.japanese: 床が泥だらけになった。
example_sentences.english: The floor became covered in dirt.

example_sentences.japanese: パンケーキの裏側が穴だらけで気持ち悪い。
example_sentences.english: The underside of this pancake is covered in holes so it is gross.

example_sentences.japanese: この公園はゴミだらけだからこどもを連れて来たくない。
example_sentences.english: This park is covered in garbage, so I don't want to bring my kids here.

example_sentences.japanese: 傷だらけの車に乗っているのを見られたくないからいつも妻の車に乗ってる。
example_sentences.english: I don't want someone to see me drive a car covered in scratches, so I always drive my wife's car.

example_sentences.japanese: 泥だらけの服を洗濯機にいれないで！
example_sentences.english: Don't put mud-covered shirts in the washing machine!

example_sentences.japanese: 汗だらけでもかまわない。
example_sentences.english: I don't mind being covered in sweat.

example_sentences.japanese: あの壁はいつも落書きだらけだ。
example_sentences.english: That wall is always covered with graffiti.

example_sentences.japanese: 欠点だらけの人はいない。
example_sentences.english: No one is completely full of  faults.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人の話は矛盾だらけだ。
example_sentences.english: That person's stories are full of contradictions.

example_sentences.japanese: あの土地、知らないうちに雑草だらけになってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Before I knew it, that land had been completely overgrown with weeds.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかく海に来たのに、ビーチがゴミだらけだ。
example_sentences.english: I took the trouble to come to the ocean, and yet I found the beach completely covered in trash.

example_sentences.japanese: 初めての仕事だから、不安だらけですよ。
example_sentences.english: This is my first job, so I am filled with anxiety.

example_sentences.japanese: 先週、事故があって、血だらけの現場を見てしまった。今も夜、寝付きが悪い。
example_sentences.english: There was an accident last week where I witnessed a blood-covered scene. Now, I still have difficulties falling asleep.

example_sentences.japanese: 相撲の稽古がきつすぎて、全身傷だらけですよ。
example_sentences.english: My sumo training is too rough, and I have scars completely covering my body.

example_sentences.japanese: 歯医者に行ったら、「虫歯だらけだ」と言われてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I went to the dentist, and I was told that my teeth are 'full of cavities'.

example_sentences.japanese: 君の文章は間違いだらけ。書き直した方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: Your passage is full of mistakes. It would be better to rewrite it.

example_sentences.japanese: 壁をしろだらけに塗ってください。
example_sentences.english: Please cover my wall with white paint. (Unnatural, unless the speaker specifically wanted paint speckled, rather than covering the wall)

example_sentences.japanese: 血だらけのシャツをクリーニングに出した。
example_sentences.english: I took my blood-covered shirt to the dry cleaner. (Natural, as blood drops may be scattered)

general_translation: Although, But, However, For all that, Provided that
formation: Phrase (A)。もっとも + Phrase (B)。
casual_structure: Phrase (A)。もっとも + Phrase (B)。
explanation: An expression that highlights the previous statement as being reasonably or plausibly true, but (B) is the whole truth.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語を話せます。もっとも、少しだけですが。
example_sentences.english: I can speak Japanese. But only a bit.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の妹はピアノを弾くのがじょうずだ。もっとも、弾けるのは一曲だけだ。
example_sentences.english: My sister is good at playing the piano. Although, she can only play one song.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺はすき焼きが大好きだ。もっとも、毎日食べれる訳では無い。
example_sentences.english: I love sukiyaki. Although, it does not mean that I can eat it everyday.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は韓国についてものすごく詳しいです。もっとも、韓国には行った事が無いけど。
example_sentences.english: I am very knowledgeable about Korea, although I have never been there.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は会社に自分のパソコンを持ってきた。もっとも、自分のパソコンはいらないが。
example_sentences.english: I brought my own computer to work today, although I don't need to.

example_sentences.japanese: みんなラーメンが好きだ。もっとも、例外もありますよ。
example_sentences.english: Most people like ramen. But, there are exceptions.

example_sentences.japanese: それはいい質問です。もっとも、十分に説明できませんが。
example_sentences.english: This is a great question. However, I am not able to fully explain it.

example_sentences.japanese: 君は正しい。オレの一番好きなものは、ラーメンだ。もっともいつも食べられるわけではない。
example_sentences.english: You are right! My favorite one is ramen. But it doesn't mean I can always eat it.

example_sentences.japanese: とうとう仕事を見つけた。もっとも今では自分の時間がなくなったけど。
example_sentences.english: Finally, I have found a job. But now I don't have time for myself.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人の話は、ある程度まで信用できるようだ。もっともまだ疑わしい部分もあるけど。
example_sentences.english: It seems that that man's story can be trusted to some extent. However, there are still parts I doubt.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京について多くのことを知っているような気がする。もっとも行ったことはないけど。
example_sentences.english: It feels like I know a lot about Tokyo. But I have never been there.

example_sentences.japanese: 母さん。コンクールでは、オレが３番目で彼は最後から２番目だと言った。もっとも、参加者が３人だけだった。
example_sentences.english: Mom. Speaking of competition, I told you that I was third and he was next-to-last. But, there were only three participants.

example_sentences.japanese: ここにたくさんの杯があります。もっとも、私はどれが本物の聖杯かを教えることができませんが。上手く選んでください。
example_sentences.english: There are many cups here. However, I cannot tell you which one is the real holy grail. Choose wisely.

example_sentences.japanese: そのソフトのインストールプロセスは簡単だ。もっとも、上級ユーザーのために詳細オプションもあるけれども。
example_sentences.english: The installation process of that software is simple. But there are also advanced settings for advanced users.

example_sentences.japanese: この宝石は非常に貴重だ。もっとも私が持っている中で一番大切なわけではない。
example_sentences.english: This gem is incredibly precious. However, it does not mean it is the most valuable among the ones I have.

example_sentences.japanese: たけしさんは上手に描ける。もっとも、アニメのキャラクターだけ。
example_sentences.english: Takeshi can draw well. But only anime characters.

general_translation: Again, Once more, A second time
formation: ふたたび + Phrase
casual_structure: ふたたび + Phrase
explanation: A somewhat formal way to express that (A) will be done again, or for a second time.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はふたたび紙飛行機を飛ばした。
example_sentences.english: He threw a paper airplane a second time. (once more)

example_sentences.japanese: ふたたびふるさとに戻りたいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to go back to my home town again.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は刑務所から出て、ふたたび犯罪を犯した。
example_sentences.english: After he left prison, he committed a crime once more.

example_sentences.japanese: 免許をなくして、ふたたび発行してもらった。
example_sentences.english: I lost my driver's license and had it issued again. (a second time)

example_sentences.japanese: 来年もふたたびここに来たいです。
example_sentences.english: I want to come here again next year. (a second time)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はふたたび夜空を眺めた。
example_sentences.english: She looked at the night sky once more. (a second time)

example_sentences.japanese: 今家に帰ったばかりなのに、ふたたび呼び出された。
example_sentences.english: I just got home, but I was called in again. (a second time)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はやっとしゃべるところでしたが、ふたたび黙り込んでしまった。
example_sentences.english: He was about to finally talk, but he sunk into silence again. (a second time)

example_sentences.japanese: ふたたび訪れた土地で、懐かしい出会いがあった。
example_sentences.english: Visiting the land once more brought about a nostalgic encounter. (a second time)

example_sentences.japanese: ふたたび罪を犯さないようにして、真面目に生きてください。
example_sentences.english: Please live a serious life, make sure to not commit crime again. (a second time)

example_sentences.japanese: 不祥事で辞職したから、ふたたび選挙だ。
example_sentences.english: He resigned over the scandal, so we will hold an election once more. (a second time)

example_sentences.japanese: 私は一度やめた勉強をふたたび始めることにした。
example_sentences.english: I decided to start studying something again after stopping. (a second time)

example_sentences.japanese: すぐ退院すると思っていたが、ほかの病気のため、ふたたび入院してしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I thought I would soon leave the hospital but ended up getting hospitalized again due to another illness. (a second time)

example_sentences.japanese: 一度コーヒーを取りに行って、ふたたび読書に取り掛かった。
example_sentences.english: I got up once to grab some coffee, and then set about reading once more. (a second time)

example_sentences.japanese: また来週会いましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's meet again next week. (Natural)

example_sentences.japanese: 再び来週会いましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's meet once more next week. (Unnatural)

general_translation: ~ness, Used to indicate conditions or nature
formation: ［な］Adjective + み［い］Adjective［い］+ み
casual_structure: ［な］Adjective + み［い］Adjective［い］+ み
explanation: A suffix used to indicate the conditions or innate nature of an adjective, rather than the amount.

example_sentences.japanese: このスープは魚のうまみが感じられるね。
example_sentences.english: I can taste the deliciousness of the fish in this soup, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 大人になってから将棋の楽しみが分かってきた。
example_sentences.english: Since becoming an adult, I understand shogi's fun.

example_sentences.japanese: この色からこのフルーツの新鮮みがかんじられる。
example_sentences.english: From the color of this fruit, you can see its freshness.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達の大切みがわかった。
example_sentences.english: Now, I understand the importance of friends.

example_sentences.japanese: 温かみのある家に住みたいな。
example_sentences.english: I want to live in a house with warmth.

example_sentences.japanese: 人のいたみがわかる人間になろう。
example_sentences.english: Let's become people who can understand the pain of others. (~ness)

example_sentences.japanese: よわみを人に見せたくない。
example_sentences.english: I don't want to show others my weakness.

example_sentences.japanese: この文章は全然おもしろみがないな。
example_sentences.english: This sentence is not interesting at all. (~ness)

example_sentences.japanese: しぶみがある食べ物は苦手だ。
example_sentences.english: I don't really like foods that have a bitter taste. (bitterness)

example_sentences.japanese: たかみの見物といきますか。
example_sentences.english: Will you be a spectator? (Will you watch from (great) heights?)

example_sentences.japanese: この茶碗はとてもふかみがありますね。
example_sentences.english: This tea bowl has great depth, doesn't it? (~ness)

example_sentences.japanese: このまるみを帯びたデザインが好きだよ。
example_sentences.english: I love the slight roundness in the design.

example_sentences.japanese: 君のつよみは笑顔が素晴らしいことだ。
example_sentences.english: Your strength is your amazing smile. (~ness)

example_sentences.japanese: 子供の頬はうっすらとあかみを帯びている。
example_sentences.english: There is a slight redness to the child's cheeks.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日何かもらっていると、だんだんありがたみがなくなってくる。
example_sentences.english: If you receive something everyday, you will gradually lose the feeling of gratitude. (gratefulness)

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに隠していても、悪いことをすればいつかあかるみに出ますよ。
example_sentences.english: No matter how hard you try to hide it, if you do something bad, it will eventually come out into the light. (brightness)

example_sentences.japanese: どれぐらいの辛みの物が食べられる？
example_sentences.english: What's the hotness of something that you can eat? (Unnatural, as どれぐらい implies an amount, rather than a quality)

example_sentences.japanese: このケーキの甘みがちょうどいい。
example_sentences.english: The sweetness of this cake is perfect. (Natural, as this just means the 'type' of sweetness, rather than the 'level')

example_sentences.japanese: 昆布の旨味がちゃんと出てる！
example_sentences.english: The flavor of the kelp is really coming out! (The savory quality, rather than the intensity of savory flavor)

example_sentences.japanese: 髪を染めてから、赤みがなくなった。
example_sentences.english: After dying my hair, the redness has gone away. (The red quality, rather than the intensity of redness)

general_translation: About the same as, About as, No less
formation: Noun + と同（おな）じ + くらい(1)Noun + と同（おな）じ + くらい(1) + の + Noun(1) ぐらい
casual_structure: Noun + と同（おな）じ + くらい(1)Noun + と同（おな）じ + くらい(1) + の + Noun(1) ぐらい
explanation: A structure highlighting that something is approximately or about the same as (A).

example_sentences.japanese: うちのぽちはこの箱とおなじくらいの大きさだ。
example_sentences.english: Our Pochi is about the same size as this box.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼のパソコンはプリンターとおなじぐらい大きい。
example_sentences.english: His computer is about as big as his printer.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生、昨日とおなじぐらい痛いです。
example_sentences.english: Doctor, it hurts about the same as yesterday.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は車とおなじぐらいのスピードで走れる。
example_sentences.english: He can run at about the same speed as a car.

example_sentences.japanese: 今飼っている犬とおなじぐらいのサイズのワンチャンが欲しいです。
example_sentences.english: I want a puppy that is about the same size as the one I have now.

example_sentences.japanese: 値段が同じぐらいになるのなら、もっといいのを買います。
example_sentences.english: If the price is going to be about the same, I will buy the better one.

example_sentences.japanese: あの女の人はお母さんとおなじぐらいに見えたけど、年齢を聞いたらお祖母ちゃんと同い年だった。
example_sentences.english: That lady looked about the same age as my mother, but when I asked her, she was the same age as my grandma.

example_sentences.japanese: いつか、トモキとおなじくらいの身長になりたいな。
example_sentences.english: One day, I want to be about the same height as Tomoki.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの娘はきみの息子とおなじくらいの年齢だね？
example_sentences.english: My daughter is about the same age as your son, right?

example_sentences.japanese: ぼくにとってきみは金とおなじくらい貴重だよ。
example_sentences.english: For me, you are about as precious as gold. (about the same as)

example_sentences.japanese: このトランペットはピラミッドとおなじくらい古いです。
example_sentences.english: This trumpet is about as old as the pyramids. (about the same as)

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の気温は今日とおなじくらいで、１７℃前後になります。だから暖かい服装をしてください。
example_sentences.english: The temperature tomorrow will be about the same as today, around 17℃. Therefore, please put on warm clothes.

example_sentences.japanese: この唐辛子を食べるのは赤熱した鉄を触るのとおなじくらい痛いです。
example_sentences.english: Eating this chili pepper is about as painful as touching red hot iron. (about the same as)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は８０歳なのに、彼には初めて出会った時とおなじくらいに見えた。
example_sentences.english: Even though she was 80, for him she looked about the same as the time he met her for the first time.

example_sentences.japanese: このレシピは簡単そうです。難易度は炒り卵とおなじぐらいです。
example_sentences.english: This recipe seems easy. The degree of difficulty is about the same as scrambled eggs.

example_sentences.japanese: この自転車はカーボンファイバーからできているので、ラップトップとおなじぐらいの重さです。
example_sentences.english: This bike is made from carbon fiber, so it weighs about the same as a laptop.

example_sentences.japanese: これとおなじくらいの大きさのアニメのキャラクターのキーホルダーを見たことがありますか？
example_sentences.english: Have you ever seen a keychain with an anime character that is about the same size as this?

example_sentences.japanese: 店員さん：「申し訳ありませんが、このスマホを修復する値段は、新しいモデルを買うのとおなじくらいになりますので、新しいものを、ご購入なさった方がお得ですよ。」
example_sentences.english: Shop clerk：「I am awfully sorry, but the cost of repairing this smartphone is about the same as buying a new device, therefore buying a new device would be more economical.」

grammar_point: とおなじで・とちがって
general_translation: Like, Similar to, Unlike, Dissimilar to
formation: Noun + と + 同（おな）じでNoun + と + 違（ちが）って
casual_structure: Noun + と + 同（おな）じでNoun + と + 違（ちが）って
explanation: One of two phrases which may express something being like or similar to (A), or unlike or differing from (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 君とおなじでその意見に賛成だ。
example_sentences.english: Like you, I agree with that opinion.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は僕とおなじで、猫アレルギーです。
example_sentences.english: Just like me, he is allergic to cats.

example_sentences.japanese: 母も私とおなじで、アウトドアが好きです。
example_sentences.english: Just like me, my mother likes the outdoors.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は弟とちがって、本を読むのが大好きです。
example_sentences.english: Unlike my brother, I love to read books.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は私とちがって、遊園地が苦手です。
example_sentences.english: Unlike me, she does not like amusement parks very much.

example_sentences.japanese: フィンランドとちがって、ハワイは一年中暖かい。
example_sentences.english: Unlike Finland, Hawaii is warm year round.

example_sentences.japanese: 天気予報とちがって今日はとても暖かい。
example_sentences.english: Unlike what the forecast said, today is very warm.

example_sentences.japanese: 大統領とちがって、副大統領は優しい。
example_sentences.english: Unlike the president, the vice president is kind.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生とおなじで、僕も日本語が大好きです。
example_sentences.english: Like my teacher, I love Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 普段とちがって、随分お洒落をしてどこに行くんですか？
example_sentences.english: That's quite different from what you normally wear. Where are you going in such fancy dress?

example_sentences.japanese: 空気とおなじで、電波は見えないけど存在しています。
example_sentences.english: Similar to air, radio waves exists even though you can't see them.

example_sentences.japanese: チョコの入った箱とおなじで、人生は驚きに満ちているものだ。
example_sentences.english: Like a box of chocolates, life is full of surprises.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼も私とおなじでスポーツカーを運転するのが好きだ。
example_sentences.english: Like me, he likes to drive sports cars.

example_sentences.japanese: 父親とおなじで、彼はとても働き者だ。
example_sentences.english: Just like his father, he is a hard worker.

example_sentences.japanese: 他人とちがって家族の縁はなかなか切れない。
example_sentences.english: Unlike other people, I find it hard to cut ties with my family.

example_sentences.japanese: 母親とちがって、彼女はとても料理が上手です。
example_sentences.english: Unlike her mother, she is good at cooking.

general_translation: In line with, Comparable with, Along with, Just like, As … as
formation: Noun + と並（なら）んでNoun + と並（なら）ぶほど
casual_structure: Noun + と並（なら）んでNoun + と並（なら）ぶほど
explanation: A formal expression showing that something is comparable to (A), due to being in line with it.

example_sentences.japanese: ラーメンもまた、寿司とならんで人気の日本食だ。
example_sentences.english: In line with sushi, ramen is also a popular Japanese food.

example_sentences.japanese: 日産はトヨタとならぶほど車を出しています。
example_sentences.english: Nissan produces about in line with the same number of cars as Toyota.

example_sentences.japanese: このアニメはサザエさんとならんで、日本中で愛されている。
example_sentences.english: This anime is as loved as Sazae-san in Japan. (In line with the same level of love)

example_sentences.japanese: ここではきしめんも手羽先とならんで人気です。
example_sentences.english: Here, kishimen is comparable in popularity to chicken wings.

example_sentences.japanese: この映画はあの映画とならぶほどいいが、ほとんどの人はこの映画を選ぶ。
example_sentences.english: This movie is almost comparable to that movie in how good it is, but most people would choose this one.

example_sentences.japanese: この芸術作品はモナ・リザとならんで高く評価されている。
example_sentences.english: This piece of art is valued as highly as Mona Lisa. (comparable・along with)

example_sentences.japanese: 喫煙は揚げ物とならんで癌を引き起こす確率が高い。
example_sentences.english: Smoking has as high a probability of causing cancer as deep-fried foods do. (comparable・along with)

example_sentences.japanese: 東京大学は慶應義塾大学や早稲田大学とならんで日本屈指の大学として考えられている。
example_sentences.english: The University of Tokyo, along with Keio University and Waseda University, are considered to be Japan's best universities. (comparable with)

example_sentences.japanese: 宮崎駿は小津安二郎や黒澤明とならんで日本三大監督の一人と言われている。
example_sentences.english: Hayao Miyazaki is said to be one of the three great Japanese directors, along with Akira Kurosawa and Yasujiro Ozu. (comparable)

example_sentences.japanese: 交通事故の原因で不注意運転はスピード違反とならんで第一位となっています。
example_sentences.english: Distracted driving has become a primary cause of traffic accidents, along with speeding. (comparable with)

example_sentences.japanese: 横浜は大阪や名古屋とならんで日本の大都市の一つである。
example_sentences.english: Yokohama is one of the biggest Japanese cities, along with Osaka and Nagoya. (comparable)

example_sentences.japanese: 新しい研究によると食事制限は運動とならんで重要です。
example_sentences.english: According to a new study, food restriction is as important as exercising. (comparable・along with)

example_sentences.japanese: それにより、北海道は沖縄とならんで人気のある観光地となっていた。
example_sentences.english: Because of that, Hokkaido has become a tourist destination as popular as Okinawa. (comparable・along with)

example_sentences.japanese: それにしても前者は後者とならんで英雄として称されるようになった。
example_sentences.english: Despite that, the former became known as a hero along with the latter. (comparable)

example_sentences.japanese: 『1Q84』は『ノルウェイの森』とならんでむらかみはるきの最高小説の一つとして評価が高い。
example_sentences.english: '1Q84' is highly valued as one of best Haruki Murakami novels, comparable with 'Norwegian Wood'. (along with)

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「寿司は最近、国際的に人気になったんですね。」Ｂ：「そうですね。アニメ、日本車とならんで日本の三大輸出品の一つとも言われているんですよ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Sushi has recently become popular internationally, hasn't it?'B: 'That's right. Along with anime and cars, it is said to be one of Japan's three major exports.' (comparable with)

general_translation: There is no doubt that, I'm sure
formation: Verb + に違（ちが）いない［い］Adjective + に違（ちが）いない［な］Adjective + に違（ちが）いないNoun + に違（ちが）いない
casual_structure: Verb + に違（ちが）いない［い］Adjective + に違（ちが）いない［な］Adjective + に違（ちが）いないNoun + に違（ちが）いない
polite_structure: Verb + に違（ちが）いありません［い］Adjective + に違（ちが）いありません［な］Adjective + に違（ちが）いありませんNoun + に違（ちが）いありません
explanation: An expression that highlights that there is no mistaking (A).

example_sentences.japanese: あの顔は日本人にちがいない。
example_sentences.english: That face... there is no doubt that that person is Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼らは、先生がいなくなったらふざけるにちがいない。
example_sentences.english: There is no doubt that they will muck around once the teacher has gone.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたが美味しいというなら、美味しいにちがいない。
example_sentences.english: If you say that it is good, I have no doubt that it is.

example_sentences.japanese: タナカ君は全然料理を食べてない。この料理が嫌いにちがいない。
example_sentences.english: Tanaka-kun is not eating his food at all. There is no doubt that he does not like it.

example_sentences.japanese: 今のピンポンは近所の子供のいたずらにちがいない。
example_sentences.english: There's no doubt that the doorbell I just heard must have been a prank by the neighbor's kid.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は病気にちがいない。
example_sentences.english: There is no doubt that she is sick.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなに遅いなんて…、何かあったにちがいない。
example_sentences.english: Being so late... there is no doubt that something happened.

example_sentences.japanese: あの言い方だと、何か隠しているにちがいない。
example_sentences.english: From the way he speaks, there is no doubt that he is hiding something.

example_sentences.japanese: 大雪が降って大変だったにちがいない。
example_sentences.english: I am sure that it was tough after that heavy snowfall.

example_sentences.japanese: あんな転び方をして、痛いにちがいない。
example_sentences.english: Falling in that way, there is no doubt that it hurts.

example_sentences.japanese: 電話の声からいって、２０代にちがいない。
example_sentences.english: Judging from the voice on the phone, I am sure they were in their twenties.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近全然休みがないから、彼は疲れているにちがいない。
example_sentences.english: He hasn't rested at all recently, so I am sure he is tired.

example_sentences.japanese: あの格好からいって、あの人はお金持ちにちがいない。
example_sentences.english: Judging from appearances, I am sure that person is loaded.

example_sentences.japanese: あの体つきからいって、相当筋トレをしているにちがいない。
example_sentences.english: Judging from his body build, there is no doubt that he is working out a lot.

example_sentences.japanese: 何回呼び鈴を押しても出てこない。きっと寝ているにちがいない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how many times I ring the bell, they won't come out. I am sure they are sleeping.

example_sentences.japanese: 現場で彼の髪の毛が見つかったので、彼は犯人にちがいない。
example_sentences.english: His hair was found at the scene. There is no doubt that he is the offender.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人はカメラマンに囲まれている、有名人に違いない。
example_sentences.english: That person is surrounded by cameramen. There is no discrepancy in that person being famous. (No reason to disbelieve)

general_translation: Per~, A~, Apiece, Each
formation: Number + Counter + 当（あ）たり
casual_structure: Number + Counter + 当（あ）たり
explanation: A word used to indicate set units of (A), or per (A). With each being expressed as strikes or hits.

example_sentences.japanese: これは１個あたり５０キロカロリーあります。
example_sentences.english: These have 50 kilocalories apiece.

example_sentences.japanese: 一個あたり五円で作ることができます。
example_sentences.english: We are able to make this for 5 yen each.

example_sentences.japanese: 一食あたりのカロリーは５００ｋＣａｌです。
example_sentences.english: It has 500 calories per serving.

example_sentences.japanese: このコーヒーは一缶あたり￥１３０（税込）。
example_sentences.english: This coffee is 130￥per can (tax included).

example_sentences.japanese: 一個あたりの代金は千円です。
example_sentences.english: The price is 1000 yen per item.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人あたり三個ずつパンを配ります。
example_sentences.english: I will hand out three pastries per person.

example_sentences.japanese: １日あたり１０００円の手当てが出ます。
example_sentences.english: 1000 yen will be provided per day.

example_sentences.japanese: 一世帯あたりの食費を調査しています。
example_sentences.english: I am taking a survey on food expenses per household.

example_sentences.japanese: あの土地の一平米あたりの価格が知りたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to know how much that land costs per square meter.

example_sentences.japanese: 一週間あたりのスマホの使用時間を書き出してみたら、かなりの時間になった。
example_sentences.english: I recorded the hours I spent using my smartphone each week, and it turned out to be quite lot of time.

example_sentences.japanese: 給料は年俸だけど、一か月あたり三十万くらいかな。
example_sentences.english: I get an annual salary, but it comes out to about 300,000 yen per month.

example_sentences.japanese: 一国あたりの二酸化炭素排出量ランキングが気になって調べてみた。
example_sentences.english: I was curious about the rankings of carbon dioxide emissions per country and looked it up.

example_sentences.japanese: 車１台あたり４人ずつ乗っていきましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's go 4 people per car.

example_sentences.japanese: このチケット１枚あたり３人入場できます。
example_sentences.english: 3 people per ticket are allowed to enter.

example_sentences.japanese: この車は１台当たり１トンあります。
example_sentences.english: This car equates to 1 ton per vehicle.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人当たり５０００円で入場できます。
example_sentences.english: The price for entry per person equates to 5000 yen.

general_translation: Correspond to, Amounts to, Equals to, Is appropriate
formation: Noun + に当（あ）たるNoun + に当（あ）たる + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + に当（あ）たるNoun + に当（あ）たる + Noun
polite_structure: Noun + に当（あ）たりますNoun + に当（あ）たる + Noun
explanation: A construction showing that something corresponds to, or equals (A). Hits the mark on (A).

example_sentences.japanese: おじと呼んでいるけど、実はいとこにあたるんだ。
example_sentences.english: I call him 'uncle,' but in reality, he is my cousin.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年は仕事を始めてから５年目にあたる。
example_sentences.english: This year amounts to the 5th year since I've started working. (It's been 5 years since I've started this job)

example_sentences.japanese: 先生はタナカ君のいとこにあたる。
example_sentences.english: The teacher is Tanaka-kun's cousin.

example_sentences.japanese: 英語の「what's up」は日本語の「元気」にあたる表現だ。
example_sentences.english: 'What's up' in English corresponds to the expression 'genki' in Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: その人は私の親戚にあたる人です。
example_sentences.english: That person is my relative.

example_sentences.japanese: ハクは納豆を食べるのが好きなのに対して、チヒロは納豆があまり好きじゃない。
example_sentences.english: As opposed to Haku who likes eating natto, Chihiro does not like eating it as much.

example_sentences.japanese: 「Hello」は日本で「こんにちは」にあたる言葉です。
example_sentences.english: 'Hello' corresponds to the Japanese word 'konnichiwa'.

example_sentences.japanese: 江戸という都市は現在の東京にあたる。
example_sentences.english: The city called 'Edo' corresponds to present-day Tokyo.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女の長男のリンゴパンはパムの父にあたる。
example_sentences.english: Her eldest son, Ringopan, also corresponds to the father of Pamu.

example_sentences.japanese: 「地下鉄」にあたる言葉は、イギリスでは「underground」で、アメリカでは「subway」です。
example_sentences.english: The word corresponding to 'chikatetsu' is 'underground' in the United Kingdom, and 'subway' in the United States.

example_sentences.japanese: ドイツでは日本の首相にあたる役職を「Bundeskanzler 」と呼んでいる。
example_sentences.english: In Germany, the position corresponding to the Japanese prime minister is called 'Bundeskanzler'.

example_sentences.japanese: ２００６ＦＩＦＡワールドカップ・決勝を見ていたのは約７億５０００万人。つまり、これは当時の世界人口の１０人に１．１人にあたる。
example_sentences.english: The amount of people who watched the 2006 FIFA World Cup Final was about 750 million. In other words, this corresponds to 1.1 out of 10 of the world's population at that time.

example_sentences.japanese: オレはきみのお母さんの弟なんだよ。つまり、きみにとってオジサンにあたるんだよ。
example_sentences.english: I am the younger brother of your mother. In short, to you, I am your uncle.

example_sentences.japanese: ミオ：「ペソしか持ってないけど、アルゼンチン・ペソは日本円で、いくらにあたるかな？」ユコ：「だいたい２．５円にあたるでしょうね。」
example_sentences.english: Mio: 'I have only the peso, but I wonder how much the Argentinian peso corresponds to the Japanese yen?'Yuko: 'It amounts to 2.5 yen.'

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の「すみません」にあたる表現は英語では「I'm sorry」はもちろん「Thank you」や「Excuse me」でもある。
example_sentences.english: The expression corresponding to Japanese 'sumimasen' is not only 'I'm sorry' but also 'thank you' and 'excuse me' in English.

example_sentences.japanese: とある漫画家によるとポーランド語の「 ザクシャ・イン・ラブ 」はおおよそ日本語の「愛を永遠に」にあたるらしい。
example_sentences.english: According to a certain manga artist, the Polish 'Zawsze in love' is roughly equivalent to the Japanese 'forever in love'.

example_sentences.japanese: 英語には仕事を終えて帰る時に言う「お疲れ様でした。」にあたる表現はない。
example_sentences.english: In English, there is no expression corresponding to 'otsukaresamadeshita,' which is said when leaving to go home after finishing work.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語能力試験中には「四つの言葉の選択肢のうち、★の位置にあたるものはどれですか」のような問題もある。
example_sentences.english: There are also questions on the JLPT like 'Among these four (word) choices, which one corresponds to the field with the ★?'.

general_translation: Nothing better than, There's nothing like, Limited to
formation: Verb［る］(1) + に限（かぎ）るNoun + に限（かぎ）る(1) Verb［ない］
casual_structure: Verb［る］(1) + に限（かぎ）るNoun + に限（かぎ）る(1) Verb［ない］
polite_structure: Verb［る］(1) + に限（かぎ）りますNoun + に限（かぎ）ります(1) Verb［ない］
explanation: An expression showing that something is limited to being within or in (A). Highlighting that there's nothing like (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 疲れた時は寝るにかぎる。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than sleep when you are tired.

example_sentences.japanese: 暑い日は冷たいシャワーを浴びるにかぎる。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than taking a cold shower on a hot day.

example_sentences.japanese: 回転寿司はくら寿司にかぎる。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than Kurazushi when it comes to kaiten-sushi.

example_sentences.japanese: 寒い日には温かい部屋を出ないにかぎる。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better to do than not leaving your warm room on a cold day.

example_sentences.japanese: 休みの日には仕事をしないにかぎる。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than doing no work on a day off.

example_sentences.japanese: 寒い夜は鍋にかぎる。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than nabe on a cold night.

example_sentences.japanese: やっぱり秋刀魚は目黒にかぎる。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing like Samma (fish) from Meguro.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事の後はジュースにかぎる。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than a juice after work.

example_sentences.japanese: 登山をするなら、富士山にかぎる。
example_sentences.english: If you are going climbing, there is nothing like Mt. Fuji.

example_sentences.japanese: 家具を買うなら、このお店にかぎる。
example_sentences.english: If you are going to buy furniture, there is nowhere better than this place.

example_sentences.japanese: 暇な時は読書にかぎる。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than reading when you have free time.

example_sentences.japanese: ストレス解消なら、温泉にかぎる。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than onsen if you want to get rid of stress.

example_sentences.japanese: パート募集中。但し経験者にかぎる。
example_sentences.english: Part time job available - Work experience required. (Limited to experienced workers)

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行は電車にかぎる。駅弁もジュースも楽しめるから。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than going on trips by train. One can enjoy both eki-ben and juice.

example_sentences.japanese: アルバイト募集中。ただし、英語ができる人にかぎる。
example_sentences.english: They are hiring. However, the position is only limited to people who can speak English.

example_sentences.japanese: ダイエットをしたいなら、運動をするにかぎる。
example_sentences.english: There is nothing better than exercise when it comes to losing weight.

example_sentences.japanese: 暑い日にはアイスクリームを食べるに限る。
example_sentences.english: I am bound to eat ice cream on a hot day.

example_sentences.japanese: この施設を利用できるのはこのアパートの住民に限る。
example_sentences.english: Using this facility is limited to those who live in this apartment complex.

general_translation: Not necessarily so, Is not always true, There is no guarantee that
formation: Verb + とは限（かぎ）らない［い］Adjective + とは限（かぎ）らない［な］Adjective + だ + とは限（かぎ）らないNoun + だ + とは限（かぎ）らない
casual_structure: Verb + とは限（かぎ）らない［い］Adjective + とは限（かぎ）らない［な］Adjective + だ + とは限（かぎ）らないNoun + だ + とは限（かぎ）らない
polite_structure: Verb + とは限（かぎ）りません［い］Adjective + とは限（かぎ）りません［な］Adjective + だ + とは限（かぎ）りませんNoun + だ + とは限（かぎ）りません
explanation: An expression that highlights a specific phrase as not being the limit of possibilities.

example_sentences.japanese: にわとりは鳥ですが、飛べるとはかぎりません。
example_sentences.english: A chicken is a bird, but it does not necessarily mean it can fly.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本に２年間住んでいるからといって、日本語を話せるとはかぎらない。
example_sentences.english: Just because someone lives in Japan for two years does not necessarily mean that they can speak Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 日が出てても暖かいとはかぎらない。
example_sentences.english: Just because the sun is out, doesn't necessarily mean that it is warm.

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎でも静かだとはかぎらない。
example_sentences.english: A place being rural doesn't necessarily mean that it is quiet.

example_sentences.japanese: 社長だからといって乗っている車が高級車だとはかぎらない。
example_sentences.english: It is not limited to him driving a luxury car, just because he is the CEO.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰もがお寿司が好きだとはかぎらない。
example_sentences.english: Not everyone necessarily likes sushi.

example_sentences.japanese: たとえどんなに緻密な計画を立てても、うまくいくとはかぎらない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how detailed your plan, it is not guaranteed to go well.

example_sentences.japanese: 君の言うことがいつも正しいとはかぎらないでしょ。
example_sentences.english: The things you say are not necessarily always right.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強ができても、頭がいいとはかぎらない。
example_sentences.english: Just because one is good at studying, doesn't necessarily mean that he (she) is smart.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人の言うことが全て事実とはかぎらない。
example_sentences.english: The things that person says are not always true.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎年冬に必ず雪が降るとはかぎらない。
example_sentences.english: It is not necessarily the case that it will snow every winter.

example_sentences.japanese: すべての人間が上手に歌えるとはかぎらない。
example_sentences.english: It is not necessarily true that everybody can sing well.

example_sentences.japanese: 裕福になっても、幸福になれるとはかぎらない。
example_sentences.english: Even if you become rich, there is no guarantee that you will be happy.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で暮らしている人が、みんな寂しい思いをしているとはかぎらない。
example_sentences.english: It is not always true that all people living alone have lonely thoughts.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は「愛している」と言ってくれているが、離婚しないとはかぎらない。
example_sentences.english: Just because she says she loves me doesn't necessarily mean we won't get divorced.

example_sentences.japanese: いつも答えが同じだとはかぎりません。気分によって変わることもあります。
example_sentences.english: It is not always true that I answer in the same way. It depends on my mood. (not necessarily)

general_translation: Hardly, Rarely, Seldom
formation: めったに + Verb［ない］Noun + は + めったにない
casual_structure: めったに + Verb［ない］Noun + は + めったにない
polite_structure: めったに + Verb［ない］Noun + は + めったにありません
explanation: A phrase that means something is seldom done, but literally means not done thoughtlessly or recklessly.

example_sentences.japanese: 父はめったにテレビを見ない。
example_sentences.english: My father rarely watches TV.

example_sentences.japanese: 大人になってから駄菓子屋にはめったに行かない。
example_sentences.english: Ever since I became an adult, I hardly go to candy stores.

example_sentences.japanese: 親とは正月以外にはめったに会わない。
example_sentences.english: Other than New Years, I hardly see my parents.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなチャンスはめったにないぞ！
example_sentences.english: A chance like this is very rare.

example_sentences.japanese: パーティーに行くことはめったにない。
example_sentences.english: I rarely go to parties.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなにいい話しはめったにない。
example_sentences.english: Such a nice story is rarely (heard).

example_sentences.japanese: めったに泣かない彼が泣いていた。
example_sentences.english: He, who hardly cries, was crying. (seldom・rarely)

example_sentences.japanese: 僕のおじいちゃんはめったに笑わない。
example_sentences.english: My grandpa seldom smiles.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はめったに忘れないのに、今日はどうしたんだろう？
example_sentences.english: He rarely forgets, I wonder what happened today?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は出不精だから、めったに出かけない。
example_sentences.english: Since he is a homebody, he hardly goes out. (seldom・rarely)

example_sentences.japanese: 最近は彼にめったに会わない。どうしたんだろう？
example_sentences.english: I rarely see him around these days. I wonder what's up?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女についての悪口をめったに聞かない。
example_sentences.english: I seldom hear bad things about her.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかく日本語を勉強したけど、めったに話さないね。
example_sentences.english: After going through all the trouble of studying Japanese, you hardly speak it. (seldom・rarely)

example_sentences.japanese: うちの親はめったに怒りませんが、本当に悪いことをした時には怒ります。
example_sentences.english: My parents seldom get angry, but when I do something really bad, they will get mad.

example_sentences.japanese: めったに休まない彼が休んでいるのだから、かなり体調が悪いんだろうな。
example_sentences.english: Since he, who rarely takes leave, took time off, his condition is probably quite bad.

example_sentences.japanese: めったに本を読みませんが、珍しく読みたい本があったので買ってみました。
example_sentences.english: I seldom read, but there was a book that I wanted to read, so I bought it.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は何か大事が起きない限り、電話はめったに掛けない。
example_sentences.english: Unless something big happens, I don't mindlessly make phone calls.

example_sentences.japanese: 家の誰かがテレビを見ていない限り、自分からはテレビをめったに見ない。
example_sentences.english: Unless someone in my house is watching TV, I don't aimlessly watch TV on my own.

general_translation: Although, Despite, Rather...for, Unexpectedly, Comparatively, Considering
formation: Verb + わりに［い］Adjective + わりに［な］Adjective + な + わりにNoun + の + わりに
casual_structure: Verb + わりに［い］Adjective + わりに［な］Adjective + な + わりにNoun + の + わりに
explanation: A phrase that shows that something is unexpected, proportionately to what the norm of (A) is.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は冬のわりに暖かい。
example_sentences.english: Today is rather warm for winter.

example_sentences.japanese: この肉、高いわりには味がないね。
example_sentences.english: Although this meat is expensive, it is not flavorful.

example_sentences.japanese: 太っているわりには運動神経がいいんだね。
example_sentences.english: Although you are fat, you are very athletic, aren't you?

example_sentences.japanese: この機械のパワーは強いわりにめちゃくちゃ遅いです。
example_sentences.english: Although this machine is very powerful, it is very slow.

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋は綺麗なわりには臭いね。
example_sentences.english: Although this room is clean, it smells bad.

example_sentences.japanese: ラッシュアワーのわりには空いていますね。
example_sentences.english: Although it is during rush hour, the road is very clear.

example_sentences.japanese: 高い食べ物のわりに、美味しくなさそう。
example_sentences.english: The expensive food looks unexpectedly unappetizing.

example_sentences.japanese: 私はたくさん勉強したわりに、テストの点数が悪かった。
example_sentences.english: Although I studied a lot, I got a bad score on the test.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は頭が良いわりに、コミュニケーションが苦手です。
example_sentences.english: Although that person is smart, he is bad at communication.

example_sentences.japanese: 疲れているわりには、かなり動けた方だと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think he is quite active for how tired he is.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は年齢のわりにかなり元気な方だと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think my dad is rather energetic for his age.

example_sentences.japanese: 偉そうだったわりにあの人サッカーが下手だな。
example_sentences.english: Although he acted all high and mighty, he is actually not good at soccer.

example_sentences.japanese: このジュース、高かったわりに普通の味でがっかりした。
example_sentences.english: To my disappointment, this juice had a rather ordinary taste for such a high price.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はお金がないと言っているわりに、しょっちゅう服を買っている。
example_sentences.english: Despite saying she has no money, she keeps buying clothes.

example_sentences.japanese: このみかん、安かったわりには美味しかった。
example_sentences.english: This mandarin tasted rather good for such a low price.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語はそんなに勉強していないと言うわりに、随分上手に話せるんですね。
example_sentences.english: You speak surprisingly well given what you were saying about not studying much.

example_sentences.japanese: この会社、仕事が簡単なわりに給料がいい。
example_sentences.english: This company pays you rather well for such easy work.

example_sentences.japanese: これ割と美味しいよ。
example_sentences.english: This is unexpectedly tasty.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日買った包丁は割といい。
example_sentences.english: The knife I bought yesterday is quite good.

general_translation: Try to, Attempt to, To be about to
formation: Verb［おう］ + とする
casual_structure: Verb［おう］ + とする
polite_structure: Verb［おう］ + とします
explanation: A structure that highlights the strong will to attempt, or be about to perform an action.

example_sentences.japanese: 一度に二つのことをしようとするな。
example_sentences.english: Don't try to do two things at once.

example_sentences.japanese: この子はなんでも食べようとするから、お菓子は隠してね。
example_sentences.english: This one will try to eat anything, so please hide any snacks.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生が話している間に帰ろうとすると、先生に怒られる。
example_sentences.english: If you try to go home while the teacher is talking, he will yell at you.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年は毎日日本語の勉強をしようとしたが、時間がなくて出来なかった。
example_sentences.english: I tried to study Japanese everyday this year, but I couldn't because I didn't have time.

example_sentences.japanese: クラスメイトのスズキさんに話し掛けようとしたけど、緊張し過ぎて話せなかった。
example_sentences.english: I tried to talk to my classmate, Suzuki-san, but I got so nervous that I couldn't.

example_sentences.japanese: ひよこは親のようにとぼうとしても、できなかった。
example_sentences.english: Even though the chick attempted to fly like its parents, it couldn't.

example_sentences.japanese: こたえようとしたのに、隣の人に遮られた。
example_sentences.english: I tried to answer but the person next to me cut me off.

example_sentences.japanese: みようとしたわけではないのに、見えてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Even though I tried not to look, I inevitably saw it. (It's not like I tried to look)

example_sentences.japanese: 私はとめようとしたのに、言うことを聞いてくれないんです。
example_sentences.english: I attempted to stop them, but they won't listen to what I say.

example_sentences.japanese: 見て！子犬がしっぽをつかまえようとしている！とてもかわいい！
example_sentences.english: Look! The puppy is trying to catch its tail! It's so cute!

example_sentences.japanese: 犯人は、にげようとした時に、警察に捕まえられた。
example_sentences.english: Just as the culprit tried to escape, he was caught by police.

example_sentences.japanese: 「鬱」の書き順が何回おぼえようとしても、覚えられない。
example_sentences.english: No matter how many times I try to remember the stroke order of '鬱' I cannot remember it.

example_sentences.japanese: 囚人１：「 どうしてここにいるんだ？」囚人２：「天皇の最も貴重な宝石をぬすもうとしたんだ。」
example_sentences.english: Prisoner 1: 'Why are you here?'Prisoner 2: 'I attempted to steal the Emperor's most valuable gem.'

example_sentences.japanese: 禁煙区域でタバコをすおうとする人が多いので、監視装置を設置することになった。
example_sentences.english: There are many people who attempt to smoke at non-smoking areas, so it has been decided that surveillance equipment will be installed.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「なぜ君はそんな顔をしているの？」Ｂ：「 昨日、好きな人を呼び出して、告白しようとした・・・」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Why are you making such a face?' B: 'Yesterday I called the person I like and tried to confess my love…'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「何をしているの？！」Ｂ：「ネズミをつかまえようとしているわ。そんなに驚かないで！とにかく、手伝って！」
example_sentences.english: A: 'What are you doing?!'B: 'I am trying to catch a mouse! Don't be so taken aback! Just help me!'

example_sentences.japanese: 家を出ようとしたら、急に雨が降り始めた。
example_sentences.english: It suddenly started to rain when I was about to leave the house.

example_sentences.japanese: 部屋が暗かったから電気を点けようとしたら、妻に電気を点けるなと言われた。
example_sentences.english: As I tried to turn on the lights in my room because it was dark, my wife told me not to.

grammar_point: う・よう + としたが
general_translation: Tried to ~ but ~, Was about to ~ but ~, Was going to ~ but ~
formation: Verb［おう］ + としたが(1) + ResultVerb［おう］ + としたら + Result(1) けれども、けれど、けど
casual_structure: Verb［おう］ + としたが(1) + ResultVerb［おう］ + としたら + Result(1) けれども、けれど、けど
explanation: A phrase which indicates that someone had the will or intent to do (A), but was unable to complete the action for some reason.

example_sentences.japanese: 兎の世話をしようとしたが逃げられた。
example_sentences.english: I was going to take care of the rabbit but it ran away.

example_sentences.japanese: クライアントに電話を掛けようとしたが、夜遅かったので朝まで待つことにした。
example_sentences.english: I was going to make a phone call to our client, but it was late at night so I decided to wait until morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 池で泳ごうとしたら、警察に止められた。
example_sentences.english: I was stopped by the police when I was about to swim in the lake.

example_sentences.japanese: 逃げようとしたけど、捕まったら大変なことになるから逃げなかった。
example_sentences.english: I was about to run away, but if I got caught, it would have become a bigger deal, so I didn't.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は徹夜しようとしたけれど寝てしまった。
example_sentences.english: He tried to pull an all-nighter, but fell asleep.

example_sentences.japanese: 説得しようとしたが、失敗した。
example_sentences.english: I tried to persuade him, but I failed.

example_sentences.japanese: お弁当をたべようとしたが、箸が入っていなかった。
example_sentences.english: I was about to eat my bento, but there were no chopsticks inside.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は彼女の手伝いをしようとしたが、断られた。
example_sentences.english: I tried to help her, but was rejected.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強しようとしたが、あまりにも疲れていたのでやめました。
example_sentences.english: I tried to study, but I was too tired and I gave up.

example_sentences.japanese: 謝罪しようとしたけれど、受け入れてもらえませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I tried to apologize, but they didn't accept my apology.

example_sentences.japanese: でかけようとしたけれど、あまりにも天気が悪いのでやめました。
example_sentences.english: I was about to go out, but I ended up changing my mind because the weather wasn't looking too great.

example_sentences.japanese: 質問をしようとしたが、機嫌が悪そうだったのでやめました。
example_sentences.english: I was about to ask a question, but she looked like she was in a bad mood, so I thought I better not.

example_sentences.japanese: 家に帰ってすぐ宿題をすませようとしたが、難しくてできなかった。
example_sentences.english: I was going to finish my homework as soon as I got home, but I couldn't do it because it was too hard.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕と彼は同時にジャンプしようとしたけれど、失敗した。
example_sentences.english: He and I both tried to jump at the same time, but messed up.

example_sentences.japanese: 犯人はにげようとしたが、すぐに警察が犯人を取り押さえた。
example_sentences.english: The criminal tried to run, but the police subdued him.

grammar_point: 言（い）うまでもない ②
general_translation: It goes without saying, It is needless to say, Of course, Obviously
formation: 言（い）うまでもない + こと(1) + だが + Phrase(Phrase (A)) + 言（い）うまでもなく + Phrase (B)(Phrase (A)) + 言（い）うまでもない + が(2) + Phrase (B)(1) の(2) けれども、けれど、けども、けど
casual_structure: 言（い）うまでもない + こと(1) + だが + Phrase(Phrase (A)) + 言（い）うまでもなく + Phrase (B)(Phrase (A)) + 言（い）うまでもない + が(2) + Phrase (B)(1) の(2) けれども、けれど、けども、けど
explanation: An expression showing that even going until (A) needs to be said is not required, due to being obvious.

example_sentences.japanese: いうまでもないけど、それが恋だった。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying, but that was love.

example_sentences.japanese: いうまでもないことだが、毎日漢字の勉強をすれば、どんどん漢字を覚えることができる。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that if you practice kanji everyday, you will steadily memorize them.

example_sentences.japanese: 電化製品を使っている間、いうまでもないが、濡れた手や水の周りで使うのは危険だ。
example_sentences.english: While you are using electronics, it is needless to say that it is dangerous to use them with wet hands or around water.

example_sentences.japanese: いうまでもないけど、君に会えて良かった。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying, but I am glad that I met you.

example_sentences.japanese: いうまでもなくもうこんなこと知ってるよね。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that you already know this, right?

example_sentences.japanese: しかし、いうまでもなく、私たちはいつものように負けた。
example_sentences.english: However, it goes without saying, we lost just as always.

example_sentences.japanese: いうまでもないことだが、文章を読みやすくするために、括弧は使われている。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that brackets are used to make reading easier.

example_sentences.japanese: さだおさんの妻のえみさんは英語はいうまでもなく、韓国語も話せます。
example_sentences.english: Sadao-san's wife, Emi-san can speak Korean, not to mention English.

example_sentences.japanese: いうまでもないことだが、アルコールを飲んで泳いだら、溺れて死んでしまうかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that if you drink and go swimming, then you might drown.

example_sentences.japanese: いうまでもないことだが、家のドアを開けっぱなしにしてしまうのは泥棒を家へ招くこととおなじだ。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that leaving your house doors open is equivalent to inviting in thieves.

example_sentences.japanese: いうまでもないだろうが、借りたものは持ち主に返すべきだ。
example_sentences.english: It probably goes without saying that anything you borrow should be returned to its rightful owner.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京オリンピックのあいだ、いうまでもないが電車やバスなどはすごく混むだろう。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that during the Tokyo Olympics, trains, buses, etc will be extremely crowded.

example_sentences.japanese: それが人によるのはいうまでもないですが、広い視野からいうと共通の特徴もあります。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that it depends on the person, but if you look from a wider perspective, there are also some common features.

example_sentences.japanese: いうまでもないのだが、より良い商品はより高価である。
example_sentences.english: It goes without saying that better goods are more expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「あのさ近づいちゃいけない動物っているの？」Ｂ：「う～ん....ライオンやヘビみたいなのはいうまでもないけどカバも危ないよ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Hey, are there any animals I shouldn't approach?'B: 'Hmm, lions and snakes go without saying, but hippos are also dangerous.'

example_sentences.japanese: いうまでもないことだが、お酒を飲んで運転をしてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: Obviously,  you should not drink and drive.

general_translation: Very unlikely to, Does not seem that, Does not appear that
formation: Verb［stem］+ そうもない
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ そうもない
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ そうもありません
explanation: A grammar point which states that the action of (A) does not even seem likely.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回のテストはうかりそうもない。
example_sentences.english: It is very unlikely I will pass the test this time.

example_sentences.japanese: 腕がまだ治っていないから、あと一週間ぐらい運動が出来そうもない。
example_sentences.english: My arm hasn't healed yet, so it is very unlikely that I will exercise for another week.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は雷が酷いから、釣りに行けそうもない。
example_sentences.english: Since the thunder is very bad today, it does not even appear like I can go fishing.

example_sentences.japanese: このテーブルは重たいから、一人ではこべそうもない。
example_sentences.english: Since this table is so heavy, it's very unlikely that I'll be able to carry it by myself.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人、僕の意見をきいてくれそうもない。
example_sentences.english: It is very unlikely that that person will listen to my opinion.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなすごい技、僕にはできそうもない。
example_sentences.english: It's very unlikely that I will be able to perform such a cool trick.

example_sentences.japanese: 予報は雨だけど、全然ふりそうもない。
example_sentences.english: The forecast predicted rain, but it doesn't appear that it will rain at all.

example_sentences.japanese: この調子じゃ、彼は今日もきそうもない。
example_sentences.english: It is very unlikely that he will come today if it keeps on like this.

example_sentences.japanese: 怪我をしてしまったから、来週の旅行はいけそうもない。
example_sentences.english: It is very unlikely that I will be able to go on the trip next week because I injured myself.

example_sentences.japanese: 実現できそうもない目標ばかり立てるのはやめてください。
example_sentences.english: Please stop setting goals that are very unlikely to become a reality.

example_sentences.japanese: 荷物が多すぎて、バッグにはいりそうもない。
example_sentences.english: I have so many things to pack, it is very unlikely that it will all fit in the bag.

example_sentences.japanese: まだ怒っているみたいだから、許してもらえそうもない。
example_sentences.english: She still looks angry, so it is very unlikely she will forgive you.

example_sentences.japanese: あんまり雪が降っていないから、スキーができそうもない。
example_sentences.english: It's very unlikely that we'll be able to ski since it didn't snow very much.

example_sentences.japanese: ごめんね、今週末は忙しくてあそべそうもない。
example_sentences.english: Sorry, it's very unlikely that I'll be able to hang out this weekend because I'm so busy.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな量、食べられそうもない。
example_sentences.english: This amount, it doesn't even seem like I can eat it! (There is way too much to even seem possible to eat)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は１１時まで帰って来ないかもしれないから、いつも見ているテレビ番組が見られそうもない。
example_sentences.english: Today, I might not be coming home until 11, so I might not be able to watch the show I always watch.

general_translation: Is not impossible, It doesn't mean that it isn't
formation: Verb［ない］+ ことはない(1)［い］Adjective［ない］+ ことはない(1)［な］Adjective + ではない(2) + ことはない(1)(1) こともない(2) じゃない
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ ことはない(1)［い］Adjective［ない］+ ことはない(1)［な］Adjective + ではない(2) + ことはない(1)(1) こともない(2) じゃない
polite_structure: Verb［ない］+ ことはありません(1)［い］Adjective［ない］+ ことはありません(1)［な］Adjective + ではない(2) + ことはありません(1)(1) こともありません(2) じゃない
explanation: A structure that expresses the thing that is (A) as not being impossible, or not what isn't meant.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「浅いからここで泳ごう！」 Ｂ：「浅いけど、あぶなくないことはない。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'It's shallow so let's swim here!' B: 'It is shallow, but that doesn't mean that it isn't dangerous.'

example_sentences.japanese: 映画は見ないことはないが、詳しくもない。
example_sentences.english: It's not that I don't watch movies, but I am just not knowledgeable about them at all.

example_sentences.japanese: ここは危なくないことはないから、気をつけた方がいい。
example_sentences.english: It's not that this place isn't dangerous, so you should be careful.

example_sentences.japanese: 元気ではないことはないけど、すごく元気なわけでもない。
example_sentences.english: It doesn't mean that I am not healthy, but it is not the case that I am very fit.

example_sentences.japanese: 清水：「昨年買ったドレスを着たら、どう？」木村：「きれないことはないが、少しサイズが小さいな。」
example_sentences.english: Shimizu: 'What about wearing the dress you bought last year?'Kimura: 'It's not that I can't wear it, but it's a bit too small…'

example_sentences.japanese: 林：「怪我はないか？歩ける？」森：「歩いていけないことはないんですが、かなりゆっくりですね。」
example_sentences.english: Hayashi: 'Are you hurt? Can you walk?'Mori: 'It's not that I can't walk, but I'll be quite slow…'

example_sentences.japanese: 小川：「ビットコインのことを何か知ってるの？」村上：「何もしらないことはないが、詳しくもない。」
example_sentences.english: Ogawa: 'Do you know anything about bitcoin?'Murakami: 'It's not that I don't know anything, but I am not familiar either.'

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「お金がないから君と一緒に旅行にいけないんだ。」 Ｂ：「お金がなくても旅行にいけないことはないよ。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'I don't have money so I can't go on a trip with you.' B: 'It is not impossible to take a trip without any money.'

example_sentences.japanese: 片岡：「何を話してたのか知らないんだよ！」小池：「あんなに近くにいてきこえないことはないでしょ。」
example_sentences.english: Kataoka: 'I have no idea what they were talking about!'Koike: 'You were so close, there is no way that you didn't hear...'

example_sentences.japanese: 吉田：「あなたは誕生日ケーキをカットしてみたい？」山田：「 僕にもできないことはないけど、君がやった方がいいと思う。」
example_sentences.english: Yoshida: 'Do you want to cut the birthday cake?'Yamada: 'It's not that I can't do it, but I think it would be better if you did it.'

example_sentences.japanese: 水野：「トリプルビーのコンサートチケットを手に入れてもらえる？」安田：「とれないことはないけど、あの歌手のチケットは相当高いよ。」
example_sentences.english: Mizuno: 'Can you get the tickets for the BBB concert?'Yasuda: 'It's not impossible to get them, but the tickets for that singer are quite expensive.'

example_sentences.japanese: 石川：「彼は手術後は、歩けるようになるでしょうか？」上田：「そんなあるけないことはないけど、見たことがありません。」
example_sentences.english: Ishikawa: 'Will he be able to walk after the operation?'Ueda: 'It is not impossible (walking), but I have never seen it (happen).'

example_sentences.japanese: 竹内：「エンジンはどのように動作するのか？話してくれる？」杉本：「いえないことはないんですが、うまく説明できないんです。」
example_sentences.english: Takeuchi: 'How does the engine work? Could you tell me?'Sugimoto: 'It's not that I can't tell you, but I can't explain it well.'

example_sentences.japanese: スクルージ：「オレはオジサンになったから新しいことを全然学べない。」 ヒューイ：「どんなに歳を取っても新しいことをまなべないことはない。」
example_sentences.english: Scrooge: 'I got old, so I can't learn new things at all.' Huey: 'No matter how old you get, it is not impossible to learn new things!'

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の生徒：「先生、友達と話す時、敬語を使用できますか？」先生：「つかわないことはないですが、堅苦しいです。」
example_sentences.english: Student: 'Can I use keigo when I am talking with friends?'Teacher: 'It's not that you can't use it, but it's pretty formal.'

example_sentences.japanese: 納豆は食べられないことはないけど、自分から買って食べようとは思わない。
example_sentences.english: It's not that I don't like natto, it's just that I don't think I will buy it myself to eat.

example_sentences.japanese: 歩いていけないことはないけど、歩いたら６時間ぐらいかかるよ。
example_sentences.english: It's not that you can't walk there, but if you did, it would take about six hours.

general_translation: Such as, Things like, Emphasis
formation: Verb + なんて［い］Adjective + なんて［な］Adjective + なんてNoun + なんて(1)(1) なんか
casual_structure: Verb + なんて［い］Adjective + なんて［な］Adjective + なんてNoun + なんて(1)(1) なんか
explanation: A casual expression used for emphasis or pointing out similar things. Often used simply to fill in the silence in sentences.

example_sentences.japanese: 人生なんてそんなもんさ。
example_sentences.english: Such is life.

example_sentences.japanese: こんな嵐の中走るなんて、頭おかしいんじゃない。
example_sentences.english: You are going to do something like run in the storm? You must be crazy.

example_sentences.japanese: 北海道がこんなに寒いなんておもわなかった。
example_sentences.english: I didn't think Hokkaido would be this cold or anything.

example_sentences.japanese: 心配なんてしている場合じゃない。
example_sentences.english: This is no time for things such as worrying.

example_sentences.japanese: テレビなんか叩けばだいたい直るだろ。
example_sentences.english: Things like TV's will be fixed most of the time if you hit them, right?

example_sentences.japanese: お世辞なんて大嫌いだ！
example_sentences.english: I hate things like flattery!

example_sentences.japanese: 嘘なんかつかないよ。信じてよ。
example_sentences.english: I would never do something like lie to you. Trust me.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が太っているなんて言わないで。
example_sentences.english: Don't say things like I am fat.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕には道案内なんてできませんよ。
example_sentences.english: I am unable to do things like give directions.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨なんかに負けている場合じゃないですよ。
example_sentences.english: Now is not the time to give in to something like rain.

example_sentences.japanese: あんな高い絵を買うなんてどうかしている。
example_sentences.english: That person is crazy to buy an expensive picture such as that.

example_sentences.japanese: あの強いチームに勝つなんて思わなかった。
example_sentences.english: Things like winning against that good team didn't even cross my mind.

example_sentences.japanese: 紹介なんていりません。自分で恋人を見つけます。
example_sentences.english: I don't need things like referrals. I can find my own lover.

example_sentences.japanese: 「夢なんか捨てちまえ」って言われたけど、僕は諦めたくないんだ。
example_sentences.english: I was told 'things like dreams should be tossed aside', but I won't give up (on mine).

example_sentences.japanese: 人の話なんか全然聞いていないんだから、困ったもんだ。
example_sentences.english: Since that person doesn't listen to things like what other people are saying, I'm in a bind.

example_sentences.japanese: 泣き寝入りなんてしたくない。最後まで戦う！
example_sentences.english: I refuse to do something like giving up in frustration! I will fight to the end!

example_sentences.japanese: 私なんか５年間スペイン語の勉強をしているのにまだ全然会話ができないです。
example_sentences.english: I have studied Spanish for 5 years, but I can't speak it at all yet. (Humility)

example_sentences.japanese: お前なんてどうせ、家でゴロゴロしているだけだろ。
example_sentences.english: Someone like you probably just loafs around the house, don't you? (Insult)

example_sentences.japanese: 酷いことを言ったのは分かるんだけど、なんか、感情的になって言っちゃった。
example_sentences.english: I am aware that I said something mean, but, you know, I said it because I got emotional.

general_translation: Moreover, Additionally, And also, In addition, Furthermore, Or
formation: Phrase、また + Noun +（も）Phrase。また + Noun +（も）
casual_structure: Phrase、また + Noun +（も）Phrase。また + Noun +（も）
explanation: An expression indicating that in addition to (A), (B). Branching off from (A), also (B). Usually (A) and (B) are equally important.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬はイヌ科である。また、狐もイヌ科である。
example_sentences.english: Dogs are canidae. Additionally, foxes are also canidae.

example_sentences.japanese: このキーボードはピアノの音が出せる。また、ギターの音も出せる。
example_sentences.english: This keyboard can make piano sounds. Additionally, it can produce guitar sounds.

example_sentences.japanese: この電子レンジはオーブンとして使えて、またトースターとしても使える。
example_sentences.english: This microwave can be used as an oven, additionally, it can be used as a toaster.

example_sentences.japanese: ササキ先生は理科の先生です。また、地理の先生でもある。
example_sentences.english: Sasaki-sensei is a science teacher. She is also a geography teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達は何でも買います。また、古くても買い取ります。
example_sentences.english: We will buy anything. Moreover, we will buy it even if it's old.

example_sentences.japanese: その詩は悲しく、また、感動させる文学でもある。
example_sentences.english: That poem is sad, additionally, it is also a touching piece of literature.

example_sentences.japanese: このアプリはＪＰＧファイルを読み、また、ＰＮＧファイルも読む。
example_sentences.english: This application reads JPG files, in addition, it also reads PNG files.
