example_sentences.japanese: 燕尾服を着てもよいです。また、スーツを着てもよいです。
example_sentences.english: You can wear a tailcoat. Additionally, you can also wear a suit.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は有名な歌手であり、また、腕のいい外科医でもある。
example_sentences.english: He is a famous singer, additionally, he is also a skilled surgeon.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近のスマートフォンはポータブルコンピュータとして使えるし、また、コンパスなどの機能もある。
example_sentences.english: Modern smartphones can be used as portable computers, furthermore, they also have functions like compass, etc.

example_sentences.japanese: ブラックホールは魅力的であり、また、それと同時に危なくもあります。
example_sentences.english: Black holes are captivating, in addition to (also) being dangerous at the same time.

example_sentences.japanese: このおもちゃは１０〜１５歳のお子様向けです。また、６歳以上のお子様なら保護者同伴でご使用いただけます。
example_sentences.english: This toy is suitable for children between the ages of 10 and 15. Additionally, it can also be used by children over six, under the supervision of the guardian.

example_sentences.japanese: １８世紀の芸者は踊ったり三味線などを弾いたりして客人を楽しませ、また、芸者の中には腕のいい書道家や詩人もいた。
example_sentences.english: 18th-century geisha entertained clients with things like dancing or the playing of instruments like the shamisen, furthermore, some were also skilled calligraphers and poets.

example_sentences.japanese: この青い丸薬を選んでもよい。そうすると物語が終わる。また、赤いのを選んでもよい...
example_sentences.english: You can take this blue pill. And the story ends. Additionally, you can also take the red one...

example_sentences.japanese: ＳＳＤはＨＤＤと比べて機械部品は少ないし、また、書き込みや読み出し速度もずっと高速である。
example_sentences.english: SSD, when compared to HDD, has few mechanical parts, furthermore, the writing and reading speeds are also much faster.

example_sentences.japanese: 「から」は理由や原因を表す。また、「スマホの画面はガラスからできている。」のように何かの起源やソースも表すことがある。
example_sentences.english: 'から' indicates reason or cause. Additionally, there are also times when it indicates an origin or source of something like 'Smartphone screens are made from glass.'.

general_translation: While you are at it, On the occasion
formation: Verb + ついでにNoun + の + ついでにPhrase。ついでに + Phrase
casual_structure: Verb + ついでにNoun + の + ついでにPhrase。ついでに + Phrase
explanation: An expression that says if (A) is the precedence, or originally happening, then (B) can be done while you're at it.

example_sentences.japanese: ついでに君の分も払ってあげるよ。
example_sentences.english: While I am at it, I will pay for your share too.

example_sentences.japanese: 買い物に行くついでに、郵便局に行ってこの荷物を出しておいてくれる？
example_sentences.english: Can you bring these packages to the post office while you go shopping?

example_sentences.japanese: 散歩のついでに寄って行ってください。
example_sentences.english: Please go and visit while you are on a walk.

example_sentences.japanese: お母さんの所にテレビを返しに行くのでしょう？ついでにこの、私が作った梅酒を持って行って。
example_sentences.english: You are going to go to your mother's place to give back the TV you borrowed, right? While you're at it, can you take the Umeshu I made?

example_sentences.japanese: ついでに君の車も洗ってあげようか？
example_sentences.english: While I am at it, do you want me to wash your car too?

example_sentences.japanese: ここまで来たならついでにうちにも寄ってよ。
example_sentences.english: On the occasion of coming this far, why don't you drop by my house?

example_sentences.japanese: 話のついでに言っておきたいことがあります。
example_sentences.english: While I am on the subject, I want to tell you something.

example_sentences.japanese: 給油のついでに車を点検してもらいました。
example_sentences.english: While I was refueling, I also had my car checked.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼に会うなら、ついでにこのＣＤを渡してもらえないかな？
example_sentences.english: If you are meeting him anyway, could you give him this CD while you are at it?

example_sentences.japanese: 東京に行ったついでに、ディズニーランドへ行った。
example_sentences.english: While I was in Tokyo, I went to Disneyland.

example_sentences.japanese: 注文のついでに、お水のおかわりもお願いします。
example_sentences.english: While you are at it (ordering), could you get me another cup of water.

example_sentences.japanese: 遊びに来るんだったら、ついでに漫画も持ってきてよ。
example_sentences.english: If you are dropping by, bring some manga while you're at it.

example_sentences.japanese: お風呂に入るついでに、お風呂掃除もしてしまおう。
example_sentences.english: While I am in the bath, I will clean it.

example_sentences.japanese: コンビニでお菓子を買うついでに、水道料金の支払いもした。
example_sentences.english: While buying snacks at the convenience store, I also paid the water bill. (while I am at it)

example_sentences.japanese: 散歩のついでに、郵便局に寄って切手を買いました。
example_sentences.english: I was taking a walk and, while I was at it, I stopped by the post office and bought stamps.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達を家に送ったついでに、床屋に行った。
example_sentences.english: On the way back from driving my friend home, I went to the barber. (One-off occurrence)

example_sentences.japanese: 旦那はいつも、私が寝てる間に帰ってくる。
example_sentences.english: My husband always comes back while I am sleeping. (Regular occurrence)

example_sentences.japanese: 私は晴れているときに出かける。
example_sentences.english: I go out when it is sunny. (Regular occurrence)

general_translation: Together with, At the same time,  As well as
formation: Verb + と共（とも）に［い］Adjective + と共（とも）に［な］Adjective + である + と共（とも）にNoun + と共（とも）に
casual_structure: Verb + と共（とも）に［い］Adjective + と共（とも）に［な］Adjective + である + と共（とも）にNoun + と共（とも）に
explanation: A grammar point that shows two or more things happening or existing in unison, or as one.

example_sentences.japanese: 風とともに去りぬ。
example_sentences.english: Gone with the Wind.

example_sentences.japanese: 風が強くなるとともに雨が降ってきます。
example_sentences.english: As the wind gets strong, it will start to rain.

example_sentences.japanese: あの先生は厳しいが、厳しいとともに優しい。
example_sentences.english: That teacher is strict, but as strict as he is, he is also very kind.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕が住んでいる場所は静かであるとともに、空気が綺麗だ。
example_sentences.english: The place I live is very quiet, together with the air being clean.

example_sentences.japanese: 私とともに人生を歩んでくれませんか。
example_sentences.english: Would you please walk together with me forever. (歩（あゆ）む is a poetic way of saying 'to walk' that often means 'to travel a passage')

example_sentences.japanese: 心身とともに健康だ。
example_sentences.english: I am healthy physically, as well as mentally.

example_sentences.japanese: 夜明けとともに旅立った。
example_sentences.english: (I) departed with the break of dawn. (together with)

example_sentences.japanese: 驚きとともに喜びが溢れ出してきた。
example_sentences.english: I am becoming overwhelmed with surprise coupled with delight.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は今でも父とともに仕事をしています。
example_sentences.english: I still work together with my father.

example_sentences.japanese: 私とともに論文の発表をしてくれませんか。
example_sentences.english: Would you mind presenting the paper with me?

example_sentences.japanese: 息子が日本に住んでいるので、寂しいとともに、誇りもあります。
example_sentences.english: Since my son lives in Japan, I feel sad as well as proud.

example_sentences.japanese: 年を取るとともに、体が動きにくくなる一方だ。
example_sentences.english: As we grow older, it becomes more and more difficult to move our bodies. (Along with)

example_sentences.japanese: そのシリーズ本は怪奇であるとともに、恐ろしいと考えられている。
example_sentences.english: That book series is considered mysterious, as well as terrifying.

example_sentences.japanese: スマホの普及とともに、生活スタイルも変わってきた。
example_sentences.english: Everyone's lifestyle has changed together with the popularization of the smartphone.

example_sentences.japanese: 仲間とともに助け合い、なんとか頂上に辿り着いた。
example_sentences.english: I finally reached the summit together with my friends, thanks to everyone's cooperation.

example_sentences.japanese: 今後も妻とともに二人三脚で、人生を歩んでいきたいと思っています。
example_sentences.english: I plan to walk through life together with my wife now and forever.

example_sentences.japanese: 年を取ると共に、身体がどんどん硬くなってきた。
example_sentences.english: As I get older, I am starting to get less flexible.

example_sentences.japanese: この池は綺麗であると共に、危険である。
example_sentences.english: This lake is beautiful and dangerous at the same time.

general_translation: As…then, In proportion to, (Along) with
formation: Verb［る］+ につれ（て）Noun + につれ（て）
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ につれ（て）Noun + につれ（て）
explanation: A phrase that shows that (B) will be taken along with (A), and act in proportion or equivalence to it.

example_sentences.japanese: 日がたつにつれて、怪我が悪化してきた。
example_sentences.english: As the days go by, my injury gets worse and worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日運転をするにつれて、どんどん運転が嫌いになってきた。
example_sentences.english: As I drove everyday, I came to dislike driving more and more.

example_sentences.japanese: 夏になるにつれて、日が昇るのが早くなってきた。
example_sentences.english: Along with it becoming summer, the time the sun comes up is getting earlier.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬の成長につれて、食欲が変わる。
example_sentences.english: As the dog grows, how much he eats changes (in proportion).

example_sentences.japanese: 時代の変化につれて、食文化も変わる。
example_sentences.english: As the times change, food culture also changes.

example_sentences.japanese: 冬になるにつれて、太陽が沈む時間が早くなる。
example_sentences.english: Along with it becoming winter, the time the sun sets gets earlier. (Natural, as winter directly affects the time the sun sets)

example_sentences.japanese: 冬になるにつれて、犬が成長していく。
example_sentences.english: In tow with it becoming winter, the dog grows more. (Unnatural, as there is no relationship)

example_sentences.japanese: こちらの木が大きくなるにつれて、影が広がります。
example_sentences.english: As these trees grow tall, their shade spreads.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供は、成長するにつれて、性格が変わる。
example_sentences.english: Along with their growth, the personality of children changes.

example_sentences.japanese: 進むにつれて道がどんどん狭くなるから心配になってきた。
example_sentences.english: As I continued on, the road grew increasingly more narrow, so I started to feel anxious.

example_sentences.japanese: 経済の発展につれて一般市民の日常生活は良くなっていく。
example_sentences.english: As the economy develops, the daily life of citizens improves.

example_sentences.japanese: 冬の間は、日が沈むにつれてどんどん温度が下がっていく。
example_sentences.english: During winter, the temperature rapidly decreases as the sun goes down.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が大きくなるにつれて、一緒に出かける機会が少なくなってきた。
example_sentences.english: As your children grow older, you have fewer and fewer chances to go out and do things with them.

example_sentences.japanese: 商品が売れるにつれて、品質が落ちることもあるようです。
example_sentences.english: As sales increase, the quality of the product could sometimes get worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 大人になるにつれて、いい人も悪い人もいるということが分かってきた。
example_sentences.english: As I grow older, I am beginning to realize that there are good and bad people.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事が忙しくなるにつれて、睡眠時間が少なくなっています。
example_sentences.english: As I get busier with my job, I have less and less time for sleep.

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚式を挙げる日が近づくにつれて、色々と不安になってきた。
example_sentences.english: (Along) with our wedding day drawing nearer, I am starting to feel anxious about various things.

example_sentences.japanese: パソコンを使う機会が増えるにつれて、だんだん漢字が書けなくなっている。
example_sentences.english: As the opportunity to use computers increases, people gradually lose their ability to write kanji.

general_translation: At once, Immediately, As soon as
formation: 直（ただ）ちに + Phrase
casual_structure: 直（ただ）ちに + Phrase
explanation: An expression meaning that (A) will intentionally be done immediately, with the nuance of directly, or straight away.

example_sentences.japanese: 効果はただちに現れるわけではありません。
example_sentences.english: The effect will not become immediately apparent.

example_sentences.japanese: ただちに避難所へ向かってください。
example_sentences.english: Please head to the evacuation point immediately.

example_sentences.japanese: この山から、 ただちに出て行ってください。ここは私有地です。
example_sentences.english: Please leave this mountain at once. This is private property.

example_sentences.japanese: 地震が起きたらただちに家を出てください。
example_sentences.english: If an earthquake occurs, please leave the house immediately.

example_sentences.japanese: ただちに安定した仕事を見つけなければ。
example_sentences.english: I must find a stable job at once.

example_sentences.japanese: この案件はただちに対応する必要がある。
example_sentences.english: It is necessary to deal with this problem immediately.

example_sentences.japanese: 結果が出たらただちにお伝えします。
example_sentences.english: I will tell you as soon as the results are available.

example_sentences.japanese: 急ごう。ただちに出発した方がいい。
example_sentences.english: Let's hurry. We'd better leave at once.

example_sentences.japanese: ただちに行動しないと、手遅れになりますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you don't start acting at once, it will be too late.

example_sentences.japanese: イベントが終わったらただちに片付けてください。
example_sentences.english: Please clean immediately after the event finishes.

example_sentences.japanese: ただちに影響が出るほどのことではありません。
example_sentences.english: It's not so serious that it will have an immediate effect.

example_sentences.japanese: ただちに改善案を出してください。
example_sentences.english: Please submit suggestions for improvement at once.

example_sentences.japanese: ただちに車を移動させてください。そこは駐車禁止です。
example_sentences.english: Please move your car immediately. This is a no parking zone.

example_sentences.japanese: 判決はただちには出ません。裁判は何年もかかるかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: The judgment won't be given immediately. The trial might take several years.

example_sentences.japanese: 締め切りが迫っているので、ただちに印刷してください。
example_sentences.english: The deadline is swiftly approaching. Please print it at once.

example_sentences.japanese: 計画が変わったら、ただちに報告してください。
example_sentences.english: If the plan changes, please notify me immediately. (Intentional)

example_sentences.japanese: このファッションは忽ち世界で広まった。
example_sentences.english: This fashion spread around the world immediately. (Unintentional)

general_translation: The instant or moment, As soon as, Just as
formation: Verb［た］+ とたん(に)
casual_structure: Verb［た］+ とたん(に)
explanation: A phrase that indicates something happening the instant that (A) does, or on the tip of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: でたとたんに、雨が降り始めた。
example_sentences.english: The instant I went outside, it began to rain.

example_sentences.japanese: 高速に乗ったとたんに、タイヤがパンクした。
example_sentences.english: The moment I got on the highway, my tire got punctured.

example_sentences.japanese: 布団に入ったとたんに先輩から電話がかかってきた。
example_sentences.english: The moment I got into my futon, I received a call from my senpai.

example_sentences.japanese: 帰ろうとしたとたん、仕事を頼まれた。
example_sentences.english: Just as I was about to leave, I was given more work to do.

example_sentences.japanese: 青になったとたんに飛び出すのは危ないよ。
example_sentences.english: It's dangerous to speed off the instant (a traffic light) turns (became) green.

example_sentences.japanese: 家にはいったとたん呼び鈴が鳴った。
example_sentences.english: Just as I got into the house, the doorbell rang.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女をみたとたんに恋をしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I fell in love the instant I saw her.

example_sentences.japanese: 店をひらいたとたん、お客さんが殺到した。
example_sentences.english: The instant (we) opened the shop, customers rushed in.

example_sentences.japanese: すわったとたん用事を思い出した。
example_sentences.english: As soon as I sat down, I remembered something I had to do.

example_sentences.japanese: 窓をあけたとたん、鳥が部屋の中に入ってきた。
example_sentences.english: As soon as I opened the window, a bird flew into the room.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はメールをみたとたん泣き出してしまいました。
example_sentences.english: She started crying as soon as she saw the text.

example_sentences.japanese: ユナちゃんは布団にはいったとたん寝てしまいました。疲れていたんですね。
example_sentences.english: Yuna fell asleep as soon as she got into bed. She must have been worn out.

example_sentences.japanese: ほしいものを手にいれたとたんに興味を失ってしまう人もいる。
example_sentences.english: There are people who lose interest in things they wanted as soon as they get it.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は随分大人になっていたが、みたとたんあの子だと分かった。
example_sentences.english: She had grown up a lot, but I knew that child was her the moment I saw her.

general_translation: Repeated at intervals, Every other, Every, At intervals of
formation: Number + Counter + おきに
casual_structure: Number + Counter + おきに
explanation: A phrase which indicates something happening every (A), focusing on repeated intervals or spaces of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: ３０分おきに休憩しよう。
example_sentences.english: Let's take a break in intervals of 30 minutes.

example_sentences.japanese: この薬は一日おきに飲んでください。
example_sentences.english: Please drink this medicine at intervals of one day. (Every second day)

example_sentences.japanese: 一ヶ月おきに病院に来るように先生に言われました。
example_sentences.english: I was told by the doctor to come to the hospital at intervals of one month. (Every second month)

example_sentences.japanese: 二日おきに部屋の掃除をしないと気が落ち着かない。
example_sentences.english: I can't relax if I don't clean my room at intervals of two days. (Every three days)

example_sentences.japanese: 約３分おきに電車が来ます。
example_sentences.english: Trains come about every 3 minutes.

example_sentences.japanese: １時間おきに温度を測ってください。
example_sentences.english: Please check the temperature every other hour.

example_sentences.japanese: ５０メートルおきに自動販売機がある。
example_sentences.english: There are vending machines every 50 meters.

example_sentences.japanese: 階段を一段おきに飛ばして上がる。
example_sentences.english: He goes up the stairs skipping every second step.

example_sentences.japanese: 一部屋おきに消火器を設置しました。
example_sentences.english: I installed fire extinguishers in every other room.

example_sentences.japanese: 一週間おきに、水槽の水を換えています。
example_sentences.english: We change the water of the fish tank every other week.

example_sentences.japanese: 金魚には餌を一日おきにやればいいらしい。
example_sentences.english: I've heard that you can feed goldfish every second day.

example_sentences.japanese: この地域はだいたい一軒おきに新聞をとっている。
example_sentences.english: In this area, every other house is subscribed to the newspaper.

example_sentences.japanese: メイ：「バスは何分おきにくるの？」 サツキ：「１時間おきに。」
example_sentences.english: Mei: 'How often does the bus come?' Satsuki: 'Every other hour.'

example_sentences.japanese: だいたい二年おきにスマホを買い替えます。
example_sentences.english: I change my smartphone at about two-year intervals.

example_sentences.japanese: 数時間おきに目が覚めるから寝不足です。
example_sentences.english: I lack sleep because I wake up every few hours.

example_sentences.japanese: 一日ごとに目薬を差す。
example_sentences.english: I use my eye drops every day. (It doesn't matter what part of the day, but it does happen every day)

example_sentences.japanese: 一日おきに目薬を差す。
example_sentences.english: I use my eye drops every second day. (It makes sense to wonder when it may occur during the second day, but we know it doesn't happen for at least an interval of one whole day)

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日２時間ごとに体を動かしている。
example_sentences.english: I move my body every two hours, every day. (At some point during every group of 2 hours)

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日２時間おきに体を動かしている。
example_sentences.english: I move my body every two hours, every day. (After every interval of two hours. Nobody cares about 'when during the third hour', so we just understand it as 'every two hours')

general_translation: Each time, Every time, Whenever
formation: Verb［る］+ たびにNoun + の + たびに
casual_structure: Verb［る］+ たびにNoun + の + たびに
explanation: An expression that states that something happens every (A), where the focus is on the unique occurrence or degree of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 君は会うたびに大人になってゆく。
example_sentences.english: Every time I see you, I see how much you have matured.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は休みのたびにハワイへ行きます。
example_sentences.english: Whenever I have a holiday, I go to Hawaii.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は洗い物のたびに指を切る。
example_sentences.english: Every time he does the dishes, he cuts his finger.

example_sentences.japanese: タナカ君と飲みに行くたびに、二日酔いになる。
example_sentences.english: Every time I go out to drink with Tanaka-kun, I get a hangover.

example_sentences.japanese: 牛乳を飲むたびにお腹が痛くなる。
example_sentences.english: Every time I drink milk, I get a stomach ache.

example_sentences.japanese: この映画を見るたびに、泣いてしまう。
example_sentences.english: Every time I watch this movie, I cry.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行のたびに、いい思い出を作ろう。
example_sentences.english: Let's make good memories each time we take a trip.

example_sentences.japanese: 冬の間は、休みのたびにスキーに行っています。
example_sentences.english: I go skiing every holiday in winter.

example_sentences.japanese: 買い物へ行くたびに、いらないものを買っちゃう。
example_sentences.english: Whenever I go shopping I buy things I don't need.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車が通るたびに音が鳴るからストレスだ。
example_sentences.english: I am stressed out because every time the train passes it makes noise.

example_sentences.japanese: 何かが起こるたびに呼び出されて大変です。
example_sentences.english: I am called in every time something happens, and it is driving me nuts.

example_sentences.japanese: 車の調子がおかしいな。曲がるたびに音がする。
example_sentences.english: There is something wrong with my car. It makes a sound every time I make a turn.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強するたびに、どんどん日本語が上手くなりますね。
example_sentences.english: Your Japanese improves every time you study.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は来るたびに長居するからあまり来て欲しくない。
example_sentences.english: I don't want him to visit me because he stays so long every time he comes.

example_sentences.japanese: 冬こそ大嫌いな季節ですよ。雪が降るたびに雪かきをしなければいけないからです。
example_sentences.english: I hate winter more than any other season. Because every time it snows, I have to clear snow away.

example_sentences.japanese: 検査のたびに何か病気が見つかるのは年のせいかな。
example_sentences.english: Every time I get a medical check up, some kind of illness is discovered. I wonder if it has to do with my age.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事を休むたびに、雨が降って予定が台無しになる。
example_sentences.english: Every time I take a day off, it rains and messes up my plans. (Natural Japanese, as たびに follows an action)

example_sentences.japanese: ２週間たびに、実家に帰る。
example_sentences.english: Every two weeks, I go to my parents house. (Unnatural Japanese, as たびに does not follow an action. ２（に）週間（しゅうかん）経（た）つたびに would work here)

general_translation: Or, Possibly, Maybe, Perhaps, Or possibly
formation: Verb + か + あるいは［い］Adjective + か + あるいは［な］Adjective + か + あるいはNoun + （か） + あるいはあるいは + Phrase + かもしれない
casual_structure: Verb + か + あるいは［い］Adjective + か + あるいは［な］Adjective + か + あるいはNoun + （か） + あるいはあるいは + Phrase + かもしれない
polite_structure: Verb + か + あるいは［い］Adjective + か + あるいは［な］Adjective + か + あるいはNoun + （か） + あるいはあるいは + Phrase + かもしれません
explanation: An expression used to say or, possibly, or maybe, literally indicating (A) or a certain (B) which is like (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 鍋あるいは深めのフライパンを使いましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's use a pot or a deep frying pan.

example_sentences.japanese: 牛乳あるいはチーズが使われている料理は食べられません。
example_sentences.english: I can't eat anything that uses milk, or another possibility is cheese.

example_sentences.japanese: 月曜日あるいは火曜日に新しい生徒が来ます。
example_sentences.english: A new student will come on either Monday, or another possibility is Tuesday.

example_sentences.japanese: 土曜日かあるいは日曜日までには終わらせておきます。
example_sentences.english: I will try to have it finished by either Saturday or possibly Sunday.

example_sentences.japanese: 有名かあるいは綺麗であれば誰でも入れるらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that if you are famous or maybe beautiful, anyone can get in.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動をさせるかあるいは餌を減らしてください。
example_sentences.english: Please make them exercise or possibly lessen the amount of food.

example_sentences.japanese: パソコンの動作が遅いかあるいは電源が点かなくなった場合は、私達が直します。
example_sentences.english: In the event that the computer gets slow or doesn't turn on, we will fix it.

example_sentences.japanese: 動画あるいは写真でもいいので送ってください。
example_sentences.english: Please send me video or pictures, anything is ok.

example_sentences.japanese: 月曜日あるいは火曜日であれば、参加できます。
example_sentences.english: If it is Monday or Tuesday, I can attend.

example_sentences.japanese: 植物あるいは昆虫を観察しましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's observe some plants or bugs.

example_sentences.japanese: 晴れあるいは曇りであれば、お祭りに行きましょう。
example_sentences.english: Whether it is sunny or cloudy, let's go to the festival.

example_sentences.japanese: 今年あるいは来年には、そちらに行けるかと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think I will be able to go there this year or next year.

example_sentences.japanese: キャンディ：「あるいは、リリーさんはこちらに行ったかもしれません。」
example_sentences.english: Candy: 'Perhaps, Lily might have gone this way.'

example_sentences.japanese: 父親あるいは母親に迎えに来てもらいましょう。
example_sentences.english: Let's have your dad or mom come pick you up.

example_sentences.japanese: ツイッターあるいはフェイスブックのどちらかで、情報発信をしてほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to start spreading information on twitter or facebook.

example_sentences.japanese: バドミントンあるいはフットサルなど、室内でできるスポーツ大会を企画してほしい。
example_sentences.english: I want you to plan an indoor sport event, like badminton or futsal.

example_sentences.japanese: この子は世界の救世主になるかもしれません。あるいは世界にとって強大な敵になるかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: This child might become the savior of the world. Or, perhaps a powerful enemy of it.

example_sentences.japanese: 社内あるいは帰り道のどこかで、財布を落としてしまったようだ。
example_sentences.english: It appears that I dropped my wallet at work, or on the way home.

general_translation: But, Even while, Even though, Despite, Although
formation: Verb［stem］+ ながら(も)［い］Adjective + ながら(も)［な］Adjective + ながら(も)Noun + ながら(も)
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ ながら(も)［い］Adjective + ながら(も)［な］Adjective + ながら(も)Noun + ながら(も)
explanation: A phrase that highlights that even while (A) is true or continuing, (B) will still be the result.

example_sentences.japanese: すこし狭いながらも楽しい我が家。
example_sentences.english: Although it is a bit small, it is a happy home. (even while)

example_sentences.japanese: 「こんなことしちゃだめだ」と思いながらもやってしまった。
example_sentences.english: Even while I thought to myself, 'I shouldn't do something like this,' I did it.

example_sentences.japanese: 緊張しながらも、初めての舞台でのびのびと歌うことが出来た。
example_sentences.english: Although I was nervous, I was able to sing comfortably at my first concert.

example_sentences.japanese: 才能を持ちながらも、彼は色々と苦労した。
example_sentences.english: Although he is talented, he struggled with various things.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は悲しみを感じながらも、笑顔で友達に話しました。
example_sentences.english: Even while she was sad, she talked with her friends with a smile on her face.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は料理が苦手ながらも、一生懸命作りました。
example_sentences.english: Although he is not good at cooking, he gave it his all and cooked.

example_sentences.japanese: 私達は貧乏ながらも、定期的にコンサートへ行っている。
example_sentences.english: Although we are poor, we go to concerts every now and then.

example_sentences.japanese: 「やらなきゃいけない」とおもいながらもダラダラしてしまう。
example_sentences.english: Despite thinking 'I have to do it', I just end up idling around. (even while)

example_sentences.japanese: 不本意ながらも、従うしかない。
example_sentences.english: Although I am unwilling, I have no other choice but to obey. (even while)

example_sentences.japanese: 足をひきずりながらも、マラソンを完走しました。
example_sentences.english: Despite my legs turning to jelly, I finished the marathon. (even while)

example_sentences.japanese: 良くないとしっていながらも、注意することができませんでした。
example_sentences.english: Despite knowing that it was not right, I just couldn't warn them. (even while)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はわらいながらも、心では泣いていたのだろう。
example_sentences.english: Despite smiling, she was definitely crying inside. (even while)

example_sentences.japanese: 微力ながらも、協力させていただきます。
example_sentences.english: Although I can't do much, let me help you. (even while)

example_sentences.japanese: お金を沢山もちながらも、彼は幸せではないらしい。
example_sentences.english: Despite having a lot of money, I heard that he isn't happy. (even while)

example_sentences.japanese: 文法の勉強をしなければいけないとしっていながらも、遊んでしまう。
example_sentences.english: Despite knowing that I have to study grammar, I still unfortunately goof off. (even while)

example_sentences.japanese: 緊張しながらも、３００人の前で堂々と発表をすることが出来た。
example_sentences.english: Despite being nervous, I was able to confidently give the presentation in front of 300 people. (even while)

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は、豪快ながらも繊細な神経の持ち主だ。
example_sentences.english: Despite being heroic, that person has a delicate side. (even while)

example_sentences.japanese: 敵でありながらも、相手の素晴らしいプレーを讃える選手もいる。
example_sentences.english: Despite being adversaries, there are also players that extol the other team if they make a great play. (even while)

general_translation: In, On, At, Regarding, In terms of
formation: Noun + においてNoun + における (1) + Noun(1) においての
casual_structure: Noun + においてNoun + における (1) + Noun(1) においての
explanation: A formal expression that can replace the meaning of several different particles, regarding something that is in, on, or at (A).

example_sentences.japanese: 数においては劣っているが、力においては負けていない。
example_sentences.english: Although we are fewer in numbers, we aren't losing in strength.

example_sentences.japanese: 現代において、インターネットなしの生活は考えられない。
example_sentences.english: In this day and age, it is impossible to think of a life without the internet.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分の住んでいる地域における、井戸水の汚染について研究をしている。
example_sentences.english: I am doing research regarding pollution in wells in the area that I am living in.

example_sentences.japanese: これはこの工事においての難しい作業になります。
example_sentences.english: This will be a difficult task in this construction project.

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎における高齢化の問題は深刻です。
example_sentences.english: The aging population in the countryside is very serious.

example_sentences.japanese: 大都市における渋滞の問題は深刻だ。
example_sentences.english: The problem of traffic jams in big cities is serious.

example_sentences.japanese: この文脈においての「空」は、「そら」ではなく「から」だと思う。
example_sentences.english: I think this kanji is read 'kara' rather than 'sora' in this context.

example_sentences.japanese: 現代において、電気のない生活は考えられない。
example_sentences.english: In this day and age, it is impossible to think of life without electricity.

example_sentences.japanese: 東京における環境についての会議を行います。
example_sentences.english: We will hold a meeting concerning environmental issues in Tokyo.

example_sentences.japanese: 日常生活において、必要なものはすべてそろっています。
example_sentences.english: In daily life, I have gathered everything necessary.

example_sentences.japanese: 過去において、問題となっていた点は、もう完全に解決されました。
example_sentences.english: In the past, the points that were causing problems have already been completely resolved.

example_sentences.japanese: 企業における残業の問題が少しは改善されているようだ。
example_sentences.english: The issue of overtime work in business seems to be improving a bit.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校におけるいじめについて、もっと真剣に話し合うべきだ。
example_sentences.english: We should talk about bullying in schools more seriously.

example_sentences.japanese: 経済における優先事項については、様々な意見がある。
example_sentences.english: There are various opinions in regards to priorities in the economy.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本における相撲の位置づけは、海外の方には理解しにくい。
example_sentences.english: The standing of sumo in Japan is hard to understand for foreigners.

example_sentences.japanese: アクメ・コーポレーションの商品は価格においては一流だが、品質においては三流だ。
example_sentences.english: Acme Corporation products are top grade in terms of price, but poor in terms of product quality.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本においての、電車やバスなしの生活は考えられない。
example_sentences.english: Within the scope of Japan, it is impossible to think of a life without buses or trains.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社においての、パワハラについてのミーティングが行われた。
example_sentences.english: A meeting was held regarding power harassment within the scope of our company.

general_translation: Start, First (point), Foremost, To begin with
formation: 第一（だいいち）に + Phrase第一（だいいち） + の + Nounだいいっ + Noun (Chapter)Phrase + 第一（だいいち） + だ
casual_structure: 第一（だいいち）に + Phrase第一（だいいち） + の + Nounだいいっ + Noun (Chapter)Phrase + 第一（だいいち） + だ
polite_structure: 第一（だいいち）に + Phrase第一（だいいち） + の + Nounだいいっ + Noun (Chapter・Section)Phrase + 第一（だいいち） + です
explanation: A structure showing that (A) is first, or the most important, due to it being the first number or position in a series.

example_sentences.japanese: 安全はだいいちだ。
example_sentences.english: Safety first.

example_sentences.japanese: これはここのだいいちのルールだ。
example_sentences.english: This is the number one rule here.

example_sentences.japanese: お金よりも健康でいることがだいいちだ。
example_sentences.english: More than money, being healthy is the most important thing.

example_sentences.japanese: だいいち彼は何であんな時間にここにいたんだ。
example_sentences.english: First of all, why was he here at that time?

example_sentences.japanese: まずだいいちにこの計画を担当する人を決めましょう。
example_sentences.english: Firstly, let's pick the person that will be in charge of this plan.

example_sentences.japanese: だいいっ節だいいっ款検察官の義務等。
example_sentences.english: Section 1, Subsection 1, Duties of public prosecutor, etc. (one・first)

example_sentences.japanese: ハグ・クラブルールのだいいち、ハグ・クラブのことを明かすな。
example_sentences.english: The first rule of Hug Club is: you do not talk about Hug Club.

example_sentences.japanese: オリンピック選手になるには、優れた身体能力がだいいち条件だ。
example_sentences.english: The first condition to become an Olympic athlete is outstanding physical ability.

example_sentences.japanese: だいいっ章：「自動販売機として生まれ変わった日。」
example_sentences.english: Chapter 1: 'The day I got reincarnated as a vending machine.'

example_sentences.japanese: 「では、労働組合からのだいいちの要求はＸです。次はＹです。その次はＺです。」
example_sentences.english: 'So, the first demand of the trade union is X. The next is Y. After that, Z.'

example_sentences.japanese: 調査によると事故が起こったまずだいいちの原因はヒューマンエラーということだ。
example_sentences.english: According to the investigation, the foremost reason for accidents is human error.

example_sentences.japanese: 火事の場合には自分の安全を何よりもだいいちに考えるべきだ。
example_sentences.english: In case of a fire, you should put your safety first.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事から家に帰ったら、まずだいいちに日本語の文法を勉強します。最高に楽しいです。
example_sentences.english: The first thing I do when I get home is study Japanese grammar. It is so much fun!

example_sentences.japanese: ばかな事を言ってしまう前にまずだいいちに状況を考えるものだ。
example_sentences.english: First of all, think of the situation before you say something stupid!

example_sentences.japanese: 筋肉をつけたい場合は筋力のトレーニングではなくてダイエットをだいいちにするべきだ。
example_sentences.english: If you want to gain muscle, rather than training you should prioritize your diet.

example_sentences.japanese: 探偵：「だいいち、犯人はここにどうやって押し入ったのか。」
example_sentences.english: The detective: 'How did the burglar break in to begin with?'

general_translation: Increasingly, More and more, Decreasingly, Less and less, Keep -ing
formation: ますます + Phrase
casual_structure: ますます + Phrase
explanation: A word which indicates (A) happening or trending more and more, or to keep doing (A). May signify changes in either volume or intensity.

example_sentences.japanese: ますます寒さが厳しくなってまいりました。
example_sentences.english: It's growing increasingly colder.

example_sentences.japanese: 良いにおいだね。この匂いを嗅いでるとますますお腹が空いてくる。
example_sentences.english: That smells good, doesn't it? I am going to get more and more hungry if I keep smelling it.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は成長するにつれて、ますます美しくなっています。
example_sentences.english: She is getting more and more beautiful as she develops.

example_sentences.japanese: 年を取るにつれて、ますます目が悪くなっていくよ。
example_sentences.english: As I get older, my eyes are getting worse (and worse).

example_sentences.japanese: 景気はますます悪くなるばかりだ。
example_sentences.english: The economy is getting worse and worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 商売はますます繁盛している。
example_sentences.english: My business is more and more prosperous.

example_sentences.japanese: ますます責任が重くなってきた。
example_sentences.english: My responsibilities are getting more and more difficult to bear.

example_sentences.japanese: 水不足がますます深刻になってきている。
example_sentences.english: The water shortage is growing more and more severe.

example_sentences.japanese: 余計なことを言ってますます怒らせてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I made her more and more angry by saying things that were better left unsaid.

example_sentences.japanese: 約束を破るせいで、彼の信頼度はますます下がっている。
example_sentences.english: Because he breaks promises, his credibility is dropping more and more.

example_sentences.japanese: 時間が経つと共に、ますます頭痛がひどくなってきた。
example_sentences.english: As time goes on, my headache gets worse and worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 父は６０を過ぎ、ますます元気になっているからすごい。
example_sentences.english: My dad is past 60, and he is getting more and more energetic. It's amazing.

example_sentences.japanese: 息子は高校生になって、ますます生意気になってきた。
example_sentences.english: Ever since my son became a high school student, he has gotten more and more cheeky.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回テストでいい点が取れたので、ますますやる気が出てきました。
example_sentences.english: I got a good score this time which gave me more and more motivation.

example_sentences.japanese: ますます試してみたくなってきた。
example_sentences.english: That made me want to try more and more.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日日本語の勉強をしているので、ますます日本語が話せるようになってきた。
example_sentences.english: Because I am studying Japanese everyday, I am able to speak more and more.

example_sentences.japanese: 冬になってから、ますます涼しくなった。
example_sentences.english: Since becoming winter, it has become more and more brisk.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事が忙しくて、ますます子供と過ごす時間が減っていく。
example_sentences.english: Because work is so busy, I have less and less time to spend with my children.

example_sentences.japanese: コロナのせいで観光客がますます減って行く。
example_sentences.english: Because of Covid, the number of tourists is becoming less and less.

general_translation: More and more, Continue to, Keep on, -er and -er
formation: Verb + 一方（いっぽう）だVerb + 一方（いっぽう）で +  Phrase
casual_structure: Verb + 一方（いっぽう）だVerb + 一方（いっぽう）で +  Phrase
polite_structure: Verb + 一方（いっぽう）ですVerb + 一方（いっぽう）で +  Phrase
explanation: A grammar point that expresses the way that a certain trend is continuing, regarding either intensity or number.

example_sentences.japanese: 災害は増えるいっぽうです。
example_sentences.english: More and more disasters happen.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカとロシアの関係は悪化するいっぽうだ。
example_sentences.english: The relationship between the US and Russia keeps on getting worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事の量が増えるいっぽうで、休みが取れない。
example_sentences.english: Because the amount of work keeps on increasing, I can't take a day off.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社の財政は厳しくなるいっぽうだ。
example_sentences.english: The financial situation of the company continues to get more and more strict.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの町の人口は減るいっぽうだ。
example_sentences.english: The population of my town keeps on decreasing.

example_sentences.japanese: このままだと借金が増えるいっぽうだ。
example_sentences.english: If I keep going on like this, my debts will continue to increase.

example_sentences.japanese: 残念ながらこんな事件が増えるいっぽうだ。
example_sentences.english: Unfortunately, there are more and more cases like these.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなに頑張っているのに、評価は下がるいっぽうだ。
example_sentences.english: Although we are doing our best, the value (of our company) continues to drop.

example_sentences.japanese: 出費がかさむいっぽうで、全然お金が貯まらない。
example_sentences.english: I can't save any money, expenses keep on piling up.

example_sentences.japanese: 上昇し続ける物価のせいで生活は苦しくなるいっぽうだ。
example_sentences.english: Due to the continuous growth of prices, life keeps on getting harder and harder.

example_sentences.japanese: 皆が何もしようとしないから、地球温暖化が悪くなるいっぽうだ。
example_sentences.english: Because no one is doing anything about it, global warming is continuing to get worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 景気は悪くなるいっぽうだから、ボーナスは出ないかもしれないですよ。
example_sentences.english: We might not get a bonus because the market keeps getting worse and worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の怒りは募るいっぽうだから、少しそっとしておいた方がいいですね。
example_sentences.english: I think you should leave him alone because he is getting more and more angry.

example_sentences.japanese: 親の病気は悪化するいっぽうだから、回復する見込みはないのかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: My parent's disease continues to get worse, there might not be any hope of recovery.

example_sentences.japanese: 高齢化が進んで、人口が減る一方だ。
example_sentences.english: Because of the aging society, the population continues to decline. (Natural)

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が怪我をして泣く一方だ。
example_sentences.english: The child cries in one direction because he got injured. (Unnatural)

general_translation: On the other hand, At the same time, While
formation: Verb + 一方（いっぽう）（で）［い］Adjective + 一方（いっぽう）（で）［な］Adjective + な(1) + 一方（いっぽう）（で）Noun + の(1) + 一方（いっぽう）（で）Phrase。 一方（いっぽう）(2) + Phrase(1) である(2) その一方（いっぽう）(で)
casual_structure: Verb + 一方（いっぽう）（で）［い］Adjective + 一方（いっぽう）（で）［な］Adjective + な(1) + 一方（いっぽう）（で）Noun + の(1) + 一方（いっぽう）（で）Phrase。 一方（いっぽう）(2) + Phrase(1) である(2) その一方（いっぽう）(で)
explanation: A phrase that highlights one direction, before expressing that another way could differ.

example_sentences.japanese: この靴は、温かいいっぽうで、重いです。
example_sentences.english: These shoes are warm but on the other hand they are heavy.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は関西は晴れるいっぽうで、関東では雨が降るそうです。
example_sentences.english: While today will be sunny in Kansai, I hear that it will rain in Kanto.

example_sentences.japanese: 甘えるのが好きな猫がいるいっぽうで、人間を警戒する猫も多くいます。
example_sentences.english: There are cats that like being affectionate, but on the other hand, there are also lots of cats that are wary of people.

example_sentences.japanese: 田舎は、日中は静かないっぽうで、夜になると虫やカエルの鳴き声でうるさいです。
example_sentences.english: The countryside is very quiet during the daytime, but on the other hand, the calls of insects and frogs are annoying once it's night.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は歌手であるいっぽうで、政治家でもある。
example_sentences.english: He is a singer, while at the same time, a politician.

example_sentences.japanese: いっぽうで、長野県では夏祭りが開催される。
example_sentences.english: On the other hand, the summer festival will be held in Nagano Prefecture. (The previous sentence would have had some contradictory information)

example_sentences.japanese: あの食べ物は体に良いいっぽうで、食べ過ぎたら、体に悪い。
example_sentences.english: On the one hand, that food is good for your body. On the other hand, if you eat too much, it is bad for you.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の会社が儲かるいっぽうで、うちの会社は経営状態が悪化している。
example_sentences.english: His company seems to be profitable, but, on the other hand, the condition of our administration is growing worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 友人たちがスキーを楽しむいっぽうで、私は働かなくてはいけない。
example_sentences.english: My friends are having a fun time skiing, but I, on the other hand, have to work.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社ではいい上司だが、そのいっぽうで、家では酒乱だ。
example_sentences.english: He is a good boss at the company, but, at the same time, he is a violent drunk at home.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本では多くの食べ物が廃棄処分されているいっぽうで、アフリカでは餓死している人々がいる。
example_sentences.english: At the same time as lots of food is getting scrapped in Japan, there are people that die of starvation in Africa.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社でサイコパスは部下には偉そうにしているいっぽうで、上司にはいつもペコペコしている傾向がある。
example_sentences.english: Psychopaths at work tend to be snobbish towards subordinates, but at the same time are subservient to their bosses.

example_sentences.japanese: 平日は勉強をしているいっぽうで、週末はずっとアルバイトをして学費を稼いでいる。
example_sentences.english: I study on weekdays, and at the same time I earn money for my tuition by working as a part-timer on weekends.

example_sentences.japanese: 車は便利であるいっぽうで、交通事故などの危険もある。
example_sentences.english: Cars are convenient, but, on the other hand, there is a risk of things like traffic accidents.

example_sentences.japanese: 雪が多いと大変ないっぽうで、スキーなどを楽しめるという利点もある。
example_sentences.english: Snow causes a variety of problems, but, on the other hand you can also enjoy merits such as skiing.

example_sentences.japanese: インターネットは便利ないっぽうで、信用できない情報も溢れている。
example_sentences.english: The internet is convenient, but on the other hand, it is overflowing with untrustworthy information.

example_sentences.japanese: 経済ばかり良くなるいっぽうで、治安や公衆衛生は悪化している。
example_sentences.english: At the same time just as the economy is getting better, order and public health is worsening.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のお金は貯まっていく一方で、彼のお金は減っていくばかりです。
example_sentences.english: My savings is increasing, but on the other hand, his savings continue to decline.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎月お金が減っていく一方で、全然貯まりそうもない。
example_sentences.english: Every month I keep losing money, and it doesn't even seem like it will increase.

general_translation: Finally, At last
formation: ついに + Phrase
casual_structure: ついに + Phrase
explanation: A grammar point expressing that (A) has finally happened, with the nuance of having been long awaited, or getting it over with.

example_sentences.japanese: ついに論文を書き上げた。
example_sentences.english: I finally finished writing my thesis.

example_sentences.japanese: ついに日本上陸！！！
example_sentences.english: Finally it has arrived in Japan!!!

example_sentences.japanese: ついにドラゴンズが勝った！
example_sentences.english: The Dragons have finally won!

example_sentences.japanese: ついに最後の日ですね、今まで色々とありがとうございました。
example_sentences.english: Finally it is your last day. Thank you for everything up until now.

example_sentences.japanese: とうとう今日で最後だね。今まで色々とありがとう。
example_sentences.english: It's finally your last day. Thank you for everything up until now.

example_sentences.japanese: ついに犯人を捕まえることができた。
example_sentences.english: I was finally able to catch the criminal.

example_sentences.japanese: ついに借金を払い終えた。
example_sentences.english: I was finally able to pay off my debt.

example_sentences.japanese: ついに孫に身長で負けてしまった。
example_sentences.english: My grandchild outgrew me at last.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女にプロポーズをする日がついに来た。
example_sentences.english: The day I propose to her has finally come.

example_sentences.japanese: 料理が美味しいことで評判のお店に、ついに来ることができた。
example_sentences.english: I was finally able to go to a restaurant known for its delicious food.

example_sentences.japanese: 何日も降り続いた雪がついにやみました。
example_sentences.english: The snow, that had lasted for many days, finally stopped.

example_sentences.japanese: 何百回と失敗を繰り返し、ついに成功した。
example_sentences.english: After failing repeatedly hundreds of times, I finally succeeded.

example_sentences.japanese: 待ちに待った報告書が、ついに届いた。
example_sentences.english: The report I had been waiting forever for, finally arrived.

example_sentences.japanese: 何年もお付き合いをしていた二人が、ついに結婚しました。
example_sentences.english: The couple that had been going out for years, finally married.

example_sentences.japanese: 憧れのあの人に会えて、ついに夢が叶った。
example_sentences.english: I met the person that I had been yearning to meet and finally realized my dream.

example_sentences.japanese: 昔から欲しかった車を、ついに買うことができました。
example_sentences.english: I finally was able to buy a car I had wanted for a very long time.

example_sentences.japanese: 遂に結婚したのか！おめでとう！
example_sentences.english: You finally married!? Congrats! (Natural)

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日貰った袋を遂に捨てた。
example_sentences.english: I finally threw away the bag I bought yesterday. (Unnatural)

general_translation: Already, Too late
formation: すでに + Phrase
casual_structure: すでに + Phrase
explanation: A formal phrase highlighting that (A) has already happened, often with the nuance of completion, and inability to return to a previous state.

example_sentences.japanese: 時すでに遅し。
example_sentences.english: You are already too late.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はすでに国民から名前を忘れられている。
example_sentences.english: His name has already been forgotten by the citizens. (Universal opinion)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はすでにみんなと仲良くなっていた。
example_sentences.english: He was already becoming friends with absolutely everyone. (Altogether)

example_sentences.japanese: さっき食べたばかりなのに、もうすでにお腹が空いてきた。
example_sentences.english: I just ate earlier, but I am already starting to get hungry.

example_sentences.japanese: もうすでにチケットは売り切れです。
example_sentences.english: The tickets are already sold out. (Nothing remains)

example_sentences.japanese: すでにお支払い済みです。
example_sentences.english: It has already been paid for.

example_sentences.japanese: お湯はすでにわいている。
example_sentences.english: The hot water is already boiled.

example_sentences.japanese: これはすでに決まった事なので、もう私達じゃ何もできません。
example_sentences.english: It is beyond doubt that this has been decided, so we can't do anything about it. (Beyond doubt)

example_sentences.japanese: 電話料金はすでに払い終えました。
example_sentences.english: I have already paid the telephone bill.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたの席はすでにここと決まっています。
example_sentences.english: It has already been decided that your seat will be here.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕が来た時には、電気はすでにつけてあった。
example_sentences.english: The light was already on when I arrived.

example_sentences.japanese: 旅行に行くための休みはすでに取りました。
example_sentences.english: I had already taken a day off for a trip.

example_sentences.japanese: もうすでにお腹いっぱいで、これ以上は食べられない。
example_sentences.english: I am already full, I cannot possibly eat more than this.

example_sentences.japanese: 一番乗りだと思ったら、すでに先客がいた。
example_sentences.english: I thought I was the first to arrive, but there was already someone there before me.

example_sentences.japanese: 焼きたてのパンを買おうとした時にはすでに売り切れでした。
example_sentences.english: The freshly baked bread was already sold out when I was about to buy it.

example_sentences.japanese: すでに知っているかもしれませんが、確認のためにもう一度聞いてください。
example_sentences.english: You may already know, but please listen once more just to be sure.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕もメンバーに立候補しようと思っていたのですが、すでに決まっていました。
example_sentences.english: I was going to announce my candidacy, but it had already been decided.

example_sentences.japanese: そのアドレスはすでに使われているので、違うのにしてください。
example_sentences.english: The address is already being used so please choose another one.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車はすでに出発しました。
example_sentences.english: The train has left already. (And there is nothing we can do about it)

general_translation: Without doing
formation: Verb［ない］+ ず(に)Exceptions:する ￫ せず(に)
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ ず(に)Exceptions:する ￫ せず(に)
explanation: A somewhat old-fashioned way to express that something will be done, without doing (A).

example_sentences.japanese: わすれずに届けてくれてありがとうございます。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for delivering it for me (without forgetting).

example_sentences.japanese: 朝ご飯を食べずに仕事に行ったから、仕事中に倒れた。
example_sentences.english: Because I went to work without eating breakfast, I fainted in the middle of my job.

example_sentences.japanese: 水を飲まずに運動をしていたから、頭が痛い。
example_sentences.english: Because I exercised without drinking water, I have a headache.

example_sentences.japanese: 何もしらずにあんなこと言ってごめんなさい。
example_sentences.english: Sorry for saying those things without knowing the full story.

example_sentences.japanese: なやまずに生きるなんて不可能なのかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: It might not be possible to live without worrying.

example_sentences.japanese: 値段をみずに買ったら大変なことになった。
example_sentences.english: I bought it without checking the price and now I am in a bind.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は朝ごはんをたべずに仕事に行きました。
example_sentences.english: He left for work without eating breakfast.

example_sentences.japanese: やすまず、一日中ゲームをやり続けた。
example_sentences.english: Without taking a break, I continued to play video games throughout the day.

example_sentences.japanese: 試合に一回もまけず、優勝した。
example_sentences.english: Without losing a single game, they won the championship.

example_sentences.japanese: 肩の力を抜いて、りきまずにスウィングした方がいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: You'd better relax your shoulder and swing without straining yourself.

example_sentences.japanese: ラーメン屋でラーメンを注文せずにチャーハンだけ食べました。
example_sentences.english: At a ramen restaurant, I just had fried rice without ordering any ramen.

example_sentences.japanese: あきらめずに続ければ、日本語もっと上手になりますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you keep on (studying) without giving up, your Japanese will get better.

example_sentences.japanese: わからずに操作すると故障の原因になるのでやめてください。
example_sentences.english: Please do not operate (the machine) without understanding (the machine), as it could be damaged as a result of improper use.

example_sentences.japanese: 気をゆるめず、次の試合も頑張ってください。
example_sentences.english: Without losing focus, please try your best in the next match, too.

example_sentences.japanese: 勉強せずにテストを受けたから、テストの点数が低かった。
example_sentences.english: Because I took the test without studying, I got a low score.

example_sentences.japanese: あんまり無理をせずに頑張ってくださいね。
example_sentences.english: Please do your best without trying too hard.

general_translation: Cannot help doing something, Cannot resist doing something
formation: Verb［ない］+ ずにはいられない
casual_structure: Verb［ない］+ ずにはいられない
polite_structure: Verb［ない］+ ずにはいられません
explanation: A somewhat old-fashioned way to show that not doing (A) cannot be lived with, or is unbearable.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供が生まれてなかずにはいられない。
example_sentences.english: You can't help but cry when your child is born.

example_sentences.japanese: 美味しそうなステーキが目の前にあったら、食べずにはいられない。
example_sentences.english: If there is a delicious looking steak in front of me, there is no way I can resist eating it.

example_sentences.japanese: この映画を見ると誰でも泣かずにはいられない。
example_sentences.english: No matter who you are, if you watch this movie, there is no way you can not cry.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はよく嘘をつくから、うたがわずにはいられない。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but be suspicious because he always tells lies.

example_sentences.japanese: 事故を目撃したら、たすけずにはいられない。
example_sentences.english: When you witness an accident, you can't help but help out.

example_sentences.japanese: それを思い出すたびにはずかしくならずにはいられない。
example_sentences.english: Everytime I recall that I can't help but get embarrassed.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の変顔は面白すぎて、わらわずにはいられません。
example_sentences.english: His strange faces are just too funny, I can't help but laugh.

example_sentences.japanese: たべずにはいられない。このチョコ美味しすぎるよ。
example_sentences.english: This chocolate is just too good. I can't stop myself from eating it.

example_sentences.japanese: 新しいラーメン屋を見つけたら、はいらずにはいられません。
example_sentences.english: If I find a new ramen shop, I can't stop myself from going in.

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪をひいたから、くしゃみをせずにはいられないんです。
example_sentences.english: I can't stop myself from sneezing because I have a cold.

example_sentences.japanese: 「気にしないで」と言われても、きにせずにはいられない。
example_sentences.english: Even if I am told 'don't worry about it,' I can't help but worry.

example_sentences.japanese: 審判が不公平すぎて、文句をいわずにはいられない。
example_sentences.english: I can't help but complain. The trial was just too unfair.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の生い立ちを聞いたら、同情せずにはいられない。
example_sentences.english: Hearing his story, I can't help but feel sympathy for him.

example_sentences.japanese: 一部だけ読んだ小説の結末に興味を持つようになって、よまずにはいられない。
example_sentences.english: Since I am so curious about the ending of a book I read only part of, I can't stop myself from reading it.

example_sentences.japanese: この１０年間色々とお世話になったから、先輩には感謝をせずにはいられない。
example_sentences.english: This past 10 years, I have been helped a lot by my senpai, so there is no way I can go on without showing them some appreciation.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は猫アレルギーなのでくしゃみをせずにはいられない。
example_sentences.english: I am allergic to cats so I can't not sneeze.

general_translation: Without, No
formation: Noun + なしで（は）Phrase + なしだNoun + なし + の + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + なしで（は）Phrase + なしだNoun + なし + の + Noun
polite_structure: Noun + なしで（は）Phrase + なしですNoun + なし + の + Noun
explanation: A slightly formal word used to show that something is without (A). The existence of (A) is not included.

example_sentences.japanese: ことわざ：「死人に口なしだ。」
example_sentences.english: Proverb: 'Dead men tell no tales.' (Literally - Without a mouth)

example_sentences.japanese: 先輩が来ると盛り下がるから、先輩なしにしよう。
example_sentences.english: Let's avoid inviting our senpai because he kills the mood.

example_sentences.japanese: その考えは間違いなしだ。
example_sentences.english: That way of thinking is without error. (That way of thinking is flawless)

example_sentences.japanese: 許可なしで公園に店を出さないで下さい。
example_sentences.english: Please don't put up a store in the park without permission.

example_sentences.japanese: 肉なしの人気料理はなんですか。
example_sentences.english: What is a popular dish without meat?

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日は沢山食べたから、今日は昼飯なしにする。
example_sentences.english: Because I ate a lot yesterday, I am going to skip eating lunch today.

example_sentences.japanese: 告白：「あなたなしで生きていけない。」
example_sentences.english: Confession of love: 'I cannot live without you.'

example_sentences.japanese: 商品ラベル：「砂糖なしのダイエットドリンク」
example_sentences.english: Product label: 'Diet drink without sugar'

example_sentences.japanese: エッセイ：「今では現生人類はスマホなしでは生活できないだろう。」
example_sentences.english: Essay: 'Nowadays, modern humans probably cannot live without smartphones.'

example_sentences.japanese: テスト飛行は文句なしの成功でした。
example_sentences.english: The test flight was an undisputed success. (without)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との会話：「今月はもうお金なしだ。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'I am already without money this month.'

example_sentences.japanese: コンテクストなしでは、文の意味を理解することはできない。
example_sentences.english: The meaning of a sentence cannot be understood without context.

example_sentences.japanese: 警告サイン：「同意なしで写真を撮らないでください。」
example_sentences.english: Warning sign: 'Please do not take photos without consent.'

example_sentences.japanese: ユーチューブの動画のタイトル：「マウスなしのワープロの使い方（方法）」
example_sentences.english: Youtube video title: 'Using a word processor without a mouse (method)'

example_sentences.japanese: エッセイ：「しかし、いい経験になること間違いなしだ。」
example_sentences.english: Essay: 'However, it will without a doubt become a good experience.'

example_sentences.japanese: エッセイ：「お金なしで何かを買うことは不可能である。」
example_sentences.english: Essay: 'It is not possible to buy something without money.'

example_sentences.japanese: ドキュメント・マニュアル：「パスワードなしでログインしようとすると、警告メッセージが表示されます。」
example_sentences.english: Documentation, manual: 'If you try to log in without a password, a warning message will be displayed.'

example_sentences.japanese: わさび抜きでお願いします。
example_sentences.english: Remove the wasabi please.

example_sentences.japanese: 唐辛子無しでお願いします。
example_sentences.english: Without the red peppers please.

general_translation: Unthinkable, Inconceivable, Unimaginable, Cannot think
formation: Noun + など(1) + 考（かんが）えられないPhrase + ということは(2) + 考（かんが）えられない(1) なんて、は(2) ことは、など、なんて
casual_structure: Noun + など(1) + 考（かんが）えられないPhrase + ということは(2) + 考（かんが）えられない(1) なんて、は(2) ことは、など、なんて
polite_structure: Noun + など(1) + 考（かんが）えられませんPhrase + ということは(2) + 考（かんが）えられません(1) なんて、は(2) ことは、など、なんて
explanation: A common expression used to show that (A) is unimaginable. It cannot even be considered.

example_sentences.japanese: 「ほかの方法はかんがえられない。」
example_sentences.english: 'I cannot think of another way.' (unthinkable)

example_sentences.japanese: ２０年前は、携帯で映画を見たりゲームをしたりすることはかんがえられなかったでしょう。
example_sentences.english: It was probably unthinkable 20 years ago that you could do things like watch movies and play video games on your phone.

example_sentences.japanese: 人に手を出すなんて私にはかんがえられない。
example_sentences.english: It is unimaginable that I would raise my hand at a person.

example_sentences.japanese: あんなに小さな人が相撲をやろうと思ったとはかんがえられない。
example_sentences.english: It is unthinkable that a person that small decided they wanted to do sumo.

example_sentences.japanese: 人違いだったことはかんがえられないか？
example_sentences.english: Is it unthinkable that you misremembered the person?

example_sentences.japanese: 論文：「チタンはかんがえられないほど硬いので、飛行機によく使用される。」
example_sentences.english: Article/essay: 'Since titanium is unthinkably strong, it is often used in airplanes.'

example_sentences.japanese: ブログの投稿：「君の事以外は何もかんがえられない。」
example_sentences.english: Blog post: 'I cannot think about anything but you.' (unthinkable)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「子供がそんな難しい数学の問題を解くということはかんがえられない。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'It is unthinkable for a child to solve such a difficult mathematical problem.'

example_sentences.japanese: ブログの投稿：「電気なしの生活は私にはかんがえられない。」
example_sentences.english: Blog post: 'Life without electricity is unimaginable for me.' (unthinkable)

example_sentences.japanese: 新聞：「靴を脱がずに家に上がることは、日本ではかんがえられない行為ですが、アメリカでは普通です。」
example_sentences.english: Newspaper: 'Entering a house without removing your shoes is an unthinkable act in Japan, but it is normal in the USA.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「まさかあんなに真面目な人が、物を盗むなんてかんがえられない。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'It is absolutely inconceivable that such a serious person would do something like stealing.' (unthinkable)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「昨日まで元気だったのに、急に亡くなるなんてかんがえられない。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: "Despite being healthy just yesterday, (he) suddenly died. It's something unimaginable." [unthinkable]

example_sentences.japanese: １０年前は紙の地図を見ながら旅行していたなんて、今の私にはかんがえられない。
example_sentences.english: It's unimaginable to me now that ten years ago I would travel while using paper maps. (unthinkable)

example_sentences.japanese: 告白：「あなたを愛しているから、あなたのいない人生なんてかんがえられない。」
example_sentences.english: Love confession: '(Something like) a life without you is unimaginable because I love you.' (unthinkable)

example_sentences.japanese: 突然親切になった人について友達との話、Ａ：「彼女はなぜ親切なの？友達になりたいの？」Ｂ：「そんなことはかんがえられない。何か裏があるはずだ。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends about a person that suddenly became nice, A: 'Why is she nice? Does she want to be friends?'B: 'Something like that is inconceivable. She surely has some kind of end game.' (unthinkable)

example_sentences.japanese: 論文：「スマホ、パソコン、映画などは江戸時代にはかんがえられないことでした。」
example_sentences.english: Article/essay: 'Things like smartphones, PCs, and movies were unthinkable during the Edo period.'

example_sentences.japanese: 友達が車に無断で乗ろうとしていた不審人物について話している：「車を間違えたってことはかんがえられないか？ もしかしたら君のを盗むつもりだったのかもしれない？」
example_sentences.english: Friends talking about a stranger that tried to get into their car without permission: It’s not inconceivable/strong> that he mistook it for his own car, is it? Maybe he possibly planned to steal yours.' (unthinkable)

example_sentences.japanese: 死んだ後のことなどほとんど考えない。
example_sentences.english: I don't think about what happens after dying.

example_sentences.japanese: 結婚した後の事など考えていない。
example_sentences.english: I'm not thinking about stuff like what happens after getting married.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻と離婚することなど考えられない。
example_sentences.english: It is unimaginable that I would get a divorce with my wife.

general_translation: Possibility, To have, With
formation: Phrase + あり
casual_structure: Phrase + あり
explanation: A fairly casual expression that is used to highlight the inclusion or possibility of something.

example_sentences.japanese: 遊びに行くなら、遊園地もありだ。
example_sentences.english: If we're going to hang out, a theme park is also a possibility.

example_sentences.japanese: ラーメンもありじゃない？
example_sentences.english: Ramen is possible, isn't it?

example_sentences.japanese: 駐車場ありのホテルを取っておいてください。
example_sentences.english: Please book a hotel with a parking lot.

example_sentences.japanese: 字幕ありで見たいから字幕つけてもらえない？
example_sentences.english: I want to watch it with subtitles, so could you please turn it on?

example_sentences.japanese: 鈴木先輩：「来週ＢＢＱもありじゃない？」浜崎くん：「めっちゃありです。」
example_sentences.english: Suzuki senpai: 'Don't you think a BBQ would be a good option next week?' Hamazaki-kun: 'That is totally possible.'

example_sentences.japanese: 何か動物を飼いたい。ネコもありだ。
example_sentences.english: I wanna have some kind of animal. Even a cat is a possibility.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日のデート、水族館もありじゃない？
example_sentences.english: The aquarium is also a possibility for tomorrow's date, right?

example_sentences.japanese: キッズメニューありのレストランに行こう。
example_sentences.english: Let's go to a restaurant with a kids menu.

example_sentences.japanese: この香りもありだけど、あの香りの方が好き！
example_sentences.english: This scent is also an option, but I like that scent better!

example_sentences.japanese: お酒もありだけど今日はジュースを飲もうかな。
example_sentences.english: Alcohol is a possibility, but I think I'll drink juice today.

example_sentences.japanese: この飲食店はキッズスペースありだって！珍しいね！
example_sentences.english: I heard that this is a restaurant with a kids' space! Pretty rare, huh?

example_sentences.japanese: あの白いドレスもありだし、ピンクのドレスも君に似合うよ。
example_sentences.english: That white dress is a possibility, and the pink dress also suits you.

example_sentences.japanese: お腹が空いた…。カツ丼や牛丼もありだな…。
example_sentences.english: I am starving… Even something like katsu-don or a gyu-don would be a possibility.

example_sentences.japanese: あの職場は近いからありだが雰囲気がイマイチだ。
example_sentences.english: That workplace is a possibility because it's close, but the atmosphere leaves something to be desired.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供は暴力シーンありの映画を見られません。
example_sentences.english: Kids are not able to see movies with violent scenes.

example_sentences.japanese: 張り紙：「ベジタリアン用のメニューあり！ベジタリアンの方も、様々なメニューを楽しんで頂けます！」
example_sentences.english: Poster: 'We have vegetarian menu items! Vegetarians may also enjoy various things!

general_translation: Not always, Not entirely, Not necessarily
formation: 必（かなら）ずしも + Phrase + わけではない(1)必（かなら）ずしも + Phrase + とは限（かぎ）らない必（かなら）ずしも + Phrase + とは言（い）えない(1) わけじゃない
casual_structure: 必（かなら）ずしも + Phrase + わけではない(1)必（かなら）ずしも + Phrase + とは限（かぎ）らない必（かなら）ずしも + Phrase + とは言（い）えない(1) わけじゃない
polite_structure: 必（かなら）ずしも + Phrase + わけではありません(1)必（かなら）ずしも + Phrase + とは限（かぎ）りません必（かなら）ずしも + Phrase + とは言（い）えません(1) わけじゃありません
explanation: An expression which indicates that something is not necessarily the case, by saying that it is not invariable.
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: 失敗はかならずしも悪いわけではない。
example_sentences.english: Failure is not necessarily bad.

example_sentences.japanese: 男の人はかならずしも強いわけではない。
example_sentences.english: Men are not necessarily always strong.

example_sentences.japanese: 刑務所にいる人たちはかならずしも犯罪を犯したとは限らない。
example_sentences.english: People in prison are not always in there because they have committed a crime.

example_sentences.japanese: 女の人はかならずしも買い物が好きだとは言えない。
example_sentences.english: Women do not necessarily love shopping.

example_sentences.japanese: かならずしも上達するわけではない。
example_sentences.english: You will not necessarily become more proficient.

example_sentences.japanese: 思い出がかならずしも美しいとは限らない。
example_sentences.english: Memories are not always beautiful.

example_sentences.japanese: 天気予報はかならずしも当たるわけではない。
example_sentences.english: Forecasts are not always right.

example_sentences.japanese: かならずしもこの情報が正しいとは限らない。
example_sentences.english: This information is not necessarily correct.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生だけど、かならずしもいい人とは限りません。
example_sentences.english: Even though he is a teacher, it does not necessarily mean he is a good person.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本人というだけで、かならずしも漢字が得意なわけではない。
example_sentences.english: Just being Japanese does not always mean being good with kanji.

example_sentences.japanese: 強い者がかならずしも勝つわけではありません。
example_sentences.english: Those who are strong do not always win.

example_sentences.japanese: この仕事はかならずしも今日中にやらなければいけないわけではない。
example_sentences.english: I do not necessarily have to finish this work today.

example_sentences.japanese: 良かれと思ってやったことが、かならずしも感謝されるとは限らない。
example_sentences.english: Even if you do something good for them, they will not necessarily be thankful.

example_sentences.japanese: 男の人がかならずしも運転が上手とは限らない。
example_sentences.english: Men are not necessarily good drivers.

example_sentences.japanese: 訴えられているだけでかならずしも有罪となるとは限らない。
example_sentences.english: Just being accused does not always mean to be found guilty.

general_translation: Formal Conjunctive
formation: Verb［stem］+ Phrase［い］Adjective［て］+ Phrase
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ Phrase［い］Adjective［て］+ Phrase
explanation: A formal conjugation pattern used to say and, then, or several other meanings that could also be implied by て form.
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: 風がふき、悪魔が現れた。
example_sentences.english: The wind blew, a demon appeared.

example_sentences.japanese: 飛行機のエンジンが爆発をし、海に墜落した。
example_sentences.english: The engine of the airplane exploded, (and) it crashed into the ocean.

example_sentences.japanese: 朝食を食べ、出かける準備をしてください。
example_sentences.english: Eat your breakfast, (and) please get ready to go out.

example_sentences.japanese: 北海道は寒く、景色が綺麗。
example_sentences.english: Hokkaido is cold, (and) the scenery is pretty.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校は楽しく、色々学べるので学校が好きです。
example_sentences.english: School is fun, (and) I can learn various things so I like it.

example_sentences.japanese: 空はあおく、海より広い。
example_sentences.english: The sky is blue, (and) bigger than the sea.

example_sentences.japanese: スピードを出しすぎ、警察に捕まった。
example_sentences.english: I was going too fast, (and) a cop pulled me over.

example_sentences.japanese: 公園にいき、子供と遊んだ。
example_sentences.english: I went to the park, (and) played with kids.

example_sentences.japanese: 夢はおおきく、志は高く！
example_sentences.english: Have big dreams, (and) be ambitious!

example_sentences.japanese: 時が過ぎるのははやく、取り戻せない。
example_sentences.english: Time passes quickly, (and) you can't get it back.

example_sentences.japanese: 天候がくずれ、遠足は延期になった。
example_sentences.english: The weather took a turn for the worse, (and) the trip was postponed.

example_sentences.japanese: スピーチを失敗し、ため息が出てしまった。
example_sentences.english: I messed up my speech (and), without thinking, let out a sigh.

example_sentences.japanese: 本を暗記し、試験に臨んだ。
example_sentences.english: Memorizing the book, I then set my sights on the test.

example_sentences.japanese: 会社に遅刻し、上司に大声で、叱られた。
example_sentences.english: I showed up late, (and) was scolded by my boss.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事が成功し、彼女はやっと笑顔を見せた。
example_sentences.english: The job was successful, (and) she finally showed me her smile.

example_sentences.japanese: ナレーター：「ロナルドは赤信号でとまり、信号が青になるまで静かに待ちながら手動で時計を設定した。その時彼はその簡単に見えることが来週、死の原因になろうとは全く知らなかった。」ロナルド：「なに？なんて言ったの？」
example_sentences.english: Narrator: 'Ronald stopped at the red light and waited calmly for the signal change while manually setting his wristwatch. Little did he know that this seemingly simple act would lead to his death only a week later.' Ronald: 'What? What did you say?'

general_translation: Suitable for, Facing
formation: Noun + 向（む）き
casual_structure: Noun + 向（む）き
explanation: A phrase that highlights something as facing (A), or suitable for (A).
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋は南むきですか。
example_sentences.english: Does this room face south?

example_sentences.japanese: あなたは本当に前むきな人なのですね。
example_sentences.english: You really are a forward facing person! (You really are a positive thinker)

example_sentences.japanese: この部屋のベランダは南むきですか？
example_sentences.english: Is this room's veranda south facing?

example_sentences.japanese: この本は初心者むきですか？
example_sentences.english: Is this book suitable for beginners?

example_sentences.japanese: それだとむきが逆ですよ。
example_sentences.english: If that's the case, the way it's facing is back to front.

example_sentences.japanese: 経済は上むきのようですね。
example_sentences.english: The economy seems to be looking up. (facing)

example_sentences.japanese: あなたはいつも前むきな人だ。
example_sentences.english: You are always positive. (Facing forward)

example_sentences.japanese: これは若い者むきの本だな。
example_sentences.english: This book is suitable for young people. (facing)

example_sentences.japanese: 僕はいつも横むきで寝る。
example_sentences.english: I always sleep facing sideways.

example_sentences.japanese: 風むきが変わってきたようだ。
example_sentences.english: It appears that the direction of the wind has changed. (facing)

example_sentences.japanese: このテキストは初心者むきにできている。
example_sentences.english: This textbook is suitable for beginners. (Literally - Facing)

example_sentences.japanese: この車は大人数の家族むきです。
example_sentences.english: This car is suitable for large families. (facing)

example_sentences.japanese: これは小さな子供むきのおもちゃである。
example_sentences.english: This toy is suitable for small children. (facing)

example_sentences.japanese: 誰にでもむき不むきがあるのは当然だ。
example_sentences.english: Of course, everyone has different suitabilities. (facing・suitable for)

example_sentences.japanese: サラリーマンの仕事むきのスーツだから、これを買うことにしたんだ。
example_sentences.english: This suit is suitable for office work, so I decided to buy it. (facing)

example_sentences.japanese: 私は子供向けの本を書いています。
example_sentences.english: I write books for children. (Intended for children)

example_sentences.japanese: 子供向きの本を探しているのですが、お勧めはありますか？
example_sentences.english: I am looking for books suitable for children, but do you have any recommendations? (Not necessarily intended for children, but still suitable)

general_translation: Intended for, Aimed at
formation: Noun + 向（む）け（に）Noun + 向け + の + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + 向（む）け（に）Noun + 向け + の + Noun
explanation: A phrase that highlights something faced toward (A), or specifically intended for (A).
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: この番組は大人むけだ。
example_sentences.english: This TV program is aimed at adults.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供むけに書かれた本を読んで日本語を勉強したら？
example_sentences.english: Why don't you study Japanese by reading books written for children?

example_sentences.japanese: オフィスむけのパソコンを１０台買うとしたらいくらになりますか。
example_sentences.english: If I were to buy 10 computers intended for office use, how much would that cost?

example_sentences.japanese: この教科書は上級者むけに書いてある。
example_sentences.english: This textbook is written oriented toward advanced people.

example_sentences.japanese: これは大人むけの映画だから、お前には見せれないよ。
example_sentences.english: This movie is intended for adults so I can't show it to you.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が住んでいる所は一人暮らしむけのアパートだけれども、３人家族でもなんの不便無く住める。
example_sentences.english: The place I am living is intended for one person, but even as a three person family, we can live there with no inconveniences.

example_sentences.japanese: これは女性むけの服だから、僕には着れない。
example_sentences.english: These clothes are intended for women so I can't wear them.

example_sentences.japanese: Ｘというライトノベルは子供むけに書かれたんだ。
example_sentences.english: The light novel called X was written for children.

example_sentences.japanese: このアプリは学生むけだが、誰でも使用できる。
example_sentences.english: This app is intended for students, but anyone can use it.

example_sentences.japanese: これは海外むけの番組だから、何を言っているのか全然分からない。
example_sentences.english: This is a TV program aimed at foreigners, so I have no idea what is being said.

example_sentences.japanese: この映画は大人むけであり、子供に見せないでください。
example_sentences.english: This movie is intended for adults. Please do not let children watch it.

example_sentences.japanese: この商品は小企業むけに設計されました。
example_sentences.english: This product was designed with small companies in mind.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、韓国むけの輸出は好況なようです。
example_sentences.english: Lately, exports aimed at Korean audiences seem to be flourishing.

example_sentences.japanese: まずは初心者むけの参考書を勉強した方がいいですよ。
example_sentences.english: First of all, I think it would be better if you studied with a textbook aimed at beginners.

example_sentences.japanese: これは研究者むけの本だから、さっぱり意味が分からない。
example_sentences.english: This book is intended for scholars so I don't understand it at all.

example_sentences.japanese: ドラゴンボールはアニメだけど、若者むけだ。小学生以下の子供むけじゃない。
example_sentences.english: 'Dragonball' is an anime aimed at young people, but it is not intended for elementary school students or younger.

example_sentences.japanese: この教科書は算数を学んでいる人むけだから、日本語を学んでいる人に役には立たない。
example_sentences.english: This textbook is intended for people who are learning math, so it won't help those who are studying Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: そのおもちゃは猫向けに作られている。
example_sentences.english: That toy is made for cats.

example_sentences.japanese: 上級者向きの本は難しいです。
example_sentences.english: Books suitable for advanced learners are hard.

general_translation: Something is finished, To finish something, Something has come to an end, To do something completely, To do something through
formation: （Noun + が） + Verb ［stem］ + 上（あ）がる（Noun + を） + Verb ［stem］ + 上（あ）げる
casual_structure: （Noun + が） + Verb ［stem］ + 上（あ）がる（Noun + を） + Verb ［stem］ + 上（あ）げる
polite_structure: （Noun + が） + Verb ［stem］ + 上（あ）がります（Noun + を） + Verb ［stem］ + 上（あ）げます
explanation: A structure used for showing that a particular action has been finished up, or finished to completion.
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: ところで、やっと絵がえがきあがったよ。
example_sentences.english: By the way, the picture has finally been completely painted.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は砂を使って小さな街を作りあげた。
example_sentences.english: He used sand to build up a small city.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の作品は５分で書きあがる。
example_sentences.english: His pieces are drawn up in 5 minutes.

example_sentences.japanese: 古いコンピューターは立ちあがるのに１０分かかる。
example_sentences.english: It takes an old computer 10 minutes to finish up booting.

example_sentences.japanese: レポートは書きあげた？
example_sentences.english: Did you finish writing the paper?

example_sentences.japanese: この炊飯器を使えば２０分でご飯が炊きあがるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you use this rice cooker, your rice will finish cooking in 20 minutes.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日の朝までに書きあげるのは無理かな？頑張らなきゃ。
example_sentences.english: Is it impossible to finish up writing this paper by tomorrow? I should give it my all.

example_sentences.japanese: 作品がしあがる。
example_sentences.english: The piece will be finished.

example_sentences.japanese: なんとかドレスをぬいあげました。
example_sentences.english: I have somehow managed to finish sewing the dress.

example_sentences.japanese: ご飯がたきあがる。
example_sentences.english: The rice will finish up cooking.

example_sentences.japanese: 空は雨の後ではれあがった。
example_sentences.english: The weather cleared completely after the rain.

example_sentences.japanese: 論文がかきあがる。
example_sentences.english: To finish up writing an essay.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供は雪で城をつくりあげた。
example_sentences.english: Children have finished making a snow castle.

example_sentences.japanese: その日のうちに部屋の壁をぬりあげた。
example_sentences.english: I finished painting the room walls before the day was over.

example_sentences.japanese: 本物そっくりの模型ができあがった。
example_sentences.english: The model that looks exactly like the real thing has been completed.

example_sentences.japanese: ５分後に、卵を加えて一緒にゆであげる。
example_sentences.english: After five minutes add an egg and boil it together until it is done.

example_sentences.japanese: やっぱりご飯はたきあがったばかりのに限るね。
example_sentences.english: As expected, the rice that has just finished cooking is the best.

example_sentences.japanese: 家族の後押しのおかげで初めての子供向けの本をかきあげることができました。
example_sentences.english: Thanks to the support of my family I was able to finish writing my first book for children.

example_sentences.japanese: ラッピングが仕上がったら番号でお呼びします。
example_sentences.english: We will call you by your number once we finish wrapping it.

example_sentences.japanese: あれはどんな風に仕上がるかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder how that will be completed.

general_translation: To do something completely to the end, Utterly, Resolutely
formation: Verb［stem］+ 切（き）る
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ 切（き）る
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ 切（き）ります
explanation: A grammar point that expresses (A) being done completely, or to the cutoff point.
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: つかいきってから次のジャムを買ってよ。
example_sentences.english: Buy another jar of jam after you use one up completely.

example_sentences.japanese: 自分は全部使いきるまで、新しいのを買わない。
example_sentences.english: Personally, I don't buy new ones until I use everything up.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日はライトノベルを２冊も読みきった。
example_sentences.english: I finished reading 2 light novels today.

example_sentences.japanese: 水筒の水を飲みきったがまだのどが渇いている。
example_sentences.english: I finished drinking the water in my bottle, but am still thirsty.

example_sentences.japanese: このカーブではスピードを落とさずに走りきるのが重要だ。
example_sentences.english: At this curve, it is important to drive at full pelt without slowing down.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回の大会で全力を出しきることができて良かったです。
example_sentences.english: I am happy that I was able to do the best that I can do at this tournament. (Full capacity of power)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の寒さでひえきってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Because of the cold today, I am completely frozen. (utterly)

example_sentences.japanese: 給料をもらった日につかいきってしまった。
example_sentences.english: I completely used up my entire paycheck the day I got it. (utterly)

example_sentences.japanese: たとえどんなことがあっても勇者さまをしんじきります。
example_sentences.english: No matter what will happen, I trust the hero completely.

example_sentences.japanese: 先週末、三冊のマンガをよみきった。
