example_sentences.english: I completely finished reading three manga last weekend.

example_sentences.japanese: これだけの薪があれば冬をのりきることが出来るでしょう。
example_sentences.english: With this much firewood, we will surely be able to make it completely through winter.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はウィスキーを水のように一気に一本のみきった。
example_sentences.english: He completely drank an entire bottle of whiskey like it was water.

example_sentences.japanese: 喉がかわききっていたから、水がものすごく美味しく感じた。
example_sentences.english: The water tasted amazing, because my throat was completely dry. (utterly)

example_sentences.japanese: 妻は亡き夫の代わりに本をかききった。
example_sentences.english: The wife finished writing the book in place of the late husband. (completely・resolutely)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女がお詫びをいいきらないうちに、彼は「ドンマイ」と言った。
example_sentences.english: Before she could finish her apology, he said, 'Don't worry about that.' (completely)

example_sentences.japanese: つかれきっていたから、私の代わりに兄をお母さんの迎えに行かせた。
example_sentences.english: Because I was completely worn out, I had my brother go pick up my mother in my place. (utterly)

example_sentences.japanese: 新製品は大成功でした！初ロットを一週間でうりきりました。
example_sentences.english: The new product was a great success! We completely sold the first batch in one week.

general_translation: Being unable to finish or complete
formation: Verb［stem］+ 切（き）れない
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ 切（き）れない
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ 切（き）れません
explanation: A strong phrase expressing that (A) cannot be finished, or cannot reach the cutoff point.
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: 空の星の数がかぞえきれない。
example_sentences.english: You can't completely count the number of stars in the sky.

example_sentences.japanese: 宇宙には数えきれないほどの星がある。
example_sentences.english: There are too many stars in space to count. (Can't finish counting)

example_sentences.japanese: この肉は厚すぎて歯では噛みきれない。
example_sentences.english: This meat is so thick that it is not possible to chew with your teeth.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のこの気持ちは言葉では表しきれない。
example_sentences.english: I cannot possibly explain this feeling of mine with words. (Cannot explain satisfactorily)

example_sentences.japanese: 楽しみ過ぎて待ちきれない。
example_sentences.english: I am so excited that I can't wait. (Cannot wait satisfactorily)

example_sentences.japanese: あの山は一日では登りきれない。
example_sentences.english: You can't possibly finish climbing this mountain in one day.

example_sentences.japanese: 大盛頼むの？いくらあなたでもここの大盛は食べきれないと思うよ。
example_sentences.english: Are you going to order the large one? I don't think you can possibly finish the portion they serve here.

example_sentences.japanese: お皿が多すぎて、あらいきれない。
example_sentences.english: There are too many dishes. I will be unable to finish washing them.

example_sentences.japanese: 新曲の発売日がまちきれない。
example_sentences.english: I absolutely cannot wait for the release of their new song.

example_sentences.japanese: 辛かったから、たべきれなかった。
example_sentences.english: Because it was spicy, I was unable to finish eating the food.

example_sentences.japanese: この溢れる思いをおさえきれない。
example_sentences.english: I am unable to completely control my emotions from overflowing.

example_sentences.japanese: 安かったから、もちきれないほど買ってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: Because it was cheap, I bought more than I could carry.

example_sentences.japanese: 掃除機で吸ってもほこりをとりきれない。
example_sentences.english: Even if you use a vacuum cleaner, you will be unable to completely get all of the dust.

example_sentences.japanese: こんなにたくさん本を借りてきてもよみきれないんじゃないの？
example_sentences.english: Even if you borrowed all of these books you cannot possibly finish reading them all.

example_sentences.japanese: このたえきれない悲しみを一緒に乗り越えよう！
example_sentences.english: Let's overcome this completely unbearable sorrow together!

example_sentences.japanese: どんなに愛しているかを言葉でつたえきれない。結婚してくれる？
example_sentences.english: Words cannot completely convey how much I love you. Will you marry me?

example_sentences.japanese: 貨物、多すぎてのせきれない。一部を置いていくしかないな。
example_sentences.english: There is too much cargo and I cannot load it completely. There is no choice but to leave part of it.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺のためにこんなに世話をしてくれて、この気持ちは言葉であらわしきれない。
example_sentences.english: You did so much for me, I am not able to express my gratitude completely with words.

general_translation: Only, Just, Since
formation: Verb［た］ + きり(1)Noun + きりこれ(2) + きり(1)Number + Counter + きり(1)(1) っきり(2) それ
casual_structure: Verb［た］ + きり(1)Noun + きりこれ(2) + きり(1)Number + Counter + きり(1)(1) っきり(2) それ
explanation: A phrase that expresses the first and last time or limit for something as the cutoff point.
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: やっと二人っきりになれたね。
example_sentences.english: It is finally just the two of us.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日、晩ご飯食べたきり何も食べてないから、めちゃお腹が空いた。
example_sentences.english: I haven't eaten anything since last night, so I am extremely hungry.

example_sentences.japanese: お祖母ちゃんは去年病気で倒れて、寝たきりになった。
example_sentences.english: Grandma got sick last year, and has become bedridden. (Can only sleep)

example_sentences.japanese: 一人きりになれる時間が欲しい。
example_sentences.english: I  want some time where I can be alone.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼とは一度きりしか会えていない。
example_sentences.english: I was only able to meet him once.

example_sentences.japanese: 二人っきりの時間はいいね！
example_sentences.english: A time just for the two of us is nice, isn't it!

example_sentences.japanese: 寂しい時、一人っきりで泣く。
example_sentences.english: When I am sad, I cry alone. (just/only myself)

example_sentences.japanese: 父がついに寝たきりになってしまった。
example_sentences.english: My dad has become completely bedridden (only/just sleeps).

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女とは喧嘩したっきり会っていません。
example_sentences.english: I haven't seen my girlfriend since we had a fight.

example_sentences.japanese: チャンスは一度きりしかないから緊張する。
example_sentences.english: I am nervous because I have only one chance.

example_sentences.japanese: その店に一回行ったきり、行っていない。
example_sentences.english: I went to that store just once and haven't gone again.

example_sentences.japanese: ５年前に会ったきりだから、また会いたいですね。
example_sentences.english: It has been five years since we last met, so I want to see you again.

example_sentences.japanese: 一度習ったきりだから、やり方を忘れてしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I have forgotten how to do it because I had only learned it once.

example_sentences.japanese: ３年前に飲んだっきり薬を飲む機会がない。
example_sentences.english: Since I took medicine three years ago, I have not had the chance to take it (again). (only)

example_sentences.japanese: 「また後で電話します」と言ったきり全然連絡がありません。
example_sentences.english: There has been absolutely no word from them since they said that they would get back to me.

example_sentences.japanese: それっきり彼は部屋から出なくなった。
example_sentences.english: Since that, he reached the point where he would not come out of his room. (just/only)

example_sentences.japanese: 朝ご飯を食べたっきり何も食べていないから、お腹がすいている。
example_sentences.english: I haven't had anything since I ate breakfast, so I'm hungry.

general_translation: Half-, Not yet finished, About to, Begin to
formation: Verb［stem］+ かけだVerb［stem］+ かけるVerb［stem］+ かけの + Noun
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ かけだVerb［stem］+ かけるVerb［stem］+ かけの + Noun
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ かけですVerb［stem］+ かけますVerb［stem］+ かけの + Noun
explanation: A word used to show that something is only half-done, or suspended in an unfinished state.
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: たべかけのケーキでも良ければありますよ。
example_sentences.english: I have some half-eaten cake, if you would like.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺の食べかけだけど大丈夫？
example_sentences.english: This is half-eaten by me, is that okay?

example_sentences.japanese: これは私の飲みかけだ。
example_sentences.english: This is my half-drunk one.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は死にかけの子犬を救った。
example_sentences.english: He saved a puppy that was about to die. (Half dead)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は壊れかけのパソコンを買って直すのが趣味だ。
example_sentences.english: Her hobby is to buy half-broken computers and fix them. (Computers on the verge of breaking)

example_sentences.japanese: やばい、死にかけるところだった。
example_sentences.english: Wow, I was about to die right there. (Almost on the verge of dying)

example_sentences.japanese: 飲みかけた水を捨てる。
example_sentences.english: I will throw away my half drunk water.

example_sentences.japanese: かきかけの絵を早く完成させたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to finish this half-drawn picture quickly.

example_sentences.japanese: この時計こわれかけだけど、ないよりはいいか。
example_sentences.english: This watch is half-broken, but is still better than nothing.

example_sentences.japanese: わすれかけていた思い出が急に蘇った。
example_sentences.english: The half-forgotten memory suddenly came back.

example_sentences.japanese: 交通事故で危うくしにかけた。
example_sentences.english: I nearly died in the car accident. (half-dead)

example_sentences.japanese: はがれかけているポスターを貼り直してください。
example_sentences.english: Please, fix this half-peeled off poster.

example_sentences.japanese: かきかけたまま出していない手紙があります。
example_sentences.english: I have a letter that I have yet to send that is still half-written.

example_sentences.japanese: ふきかけたテーブルをちゃんと最後まで拭いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please finish wiping this half-wiped table.

example_sentences.japanese: のみかけのジュースがあるのを忘れていた。
example_sentences.english: I forgot that I have some juice that I haven't yet finished. (Half-finished)

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の宿題はもうおわりかけです。
example_sentences.english: Today's homework is about to be finished. (Half-finished)

example_sentences.japanese: 私は、何冊もよみかけの本がある。
example_sentences.english: I have a lot of books that are half-read.

example_sentences.japanese: 靴をはきかけて、靴下を履いていないことに気づいた。
example_sentences.english: I noticed that I was not wearing socks when I was about to put on my shoes. (Half-on)

example_sentences.japanese: 先週の事故で死にかけそうになった。
example_sentences.english: I was on the verge of dying in an accident last week.

example_sentences.japanese: 壊れかけていた椅子に座ったら、椅子が壊れた。
example_sentences.english: When I sat on a chair that was on the verge of breaking, it broke.

example_sentences.japanese: 終わりかけだからちょっと待って。
example_sentences.english: I'm in the process of finishing, so can you wait a little.

general_translation: Over (a period), From ~ until, Through
formation: Noun + にかけて(は)
casual_structure: Noun + にかけて(は)
explanation: An expression used to highlight a duration of time during which a certain action will be suspended in an ongoing state.
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: 今週末にかけて、雨が降るでしょう。
example_sentences.english: It looks like it is going to rain over the weekend. (through)

example_sentences.japanese: 今夜から朝にかけて大雨が降るでしょう。
example_sentences.english: It looks like it will rain from tonight through til the morning.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎年、三月末から五月の頭にかけて多くの人が引っ越しをします。
example_sentences.english: Every year, a lot of people move from the end of March through the beginning of May.

example_sentences.japanese: この一年にかけて、いろいろなことを経験したい。
example_sentences.english: I want to experience a variety of things over this next year. (through)

example_sentences.japanese: 先週にかけて降った大雪が、まだ全然溶けない。
example_sentences.english: It kept snowing all through last week, and it hasn't melted yet. (over)

example_sentences.japanese: 来年にかけての目標を立ててください。
example_sentences.english: Please establish your goals over the next year. (from ~ until)

example_sentences.japanese: 関東から東北にかけて雨が降り続いている。
example_sentences.english: It has been raining from the Kanto area to the Tohoku area. (throughout)

example_sentences.japanese: 毎年春にかけて花粉症が大流行します。
example_sentences.english: There is a hay fever epidemic all through spring each year. (over a period)

example_sentences.japanese: 今月にかけて急に仕事が増えた。
example_sentences.english: Over the period of this month, the amount of work I have to do has suddenly increased. (throughout)

example_sentences.japanese: 夜から朝にかけて急に冷え込むみたいだから、気をつけた方がいい。
example_sentences.english: You should be careful because it will get much colder from tonight until tomorrow morning. (through)

example_sentences.japanese: 今月の４日から５日にかけて、台風が上陸しそうだ。
example_sentences.english: It seems that this month typhoons will hit Japan from the fourth until the fifth. (over a period of ~)

example_sentences.japanese: 中学から高校にかけて急激に背が伸びたんです。
example_sentences.english: He/She has become much taller during the time between middle school and high school. (over a period of ~)

example_sentences.japanese: 昭和から平成にかけて変わったことと言えば何ですか？
example_sentences.english: What are the things that changed from the Showa era to the Heisei era? (until)

example_sentences.japanese: あのスーパーは今日から、明日にかけて、セールがあるらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that that supermarket is having a sale from today through tomorrow. (over a period of~)

example_sentences.japanese: 今は雨が降っていますが、朝にかけては晴れるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: It is raining right now, but it seems like it will clear up during the morning. (Limited to the extent of tomorrow morning)

example_sentences.japanese: 今月から来月にかけては忙しい時期になるので、無理せずに頑張ってください。
example_sentences.english: Limited from this month through until next month, it is going to be a busy season, so please do your best without overworking yourself.

general_translation: Freshly ~ed, Just ~ed
formation: Verb［stem］+ たてVerb［stem］+ たて + の + Noun
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ たてVerb［stem］+ たて + の + Noun
explanation: A word which indicates that (A) was just done, or freshly done. The finished product has just been established.
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: つりたての魚を食べるのは最高！
example_sentences.english: Eating freshly caught fish is the best!

example_sentences.japanese: ここにあるのは全部揚げたてですよ。
example_sentences.english: Everything here is freshly fried.

example_sentences.japanese: 釣りたてだから新鮮だよ！
example_sentences.english: It is just fished up, so it is fresh!

example_sentences.japanese: 私は出来たてのパンを食べるのが大好きです。
example_sentences.english: I like to eat freshly baked bread.

example_sentences.japanese: 生まれたての赤ちゃんっておさるさんみたいじゃない？
example_sentences.english: Don't newborn babies look like monkeys?

example_sentences.japanese: この魚はやきたてです。
example_sentences.english: This fish has been freshly cooked.

example_sentences.japanese: できたてのお菓子を食べたのは初めてだ。
example_sentences.english: It's my first time eating freshly made sweets.

example_sentences.japanese: このお店ではとりたての野菜が買えます。
example_sentences.english: You can buy freshly picked vegetables at this shop.

example_sentences.japanese: いれたてのコーヒーの香りが好きだ。
example_sentences.english: I like the smell of freshly made coffee.

example_sentences.japanese: もぎたての果物はみずみずしい。
example_sentences.english: Freshly picked fruits are so juicy.

example_sentences.japanese: 印刷したての雑誌を入手しました。
example_sentences.english: I got a magazine that was just printed.

example_sentences.japanese: むしたてのお芋を召し上がれ！
example_sentences.english: Please eat the freshly steamed sweet potatoes!

example_sentences.japanese: このベンチはペンキぬりたてのため、気を付けてください。
example_sentences.english: This bench has been freshly painted, so please be careful.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は女優になりたてです。
example_sentences.english: She has just become an actress.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は小学校に入学したてで張り切っています。
example_sentences.english: He is in high spirits, because he has just entered elementary school.

example_sentences.japanese: この農場は毎日、うみたての卵を出荷する。
example_sentences.english: This farm is shipping freshly laid eggs every day.

example_sentences.japanese: 取り立ての野菜で作るサラダは美味しい。
example_sentences.english: Making salad with freshly picked vegetables is delicious. (Natural Japanese, as the vegetables will slowly degrade in quality after picking)

example_sentences.japanese: この靴は濡れたてだから、乾かすのに少し時間がかかると思う。
example_sentences.english: These shoes got freshly wet, so it will take some time to dry. (Unnatural Japanese, as becoming wet has no time-based relevance to what happens next)

general_translation: To go into, To put into
formation: Verb［stem］ + 込（こ）む
casual_structure: Verb［stem］ + 込（こ）む
polite_structure: Verb［stem］ + 込（こ）みます
explanation: A structure expressing that the action of (A) will be done into something else. With the nuance of jamming or pressing through any obstacles.
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: 教師：「教科書に答えをかきこんでください。」
example_sentences.english: Teacher: 'Please fill in your textbooks with answers.' (put into)

example_sentences.japanese: ピンを壁に押しこむ。
example_sentences.english: To push a pin into a wall.

example_sentences.japanese: 薬を飲みこむのが苦手です。
example_sentences.english: I am not the best at drinking down medicine. (I am not the best at swallowing medicine)

example_sentences.japanese: 電車のドアが閉まる前に、電車に走りこんだ。
example_sentences.english: Before the train door closed, I ran in.

example_sentences.japanese: サウナから出て、水風呂に飛びこむように入った。
example_sentences.english: I came out of the sauna and went into the water bath as if I was leaping into it.

example_sentences.japanese: トムはジェロニモと叫びながら、プールにとびこんだ。
example_sentences.english: Tom jumped into the pool while screaming 'Geronimo!' (put into)

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ：「どうして窓が閉めてあるの？」Ｂ：「冷たい風がはいりこまないように。」
example_sentences.english: A: 'Why is the window closed?'B: 'So that cold air won't get in.' (put into)

example_sentences.japanese: バッキンガム宮殿の警護官について：「笑いをのみこみながら、移動せずに立ったままだった。」
example_sentences.english: About a Buckingham Palace guard: 'He kept standing, unmoving, while holding in a smile.' (swallowing・put into)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「彼女は泥棒の顎に見事に拳をうちこんだそうだ。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'I heard that she fantastically drove her fist into the thief's face.' (put into)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話、Ａ：「お金って、何するの？」Ｂ：「銀行にはらいこもうと思う。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends, A: 'What are you gonna do with the money?'B: 'I plan to deposit it into the bank.' (put into)

example_sentences.japanese: ライトノベル、勇者たちの会話：「一人で魔王の城にのりこむおつもりですか？おやめ下さい！」
example_sentences.english: Light novel, chat between heroes: 'Do you plan to march into the demon king's castle alone? Please, stop!' (put into)

example_sentences.japanese: 行列で：「（列に）わりこむなんて、図々しいですよ！」
example_sentences.english: In the queue: 'To cut in (line)! How impudent!' (put into)

example_sentences.japanese: ライトノベル、ナレーター：「コタカが突然、部室にはいりこんで来て、彼女の隣に席を取った。」
example_sentences.english: Light Novel, Narrator: 'Kotaka suddenly came into the club room and took the seat next to her.' (go into)

example_sentences.japanese: ライトノベル、クラスメートとの話：「ドラゴンをクラスにもちこむのはルール違反じゃないか？」
example_sentences.english: Light novel, chat between classmates : 'Taking a dragon into class, isn't that breaking the rules?' (put into)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「布団で寝ていると、猫が布団の中にもぐりこんできた。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'When I was sleeping, my cat slipped into the futon. ' (put into)

example_sentences.japanese: ノベル：「心地よい風が窓からふきこんできた。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'A pleasant breeze has started blowing in from the window.' (put into)

general_translation: Remain, To do thoroughly, Deeply, Intensely
formation: Verb［stem］+ 込（こ）む
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ 込（こ）む
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ 込（こ）みます
explanation: A grammar point expressing that the action of (A) will be done deeply or thoroughly. With the nuance of jamming or pressing through any obstacles.
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: みんないっせいにだまりこんでいた。
example_sentences.english: At once, everyone sunk into an intense silence and remained silent.

example_sentences.japanese: もうこんな時間か、話しこんじゃったな。
example_sentences.english: It's already this time, we got lost in talking, didn't we?

example_sentences.japanese: そんなに考えこまなくてもいいよ。
example_sentences.english: You don't have to think so deeply about this.

example_sentences.japanese: 警察が道の真ん中で座りこんでいる人に話しかけた。
example_sentences.english: The police went to talk to the person that remained seated in the middle of the road.

example_sentences.japanese: 今は取りこみ中なので手が空いたらかけなおします。
example_sentences.english: I am held up working right now, so I will call you back once my hands are free.

example_sentences.japanese: ノベル：「れつこは気分が悪くなり、すわりこんだ。」
example_sentences.english: Novel: 'Retsuko felt weak and sat down.' (deeply・thoroughly)

example_sentences.japanese: 疲れていたので、シャワーを浴びずにねむりこんだ。
example_sentences.english: I was tired, so I fell deeply asleep without taking a shower. (intensely・thoroughly)

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「何を長々はなしこんでたの？」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'What were you so intently talking about for so long?' (deeply・thoroughly)

example_sentences.japanese: エッセイ：「熱心にひとつの事にうちこむことが必要だと思っている。」
example_sentences.english: Essay: 'I think that devoting oneself deeply to one thing is important.'

example_sentences.japanese: 小さな花の写真を撮るためにしゃがみこむ。
example_sentences.english: To squat down deeply (with their face between their legs) in order to take a picture of a small flower.

example_sentences.japanese: 友達との話：「テストの前に単語をおぼえこむつもりだよ。」
example_sentences.english: Chat between friends: 'I plan to thoroughly memorize the vocabulary before the exam.'

example_sentences.japanese: 会社、上司：「この資料は、明日までによくよみこんでおいて。」部下：「はい。」
example_sentences.english: The company, boss: 'Thoroughly read those documents by tomorrow.'Subordinate: 'Understood.'

example_sentences.japanese: 社長：「一日中かんがえこんだあとで、会社社長を退任することに決めました。」
example_sentences.english: Company president: 'After having thought deeply about it all day, I have decided to step down from the position of company president.' (intensely・thoroughly)

example_sentences.japanese: 明日から旅行に行くから、学校の課題をやりこんでおくつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: I am going on a trip tomorrow, so I plan to thoroughly do my school homework.

example_sentences.japanese: 論文：「しかし、サンタクロースがいるとしんじこむ子供もいる。」
example_sentences.english: Essay/article: 'However, there are also children that firmly believe that Santa Claus exists.' (deeply・thoroughly)

example_sentences.japanese: ブログの投稿：「パスワードを思い出せず、しばらくかんがえこんだ。」
example_sentences.english: Blog post: 'Not being able to recall the password, I plunged deep into thought for a while.' (remained thinking・brood)

general_translation: To pretend, To act as if
formation: Verb［ている］(1) + ふりをする［い］Adjective + ふりをする［な］Adjective + な + ふりをするNoun + の + ふりをする(1) Verb［ない］、Verb［た］
casual_structure: Verb［ている］(1) + ふりをする［い］Adjective + ふりをする［な］Adjective + な + ふりをするNoun + の + ふりをする(1) Verb［ない］、Verb［た］
polite_structure: Verb［ている］(1) + ふりをします［い］Adjective + ふりをします［な］Adjective + な + ふりをしますNoun + の + ふりをします(1) Verb［ない］、Verb［た］
explanation: A structure that implies that someone is pretending to do or be (A), by taking on its outward appearance.
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: ないたふりをしたって無駄ですよ。
example_sentences.english: When you pretended to cry, it was useless.

example_sentences.japanese: この蛇は人等の大きな動物が近づくと死んだふりをするらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that this snake pretends to be dead when humans and other similar big animals approach it.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕は子供の頃、よく寝ているふりをした。
example_sentences.english: When I was a child, I would often pretend to sleep.

example_sentences.japanese: 欲しいのはこれではなかったけど、せっかく買ってくれたから嬉しいふりをする。
example_sentences.english: This is not what I wanted, but since they went out of their way and bought it for me, I will pretend that I am happy.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺の前ではそんな、元気なふりをしなくていいよ。
example_sentences.english: You don't have to pretend that you are happy in front of me.

example_sentences.japanese: カケル君はカエルが好きだからいつもカエルのふりをして遊んでいる。
example_sentences.english: Because Kakeru-kun likes frogs, he always pretends to be a frog when he plays.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の犬はねたふりをすることがある。
example_sentences.english: There are times when my dog pretends to sleep.

example_sentences.japanese: 子供は、注意された時に、きこえないふりをした。
example_sentences.english: The child pretended not to hear while she was being scolded.

example_sentences.japanese: 病気のふりをして会社を休んだ。
example_sentences.english: Pretending to be sick, I took the day off work.

example_sentences.japanese: 見て見ないふりをするのは良くない。
example_sentences.english: It's not good to turn a blind eye  to something. (pretend not to see)

example_sentences.japanese: 嬉しくないふりをしていたが、実はかなり嬉しかった。
example_sentences.english: I was pretending that I wasn't happy but, actually, I was quite happy.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は若いふりをしているが、結構歳をとっているように見える。
example_sentences.english: She is pretending to be young, but she appears to be quite old.

example_sentences.japanese: 分かっているふりをしていたが、あの説明は全然理解できなかった。
example_sentences.english: I was pretending I understood, but I couldn’t understand that explanation at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生の前でだけ真面目なふりをする人は嫌いだ。
example_sentences.english: I dislike people who pretend to be good students only in front of the teacher.

example_sentences.japanese: どんなことについてもしっているふりをする人は信頼ができない。
example_sentences.english: I don't trust people who act as if they know everything.

example_sentences.japanese: だまされたふりをして、振り込め詐欺犯の逮捕に貢献しました。
example_sentences.english: She contributed to the arrests of the bank transfer scammers by pretending to be tricked (by them).

example_sentences.japanese: 熊に遭遇した時、しんだふりをしてもあまり意味がないと聞いた。
example_sentences.english: I have heard that when you encounter a bear, even if you pretended to be dead, it won't make much difference.

general_translation: If possible
formation:
できれば + Phrase
できたら + Phrase
casual_structure:
できれば + Phrase
できたら + Phrase
explanation: A hypothetical construction which indicates that if (A) is doable, it should be done.
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: できたら運転して欲しいです。
example_sentences.english: If possible, I want you to drive.

example_sentences.japanese: できれば車で行きたいけど、電車で行った方が早いかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: If possible, I would love to go by car, but it might be faster by train.

example_sentences.japanese: できたら薬局に行って頭痛薬を買って来てくれる？
example_sentences.english: If possible, can you go to the pharmacy and buy me some headache medication?

example_sentences.japanese: できればお弁当を作ってほしいな。
example_sentences.english: If possible, I would like you to make me a bento.

example_sentences.japanese: できれば本人と会って話がしたい。
example_sentences.english: If possible, I would like to talk with him directly.

example_sentences.japanese: それができたら嬉しいんですけど。
example_sentences.english: If it's possible for you to do that, I would appreciate it.

example_sentences.japanese: できればあの会社で働きたい。
example_sentences.english: If possible, I want to work at that company.

example_sentences.japanese: できればもう帰りたい。熱があるから。
example_sentences.english: If possible, I want to go home because I feel feverish.

example_sentences.japanese: またお会いできたら嬉しいです。
example_sentences.english: If possible, I would be very glad if we had the opportunity to meet again.

example_sentences.japanese: できたら果物を買ってきてもらえませんか？
example_sentences.english: If possible, could I get you to go buy some fruit for me?

example_sentences.japanese: できれば海外で働きたいと思っています。
example_sentences.english: If possible, I think that I would like to work abroad.

example_sentences.japanese: できたらその報告書を見せてください。
example_sentences.english: If possible, please show me that report.

example_sentences.japanese: できれば締め切りを延期させてもらえませんか。
example_sentences.english: If possible, will you allow me to postpone the deadline?

example_sentences.japanese: この仕事、できれば今日中に終わらせたい。
example_sentences.english: If possible, I want to get this done today.

general_translation: If it is alright, If you don't mind, If you would like, If possible
formation: Noun + でよければ
casual_structure: Noun + でよければ
explanation: A hypothetical phrase asking if (A) is good, or if proceeding with (A) will be good.
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: この籠でよければ作れますよ。
example_sentences.english: If this is the basket that you would like, I can make it.

example_sentences.japanese: 焼き肉でよければ、うちの近くに美味しいところがあるから、そこに行かない？
example_sentences.english: If yakiniku is fine, there is a good yakiniku place near my house, so do you want to go there?

example_sentences.japanese: 中古でよければいいのが沢山ありますよ。
example_sentences.english: If used ones are fine, we have many good options.

example_sentences.japanese: 私でよければ手伝うよ。
example_sentences.english: If you don't mind, I can help you. (If I am a suitable option, I can help you)

example_sentences.japanese: 先生でよければ、先生が写真を撮ってあげるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you don't mind me, the teacher, then I can take a picture for you!

example_sentences.japanese: この傘でよければお貸しできます。
example_sentences.english: Sir, I can lend you this umbrella if you'd like.

example_sentences.japanese: 日中でよければ空いてます。
example_sentences.english: If daytime works for you, I am free then.

example_sentences.japanese: この値段でよければ売ります。
example_sentences.english: If this price works for you, then I will sell.

example_sentences.japanese: これくらいの出来でよければ、すぐに作れます。
example_sentences.english: If you don't mind this quality, I can make it for you in no time.

example_sentences.japanese: 水曜日でよければ、一緒に行けます。
example_sentences.english: If you do not mind Wednesday , I can go with you.

example_sentences.japanese: 明日でよければ、あの本を持ってきますよ。
example_sentences.english: I will bring that book, if tomorrow works for you.

example_sentences.japanese: 賃貸でよければ、いい家を見つけた。
example_sentences.english: I have found a good house, if you don't mind renting.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕のアイデアでよければ、参考にしてください。
example_sentences.english: If you don't mind my idea, please use it for reference.

example_sentences.japanese: 中古車でよければ、安い車があります。
example_sentences.english: There are cheap cars, if you don't mind used ones.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生でよければ、一緒に行ってあげるよ。
example_sentences.english: If you don't mind your teacher (me), I will go with you.

example_sentences.japanese: ウェルギリウス：「私でよければ案内しますが。」
example_sentences.english: Virgil: 'If you don't mind (me), I can be your guide.'

general_translation: As soon as
formation: Verb［stem］+ 次第（しだい）［する］Verb + 次第（しだい）
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ 次第（しだい）［する］Verb + 次第（しだい）
explanation: An expression that states that as soon as (A), (B), with (A) determining the involuntary sequence of (B).
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: 準備ができしだい出発しますよ。
example_sentences.english: We will depart as soon as you are ready.

example_sentences.japanese: 用意が出来しだい、僕に声をかけてください。
example_sentences.english: As soon as you get ready, please let me know.

example_sentences.japanese: ミュージカルが終わりしだい、連絡をください。
example_sentences.english: Please call me as soon as the musical ends.

example_sentences.japanese: 待ち合わせ場所に到着ししだい、私に連絡してください。
example_sentences.english: Please give me a call as soon as you arrive at the meet up spot.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼がきしだい、知らせてください。
example_sentences.english: Please notify me as soon as he comes.

example_sentences.japanese: プロジェクトがすみしだい、ご連絡ください。
example_sentences.english: Please contact me as soon as the project is finished.

example_sentences.japanese: お金をうけとりしだい、郵送します。
example_sentences.english: I will send it as soon as I receive the money.

example_sentences.japanese: 学校を卒業ししだい、仕事を探すつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: As soon as I graduate, I plan to look for a job.

example_sentences.japanese: 映画がおわりしだい、連絡して。迎えに行くからね。
example_sentences.english: Let me know as soon as the movie is over because I'll go pick you up.

example_sentences.japanese: 宿題の答えがわかりしだい、教えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please tell (teach) me the homework answers as soon as you know them.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨がやみしだい、大会は再開される。
example_sentences.english: The rally will resume as soon as the rain stops.

example_sentences.japanese: ポーランドにつきしだい、かならずあなたのところを訪ねる。
example_sentences.english: As soon as I arrive in Poland, I will certainly drop by your place.

example_sentences.japanese: 私たちは結婚ししだい、ハネムーンに出かけたいと思います。
example_sentences.english: As soon as we are married, we plan on going on our honeymoon.

example_sentences.japanese: 受話器をとりしだい、部長に伝えてください。
example_sentences.english: Please, notify the section director as soon as someone picks up the phone.

example_sentences.japanese: 平日、妻の仕事がおわりしだい、迎えに行ってあげている。
example_sentences.english: On weekdays, as soon as my wife finishes work, I pick her up.

example_sentences.japanese: 計画が決まり次第、あなたに報告します。
example_sentences.english: I will notify you as soon as we decide on the plan.

example_sentences.japanese: 行くか行かないかは君次第だよ。
example_sentences.english: Whether you go or not will depend on you.

example_sentences.japanese: ６人も乗れるかは車のサイズ次第だね。
example_sentences.english: Whether or not 6 people can fit will depend on the size of the car.

general_translation: In that way, Exactly, Precisely, Just as
formation: Verb［る］(1) + とおりNoun + どおりNoun + の + とおり(1) Verb［た］
casual_structure: Verb［る］(1) + とおりNoun + どおりNoun + の + とおり(1) Verb［た］
explanation: A phrase that expresses agreement about (A), due to the logic following the same road.
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: 思ったとおりでした。
example_sentences.english: It was just as I thought.

example_sentences.japanese: お客様のおっしゃるとおりです。
example_sentences.english: Honored guest, the thing you say is precisely correct. (That's exactly right)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は僕の思ったとおりの時間に帰ってきた。
example_sentences.english: Just as I expected, he came back when I thought he would come back.

example_sentences.japanese: 計画どおりに進めて行きます。
example_sentences.english: We will continue as the plan suggests.

example_sentences.japanese: ご覧のとおり、私の手には何もありません。
example_sentences.english: As you can see, I have nothing in my hands.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたのおっしゃるとおりです。
example_sentences.english: It will be precisely/just as you say.

example_sentences.japanese: 合格者は次のとおりです。
example_sentences.english: Those who passed are as follows... (Precisely)

example_sentences.japanese: お察しのとおり、彼は病気です。
example_sentences.english: Exactly/Just as you may guess, he is quite ill.

example_sentences.japanese: 物事はいつも計画どおりにはいかないものだなぁ。
example_sentences.english: Things will not always go precisely/exactly as planned.

example_sentences.japanese: 結果はすべて予想していたとおりだった。
example_sentences.english: The results were just as we expected.

example_sentences.japanese: 今回は僕の言うとおりにしてくれないか？
example_sentences.english: Can't you just do precisely/just as I say this time?

example_sentences.japanese: 契約どおり、二年間は会社を替えられない。分かるか？
example_sentences.english: Precisely/Just as the contract states, you can't change the company for two years. Got it?

example_sentences.japanese: 原因は先日報告したとおりです。
example_sentences.english: The cause is exactly/just as I reported the other day.

example_sentences.japanese: 説明書のとおりにやらないと、故障の原因になりますよ。
example_sentences.english: If you don't follow the instructions precisely/exactly, that might lead to it breaking down.

example_sentences.japanese: 今、卒業論文が順調です。予定どおりに完成させられそうです。
example_sentences.english: Right now my graduation thesis is coming along nicely. I can finish it exactly/just as planned.

example_sentences.japanese: まったくそのとおりだ。すぐにやらないからこんなことになるんだ。こう言えば満足？？
example_sentences.english: That's precisely/exactly it. It ended up like this because I didn't do it immediately. Satisfied now?

example_sentences.japanese: リカの言ったとおりだった！あそこのパン屋さんはすごくおいしかった！
example_sentences.english: It was exactly as you said, Rika! The bakery over there was very delicious!

example_sentences.japanese: 本当にそのとおりです！何でいつも私たちがやらないといけないんですか。
example_sentences.english: That's honestly exactly it! Why do we have to do it all the time?

general_translation: Be also, It also is
formation: Noun + でもある［い］Adjective + くもある［な］Adjective + でもある
casual_structure: Noun + でもある［い］Adjective + くもある［な］Adjective + でもある
polite_structure: Noun + でもあります［い］Adjective + くもあります［な］Adjective + でもあります
explanation: A construction showing that while something is (A), it is also even (B). Also even exists as (B).
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: この車は少し狭いけれども、快適でもある。
example_sentences.english: This car is a bit small, but it is also comfortable. (it also is)

example_sentences.japanese: タナカさんは英語の先生だし、休みの日は船の船長でもあるから休む時間がない。
example_sentences.english: While Tanaka-san is an English teacher, he is also the captain of a ship on his days off, so he doesn't have any time to rest.

example_sentences.japanese: これは洗濯機でもあるけど、同時に乾燥機でもある。
example_sentences.english: In spite of this being a washing machine, it is also a dryer.

example_sentences.japanese: バンジージャンプは楽しいけれども、同時に危険でもある。
example_sentences.english: In spite of bungee jumping being fun, it is also dangerous at the same time.

example_sentences.japanese: この機械は重くて邪魔だけど、同時に便利でもある。
example_sentences.english: While this machine is heavy and a nuisance, it is also useful.

example_sentences.japanese: オーストラリアは国であり、大陸でもある。
example_sentences.english: Australia is a country. It is also a continent. (it also is)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は優れたプログラマーだ。そして多言語話者でもある。
example_sentences.english: He is an excellent programmer. He is also a polyglot. (he also is)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は良い社長であったし、良い父親でもあった。
example_sentences.english: He was a good company president and also a good father. (he also was)

example_sentences.japanese: ひとみさんは中学生であるとともに社長でもある。
example_sentences.english: Hitomi is a middle school student, she is also a company president. (she also is)

example_sentences.japanese: ハイブリッド車はガソリンエンジンを持ちながら、電気自動車でもある。
example_sentences.english: Hybrid cars have a gasoline engine, but are also electric. (it also is)

example_sentences.japanese: 語学を学ぶことは楽しい。しかし、自分との戦いでもある。
example_sentences.english: Learning languages is fun. However, it is also a fight with oneself. (it also is)

example_sentences.japanese: トミー・ビゾーの伝説は不明であり、また、どのように金持ちになったのかは大きな謎でもある。
example_sentences.english: Tommy Bizo's life story is unknown, how he got rich is also a big mystery. (it also is)

example_sentences.japanese: てづかおさむ先生は漫画家として有名なのはもちろん、医科大学の卒業生でもある。
example_sentences.english: Osamu Tezuka is, of course, famous as a manga artist, but he is also a medical graduate. (he also is)

example_sentences.japanese: 金は綺麗である。また、地球で最も高い金属の一つでもある。
example_sentences.english: Gold is beautiful. It is also one of the most expensive metals on earth. (it also is)

example_sentences.japanese: カーボンファイバーは非常に軽い。一方で、非常に高価でもある。
example_sentences.english: Carbon fiber is very light. On the other hand, it is also very expensive. (it also is)

example_sentences.japanese: 「ずっと」というのは何かが長い間続いているということである。「よりずっと速い」のように、比べているものとの間に大きな隔たりがあるということを示す言葉でもある。
example_sentences.english: 'ずっと' means that something continues for a long time. It is also a phrase that indicates that there is a wide gap between things you are comparing, like in 'よりずっと速い'.

general_translation: Regardless of, No matter what
formation: Verb + と + どうしてもどうしても + Phrase
casual_structure: Verb + と + どうしてもどうしても + Phrase
explanation: A construction stating that no matter how the issue of (A) is even handled, the result will not change.
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてもお土産を買いたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to buy a souvenir no matter what.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしても我慢ができなくて買っちゃった。
example_sentences.english: I accidentally bought it because I couldn't resist no matter what.

example_sentences.japanese: 牛乳飲むとどうしてもお腹が痛くなるんです。
example_sentences.english: Regardless of anything, If I drink milk, I get a stomach ache.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしても欲しいのなら、自分で買いなさい。
example_sentences.english: If you want it no matter what, buy it yourself.

example_sentences.japanese: 寝る前にお腹いっぱいに食べるとどうしても寝れなくなっちゃうんだよね。
example_sentences.english: When I eat till I'm full, before I sleep, I am unable to sleep no matter what.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べるとどうしても眠たくなる。
example_sentences.english: If I eat, I get sleepy no matter what.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてもアイスクリームが食べたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to eat ice cream no matter what.

example_sentences.japanese: 君にどうしても伝えたいことがある。
example_sentences.english: There is something I want to tell you, no matter what.

example_sentences.japanese: この癖はどうしても治らない。
example_sentences.english: No matter what I do, this habit won't go away.

example_sentences.japanese: あの試合はどうしても見たい。
example_sentences.english: I want to watch that game no matter what.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしても諦められない夢がある。
example_sentences.english: I have a dream I won't give up on, no matter what.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてもワインのコルクが抜けない。
example_sentences.english: No matter what I do, I can't remove the cork from the wine bottle.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてもボートに乗りたい。
example_sentences.english: I want to get on that boat no matter what.

example_sentences.japanese: どうしても彼の名前が思い出せない。
example_sentences.english: I can't recall his name, regardless of how hard I try.

example_sentences.japanese: それは僕がどうしてもしないといけない仕事なんですか？
example_sentences.english: Is that the work I have to do? No matter what?

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてもお金が必要なので、貸してもらえませんか？
example_sentences.english: I need money regardless of what it takes, so could you please lend me some?

example_sentences.japanese: どうしてもヘリコプターには乗りたくない。
example_sentences.english: In any case, I don't want to ride a helicopter.

general_translation: If, Supposing
formation: もしも + Phrase［なら］(1)(1) Phrase［ば］、Phrase［と］、Phrase［ても］
casual_structure: もしも + Phrase［なら］(1)(1) Phrase［ば］、Phrase［と］、Phrase［ても］
explanation: A strong hypothetical phrase which indicates that even supposing if (A), (B).
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: もしもドラえもんがいたなら、助けてもらえるのに。
example_sentences.english: If Doraemon were here, he would help us.

example_sentences.japanese: もしも、今年中に引っ越すのならば、僕が手伝ってやるよ。
example_sentences.english: Supposing that you move within this year, I will help you.

example_sentences.japanese: もしも仕事で怪我をすると、現場が止まるので気をつけてください。
example_sentences.english: Supposing that you get hurt at work, the site will be shut down, so please be careful.

example_sentences.japanese: もしも明日休みなら、一緒に博物館へいかない？
example_sentences.english: Assuming you have a day off tomorrow, do you want to go to the museum with me?

example_sentences.japanese: もしも彼がいたとしても、今日中には終わらなかっただろう。
example_sentences.english: Supposing he were even here, don't you think we would not have been able to complete it by today?

example_sentences.japanese: もしも僕がドラえもんでも助けられない。
example_sentences.english: Even if I were Doraemon I would be unable to help.

example_sentences.japanese: もしも戦うなら囲碁がいい。
example_sentences.english: If we are going to battle, I say we settle it with a game of Go.

example_sentences.japanese: もしも可能なら、僕も仲間に入りたい。
example_sentences.english: If possible, I want to join you.

example_sentences.japanese: もしもこれが現実でも、受け入れられると思います。
example_sentences.english: Even if this is a hard fact, I think that I can accept it.

example_sentences.japanese: もしも子供がいなくても、僕はたぶん幸せだよ。
example_sentences.english: I would probably be happy even if I didn't have any children.

example_sentences.japanese: もしも私が君の立場でも、同じことをしたでしょう。
example_sentences.english: If I was in your place, I would have done the same thing.

example_sentences.japanese: もしも明日雨なら、遠足は延期になります。
example_sentences.english: If it rains tomorrow, the trip will be postponed.

example_sentences.japanese: もしもこの計画が実現したなら、この街はもっと住みやすくなるでしょう。
example_sentences.english: If the plan becomes a reality, this town will become much easier to live in.

example_sentences.japanese: もしもこの店がなくなっても、一生忘れません。
example_sentences.english: Even if something happens to this store, I will never forget it, as long as I live.

example_sentences.japanese: セレナ：「もしも願いが叶うなら、もう一度だけ君に会いたい。」
example_sentences.english: Serena:'If my dream comes true, I want to see you just one more time.'

example_sentences.japanese: シリクス：「もしも生まれ変わるなら、その時も僕と結婚してくれる？」
example_sentences.english: Sirix: 'If you were reborn, would you marry me again?'

example_sentences.japanese: もし、また宿題を忘れたら親に電話をします。
example_sentences.english: Assuming you forget your homework again, I will call your parents. (Calling their parents will be the result of forgetting their homework)

example_sentences.japanese: たとえ、テストが難しくても最後まで諦めないで頑張ってください。
example_sentences.english: If, for example, the test is hard, don't give up, and do your best until the very end. (If the test is difficult, doing your best is not a result, just one of many choices that could be made)

general_translation: Fellow, With each other, Mutually, Between, Among, Together, With
formation: Noun + 同士（どうし）Noun + 同士（どうし） + の + Noun
casual_structure: Noun + 同士（どうし）Noun + 同士（どうし） + の + Noun
explanation: A word expressing that groups of people are in the same role, or (A) is being done between people in that same position.
lesson_topic: Do it this Way, Did it that Way

example_sentences.japanese: このように紐でページどうしを結びつけることができます。
example_sentences.english: You can connect pages together with a string like this.

example_sentences.japanese: お互い大人どうしなんだから、落ち着いて話し合おうよ。
example_sentences.english: We are fellow adults, so let's calm down and talk about this.

example_sentences.japanese: あなたたちは本当に似たものどうしね。
example_sentences.english: You guys are really similar (in personality).

example_sentences.japanese: これは弁護士どうしの話しなので勝手に入って来ないで下さい。
example_sentences.english: This is a conversation between lawyers, so please don't barge in.

example_sentences.japanese: 家族どうしで会話をするときはほとんど日本語です。
example_sentences.english: When we talk between family members, we mostly use Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は友達どうしの約束を破った。
example_sentences.english: He broke a promise that was made between friends.

example_sentences.japanese: それは兄弟どうしの問題でしょ？私を巻き込まないで。
example_sentences.english: That is an issue between siblings, isn't it? Don't pull me into it.

example_sentences.japanese: 負けた者どうしで飲みに行こうよ！
example_sentences.english: Let's go out for drinks as fellow losers!

example_sentences.japanese: 中学生どうしは結婚するには若すぎる。
example_sentences.english: Middle schoolers are too young to marry (each other).

example_sentences.japanese: 同級生どうしだから、助け合わなきゃね。
example_sentences.english: We are fellow classmates, so we have to help one another, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 友達どうしの約束だったのに彼は破った。
example_sentences.english: Even though it was a promise among friends, he broke it.

example_sentences.japanese: キリンは雄どうしが喧嘩をする時互いに長い首で打ち合う。
example_sentences.english: When male giraffes fight among themselves they hit each other with their long necks.

example_sentences.japanese: そのため、日本の企業どうしの協力が以前よりも必要だ。
example_sentences.english: Because of that, cooperation among Japanese companies is needed more than before.

example_sentences.japanese: 「だって」は家族や友達どうしなどで使う、くだけた表現なので、上司などとの話し合いのときは使わないでください。
example_sentences.english: 'だって' is an informal expression used among family and friends, therefore please do not use it when discussing with superiors and the like.

example_sentences.japanese: 喧嘩をする弟たちどうしをおもちゃなどでよく落ち着かせたものだ。
example_sentences.english: I often used to calm my brothers, who were fighting among themselves, with things like toys.

example_sentences.japanese: 似た音楽が好きな者どうしは仲良くなるのがはやい。
example_sentences.english: People who share mutual taste in music have no trouble getting to know each other.

example_sentences.japanese: 幼馴染どうしの結婚はうまくいかない場合もある。
example_sentences.english: There are also cases when marriages between childhood friends do not go well.

example_sentences.japanese: インターネットへのアクセスが広がるにつれて、プレイヤーどうしで競い合うオンラインゲームが人気になってきた。
example_sentences.english: As access to the internet spread, online games, where players could compete with one another, started to gain popularity.

example_sentences.japanese: この糊は紙同士だとよくくっつきますがプラスチック同士だとあまりくっつかないです。
example_sentences.english: This glue sticks really well between paper, but between plastic, it does not stick well. (Natural, but not very common)

example_sentences.japanese: プロの格闘家同士の戦いは見ていて楽しい。
example_sentences.english: Watching a fight between two professional martial artists is fun. (Natural)

general_translation: Hard to, Difficult to
formation: Verb［stem］+ がたい
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ がたい
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ がたいです
explanation: A phrase that focuses on the difficulty of (A), in relation to the task itself being hard.

example_sentences.japanese: あの罪はゆるしがたい。
example_sentences.english: That crime is unforgivable. (Nearly impossible to forgive)

example_sentences.japanese: あいつが言う事は信じがたいが、今は信じるしかない。
example_sentences.english: It is hard to believe what he says, but we have no choice but to trust him.

example_sentences.japanese: 景気が悪化しているため、今期の売上は期待しがたい。
example_sentences.english: Since the market has worsened, it will be hard to expect good sales in this period.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の声は聞こえにくい。
example_sentences.english: His voice is a bit tricky to hear. (It is kind of hard to hear his voice, based on my ability/feeling)

example_sentences.japanese: この話が信じがたいのは分かるが、信じてくれ！
example_sentences.english: I understand that this story is impossible to believe, but please believe me! (Believing something like this is not easy)

example_sentences.japanese: もう一つのアイデアもすてがたい。
example_sentences.english: The other idea is also hard to give up.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人の言っていることはしんじがたいですね。
example_sentences.english: It's hard to believe what that person is saying.

example_sentences.japanese: わすれがたい出来事に遭遇した。
example_sentences.english: I encountered an event that is nearly impossible to forget.

example_sentences.japanese: 皆からちかよりがたいってよく言われます。
example_sentences.english: I am often told that I am hard to approach.

example_sentences.japanese: 僕には理解しがたい考え方だ。
example_sentences.english: That approach is nearly impossible for me to understand.

example_sentences.japanese: その人はしんじがたいほど勇敢だった。
example_sentences.english: That person was brave to the point that was nearly impossible to believe.

example_sentences.japanese: もう会えないと思うと、さりがたい。
example_sentences.english: Knowing that I will never see you again, it is nearly impossible for me to leave.

example_sentences.japanese: 毎日たえがたい痛みに直面しているんです。
example_sentences.english: I face pain that is nearly impossible to bear every day.

example_sentences.japanese: あの言葉は僕にとっては、何物にもかえがたい贈り物だ。
example_sentences.english: I wouldn't exchange anything in the world for what was said (to me).

example_sentences.japanese: 耐えがたいことを耐え、忍びがたいことを忍び、天に向かう！
example_sentences.english: Enduring the unendurable and suffering the insufferable, reach to the heavens!

example_sentences.japanese: 皆はその映画が面白いって言っているけど、僕はその映画が成功するとはいいがたい。
example_sentences.english: Everyone is saying that that movie is interesting, but I find it hard to say that it will succeed. (Casual)

general_translation: I never dreamed, Never, No way, Don't tell me, You don't say
formation: まさか + Phrase
casual_structure: まさか + Phrase
explanation: A strong word which emphasizes the following phrase as being unbelievable, or shocking.

example_sentences.japanese: まさかこんなところで君に出会えるなんて！
example_sentences.english: I never dreamed I would meet you in a place like this!

example_sentences.japanese: まさかタナカ君もこのジムに通っているとは思っていなかったよ。
example_sentences.english: I never would have believed that Tanaka also goes to this gym.

example_sentences.japanese: まさか彼がキャプテンなんて。
example_sentences.english: Don't tell me that he is the captain!

example_sentences.japanese: まさかこんな大雪が降るなんて思わなかった。
example_sentences.english: I never dreamed it would snow this much.

example_sentences.japanese: まさか…あのこと本当に彼に話したの？
example_sentences.english: Don't tell me... Did you really tell him about that?

example_sentences.japanese: まさか…また財布忘れたわけじゃないよね。
example_sentences.english: Don't tell me... There's no way you forgot your wallet again... right?

example_sentences.japanese: まさか彼が犯人だなんて… ショックだ。
example_sentences.english: I never dreamed that he would be the criminal… I'm in shock.

example_sentences.japanese: まさかこの問題が出るなんて予想していませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I never would have thought that this problem (on a test) would come up.

example_sentences.japanese: まさかこんな賞をいただけるなんて、夢にも思いませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I never even dreamed that I would receive this prize.

example_sentences.japanese: まさかあの少女が金メダルを取るなんて、驚いたな。
example_sentences.english: I never dreamed that that little girl would win the gold medal. I'm amazed.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日すれ違ったの、まさか君じゃないよね？
example_sentences.english: Hey...don't tell me! It wasn't you who I passed on the street yesterday, was it?

example_sentences.japanese: まさか裁判員の通知が来るとは思っていませんでした。
example_sentences.english: I never dreamed that I would be summoned to jury duty.

example_sentences.japanese: まさか同じ日に同じ美容室で会うなんて、奇遇だね。
example_sentences.english: I never imagined that we would meet at the same beauty salon, on the same day. What a coincidence!

example_sentences.japanese: 最近羽振りがいいね。まさか…宝くじでも当たったの？
example_sentences.english: Recently, things really turned around for you. Hey...You don't say, did you win the lottery or something?

example_sentences.japanese: 全然待っていないですよ。僕も今まさに着いたところです。
example_sentences.english: I didn't wait at all. I actually just arrived now.

example_sentences.japanese: まさかリアがフランスに帰るって本当なの？
example_sentences.english: Is it actually true that Lia is going back to France?

grammar_point: 前者（ぜんしゃ）は～後者（こうしゃ）は
general_translation: The former ~ the latter, The first ~ the second
formation: 前者（ぜんしゃ）は + (Comment) 後者（こうしゃ）は + (Comment)
casual_structure: 前者（ぜんしゃ）は + (Comment) 後者（こうしゃ）は + (Comment)
explanation: A slightly formal construction used for indicating the former and latter cases in a description of (A).

example_sentences.japanese: ダンゴムシとワラジムシ、ぜんしゃは触ると丸まり、後者は触っても丸まらないという違いがあります。
example_sentences.english: If you want to know the difference between pillbugs and sowbugs, the former rolls into a ball if touched and the latter doesn't.

example_sentences.japanese: どの大学に行くか迷っています。ぜんしゃは家に近いが学費が高い、後者は家から遠いが学費が半分ぐらい安い。
example_sentences.english: I am undecided on which college to go to. The former is close to my house, but the tuition is expensive. The latter is far from my house but the tuition is almost half the price.

example_sentences.japanese: 地下鉄と新幹線、ぜんしゃは地下をゆっくりと走り、後者は速いスピードで地上を走る。
example_sentences.english: Subways and bullet trains. The former runs slowly underground, and the latter runs above ground at a high speed.

example_sentences.japanese: そうめんと冷麦、前者は細く、こうしゃは少し太い。
example_sentences.english: The difference between soumen and hiyamugi noodles is that the former is thin and the latter is thick.

example_sentences.japanese: 宿泊場所の候補が二つあります。前者は温泉があり、こうしゃはご飯がおいしいです。
example_sentences.english: There are two choices for places to stay. The first has hot springs, the second has delicious food.

example_sentences.japanese: 交通の札には切符と整理券の二つがあります。ぜんしゃは電車に乗るために必要なもので、後者はバスに乗るときに取るものです。
example_sentences.english: There are two types of transportation tickets: 'kippu' and 'seiriken'. The former is a thing needed for getting on a train, and the latter is taken when boarding on a bus.

example_sentences.japanese: どちらのパソコンがいいですか？ぜんしゃは安いが性能は一般向け、後者は高いが高性能。
example_sentences.english: Which laptop is better? The former is cheap, but the specifications are average. The latter is expensive, but has better performance.

example_sentences.japanese: どちらの家にするか迷っています。前者は駅から近いが家賃が高い、こうしゃは駅から遠いが家賃も安く部屋も広い。
example_sentences.english: I can't decide which house to rent. The former is close to the nearest station, but expensive. The latter is far from the station, but cheap and spacious.

example_sentences.japanese: どちらのコートがいいだろう…。ぜんしゃは相当温かいが春秋には着れない。後者はそこまで温かくないが春も秋も冬も着れる。
example_sentences.english: Which coat should I get... The former is very warm, but I cannot use it in spring and fall. The latter is not that warm, but I can wear it during spring, fall, and winter.

example_sentences.japanese: Ａ社とＢ社、どちらに就職するか迷っています。ぜんしゃは給料がよく、後者は環境がいいのです。
example_sentences.english: I am having trouble deciding between company A and company B. The former's pay is good and the latter has a good working environment.

example_sentences.japanese: 洋服と着物どちらがいいかな？ぜんしゃはすぐに準備できる。後者は準備が大変だが、きっと喜ばれる。
example_sentences.english: Which should I wear, western clothes or kimono? I can just throw on the former. The latter is hard (to put on), however it will make them happy for sure.

example_sentences.japanese: ラーメンと寿司どちらにしよう？前者は安くて気軽に食べられるが少し脂っこい。こうしゃは美味しいしいろいろなネタを楽しめるが少し高くつく。
example_sentences.english: Which should I get, ramen or sushi? The former is cheap but quite greasy. The latter is tasty, and you can enjoy many kinds, but gets a bit expensive.

example_sentences.japanese: 参考図書はこちらとこちらの二冊です。ぜんしゃは手に入れやすいのですが、後者は絶版で手に入れるのが難しいです。
example_sentences.english: As for reference books, there are these two. The former one is easy to obtain. However, the latter is out of print and, therefore, hard to find.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の好きな詩人はＡさんとＢさんです。前者はリズム感がよく、こうしゃは共感できる内容の詩が得意です。
example_sentences.english: My favorite poets are A-san and B-san. The former has a good sense of rhythm and the latter is good at poetry you can sympathize with.

example_sentences.japanese: こっちの車とこっちの車どっちを買おう。前者は安くて古くて、後者は高くて新しい。
example_sentences.english: This car and this car, which should I buy? The former is cheap and old, and the latter is expensive and new. (Natural)

example_sentences.japanese: 明日動物園に行くか今夜本を読むかで、迷っています。前者は動物がいて空いている、後者は寝る前にゆっくりできる。
example_sentences.english: I am undecided on whether to go to the zoo tomorrow, or to read a book tonight. The former has animals and isn't crowded, but the latter is relaxing before bed. (Unnatural)

general_translation: Accidentally, Unconsciously, Against one's better judgement
formation: つい + Phrase
casual_structure: つい + Phrase
explanation: A sentence starter indicating that (A) unfortunately happened due to a lapse in time, thought, or judgement.

example_sentences.japanese: つい楽な方に流されてしまう。
example_sentences.english: I always end up unconsciously taking the easy route.

example_sentences.japanese: ごめんタケシ君のクッキーが目の前にあったからつい食べてしまった。
example_sentences.english: Sorry Takeshi-kun, your cookie was right in front of me, so I absentmindedly ate it.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生に怒られると、つい笑っちゃうんだよね。
example_sentences.english: When I am being scolded by the teacher, I unconsciously laugh.

example_sentences.japanese: 運転中に携帯を使ったらだめなのは分かっているんだけど、メールが来るとつい携帯を見ちゃう。
example_sentences.english: I know that I shouldn't use my phone while driving, but when I get a text I unconsciously look at my phone.

example_sentences.japanese: 運転中、ついよそ見をしてしまう。
example_sentences.english: I sometimes accidentally look away while driving.

example_sentences.japanese: 運動を始めると、ついやり過ぎてしまう。
example_sentences.english: When I start doing exercises, I always end up accidentally overdoing it.

example_sentences.japanese: 笑ってはいけないのに、つい笑ってしまう。
example_sentences.english: Since I am not supposed to laugh, it feels like I might accidentally laugh.

example_sentences.japanese: 「つい食べ過ぎてしまう」なんて言い訳だ。
example_sentences.english: Saying things like: 'I unconsciously eat too much' is just an excuse.

example_sentences.japanese: １００円ショップに行くとつい買い過ぎてしまいます。
example_sentences.english: I always accidentally buy too much when I go to 100 yen stores.

example_sentences.japanese: ダイエット中なのに、ついアイスクリームを食べてしまう。
example_sentences.english: Against my better judgment, I eat ice cream while on a diet.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなにおもしろくない番組でもつい見てしまいます。
example_sentences.english: Against my better judgment, I end up watching TV programs that aren't even that interesting.

example_sentences.japanese: 思い通りにいかないとついイライラしてしまう。
example_sentences.english: Against my better judgment, I always get irritated when something doesn't go as I imagined.

example_sentences.japanese: 赤ちゃんを見るとつい頬が緩んでしまう。
example_sentences.english: I can't keep myself from unconsciously smiling whenever I see babies.

example_sentences.japanese: 失敗した時、つい人のせいにしたくなる。
example_sentences.english: Against my better judgment, I find myself wanting to blame someone else when I make a mistake.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事中でもついスマホをいじってしまう。
example_sentences.english: I always find myself unconsciously fiddling with my smartphone while I am working.

example_sentences.japanese: メガネがない。ついさっきまでここにあったと思うんだけど…。
example_sentences.english: I don't have my glasses. I think only a bit of time has lapsed since they were just here but...

example_sentences.japanese: 電車が遅れると、ついイライラしてしまう。
example_sentences.english: When the train is late, I'll get angry due to a lapse in judgment.

example_sentences.japanese: お腹が空いていなくても、目の前に食べ物があるとつい食べてしまう。
example_sentences.english: Even if I am not hungry, if there is food in front of me, I will eat it due to a lapse of forethought.

general_translation: Because of, Due to, Blame
formation: Verb + せいで［い］Adjective + せいで［な］Adjective + な + せいでNoun + の + せいで
casual_structure: Verb + せいで［い］Adjective + せいで［な］Adjective + な + せいでNoun + の + せいで
explanation: A phrase which puts the blame on (A), due to something its doings have caused.

example_sentences.japanese: トムは暑さのせいで気を失った。
example_sentences.english: Tom passed out because of the heat.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日夜遅くまで起きていたせいで寝坊した。
example_sentences.english: Because I stayed up late last night, I overslept today.

example_sentences.japanese: 外が寒いせいで風邪を引いた。
example_sentences.english: Because it is chilly outside, I caught a cold.

example_sentences.japanese: 犬の手術の事が心配なせいで今日は寝れなさそう。
example_sentences.english: Due to me being worried about my dog's surgery, it doesn't seem like I am going to be able to sleep.

example_sentences.japanese: 大雪のせいで道が渋滞してる。
example_sentences.english: Because of the heavy snow, the road is congested.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰のせいでもないと思います。
example_sentences.english: I don't think it's because of anyone. (no one to blame)

example_sentences.japanese: 湿気のせいでカビがひどい。
example_sentences.english: The mold is out of control because of the humidity.

example_sentences.japanese: ストレスのせいで病気になってしまった。
example_sentences.english: I became ill due to stress.

example_sentences.japanese: 物忘れがひどいのは、たぶん年のせいです。
example_sentences.english: You are quite forgetful probably because of your age.

example_sentences.japanese: 気分が悪くなったせいで、仕事を休んでしまった。
example_sentences.english: Because I wasn't feeling well, I took the day off.

example_sentences.japanese: 雨のせいでせっかくの遠足が中止になってしまった。
example_sentences.english: The long awaited trip was cancelled because of the rain.

example_sentences.japanese: トムがお皿を割ってしまったせいで、私は怪我をしてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I got injured because Tom broke a plate.

example_sentences.japanese: 寒いのは風のせいでしょう。そんなに気温は低くないですよ。
example_sentences.english: I think you feel cold due to the wind. The temperature is not that low.

example_sentences.japanese: （彼女が）変に見えるのはたぶん、髪型のせいですよ。
example_sentences.english: I think she looks strange because of her hairstyle.

example_sentences.japanese: 人間関係がうまくいかないのは、たぶんあなたの性格のせいでしょうね。
example_sentences.english: I think your relationships are not going smoothly because of your personality.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語能力試験に失敗したのは、たぶん彼氏のせいでしょう。
example_sentences.english: I think I failed the JLPT because of my boyfriend.

example_sentences.japanese: 遅刻したのは渋滞のせいだ！
example_sentences.english: Me being late is the traffic's doing!

example_sentences.japanese: 台風のせいでまた予定が変わったよ。
example_sentences.english: Due to the typhoon's doings, my plans have changed again.

general_translation: Even though, And yet, Despite
formation: Verb + くせに［い］Adjective + くせに［な］Adjective + な + くせにNoun + の + くせに
casual_structure: Verb + くせに［い］Adjective + くせに［な］Adjective + な + くせにNoun + の + くせに
explanation: A phrase that expresses contempt or criticism that despite (A), (B) did not occur.

example_sentences.japanese: 食べきれないくせにたくさん注文するのはやめてほしい。
example_sentences.english: Even though you cannot eat it all, you order a lot. I want you to stop (doing that). (despite)

example_sentences.japanese: さっき寝るって言ってたくせにまだ起きてるの？
example_sentences.english: Even though you said that you are going to sleep earlier, are you still up?

example_sentences.japanese: 若いくせに何ダラダラしているんだ。
example_sentences.english: Why are you working so sluggishly even though you are young?

example_sentences.japanese: 自分だって下手なくせに何偉そうに言ってるんだ。
example_sentences.english: Despite you also being no pro, why are you talking so high and mighty.

example_sentences.japanese: この子は犬のくせにニャーと鳴く。
example_sentences.english: Even though he is a dog, he meows.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日休んだくせに、なんで知ったかぶりするの？
example_sentences.english: Why do you pretend to know (what we are talking about) despite having the day off yesterday?

example_sentences.japanese: あの人は先輩のくせに、いつも僕におごらせようとする。
example_sentences.english: Despite being my senior, he/she always tries to make me pay.

example_sentences.japanese: 寒いくせに「寒くない」とやせ我慢するのはやめてください。
example_sentences.english: Please stop pretending like you're not cold even though you are. (despite)

example_sentences.japanese: 給料を沢山もらっているくせに、貯金がないらしい。
example_sentences.english: Despite getting paid a lot, I have heard that he has no savings.

example_sentences.japanese: 休みで時間があるくせに、家の手伝いを何もしない。
example_sentences.english: Even though it is your day off, you don't help at all with the housework.

example_sentences.japanese: 暑がりなくせに、あの人は毎日セーターを着て仕事に行く。
example_sentences.english: Despite hating the heat, that person wears a sweater to work everyday.

example_sentences.japanese: 何も知らないくせに、偉そうなことを言うのはやめてください。
example_sentences.english: Despite not knowing anything, you surely act high and mighty. Please just stop.

example_sentences.japanese: 「男のくせに泣くな」って言われるけど、たまには泣いていいと思う。
example_sentences.english: I am told 'you are a man, don't cry,' but I think that it is okay to cry from time to time. (Despite)

example_sentences.japanese: お金もないくせに、カードで気軽に高い物を買うのはやめた方がいいよ。
example_sentences.english: Even though you have no money, you freely use your credit card to buy expensive things. It would be better to stop (doing that). (despite)

example_sentences.japanese: 本当は行きたいくせに。素直に「行きたい」って言えばいいじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: You really want to go and yet... You should just honestly say 'I want to go,' right?

example_sentences.japanese: 見てたくせに、なんで「見てない」って嘘をつくの？ なぜ真実を話してくれないの？
example_sentences.english: Despite looking, why are you lying and saying 'I didn't.' Why won't you just tell me the truth?

general_translation: Apt to do, Tend to do, Prone to do
formation: Verb［stem］+ がちNoun + がちNoun (1) + がち + な(2) + Noun(1) Verb［stem］(2) の
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ がちNoun + がちNoun (1) + がち + な(2) + Noun(1) Verb［stem］(2) の
explanation: A word that expresses strong, often negative tendencies, or things that are prone to winning out in the end.

example_sentences.japanese: それは初心者にありがちのミスですね。
example_sentences.english: That is a mistake beginners tend to make.

example_sentences.japanese: ここに来るといつもパフェを頼みがちだけど、今日はパンケーキを頼む。
example_sentences.english: When I come here I always tend to order parfait, but today I am getting a pancake.

example_sentences.japanese: うちの子は病気がちなので、週に二、三日ぐらいは学校を休みます。
example_sentences.english: My child is prone to getting sick, so they usually miss two or three days of school each week.

example_sentences.japanese: サボりがちな人はだいたい成績が悪い。
example_sentences.english: People who tend to skip school usually have bad grades.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいつも遠慮がちだ。
example_sentences.english: He always tends to hold back.

example_sentences.japanese: 私の息子は病気がちだ。
example_sentences.english: My boy is apt to get sick.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人はすぐ、痩せることをあきらめがちだ。
example_sentences.english: That person is prone to quickly give up on losing weight.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は昔から遅刻しがちだ。
example_sentences.english: I have always been prone to being late.

example_sentences.japanese: 車ばかり乗っていると、運動不足になりがちだ。
example_sentences.english: If you are always riding around in a car, you tend to not get enough exercise.

example_sentences.japanese: さぼりがちな生徒を家まで迎えに行って、学校へ連れてきた。
example_sentences.english: I went to the house of the student who tends to skip school, and brought him back.

example_sentences.japanese: 私は元気だとおもわれがちですが、実は体が弱いんです。
example_sentences.english: I am prone to be considered energetic, but I actually have a delicate constitution.

example_sentences.japanese: 好きなことを先にして、すべきことを後回しにしがちで良くないな。
example_sentences.english: It's not good that I am prone to do things I want first and postpone important things I should be doing for later.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は最近学校をやすみがちなので心配です。
example_sentences.english: I am worried because recently he has developed a tendency to skip class.

example_sentences.japanese: 恥ずかしがり屋だからなのか、彼女はいつも伏し目がちです。
example_sentences.english: She always tends to drop her eyes, maybe it is because she is shy.

example_sentences.japanese: 学生たちはわすれがちだが、この問題は意外とテストに出る。
example_sentences.english: Students are apt to forget, but this problem will actually appear on the test.

example_sentences.japanese: 暇なときはテレビを見がちだけど、忙しい時には全然見ない。
example_sentences.english: Watching TV wins out when I am bored, but when I am busy I don't watch it at all.

example_sentences.japanese: 俺が回すと当たりがちだから、俺にやらせてみろ。
example_sentences.english: Hitting the jackpot wins out when I spin it, so why don't you let me do it.

example_sentences.japanese: 釣れないことはありがちだから、落ち込まなくてもいいよ。そういう日もあるさ。
example_sentences.english: Times that you cannot catch anything often win out, so don't be so upset. It happens.

general_translation: Looking, Feeling a little, Touch of, Tending to, Slightly
formation: Verb［stem］+ 気味（ぎみ）Noun + 気味（ぎみ）
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ 気味（ぎみ）Noun + 気味（ぎみ）
explanation: A slightly casual word that expresses weak feelings or tendencies, often based on sensation.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は風邪ぎみだと言った。
example_sentences.english: She said she was feeling a little sick.

example_sentences.japanese: タカシ君疲れぎみじゃない？ちゃんと休憩取った？
example_sentences.english: Takashi-kun, you look a bit tired, did you take a proper break?

example_sentences.japanese: 最近太りぎみだから、ダイエットしなきゃ。
example_sentences.english: I feel slightly fat, so I should go on a diet.

example_sentences.japanese: 今週は色々と忙しかったから疲れぎみだ。
example_sentences.english: Because I have been busy this week with various things, I am feeling a little tired.

example_sentences.japanese: 今朝は風邪ぎみだったので、学校を休んだ。
example_sentences.english: Because I felt a little sick this morning, I took a day off of school.

example_sentences.japanese: 現場の人がほとんどバテぎみだったので、作業を中断した。
example_sentences.english: Most of the people on the site seemed a little worn out, so we stopped work.

example_sentences.japanese: 電車が遅れぎみだから、待ち合わせ時間まで間に合わないかも。
example_sentences.english: Because the train seems a bit late, I might not be able to make it by our agreed time.

example_sentences.japanese: 風邪ぎみなのかな？身体がだるい。
example_sentences.english: I feel like I have a cold, my body feels heavy.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近、彼女はふとりぎみらしい。
example_sentences.english: I heard that lately, she is a bit plump.

example_sentences.japanese: 貧血ぎみなので、採血はやめておきましょう。
example_sentences.english: Since you are looking somewhat anemic, let's not draw any blood.

example_sentences.japanese: 暗いニュースばかりで食傷ぎみだ。
example_sentences.english: I feel sick listening to nothing but negative news.

example_sentences.japanese: 台風のせいで天気があれぎみだ。
example_sentences.english: The weather is a bit stormy due to the typhoon.

example_sentences.japanese: 暑すぎて夏バテぎみだ。
example_sentences.english: It's so hot that I am feeling a bit of heat fatigue.

example_sentences.japanese: あれからずっと経済が停滞ぎみだ。
example_sentences.english: The economy has been feeling a bit sluggish ever since (then).

example_sentences.japanese: 株価が下降ぎみなのを心配している。
example_sentences.english: I am concerned about the stock prices looking like they will go down.

example_sentences.japanese: 最近つかれぎみだから、少し休んだ方がいい。
example_sentences.english: You should rest for a bit, because recently you are looking a little tired.

example_sentences.japanese: プロジェクトがおくれぎみだから手伝ってもらえない？
example_sentences.english: We are a bit late with the project, so could you give us a hand?

example_sentences.japanese: 私は発表前に緊張ぎみで倒れてしまった。
example_sentences.english: I was feeling a little nervous before my presentation and fainted.

example_sentences.japanese: 調子はあがりぎみだから、次の試合はきっと大丈夫だと思います。
example_sentences.english: I think that you should be fine for the next game, because you are looking better.

general_translation: -ish, -like, Characteristic of, Typical of, Tendency to
formation: Verb［stem］+ っぽい［い］Adjective［い］+ っぽい［な］Adjective + っぽいNoun + っぽい
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ っぽい［い］Adjective［い］+ っぽい［な］Adjective + っぽいNoun + っぽい
polite_structure: Verb［stem］+ っぽい + です［い］Adjective［い］+ っぽい + です［な］Adjective + っぽい + ですNoun + っぽいです
explanation: A casual expression that shows that something appears or is acting in a way that is like (A), but not.

example_sentences.japanese: 寅さんはほれっぽく、飽きっぽい。
example_sentences.english: Tora-san has the tendency to fall in love, and also has the tendency to lose interest. (~ish)

example_sentences.japanese: 私は飽きっぽいから、何も続かない。
example_sentences.english: Because I have a tendency to get sick of things, I can't continue with anything.

example_sentences.japanese: 白っぽいやつをください。
example_sentences.english: Please give me the whiteish one.

example_sentences.japanese: タナカ君はファッション業界では有名っぽいよ！
example_sentences.english: Apparently Tanaka-kun is popular in the fashion industry!

example_sentences.japanese: 今の話は嘘っぽいけど本当の話なの。
example_sentences.english: The story I just told you sounds like a lie, but it is actually true.

example_sentences.japanese: なんかこの牛乳はみずっぽいな。
example_sentences.english: This milk is somewhat watery… (~ish)

example_sentences.japanese: おこりっぽい人はあまり好かれない。
example_sentences.english: People that have a tendency to get angry are not liked much. (~ish)

example_sentences.japanese: トムは記憶力がいいどころか、わすれっぽいよ。
example_sentences.english: Far from having a good memory, Tom is actually pretty forgetful. (~ish)

example_sentences.japanese: こういう時はくろっぽいスーツを着るべきか？
example_sentences.english: Should I wear a blackish suit for this occasion?

example_sentences.japanese: ねつっぽいな。インフルエンザじゃなければいいんだけど…。
example_sentences.english: I feel feverish. I hope I do not have the flu.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はこどもっぽい顔をしていますが、もうすぐ３０歳です。
example_sentences.english: She has a childish face, even though she is almost 30.

example_sentences.japanese: このカバンはやすっぽいけど、タグを見たら高かった。
example_sentences.english: This bag looks cheap, but I looked at the tag and it was expensive. (~ish)

example_sentences.japanese: 唐揚げはあぶらっぽくて、食べたいと思わない。
example_sentences.english: I don't even think about wanting to eat deep-fried chicken because it looks too greasy. (~ish)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はあきっぽいから、趣味を始めてもすぐにやめてしまう。
example_sentences.english: Because he has tendency to lose interest and give up, he quits soon after starting a new hobby. (~ish)

example_sentences.japanese: 試合中、あらっぽくプレーして、審判に注意された。
example_sentences.english: I had been playing roughly in the match, and was given a warning by the referee. (~ish)

example_sentences.japanese: 彼の話はりくつっぽいから、あまり話をしたくはない。
example_sentences.english: Because he is argumentative, I don't really like talking with him. (~ish)

example_sentences.japanese: 昔は紫っぽかったのに今はなぜか赤っぽい。
example_sentences.english: Back in the day, it was purpleish, but now for some reason it is reddish.

example_sentences.japanese: この靴なんか安っぽくない？
example_sentences.english: Don't these shoes look cheapish?

general_translation: Leaving something in a certain state, Left as is, Keep on -ing
formation: Verb［stem］+ っぱなし
casual_structure: Verb［stem］+ っぱなし
explanation: A grammar point that expresses something left or released in an ongoing state, often negatively.

example_sentences.japanese: 誰かがそのドアをあけっぱなしにした。
example_sentences.english: Someone left the door open.

example_sentences.japanese: また電気点けっぱなしじゃん！何回言えば消してくれるの？
example_sentences.english: You left the light on again! How many times do I have to tell you to turn it off?

example_sentences.japanese: 冷蔵庫を開けっぱなしにしないでください。
example_sentences.english: Please don't leave the refrigerator open.

example_sentences.japanese: 歯を磨いている間、水を出しっぱなしにしていたら、お母さんに怒られた。
example_sentences.english: Because I left the water on while I was brushing my teeth, my mother scolded me.

example_sentences.japanese: ライトをつけっぱなしにしないで。
example_sentences.english: Don't leave the light on.

example_sentences.japanese: 電話がなりっぱなしだけど…大丈夫？
example_sentences.english: Your phone keeps ringing... Is that not a problem?

example_sentences.japanese: いつもあけっぱなしで、ちゃんと閉めてよね。
example_sentences.english: You always leave it open, make sure you close it ok?

example_sentences.japanese: 水をだしっぱなしにするのはやめてください。
example_sentences.english: Please stop leaving the water on.

example_sentences.japanese: エアコンをつけっぱなしで寝てしまった。
example_sentences.english: I fell asleep with the air conditioner left on.

example_sentences.japanese: カバンをおきっぱなしでみんなどこに行ったの？
example_sentences.english: Where did everyone go with their bags left here?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいつも仕事中はうごきっぱなしだ。
example_sentences.english: He always keeps moving while he is working.

example_sentences.japanese: 一日中パソコンの前ですわりっぱなしはやめて。
example_sentences.english: Please stop sitting in front of the computer all day.

example_sentences.japanese: 渋滞のせいで、１０分間とまりっぱなしだった。
example_sentences.english: Because of the traffic, I was at a standstill for ten minutes.

example_sentences.japanese: ３時間もたちっぱなしで、足が棒になってしまいました。
example_sentences.english: I kept standing for 3 hours straight, and my legs became stiff.

example_sentences.japanese: 洗濯物をほしっぱなしで出てきたのに、雨が降ってきた。
example_sentences.english: I left the laundry to dry when I left and now it's starting to rain.

example_sentences.japanese: 勝ちっぱなしだとつまらないね、たまには負けを味わいたい。
example_sentences.english: Don't you think it is boring to keep winning? I want to taste defeat sometimes. (I want to lose sometimes)

example_sentences.japanese: 秋の間は窓を開けっぱなしにして寝ています。
example_sentences.english: During autumn, I sleep with the windows left open.

general_translation: Expressly, Especially, Go out of one's way, Take the trouble to
formation: わざわざ + Phrase
casual_structure: わざわざ + Phrase
explanation: A phrase highlighting that someone has gone out of their way to do (A), or expressly done (A). Often with a positive nuance.

example_sentences.japanese: わざわざここまで働きに来ているんですね。
example_sentences.english: I see you came here expressly to work.

example_sentences.japanese: わざわざ私が好きな饅頭を買いに行ってくれたの？ありがとう！
example_sentences.english: You went out of your way to buy me my favorite manju? Thank you!

example_sentences.japanese: わざわざ会社に行って仕事しなきゃいけない理由がわからない、別に家でも出来るのに。
example_sentences.english: I don't understand the reason to go out of my way to go into an office to work, I can  work from home.

example_sentences.japanese: わざわざここまで来てくれてありがとうございます。
example_sentences.english: Thank you very much for going out of your way to come here. (Positive)

example_sentences.japanese: 何でわざわざそういうひどいこと言うの？
example_sentences.english: Why do you go out of your way to say something so mean? (Negative)

example_sentences.japanese: わざわざ批判しなくてもいいのに。
example_sentences.english: You didn't have to go out of your way to criticize.

example_sentences.japanese: わざわざ独りで行くんですか？
example_sentences.english: You will go out of your way just to go by yourself?

example_sentences.japanese: わざわざ傘を返しに来てくれたの？
example_sentences.english: Did you come all the way here expressly to return the umbrella?

example_sentences.japanese: わざわざ自慢しなくてもいいじゃないか。
example_sentences.english: You don't have to go out of your way to boast about it, do you?

example_sentences.japanese: わざわざ秘密にするほどのこと？
example_sentences.english: Is that something you have to go out of your way to keep secret?

example_sentences.japanese: こんな遠くまでわざわざ来てくださってありがとうございます。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for going out of your way to come so far.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなくだらない話、わざわざメールで伝えなくてもいいよ。
example_sentences.english: You don't have to expressly write to me about such a trivial topic.

example_sentences.japanese: わざわざ筆で書くんですか？ペンではだめですか？
example_sentences.english: You are going to go out of your way to write with a brush? Won't a pen suffice?

example_sentences.japanese: なんでわざわざ人の嫌がることをするの？
example_sentences.english: Why do you go out of your way to do things everyone hates?

example_sentences.japanese: わざわざ予約してくれたんですね。助かりました。
example_sentences.english: You went out of your way to make an appointment for me. It was really helpful.
