example_sentences.japanese: わざわざ会いに来てくれたのにごめんなさい。夫はインフルエンザなんです。
example_sentences.english: I am sorry that you came all the way here expressly to meet him. However, my husband has the flu.

example_sentences.japanese: わざと押したでしょ？あんた最低。
example_sentences.english: You pushed me on purpose, didn't you? You are the worst.

example_sentences.japanese: 何でわざわざ邪魔しに来るの？
example_sentences.english: Why do you come here especially to bother me?

general_translation: (What) the heck?, (Who) in the world?, (Where) on earth?, (How many) f*ing...
formation: いったい + Question Word + Phrase
casual_structure: いったい + Question Word + Phrase
explanation: An exclamation which shows the speaker's surprise, in a similar way to what the heck in English. Primarily used to ask questions.

example_sentences.japanese: あの人はいったい誰なのだろう…
example_sentences.english: Who the heck is that person?

example_sentences.japanese: いったいここで何が起きたんだ！
example_sentences.english: What the heck happened here?

example_sentences.japanese: これはいったいどういうことだ。
example_sentences.english: What is the meaning of this?

example_sentences.japanese: いったいなんでこんな事になったの？
example_sentences.english: Explain to me in a way that makes sense, why something like this happened?

example_sentences.japanese: いったいなんであんな奴と付き合おうと思ったの？
example_sentences.english: In a way that I can understand, why did you think of dating someone like him?

example_sentences.japanese: いったいいつ、掃除をする暇があるというんだ。
example_sentences.english: When the heck do I have time to clean?

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はいったいどういうつもりなんだ。
example_sentences.english: What on earth does he intend to do?

example_sentences.japanese: あの人はいったい何歳なんだろう。
example_sentences.english: How freaking old is that person?

example_sentences.japanese: 僕たちの未来はいったいどうなるんだろう…
example_sentences.english: What on earth will become of us in the future?

example_sentences.japanese: いったい誰がそんなひどいことを言ったんですか？
example_sentences.english: Who the heck said such a horrible thing?

example_sentences.japanese: いったいいつになったら外出の準備ができるんだろう。
example_sentences.english: When on earth are you going to be ready to go out?

example_sentences.japanese: 今年納める税金はいったいいくらになるかしら。
example_sentences.english: I wonder how much freaking tax I will pay this year.

example_sentences.japanese: この牧場にはいったい何頭の牛がいるかな。
example_sentences.english: I wonder how many freaking cows there are on this farm.

example_sentences.japanese: この気持ちの悪い生き物はいったい何ですか？
example_sentences.english: What on earth is this ugly creature?

example_sentences.japanese: いったいいくつ餅を食べれば気がすむの？食べ過ぎだよ。
example_sentences.english: How much freaking mochi will you eat before feeling satisfied? You eat too much...

example_sentences.japanese: こんな素晴らしい絵を描くなんて… 彼はいったい何者なんだ！？
example_sentences.english: To think that he drew such an amazing picture... Who the heck is he?

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカ人は一体に親切です。
example_sentences.english: Americans are generally polite.

general_translation: With trouble, At great pains, Take the trouble, Might as well..., Rare/long-awaited occasion
formation: せっかく + Phraseせっかく + の + Noun (of Event)
casual_structure: せっかく + Phraseせっかく + の + Noun (of Event)
explanation: An expression which shows that (A) has been long awaited, or arrived at after great mental or physical effort.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかくこの旅行の準備してきたのに....
example_sentences.english: Despite going through all the trouble to finish preparations for the trip...

example_sentences.japanese: せっかく君が欲しかった靴を買ってあげたのに友達にあげたの？最悪。
example_sentences.english: I took great trouble to get you the shoes that you wanted, but you gave them to your friend? How inconsiderate.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかく休みを取ったのに雨が降ったから予定が台無しだ。
example_sentences.english: I went through the trouble to get a day off, but it rained, so my plans were ruined.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかくの誕生日会を台無しにしてごめんなさい。
example_sentences.english: Sorry for ruining your long awaited birthday party.

example_sentences.japanese: 台風のせいで、せっかくの休暇が中止になった。
example_sentences.english: Due to the typhoon, my long awaited vacation has been canceled.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかくの友達との遠足だから、たくさん遊びたい。
example_sentences.english: Since this trip with friends is a rare occasion, I want to have a lot of fun.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかくのデートが風邪でつぶれた。ちょっと残念だよ。
example_sentences.english: A long-awaited date was spoiled because I caught a cold. It is a little disappointing.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかく大学を卒業したんだから、いい会社で働くつもりだ。
example_sentences.english: Because I graduated university at great pains, I plan to make use of it by finding a good job.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかく高性能のコンピューターを買ったんだから、新しいゲームをしようと思う。
example_sentences.english: Since I went through great pains to purchase a high-end computer, I am going to make use of it by playing new games.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかくの花見シーズンですが今日は雨が降りそうです。とても悲しいです。
example_sentences.english: The long-awaited flower viewing season is here, but it looks like it will rain. I am really sad.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかく運動するなら、ウォーミングアップした方が良い。しなければケガの元になる。
example_sentences.english: If you put efforts into exercising, you should warm up. If you don't, it might be the source of an injury.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかく異世界に転移したのに、チートをもらうどころか、ただの自動販売機になった。
example_sentences.english: Even though I went through the trouble of being transported to a parallel universe, instead of getting cool powers, I became a simple vending machine.

example_sentences.japanese: 妻のためにせっかく家を構築したけど、離婚した。努力はみんな無駄だった。落ち込んでいる。
example_sentences.english: Even though I went through great pains to build a house for my wife, we divorced. All of my efforts were in vain. I feel down.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかく寿司屋で日本語で注文しようと意気込んで入ったのに、寿司屋さんは英語がぺらぺらだったから、ちょっとがっかりした。
example_sentences.english: Although I was enthusiastic about having the rare chance of ordering in Japanese at a sushi restaurant, the clerk spoke fluent English, so I got a bit let down.

example_sentences.japanese: せっかく日本語を毎日数時間勉強したのに、日本語能力試験に落ちたかと心配して落ち込んだ。
example_sentences.english: I took great trouble to study Japanese for hours each day, but I got worried about whether I had passed the JLPT or not, and got depressed.

example_sentences.japanese: ウォーミングアップしないで運動するとケガの元になるかもしれない。せっかく運動してもケガをしては意味がない。
example_sentences.english: If you exercise without warming up, you might get injured. Even if you put great efforts into exercising, what's the point if you get injured?

general_translation: What is…again?, Was it... that... ?, Did you say...?
formation: Verb［た］+ っけ Verb［る］+ ん(1)だ +  っけ［い］Adjective［た］+ っけ ［な］Adjective + だった(2) + っけ Noun + だった(2) + っけ(1) の(2) だ
casual_structure: Verb［た］+ っけ Verb［る］+ ん(1)だ +  っけ［い］Adjective［た］+ っけ ［な］Adjective + だった(2) + っけ Noun + だった(2) + っけ(1) の(2) だ
explanation: A short sound often used to indicate something the speaker should know, but has been forgotten.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなもの家にあったっけ？
example_sentences.english: Was it that you had something like that at home?

example_sentences.japanese: 今日の朝は朝ご飯を食べたっけ。
example_sentences.english: Did I eat breakfast this morning?

example_sentences.japanese: あれ、テイラーの車って青かったっけ。
example_sentences.english: Um, Taylor, was your car blue, again?

example_sentences.japanese: 土曜日って暇だっけ。
example_sentences.english: Was I free on Saturday, again?

example_sentences.japanese: あの人誰だっけ。やばい、思い出せない。
example_sentences.english: Who was that again? Shoot, I can't remember.

example_sentences.japanese: クミコって納豆食べれるんだっけ。
example_sentences.english: Kumiko, were you able to eat natto again?

example_sentences.japanese: レポートの修正は君がやってるんだっけ。
example_sentences.english: You are the one editing the paper, right?

example_sentences.japanese: 明日って晴れるんだっけ？
example_sentences.english: Was it that it will be sunny tomorrow?

example_sentences.japanese: もうすぐ梅雨も終わりだっけ？
example_sentences.english: Was it that the rainy season will be over soon?

example_sentences.japanese: この資料渡したっけ？
example_sentences.english: Did I pass you this document? (was it that...?)

example_sentences.japanese: 一昨日もラーメン食べたっけ？
example_sentences.english: Did we have ramen the day before yesterday too? (was it that...?)

example_sentences.japanese: 納豆を食べられないんだっけ？
example_sentences.english: Was it that you can't eat natto?

example_sentences.japanese: まだ雪を見たことないんだっけ？
example_sentences.english: Did you say that you had never seen snow before?

example_sentences.japanese: トムの友達って、会ったことあったっけ？
example_sentences.english: Did you say that you had met Tom's friend?

example_sentences.japanese: 沖縄には行ったことないんだっけ？
example_sentences.english: Did you say that you had never been to Okinawa?

example_sentences.japanese: この学校に入るのがずっと夢だったんだっけ？
example_sentences.english: Did you say that you had been wanting to get in this school?

example_sentences.japanese: 日本語の勉強はいつから始めたんだっけ？
example_sentences.english: When did you say that you started studying Japanese?

example_sentences.japanese: 日本の文化について発表をしたのは誰だったっけ？
example_sentences.english: Who was it that gave the talk about Japanese culture?

example_sentences.japanese: トムって日本語話せるっけ。
example_sentences.english: Tom, were you able to speak Japanese again?

example_sentences.japanese: この道って通れるっけ。
example_sentences.english: Were we able to take this road again?

example_sentences.japanese: あそこのレストランって犬を連れていけるっけ。
example_sentences.english: Do you remember if we could take our dogs to that restaurant over there? (Asking another)

example_sentences.japanese: あれ、カギ掛けたっけ。
example_sentences.english: Umm, did I lock the door? (Asking oneself)

general_translation: Instead of,  In place of, In exchange for
formation: Verb + 代（か）わりに［い］Adjective + 代（か）わりに［な］Adjective + な + 代（か）わりにNoun + の + 代（か）わりに
casual_structure: Verb + 代（か）わりに［い］Adjective + 代（か）わりに［な］Adjective + な + 代（か）わりにNoun + の + 代（か）わりに
explanation: A phrase that shows that (B) is acting as a substitute or replacement for (A).

example_sentences.japanese: バターのかわりにマーガリンを使っています。
example_sentences.english: I am using margarine instead of butter.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事は大変なかわりに楽しい。
example_sentences.english: Work is fun, in exchange for it being difficult.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のかわりにやってください。
example_sentences.english: Can you do it in my place?

example_sentences.japanese: 俺が社長に電話するかわりに、お前はお客さんに電話をしておいて。
example_sentences.english: In exchange for me calling the boss, can you call the client in advance?

example_sentences.japanese: あのプールは古いかわりに安い。
example_sentences.english: That pool is cheap, to substitute for it being old.

example_sentences.japanese: コーヒーのかわりに紅茶では駄目ですか？
example_sentences.english: Is tea in place of coffee not good enough?

example_sentences.japanese: 玉ねぎのかわりに長ねぎを使おう。
example_sentences.english: Let's use green onions in place of ordinary onions.

example_sentences.japanese: 電話のかわりに、メールを送った。
example_sentences.english: Instead of calling, I sent him an email.

example_sentences.japanese: 私のかわりにこの問題を解いてください。
example_sentences.english: Please solve this question instead of me.

example_sentences.japanese: 筆記テストのかわりに面接試験がある。
example_sentences.english: I have an oral examination instead of a written test.

example_sentences.japanese: 君のかわりに僕がやってみるけど、うまくできる自信がない。
example_sentences.english: I'll try doing it instead of you, but I'm not confident I can do it well.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼が遅刻をしてしまったので、彼のかわりに発表した。
example_sentences.english: Since he was late, I presented instead of him.

example_sentences.japanese: 先生のかわりに勉強を教えてみたけど、うまく教えられなかった。
example_sentences.english: I tried teaching instead of my teacher, but I was unable to teach well.

example_sentences.japanese: この靴なら長靴のかわりになるね。ゴ*テックスだから雨でも大丈夫そうだ。
example_sentences.english: You can wear these shoes in place of boots. Because they are go*-tex, you can even use them in rain.

example_sentences.japanese: バナナが嫌いで食べれないからビタミンが取れない。バナナのかわりに何を食べたらいい？
example_sentences.english: I don't like bananas so I don't eat them and can't get those vitamins. What should I eat in place of a banana?

example_sentences.japanese: 先生が風邪をひいて休んだので、かわりに校長先生が授業をした。
example_sentences.english: Because the teacher caught a cold and took the day off, the principal taught the class in his place.

example_sentences.japanese: かわりに、もっといい方法を教えてあげるよ。
example_sentences.english: Rather than that, I'll teach you a better way!

example_sentences.japanese: かわりにこれを持って行って。
example_sentences.english: Instead of that, can you go take this?

general_translation: In place of, On behalf of, To succeed
formation: Noun + に代（か）わって(1)(1) に代（か）わり
casual_structure: Noun + に代（か）わって(1)(1) に代（か）わり
explanation: An expression used to show when (B) will substitute for (A) in some specific role, often in succession.

example_sentences.japanese: 月にかわってお仕置きよ。
example_sentences.english: On behalf of the moon, I will punish you!

example_sentences.japanese: 妹にかわって、私が買い物に行くことに決まった。
example_sentences.english: It has been decided that I am going to go shopping in place of my sister.

example_sentences.japanese: 私が彼女にかわって会議に出ます。
example_sentences.english: I will be attending the meeting in place of her.

example_sentences.japanese: タナカさんにかわり、今日は私があなたたちの担当をします。
example_sentences.english: In place of Tanaka-san, today, I am going to be in charge of you guys.

example_sentences.japanese: 世界中ではファックスにかわりメールが主流になったが、日本ではまだファックスしか使わないところが多い。
example_sentences.english: All around the world, fax has been replaced by email as the main form of communication, but there still are places in Japan that only use fax.

example_sentences.japanese: 私にかわって説明をしてくれてありがとう。
example_sentences.english: Thank you for explaining it on my behalf.

example_sentences.japanese: 私にかわって、あなたが発表をすることになった。
example_sentences.english: It has been decided that you will do the presentation instead of me.

example_sentences.japanese: 機長にかわって副操縦士が操縦した。
example_sentences.english: The co-pilot flew on behalf of the captain (of the aircraft).

example_sentences.japanese: 社長にかわって、山田さんが乾杯の挨拶をします。
example_sentences.english: On behalf of the CEO, Mr. Yamada will do the toast.

example_sentences.japanese: 欠席の課長にかわって私が会議に参加しました。
example_sentences.english: I attended on behalf of the absent section manager.

example_sentences.japanese: 西暦２０００年始めにＦＡＸにかわりメールが主流になった。
example_sentences.english: Starting in the 2000s, email has replaced fax as a mainstream form of communication.

example_sentences.japanese: 先代にかわって後を継いだ社長が、なかなかのやり手だ。
example_sentences.english: The president who took over the company in place of the previous owner is quite capable.

example_sentences.japanese: 弁護士：「依頼人にかわって手続きを進めます。」
example_sentences.english: Lawyer: 'I will proceed with the formalities on behalf of my client.'

example_sentences.japanese: 最近は新聞にかわりインターネットが、メインの情報源として使われている。
example_sentences.english: Nowadays the internet is used in place of newspapers as a main source of information.

example_sentences.japanese: 公式戦の座席は転売防止のため、直接販売にかわり抽選で配布することになっている。
example_sentences.english: In order to prevent resale, it has been decided that in place of direct distribution, seats for official matches will be distributed by a lottery.

example_sentences.japanese: 父にかわってお礼を申し上げます。
example_sentences.english: I would like to express to you my deepest gratitude on behalf of my father.

example_sentences.japanese: 今日は社長にかわって、私が会議を進めます。
example_sentences.english: Today, I will take charge of the meeting in place of the CEO.

example_sentences.japanese: 父親にかわって、息子が王になった。
example_sentences.english: Replacing his father, the son became king.

general_translation: Far from, Anything but
formation: Verb(1) + どころか［い］Adjective + どころか［な］Adjective + な + どころかNoun + どころか(1)Verb［ない］
casual_structure: Verb(1) + どころか［い］Adjective + どころか［な］Adjective + な + どころかNoun + どころか(1)Verb［ない］
explanation: A structure that highlights that the place or situation of (A) is far from the actual situation.

example_sentences.japanese: そのケーキは甘いどころか、酸っぱかった。
example_sentences.english: Far from being sweet, that cake was sour.

example_sentences.japanese: このカレーは甘いどころか、辛かった。
example_sentences.english: Far from being sweet, this curry was spicy.

example_sentences.japanese: 北海道は寒いどころか、暑かった。
example_sentences.english: Far from being cold, Hokkaido was hot.

example_sentences.japanese: 昨日の仕事は楽などころか、めちゃくちゃ大変だったよ。
example_sentences.english: Far from being easy, work yesterday was hectic.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女は酎ハイどころかビールも飲まない。
example_sentences.english: Let alone Chuhai, she doesn't even drink beer.

example_sentences.japanese: 吹雪はやむどころか、かえってひどくなっている。
example_sentences.english: Far from stopping, the storm instead got stronger.

example_sentences.japanese: 謙虚になるどころかかえって傲慢になっている。
example_sentences.english: Far from being humble, he is arrogant.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は休むどころか、全力を出し切った。
example_sentences.english: Far from taking a break, he gave everything he had.

example_sentences.japanese: 親切にしようとしたけど、感謝されるどころか、叱られた。
example_sentences.english: Even though I tried to be nice to them, far from being thanked, I was scolded.

example_sentences.japanese: 英語どころか日本語もちゃんと喋れていない気がする。
example_sentences.english: Far from speaking English, I feel that I can't even properly speak in Japanese.

example_sentences.japanese: 手伝ってくれるどころか、僕の方が手伝うことになってしまった！
example_sentences.english: Far from you helping me, it is rather me who ended up helping you!

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はヨーロッパまで行くどころか、玄関から一歩も出ていない。
example_sentences.english: Far from going to Europe, he hasn't even taken a step outside.

example_sentences.japanese: 健康にいいものでも、食べすぎたら健康になるどころか病気になりますよ。
example_sentences.english: Eating in excess even if it's healthy food is not good for you. Far from that, it will make you ill!

example_sentences.japanese: こんなに勉強しているのに、成績は良くなるどころか悪くなっている。
example_sentences.english: Despite studying so much, far from getting better, my grades got worse.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼は役に立つどころか作業の邪魔をしている。
example_sentences.english: Far from being helpful, he is disturbing the work.

example_sentences.japanese: 体調が悪いのに、休むどころかいつもよりたくさん仕事をしているから心配です。
example_sentences.english: I am worried about them, because even though they are in poor physical health, far from resting, they are working even more.

example_sentences.japanese: そんなにゆっくりしているどころか。
example_sentences.english: This is not the time to be even remotely that relaxed!

example_sentences.japanese: 俺がやるどころか？そんなことをやるのは弟しかいないだろ！
example_sentences.english: Do you honestly think I would do such a thing? My brother is the only person who would do that.

grammar_point: と言（い）う理由（りゆう）で
general_translation: For (that) reason; on the grounds of (that), With the reasoning, Under the pretext of, Due to
formation: (Reason) + という理由（りゆう）で + Phrase(Reason)。 そういう理由（りゆう）で + Phrase
casual_structure: (Reason) + という理由（りゆう）で + Phrase(Reason)。 そういう理由（りゆう）で + Phrase
explanation: A structure used for giving reasons about the thing which is called (A).

example_sentences.japanese: ストアのルールを破ったというりゆうで五つのアプリが削除されました。
example_sentences.english: 5 apps were removed on the grounds of breaking the store rules.

example_sentences.japanese: コストコは安く沢山買い物が出来るというりゆうで人気がある。
example_sentences.english: At Costco, you can shop for many things at a cheap price. For that reason it is popular.

example_sentences.japanese: 大変だというりゆうで彼は仕事を辞めた。
example_sentences.english: Being that his job was a hassle, he resigned.

example_sentences.japanese: 仕事がとても大変だった。そういうりゆうで、今日はゆっくりしたい。
example_sentences.english: Work was really rough. For that reason, I want to take it easy today.

example_sentences.japanese: ゴルゴさんはプロフェッショナルです。そういうりゆうで彼を雇う予定です。
example_sentences.english: Golgo-san is a professional. For that reason, I plan to hire him.

example_sentences.japanese: 「高すぎるなぁ」というりゆうで課長は提案に反対した。
example_sentences.english: With the reasoning: 'it is too expensive,' the section manager opposed the proposition.

example_sentences.japanese: やまださんは年寄りだというりゆうで、詐欺師によってターゲットによくされている。
example_sentences.english: Mr. Yamada is often targeted by con-artists on the grounds that he is elderly.

example_sentences.japanese: メアリーさんは仕事中に映画を見がちというりゆうで首になるかもしれない。
example_sentences.english: Mary might be fired on the grounds of her having the tendency to watch movies while at work.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼はともこさんが自分の妻を殺したというりゆうでともこさんを訴えた。
example_sentences.english: On the grounds of Tomoko-san killing his wife, he is taking Tomoko-san to court.

example_sentences.japanese: ネットショッピングはコストがより安いというりゆうで人気を集めています。
example_sentences.english: Internet shopping is gaining popularity with the reason being that it is cheaper.

example_sentences.japanese: 彼女はサガラさんを殺そうとしたというりゆうで２５年の懲役に処せられたのです。
example_sentences.english: She was sentenced to 25 years in prison on the grounds that she attempted to kill Mr. Sagara.

example_sentences.japanese: アグネスは看護師になりたいというりゆうでプログラミングの職を捨てて大学に入った。
example_sentences.english: Agnes quit her programming job and went to university with the reason being that she wanted to become a nurse.

example_sentences.japanese: 「失敗するかもしれない」というりゆうだけでせっかくのチャンスを無駄にする人が多い。
example_sentences.english: There are numerous people wasting precious opportunities just because: 'it might end in failure.'

example_sentences.japanese: 一方で、「冬にはお客様が来ないから」というりゆうで、その時期は、お店がほとんど閉まっている。
example_sentences.english: On the other hand, with the reason being that ' since customers do not come during the winter', most of the shops are closed in that period.

example_sentences.japanese: 安くて美味しいという理由で、この店の前にはいつも行列ができています。
example_sentences.english: Being that this place is cheap and delicious, they always have a long line in front of the store.

example_sentences.japanese: 一人で行きたくないという訳では無いです。一人で行くのは危ないと言いたいのです。
example_sentences.english: It is not so that I don't want to go alone. I am saying that it is dangerous to go alone.

example_sentences.japanese: という理由で、この企画はキャンセルすることにします。
example_sentences.english: For that reason, we are going to cancel this plan. (Unnatural)

example_sentences.japanese: というわけで、この企画はキャンセルすることにします。
example_sentences.english: Well with that, we will decide on canceling this plan. (Natural)

general_translation: It is (has been), Have/has become, Happen to be, Has been established
formation: ［な］Adjective + となっているNoun + となっている
casual_structure: ［な］Adjective + となっているNoun + となっている
polite_structure: ［な］Adjective + となっていますNoun + となっています
explanation: An expression highlighting that in general, (A) happens to be (B), or has been established as (B).

example_sentences.japanese: 納期限は４月３０日までとなっています。
example_sentences.english: The due date of the tax payment has been established as April 30th.

example_sentences.japanese: 日本ではドラッグは法律上、違法となっている。
example_sentences.english: In Japan, it has been established that drugs are illegal, by law.

example_sentences.japanese: このプールでは、飛び込みが禁止となっている。
example_sentences.english: At this pool, it happens to be that jumping in is not allowed.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の時代にはインターネットは必要となっている。
example_sentences.english: It is now that the internet is necessary in the present age.

example_sentences.japanese: この高校ではアルバイトが禁止となっている。
example_sentences.english: It is now that working part-time at this school is prohibited.

example_sentences.japanese: 鬼滅の刃は非常に人気となっている。
example_sentences.english: It happens to be that Demon Slayer is very popular.

example_sentences.japanese: アメリカをはじめとして、電気は主要な光源となっている。
example_sentences.english: Starting with the USA, electricity has become the main source of light.

example_sentences.japanese: 中国では男性の女性に対する割合は１１８対１００となっている。
example_sentences.english: The proportion of men to women in China happens to be 118 to 100.

example_sentences.japanese: フランツ・フェルディナント大公の暗殺が開戦の原因の一つとなっている。
example_sentences.english: The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand has been established as one of the causes of war.

example_sentences.japanese: それが標準となっていて他の方法はほとんど使用されない。
example_sentences.english: That has become a standard, and other methods are hardly used.

example_sentences.japanese: 令和という新たな年号は２０１９年５月１日からとなっている。
example_sentences.english: It has been established that the new era called 'Reiwa' will begin on May 1st of 2019.

example_sentences.japanese: その古い言語が忘れられたというよりむしろ単に科学の言語となっている。
example_sentences.english: That ancient language, rather than being forgotten, simply has become the language of science.

example_sentences.japanese: この新しいスマートフォンの販売価格は８３万円からとなっており、まもなく予約受注も始まります。
example_sentences.english: ¥830,000 has been established as the starting price for this new smartphone and pre-orders will begin soon.

example_sentences.japanese: 地球温暖化は国際的に大きな問題となっているという事を指摘したいと思います。
example_sentences.english: I would like to point out that global warming has become a global issue.

example_sentences.japanese: いくつかの州では２１才未満の子供たちや若者がアルコールを消費することは違法となっている。
example_sentences.english: In some states, it has been established that the consumption of alcohol by children and young adults under 21 is illegal.

example_sentences.japanese: １９世紀に食事前に手を洗ったり衣類や寝具を洗濯するという衛生的な習慣は、一般常識となっている。
example_sentences.english: 19th Century hygienic habits like washing hands before meals and cleaning things like clothes and bedding, have become common sense. (is currently established as...)

example_sentences.japanese: 匿名の厚生省幹部によると政府は現在６５歳からとなっている公的年金の支給の定年を７０歳に引き上げる意向だということだ。
example_sentences.english: According to an anonymous, high-ranking Ministry of Health official, the government intends to raise the age of eligibility for a public pension, that has (just) been established as 65 years old, to 70 years old.

example_sentences.japanese: 今の時代にはインターネットは必要になっている。
example_sentences.english: It is now that the internet is becoming necessary in the present age.

example_sentences.japanese: このイベントは来月５日からとなっており、明日から前売り券を買うことができる。
example_sentences.english: It is now that next month's event from the 5th has pre-order tickets that are purchasable from tomorrow.

general_translation: Influence, Impact, Control
formation: 左右（さゆう） + する(1)左右（さゆう） + する(1) + Noun(1) される
casual_structure: 左右（さゆう） + する(1)左右（さゆう） + する(1) + Noun(1) される
polite_structure: 左右（さゆう） + します(1)左右（さゆう） + する(2) + Noun(1) されます(2) される
explanation: A phrase highlighting that something is being controlled or affected. (A) is being maneuvered left and right freely.

example_sentences.japanese: 流行についてのサイト、記事のタイトル：「靴磨きが靴の寿命と美しさをさゆうする」
example_sentences.english: Website about fashion, title of an article: 'Polishing shoes influences the shoe's lifespan and beauty.' (impacts・affects)

example_sentences.japanese: 新しくできる法律が、国民の自由を大きくさゆうするかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: The new law that is being made may largely influence the freedom of citizens.

example_sentences.japanese: 砂糖を入れるか入れないかで、味を大きくさゆうすることが出来ます。
example_sentences.english: Depending on whether you put sugar in or not, you can greatly influence the taste.

example_sentences.japanese: 商品の値段はお客さんが商品を買うか買わないかをさゆうすることがある。
example_sentences.english: There are times when the price of a product dictates whether the customer will buy it or not.

example_sentences.japanese: 肉を焼いてからタレをいれることは、味を大きくさゆうする原因の一つだ。
example_sentences.english: Cooking the meat before you add the sauce is a factor that will greatly impact the flavor.

example_sentences.japanese: この人は話す人に意見をさゆうされることが多いです。
example_sentences.english: This person's opinions are easily influenced by those they talk to.

example_sentences.japanese: 農業は天気に大きくさゆうされる仕事です。
example_sentences.english: Farming is a job that is largely controlled by the weather.

example_sentences.japanese: 歴史書：「古代ギリシャ人は自分たちの生活が神々にさゆうされると信じていた。」
example_sentences.english: History book: 'Ancient Greeks believed that their lives were influenced by gods.' (impacted・controlled)

example_sentences.japanese: ビジネス記事：「新しい法律が電気自動車の需要をさゆうするかもしれない。」
example_sentences.english: Business article: 'The new law may influence the demand for electric cars.' (impact・control)

example_sentences.japanese: 教科書：「裁判官は賄賂などによってさゆうされないよう、良い給与が保証されている。」
example_sentences.english: Textbook: 'Judges are guaranteed a decent salary so that they won't be swayed (influenced) by bribes and the like. ' (impacted・controlled)

example_sentences.japanese: 記事：「平均余命を大きくさゆうするのは食生活や睡眠時間だと考えられている。」
example_sentences.english: Article: 'One's eating habits and the amount of sleep one gets are thought to have a huge influence on life expectancy.' (impact・control)

example_sentences.japanese: ライフスタイルについてのサイト上の記事：「睡眠の質は雑音の大きさにさゆうされることが多い。」
example_sentences.english: An article on a website about lifestyle: 'Quality of sleep is often influenced by noise.' (impacted・controlled)

example_sentences.japanese: お茶の葉の育て方の記事：「日光にどのくらい葉が当たるかどうかは、お茶の香り、味を大きくさゆうする要因の一つになります。」
example_sentences.english: Article about growing tea leaves: 'About how much exposure the leaves get to sunlight will be one of the factors that largely influences the smell and taste of tea.' (impact・control)

example_sentences.japanese: 講座の広告：「本講座を受講すると、ストレスなどにさゆうされにくくなります！」
example_sentences.english: Course advertisement: 'If you complete this course you will become a person that is not easily influenced by stress and the like!' (impacted・controlled)

example_sentences.japanese: 薬を服用した直後にグレープフルーツを食べると、薬の効き目がさゆうされるかもしれません。
example_sentences.english: If you eat grapefruit immediately after taking medicine, the effect of the medicine may be impacted.' (influence・affect)

example_sentences.japanese: 科学者が、校長や親に：「子供の肘の具合がどのようにスポーツ、とりわけ野球によってさゆうされるのかを調べたいです。」
example_sentences.english: Scientists, to school directors and parents: 'I want to investigate the condition of children's elbows and how they are influenced by sports, especially baseball.' (impacted・affected)

example_sentences.japanese: とあるラブコメ、語り手：「人生とは選択の連続である。その選択のそれぞれが運命をさゆうするかもしれない。」
example_sentences.english: A love comedy, the narrator: 'Life is a series of choices. Each of them might influence your fate.' (impact・control)

example_sentences.japanese: マラソン優勝者へのインタビュー、優勝者：「マラソンは精神によって大きくさゆうされるスポーツです。」
example_sentences.english: Interview with marathon winner, the winner: 'A marathon is a sport that is greatly influenced by the mind.' (impacted・controlled)
